Hi Maria,

The conference notes
This is very promising.  I think that that your notes require a bit of extra contex:
I copied them here:
Source: https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/report-european-music-economy/blob/main/background/slovak-policy-documents/conference_notes_20230918.qmd
Rendered: https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/report-european-music-economy/blob/main/docs/background/slovak-policy-documents/conference_notes_20230918.md

I think that it could be improved a bit, and perhaps written into a blogpost in the following structure?
1 paragraph: what was the conference title, where it was held, who organised it, and why it is relevant for our workshop and our Consortium's work.
2. editing your notes in a way that Arianna, Richard, or others who are not privy to what this was can understand your notes.

We are anyways desperately short of blog posts, and thinking in blog posts forces you to make documents that can be used by people who were not in our Zoom call and do not know what you have been taking notes of.
@Johannes Braunbruck&lt;mailto:johannes.braunbruck@synyo.com&gt;  can help you with editing this furher.

About the literature review for the surveys

For the extra material, I place only one of the documents into the repository.  I think that none of these files are confidential, and they have absolutely nothing to do with the SINUS Cloud, and we do not even need to store them in copy on GitHub. However, they need to be documented, because you cannot even finalise your Eurostat data request without them, so I would like to ask you to add the rest tomorrow morning, so that we can perhaps finalise the data request on Wednesday.

 To recap what we agreed on my visit to Bratisalva to you and Katerina, this is how you can make such material reviewable.  This would have saved countless of hours of work for James, Tomas and I when we desperately tried to find your references during your holiday.

- you add them to the bibliography on Zotero
- download them into a .bib file
- and add a paragraph to this reader to make sure that there is at least 1 sentence written about them (why you selected them) and to see if the reference works properly.

Like this:
https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/triple-transition/Reader.html

So, this is how I did it (you can finish yourself the rest):
- I googled EU-SILC_2021.pdf  (this could have been avoided if you place the document into our group Zotero folder or the bibliography)
- I found this document https://circabc.europa.eu/sd/a/de23ebb5-9f97-47ca-a46d-570bdebc6727/Methodological%20guidelines%202021%20operation%20v8.pdf
- I added it to our joint citation collection&lt;https://www.zotero.org/groups/4559070/digital_music_observatory/collections/CUGBQPBT&gt; (not as a file but as a citation)
- I exported the citation from Zotero into BiBlatex  (ExportedItem.bib the default file name)
- I gave it a more memorable identifier @eurostat_eu-silc_2021

It look now like this, and anybody can directly cite it in an economics journal:

@misc{eurostat_eu-silc_2021,
title = {Methodolgoical Guidelines and Description of {EU}-{SILC} Target Variables. 2021 operation (Version 8)},
url = {https://circabc.europa.eu/sd/a/de23ebb5-9f97-47ca-a46d-570bdebc6727/Methodological%20guidelines%202021%20operation%20v8.pdf},
publisher = {Eurostat},
author = {Eurostat},
urldate = {2023-09-18},
date = {2021},
year = {2021},
langid = {english},
note = {{DocSILC}065 (2021 operation)},
keywords = {2021, {EU}-{SILC}, Surveys}
}

I copied this to the bib/surveys.bib in our OPA compliant simpel file repoitory so now everybody in our project can import it or cite it.

Then I added to this Reader:
Surveys

bib/surveys.bib

  *   Methodolgoical Guidelines and Description of EU-SILC Target Variables. 2021 operation (Version 8) [@eurostat_eu-silc_2021]

Just to test out that I have recorded all data of eurostat_eu-silc_2021  correctly and it will work in Word, PDF, epub, and html:


bib/surveys.bib

  *   Methodolgoical Guidelines and Description of EU-SILC Target Variables. 2021 operation (Version 8) (Eurostat 2021&lt;http://localhost:4722/Reader.html#ref-eurostat_eu-silc_2021&gt;)

What I described now is also available in our Contributor Handbook, and we have practiced this in Bratislava. I think that it took me longer to write this email than it would take to put all the survey documentation to its proper place.

As a side note, @James Rhys Edwards&lt;mailto:JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt; was referring to a different year of EU-SILC, I do not think that EU-SILC had a 2021 CAP survey, so we need the questionnaires and methodological notes of those years where there is the data that you would like to put into your Eurostat data request.

Do you think that you can try to do that in the morning? I think this is really just 20 minutes of work until you properly copy the document's data that you already looked up today and check if all is working.   It really took me more time to write how to do this, but I do not want to copy the rest of the documents in place, because I think that this is an excellent practice for you and perhaps even Arianna who should anyways be prepared about mixed surveys.

I think that this is a very useful task, because as far as I know, every single economics journal that we may target wants to see citations in this way.

Best regards,
Daniel

Hi all,



Thank you for the productive call!



To prepare for our Eurostat microdata application, we need the most recent codebooks and questionnaires for:



  *   EU-LFS
  *   EU-SILC – also specifically 2006 and 2015 - Social and cultural participation (ilc_scp)
  *   AES – also specifically 2007 and 2011 (there may have also been an AES module on culture post-2012 when the ESSnet-Culture recommendations were published – we must check)
  *   HBS
  *   ICT
  *   HETUS



We should tender the microdata application as a research network consisting of EUBA, UVA, SSSA, and UTU (and possibly SINUS if we are recognized in time, otherwise we will tender separately for the SILC and AES data alone).

To prepare specifically for the Slovakia workshop, we also need:



  *   KULT-5-01 and KULT-19 methodological notes (as we already have for KULT-16-01)
  *   ROČ 1-01 and ROČ 2-01 questionnaires
  *   ROČ 2-01 and NSNO 1-01 sampling method
  *   To ask in workshop: response rates



We can use the Eurostat microdata application as a “template” for our Slovakian statistical authority microdata application. This should be ready to hand over to them on Thursday.



Re: the post-workshop with the other CMOs, I will prepare a partner survey on surveys (similarly to the one Magali sent around for D2.1 about airplay quotas, etc.). Basically, we will ask what national-level surveying programmes exist in the target countries, for links to codebooks and questionnaires, and about microdata access procedures. We can introduce the topic during the post-workshop, and I will send out the survey after. I imagine microdata access on a national level will become easier once we have been granted access by Eurostat.



@EUBA, let’s plan on lunch and a one-hour meeting to go over any questions on the Slovak surveying program on 19 Sept.



@Daniel and @Joost, separately SINUS will need the codebooks and questionnaires for the CEEMID surveys and UVA anti-piracy survey, respectively. However, this is lower priority.



@Richard and @Daniel, I’ll see you at 09:00 in the call with Joost tomorrow.



Please note all templates are here: https://cloud.sinus-institut.de/ws-OpenMusE/templates



Thank you again, and best regards,

James

Subject: Re: Resend links



Hi .

I was thinking a lot about the IKP presentation, and my preliminary thoughts are these.  Their interests are slightly different than what we prepared for, and I think that the best way to accommodate this is to change my short intervention talk and slides a bit.  There are two topics that appear weighty in their thinking and do not appear on ours: value for money and financing culture.

We can be spontaneous about Joost and my interventions, if we keep in mind that for any value for money, economic impact assessment, or financing gap filling they need a good measurement of existing revenues/income/costs and as a result value added. (They have plenty of revenue-increasing objectives.) And that needs improvement and that is a key focus of our work. The satellite account system uses special prices, but I think it is appropriate for the type of macro-level cost/benefit that a finance ministry may want.

My oriinal part is too technically focused, and if we will have only 0-1 statisticians in the room, then I will just briefly explain that we need to have this done but do not go into details unless asked.  However, I will talk about how good it would be if they would have a better functioning satellite account system, because they would be able to do more value for money analysis.  I can also cover the triple transition focusing on the EU sustainable finance agenda, which offers structure reform public financing and incentivised private funding.  In my view, this corresponds with their interest in financing the cultural sector and drawing on additional financing from EU/private funds. But connecting this to a good functional satellite account system, a good measurement of value added and income types.  This is also appropriate because Infostat will not come but the finance ministry analysts will come, and they certainly will like this topic and their positive feedback can carry weight with the statistical office.  For the finance ministry, objective 2 / financing the culture sector is the only interest and this way we can talk to them.

Best regards,
Daniel

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202309221141-Re_ CAP survey + ICMP Hudobne centrum-312.txt -->

Hi Daniel,

Thank you for this! I was about to write to ask for a follow-up call on this topic. I'm catching up with my other project for the most part today, but I will go through this and write down my own post-meeting thoughts over the weekend. Would you be available on Monday morning or Tuesday at any time?

Thank you and best regards,
James
________________________________
From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Friday, September 22, 2023 11:38 AM
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;; Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;; Burus István &lt;istvan.burus@reprex.nl&gt;
Subject: CAP survey + ICMP Hudobne centrum

Dear James,

I think that there is an elegant justification for doing CAP surveys in a 2x2 manner.  We need at least 2 CAP surveys in a year to claim harmonisation of the dataset, and we can say that we do not want to burn all research costs in one go before seeing what works.

We can say that WP3 is using it to create novel datasets that meet the requirements of the new ESRS sustainability standards on affected communities (if this will be factually true, I would think we can.)  This standard is going to be developed by EFRAG in 2024/2025, and we can say that we want to test ideas in different phases of the standardisation process.

I think that Artisjus, MusicAutor and SOZA will have different internal needs for a valuation or CAP.

- SOZA may want to delay work, but stay in sync with IKP [we need to assess if this is interfereing with IT work planned for 2024]
- Rosina may want to go faster [but she should line up other data sources to make this useful at all]
- Artisjus is unclear, and we need to talk with Eszter.

However, you have Italy and Germany, too, so I think that as long as you can do a country pair in 2024 and another in 2025 we are fine.

To design the ESRS survey elements there is research needed, it can be Reprex's 2 PMs, we will need to read literature on social sustainability, get in touch with EFRAG, etc.  As for CAP, whatever is needed for valuations is a D1.3 task and it is more or less ready, I will use some time but only for revision.

The critical CAPs are BG and SK, although HU is mandatory, but they are very experienced with it.  If we can go ahead with the Slovak statistical office in 2024, then we should do it in SK in 2024.  I think that IKP will help us, and we do not need a lot of harmonisation in that regard, however, the CAP survey  is our bargaining tool.  I would be more relaxed to spend the SK money after it is sure that we get what we want in return.  Richard  Cas told me that this will require 3-4 personal visits, so it is a bit unlikely that this will be all done before January 2024. I foresaw that this is why Reprex has a bigger travel budget, I knew that getting people to agree on data cooperation will require several visits.

For Rosina, I think that we can press ahead with Bulgaria only if she manages to put together a similar workshop that we had in Slovakia.  The organiser must be MusicAutor, it is their cost in my opinion, and generally I do not think that a workshop must be so extravagant. Travelling to the location is not justified for anybody who is not working on CAP or D1.3.  In my opinion, it is sufficient if I go there plus any of James, Joost, Tomas, Eszter.  I really see no need than 2 people flying there on behalf of the consortium. If we have like a minister of head of statistical office, perhaps Joost or you, if we have a technical level meeting, you, Tomas or Eszter, because perhaps Tomas and Eszter can vouch best for the usefulness of the work, but of course, they are also very busy, so they may not be able to go to Sofia.  Whatever I presented in Slovakia I can present there, too, and to be honest with you, earlier in SK, HR, and HU I was alone fine for this.

About the ICMP/Hudobne centrum change, I talked with Tomas, and we want to do it in the following way.

- We would like to come up with an original/new subproject plan for 2.3 and 4.1. programming 5.1 data observatory.
- Add people, PMs, and money needs into the plan.
- Have it first approved by you, then whoever needs it.
- We will create this subproject plan with Tomas, HC, Istvan and myself.


It would not be a good idea to go ahead without a clear plan on how this will work and how the money will be spent. There are other lingering questions, for example, what will happen with SSSA's PMs in the DMP.  If I need to contribute any further work to T1.1 T2.1 T3.1 in which case I would like the money to hire an assistant.

I would like to increase the SK budget and the Reprex budget with at least about 1-1% of the total OpenMuse budget. I generally believe that REPREX share in the first 9 months of work justifies a very slight increase in our budget, because currently we use very senior working hours and we need two types of juniors: programmer and music policy type.

Last, but not least, I think that the current hiring plan in SSSA is going to cause a lot of problems for everybody.  SSSA wants to hire a single, low-pay grade, starter person for 24 months.  That person in my opinion can only contribute to one task. However, they have performance gaps in at least 4 WPs.  There is no way that they can find a single postdoc for a 2500 euro pay who can write mathematical algorithms, contribute to music policy, data management plan, innovative data uses, etc.  I think that we have many smaller skill shortages, and those organisations should hire who can hire for short term or on a freelance basis, because we do not need 1 new contributor, but at least six.


Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder

Hi all,

Thank you both Caterina and Magali for your intensive work over the past few days, and Daniel for your quick turnaround with the review.

I have not yet had a chance to go through the review, but in principle, I agree that at this late juncture we should focus primarily on recommendations that can realistically be implemented by Thursday.

As the DX.1 series is planned to be synergistic, comprehensive reworks of D1.1 and D2.1 are anticipated in any case. I would suggest a meeting between the WP1-3 leaders immediately following the submission of D2.1, to plan the alignment process. My initial idea is that joint annexes in harmonised spreadsheet form covering data gaps, data sources, and indicator candidates in all three pillars (economy, diversity &amp; circulation, and society &amp; citizenship) would make sense. This is not least because many of our data sources in fact address multiple pillars, depending upon the analytical perspective taken.

This would realise the assertion in the D1.1, D2.1, and D3.1 descriptions that indicator candidates will be added to the OMO.

To close, as SINUS has no PM in WP2, we must leave the incorporation of reviewer comments to SSSA and the other contributors. However, we will conduct a final review prior to submission.

Best regards,
James

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;

To: Rosina Petrova &lt;rosina_petrova@musicautor.org&gt;; Balázs Huszák &lt;bhuszak@artisjus.com&gt;; Richard Demčák &lt;richard.demcak@soza.sk&gt;
Cc: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Subject: Data collection for D1.3 valuations

Hi Rosina, Balazs, Richard,

At Rosina's request, I would like you to comb together data for valuations.  I suggest that we have a meeting or call with Eszter and Balazs to talk about Artisjus's valuation needs and timeframe.

You will get access to this Google Spreadsheet and please start filling it out.  For Balazs, I think that only the annual reports are important.
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1_8k3AUWMzdvIuxjWKxmxYDfyT0-x7gVMO9-1aJjPsM8/edit#gid=0
 My internet on the train is not stable, so some of you may get this with a few hours delay.

I'd like to have the information on the following datasets in the spreadsheet, without the actual data:
- Your datasets (Excel files) as you submitted them for CISAC-GESAC and what you received back.
- A list of statistical datasets of the Bulgarian statistical office that are relevant to music or their users, i.e. radio, television, cabletv, cinema, theatre, concerts, restaurants, hotels etc.... Do not select, just collect their name in Bulgarian and English, and a link. Anything that may relate to your clients, i.e. music users of broadcasting, retransmission and public performance
- A list of potential data sources with Bulgarian state organisations, such as the media authority on anything that quantifies media use, including again any data that is related to broadcasting, retransmission and public performance.
- The annual financial reports of your biggest users, i.e. tv stations or major radio stations. Last few years.
- Any studies and data published about Bulgarian cultural participation, cultural, creative industries, without too much thinking if it is relevant or not, if it may be relevant.
- Annual reports for several years about other music organisations, most important is of course Prophon.
- Annual reports of biggest labels, music publishers.

Financial reports are publci documents, we do not need non-public data at this point. Also, if your GESAC-CISAC data is correct, at this point we do need need further internal data from you.

It is fine for me if this is Google Spreadsheet with the following fields:
- URL, Title in Bulgarian, title in English, one sentence description, for books: ISBN, journal articles: ISSN, published documents if you find them: DOI
- for your datasets, sensitive datasets you leave the URL open, and just provide the titles and description
- for the GESAC-CISAC datasets, add every spreadsheet from the Excel files in a separate row. Do not send them now yet, just write into the database if you have them for the last 3-4 years.
- and if they do not have a clear title, only use the description.

Best regards,
Daniel

**From:** Richard Wages &lt;Richard.Wages@sinus-institut.de&gt;

**Date:** 09/12/2023 15:46:58

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202309121546-OpenMusE __ Update - Bratislava workshop planning-772.txt -->

Dear OpenMusE team,

The agenda for our stakeholders workshop on the 21st of September (i.e., next week) has been finalised. Please find attached an updated (English) version of the morning agenda which had just been forwarded to me by our partner SOZA.

As several people have been asking in the meantime, here is the list of all three Bratislava sessions:

  *   Wednesday, 20.09., 14:00 – (end time not fixed): Consortium-internal “pre-workshop” – discussion of OpenMusE data collection in general
  *   Thursday, 21 .09.; 09:00 – 12:30: Slovakian stakeholder workshop – presentation of work done so far (incl. T1.1 and T2.1) and discussion of next steps in Slovakia
  *   Thursday, 21 .09.; after lunch – (end time not fixed): Consortium “post-workshops” with other CMOs – transfer of the Slovak activities to Bulgaria and Hungary

To give the organisers (SOZA &amp; EUBA) some idea of number of people to be expected and help them with their preparations, please drop a short info email for your organisation to Maria, Katarina, Richard D., and Tomas (in cc) to let them know with how many people you will attend and on which date(s).

Looking forward to seeing all of you in Bratislava.

Cheers,
Richard

**From:** Richard Wages &lt;Richard.Wages@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**To:** Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;  
**Cc:** James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;, Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;, Joost Poort &lt;j.p.poort@uva.nl&gt;  
**Date:** 09/22/2023 11:01:32

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202309221101-Re_ Wednesday data brainstorming-776.txt -->

Hi Daniel,

This overlong email states numerous things I knew already and several thoughts that are obvious to me. I.e., it remains unclear to me what the intended message was. Is there something particular you ask me to do from now on? Is there something you promise to do from now on? Is there some concrete criticism?

Thanks

Richard Wages

mob +49 179 135 1406

INTEGRAL-SINUS-OPINION Group
Berlin, Heidelberg, Nürnberg, Vienna, Singapore

Am 22.09.2023 um 10:26 schrieb Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;:

﻿
Dear Richard,

In the meeting on Wednesday, several aspects of the data workflow were touched in a brainstorming manner. In my opinion it should work between the D5.1 Observatory (REPREX), D6.3 DMP (REPREX/SSSA) and WPs like Joost's WP1 or James' WP2. Because Tomas was addressed with his organisation as a potential data source, he can also review this.

It is important that task/WP leaders, and in case of significant PM use the PMB or all WP leaders affected are on board with the plans. Working with data is central to our Consortium's work and usually we try to solve complex data programs that involve much work. The PIs and WP leaders have the seniority to vet plans and find under/overestimated research time. Underestimation of a task will cause delays with all affected organisations, and overestimation in low impact and value for money of the grant.

Example (trivial, for illustration only):
WP9 researchers Jane and John come up with a hypothesis that Andorra's economic development will not reach the levels of two other mini-states, Liechtenstein and San Marino till 2026. They want to test this, and they suggest creating an indicator to test this hypothesis: compare the projected GDP/capita of the three mini-states for 2026. They would like to use linear extrapolation of past values of the two datasets for the forecast.

They state that they need two datasets, populations of AD, LI, SM, and the GDP or AD, LI, SM. they want divide GDP values with population values for each year.  Both dataseta are available with missing data in the Eurostat data warehoulse. Jane and Jone plan to spend 3 days on the analysis.  They also state when they want to spend these 3 days. I think this is part of the "Data Collection Plan of WP9", which is in WP9.1 (novel data collection methods to fill data gaps)

They ask WP4 UTU/REPREX to access in a reproducible way and process these datasets from Eurostat, i.e. impute the missing values in both datasets, apply a linear extrapolation algorithm to provide them with the AD-LI-SM GDP/capita datasets.  UTU/REPREX say that this will take 1 day. They state when they find this day.  Reproducibility means that as the calendar turns from 2023 to 2024, new factual data will be added automatically to the dataset, and the extrapolation till 2026 will be updated till 2027. I.e. Jane and John can use their dataset throughout the project in the freshest form.

In this example, we use a trivial external data source. However, if we were to ask for data access from an external party, like the Slovak statistical office, or GESAC, we should have a clear plan that is credible and appealing to the other party.  Sending out requests to third parties that are not thought through will reflect badly on our consortium and eventually will lead to data foreclosure. On the other hand, if internal resources are needed from Aloaded, or the CMOs, then we should investigate what their internal data provision costs, and the procedure should be documented by the DMP team, too. Again, it will strain cooperation in the consortium if researchers go on unvetted fishing expeditions to the industry partners and create a lot of headaches that eventually will not lead to results.

It should be the Task/WP leader who contacts external or internal data sources with a very well-designed data request, and I think that their teams should not go out fishing for data without senior oversight. If the WP leaders need help to reach out to industry sources, including consortium industry members, they escalate it to the Coordinator, who may ask Joost, Tomas, Daniel, Rosina, Anna, Eszter with significant network in the industry and may help. That would also add an additional layer of review to the plan, because they will not risk their reputation with half-baked data use plans.

After we have secured the data, the data processing WP5.1 task (get the AD-LI-SM GDP, population dataset, impute missing values, and process it to GDP/capita), if new software code is needed for processing, it is a WP4.1 task (UTU/REPREX, UTU has the most resource), and the and the documentation of the resulting data is WP6.3 task (REPREX/SSSA, SSSA has the most resource).

The DMP must state how other researchers and computers can access the resulting AD/SM/LI dataset and properly document which countries are involved, timeframe, unit of measure, number of columns, what imputation and estimation methods were used, what is the final size in kB, etc. Currently, because SSSA has the most PMs in the DMP, this will require that somebody in SSSA uses the W3C/SDMX/DublinCore/DataCite standards to describe the dataset for human and machine use, with help from Reprex (task leader.)  Neither SSSA nor REPREX need to assign people who know about Lichtenstein, GDP or population. That is the hypothetical WP9 task. They know why these datagaps needed to be filled and how.

In the AD-LI-SM GDP/Capita we have a trivial task, and I even exaggerated their resource needs. It can be a simple email between colleagues. However, if the expected PM use exceeds 1 PM, the hypothetical WP9.1 task leader should get an approval from the WP9 leader, if at least 1 PM is affected in another WP, the Coordinator should be informed, and at one point the PMB should vet the idea, also from a research resource under/overestimation point of view to get a realistic view on who will be doing what and when.

In my opinion, the reason why and how an AD-LI-SM GDP/Capita dataset is needed is the  responsibility of the T9.1 task/WP leader.

When the AD-LI-SM GDP/Capita dataset is created, it should be professionally documented and added to the DMP. This is a data documentation and dissemination competence.  If there are licensing requirements, then it requires legal competence, too. But based on the exploitation plans so far known, I do not really see that there will be any valuable datasets created that will have licensing requirements, perhaps apart from the Listen Local datasets.

1. There should be no data requests and fishing expedition without a sound research hypothesis vetted by a WP leader.
2. If the resource need of this research is significant, the Coordinator should review if it fully aligns with the stated goals and tasks of the grant agreement.
3. If significant work is expected from other WPs their WP/task leaders must approve.
4. The Observatory (technically) DMP (in description) should make the final dataset available for internal and external stakeholders.
5. It is not an Observatory/DMP task to design the dataset and the procedures required to create it.

Am 22.09.2023 um 10:26 schrieb Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;:

﻿
Dear Richard,

In the meeting on Wednesday, several aspects of the data workflow were touched in a brainstorming manner. In my opinion it should work between the D5.1 Observatory (REPREX), D6.3 DMP (REPREX/SSSA) and WPs like Joost's WP1 or James' WP2. Because Tomas was addressed with his organisation as a potential data source, he can also review this.

It is important that task/WP leaders, and in case of significant PM use the PMB or all WP leaders affected are on board with the plans. Working with data is central to our Consortium's work and usually we try to solve complex data programs that involve much work. The PIs and WP leaders have the seniority to vet plans and find under/overestimated research time. Underestimation of a task will cause delays with all affected organisations, and overestimation in low impact and value for money of the grant.

Example (trivial, for illustration only):
WP9 researchers Jane and John come up with a hypothesis that Andorra's economic development will not reach the levels of two other mini-states, Liechtenstein and San Marino till 2026. They want to test this, and they suggest creating an indicator to test this hypothesis: compare the projected GDP/capita of the three mini-states for 2026. They would like to use linear extrapolation of past values of the two datasets for the forecast.

They state that they need two datasets, populations of AD, LI, SM, and the GDP or AD, LI, SM. they want divide GDP values with population values for each year.  Both dataseta are available with missing data in the Eurostat data warehoulse. Jane and Jone plan to spend 3 days on the analysis.  They also state when they want to spend these 3 days. I think this is part of the "Data Collection Plan of WP9", which is in WP9.1 (novel data collection methods to fill data gaps)

They ask WP4 UTU/REPREX to access in a reproducible way and process these datasets from Eurostat, i.e. impute the missing values in both datasets, apply a linear extrapolation algorithm to provide them with the AD-LI-SM GDP/capita datasets.  UTU/REPREX say that this will take 1 day. They state when they find this day.  Reproducibility means that as the calendar turns from 2023 to 2024, new factual data will be added automatically to the dataset, and the extrapolation till 2026 will be updated till 2027. I.e. Jane and John can use their dataset throughout the project in the freshest form.

In this example, we use a trivial external data source. However, if we were to ask for data access from an external party, like the Slovak statistical office, or GESAC, we should have a clear plan that is credible and appealing to the other party.  Sending out requests to third parties that are not thought through will reflect badly on our consortium and eventually will lead to data foreclosure. On the other hand, if internal resources are needed from Aloaded, or the CMOs, then we should investigate what their internal data provision costs, and the procedure should be documented by the DMP team, too. Again, it will strain cooperation in the consortium if researchers go on unvetted fishing expeditions to the industry partners and create a lot of headaches that eventually will not lead to results.

It should be the Task/WP leader who contacts external or internal data sources with a very well-designed data request, and I think that their teams should not go out fishing for data without senior oversight. If the WP leaders need help to reach out to industry sources, including consortium industry members, they escalate it to the Coordinator, who may ask Joost, Tomas, Daniel, Rosina, Anna, Eszter with significant network in the industry and may help. That would also add an additional layer of review to the plan, because they will not risk their reputation with half-baked data use plans.

After we have secured the data, the data processing WP5.1 task (get the AD-LI-SM GDP, population dataset, impute missing values, and process it to GDP/capita), if new software code is needed for processing, it is a WP4.1 task (UTU/REPREX, UTU has the most resource), and the and the documentation of the resulting data is WP6.3 task (REPREX/SSSA, SSSA has the most resource).

The DMP must state how other researchers and computers can access the resulting AD/SM/LI dataset and properly document which countries are involved, timeframe, unit of measure, number of columns, what imputation and estimation methods were used, what is the final size in kB, etc. Currently, because SSSA has the most PMs in the DMP, this will require that somebody in SSSA uses the W3C/SDMX/DublinCore/DataCite standards to describe the dataset for human and machine use, with help from Reprex (task leader.)  Neither SSSA nor REPREX need to assign people who know about Lichtenstein, GDP or population. That is the hypothetical WP9 task. They know why these datagaps needed to be filled and how.

In the AD-LI-SM GDP/Capita we have a trivial task, and I even exaggerated their resource needs. It can be a simple email between colleagues. However, if the expected PM use exceeds 1 PM, the hypothetical WP9.1 task leader should get an approval from the WP9 leader, if at least 1 PM is affected in another WP, the Coordinator should be informed, and at one point the PMB should vet the idea, also from a research resource under/overestimation point of view to get a realistic view on who will be doing what and when.

In my opinion, the reason why and how an AD-LI-SM GDP/Capita dataset is needed is the  responsibility of the T9.1 task/WP leader.

When the AD-LI-SM GDP/Capita dataset is created, it should be professionally documented and added to the DMP. This is a data documentation and dissemination competence.  If there are licensing requirements, then it requires legal competence, too. But based on the exploitation plans so far known, I do not really see that there will be any valuable datasets created that will have licensing requirements, perhaps apart from the Listen Local datasets.

1. There should be no data requests and fishing expedition without a sound research hypothesis vetted by a WP leader.
2. If the resource need of this research is significant, the Coordinator should review if it fully aligns with the stated goals and tasks of the grant agreement.
3. If significant work is expected from other WPs their WP/task leaders must approve.

Hello everyone,

After some six hours of formatting and correction work D2.1 was at last submitted to the EC by 10:30 pm sharp. So, it was good that I received the document early today and started around 4pm – otherwise we would have run into trouble. After the format cleansing the core text came down to 90 pages. However, annex II brings it up to 158 pages in total. Annex I is in xlsx format and could not reasonably be transferred into PDF form. Hence, D2.1 now has in its place a public link to the Sinus Cloud (i.e., everybody with the link can read/download the legal mapping file, but not edit it).

The deliverable is now available for download for the consortium under https://cloud.sinus-institut.de/ws-OpenMusE/deliverables as usual.

Going into the weekend now.

Cheers,
Richard

**Date:** 10/24/2023 11:00:27

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202310241100-Re_ Slovak Comprehensive Music Database _ Hudobné -5.txt -->

Dear Daniel,
I spoke with Igor on Friday and today we had a meeting with Radovan and 
Alenka Volna and we agreed more precisely on the export. Alena Volná is 
the IT person to add to your contacts - volna@awd.sk .

I have spoken to a colleague from the Slovak National Library - they are 
interested in getting to know the project and collaborating on it. They 
were interested in a framework for collaboration - some form of 
agreement - and I assume other libraries would also be interested in 
possibly joining. It could be a very simple agreement e.g. that they 
will supply db exports at a certain time interval or provide an 
endpoint, and you will exchange logos with links to each other's web 
sites. No financing necessary.
There will be a person from the National Library coming to the IAML 
meeting on Wednesday to give a comprehensive briefing on audio documents 
(CDs and LPs) in the SNK, and the regulations that apply to this area in 
the Slovak Republic.

Concerning organ database
It was created primarily as a study database of organs for researchers 
and those interested in organs, so it also contains, for example, 
entries with  organs already disappeared or organs that are not in service.
The organ database is largely not translated into English (this can of 
course be addressed).
As for the direct connection to concert venues, I have my doubts. The 
vast majority of organs are found in churches, and not all of them are 
also concert venues.
We'll send you an output from our db of concert halls just in case.
Best regards,
Anna

Dear Daniel,
I am sending you an export of our IS structure with one composer's data, 
prepared in May by Alenka Volná in sql. She also prepared a 
database-info file with translation of table names. Is this scope 
sufficient for your analysis? Will you need it in CSV or Excel? Should 
we send it with the data as well?
Thank you and kind regards,

Anna Žilková
Hudobné centrum / Music Centre Slovakia
Oddelenie dokumentácie a informatiky /
Documentation and Information Department
tel./phone +421220470310, +421911980328

Dňa 24. 10. 2023 o 13:39 Daniel Antal napísal(a):
&gt; Dear Colleagues,
&gt;
&gt;
&gt; On Tue, Oct 24, 2023 at 11:00 AM Anna Zilkova &lt;anna.zilkova@hc.sk&gt; wrote:
&gt;
&gt;     Dear Daniel,
&gt;     I spoke with Igor on Friday and today we had a meeting with
&gt;     Radovan and Alenka Volna and we agreed more precisely on the
&gt;     export. Alena Volná is the IT person to add to your contacts -
&gt;     volna@awd.sk .
&gt;
&gt;     I have spoken to a colleague from the Slovak National Library -
&gt;     they are interested in getting to know the project and
&gt;     collaborating on it. They were interested in a framework for
&gt;     collaboration - some form of agreement - and I assume other
&gt;     libraries would also be interested in possibly joining. It could
&gt;     be a very simple agreement e.g. that they will supply db exports
&gt;     at a certain time interval or provide an endpoint, and you will
&gt;     exchange logos with links to each other's web sites. No financing
&gt;     necessary.
&gt;     There will be a person from the National Library coming to the
&gt;     IAML meeting on Wednesday to give a comprehensive briefing on
&gt;     audio documents (CDs and LPs) in the SNK, and the regulations that
&gt;     apply to this area in the Slovak Republic.
&gt;
&gt;
&gt; I think that defining endpoints and a formal agreement should be aimed 
&gt; by the end of January, early February. The way I would approach it is 
&gt; to work with a few small samples, in which me and my co-researchers 
&gt; would basically design a data model and the service, and we would also 
&gt; end up in your organisation or in Reprex, as convenient, some basic 
&gt; infrastructure with endpoints. It is a bit difficult to define these 
&gt; things before we did not see data samples, but the data samples can be 
&gt; very small, like exporting the records of 5 CDs. We would like to see 
&gt; how heterogeneous are the sources, how easy they are to bring to a 
&gt; common format, and to read.
&gt;
&gt; So at this point it would be good to get a sample of data from several 
&gt; libraries, to understand the difficulties and technical preparedness, 
&gt; and we would come back with a first draft of a service plan and a 
&gt; formal agreement in November.  This would go through 1-2 rounds of 
&gt; discussion, where I would be present, and we would be able to give a 
&gt; precise (legal, technical) answer to these questions sometime very 
&gt; early next year.
&gt;
&gt;
&gt;
&gt;
&gt;     Concerning organ database
&gt;     It was created primarily as a study database of organs for
&gt;     researchers and those interested in organs, so it also contains,
&gt;     for example, entries with  organs already disappeared or organs
&gt;     that are not in service.
&gt;     The organ database is largely not translated into English (this
&gt;     can of course be addressed).
&gt;
&gt;
&gt; Dr Peter van Kranenburg is a Dutch musicology and ethnology scholar, 
&gt; who researches organs and organ builders, and he is in the process of 
&gt; connecting several countries with similar databases intended for 
&gt; organists and organ researchers. I showed him your website and he 
&gt; found it easy to understand, because he is very knowledgeable about 
&gt; organs --- while indeed some expressions would need some English 
&gt; explanation, for somebody who knows a lot about organs it was 
&gt; relatively easy to understand what was there.
&gt;
&gt; https://meertens.knaw.nl/2021/11/30/peterkr/
&gt;
&gt;
&gt;     As for the direct connection to concert venues, I have my doubts.
&gt;     The vast majority of organs are found in churches, and not all of
&gt;     them are also concert venues.
&gt;     We'll send you an output from our db of concert halls just in case.
&gt;
&gt;
&gt; Dr van Kranenburg and some other colleagues have solved a lot of 
&gt; issues that are not so much related to concerts, but the 
&gt; identification and problem of describing concert venues. For example, 
&gt; if we get to the point where we can connect your concert list with 
&gt; SOZA's, there will be many problems with changing address forms, venue 
&gt; names, etc.  For this we are developing AI solutions that track the 
&gt; changes and can make corrections, and they are already built into the 
&gt; organ database. For example, in the Netherlands, two protestant 
&gt; churches merged, which means that the names of the buildings, i.e. the 
&gt; church names that have the organs, all changed a few years ago.  
&gt; Tracing these changes manually can be very difficult, as I learned 
&gt; when I was working with SOZA's concert venue list.
&gt;
&gt; Best regards,
&gt; Daniel
&gt;

Dobrý deň pani Hudecová,

Vyhovovalo by Vám stretnutie o 14:00? Zároveň zasielam krátky úvod a zdôvodnenie potreby stretnutia od pána Antala.

On 21 September 2023 the Horizon Europe project "Open Music Europe" held a stakeholder consultation in Bratislava about the possibilities for improving the current Slovak cultural satellite accounts for cultural policy implementation, and to add details for further industries currently not covered by a separate account with the example of the music industry. These proposals are based on the best practices of using privately-held data in the making of official statistics, and sharing the results of open science with open statistics.  We would like to seek a meeting on behalf of Open Music Europe (as a potential data and know-how provider), IKP (as a potential user of the improved statistical indicators) and statistical office about the possibilities of providing data via a so-called SBR satellite to the office for the improvement of its satellite accounts. On behalf of "Open Music Europe", Daniel Antal, CFA would travel to Bratislava from the Netherlands; he is the responsible task leader for data management in this project, and he is the author of the Slovak music industry report which pioneered the use of privately-held data for public policy purposes.  Mr. Antal does not speak Slovak, but we are happy to facilitate conversation in a mix of English and Slovak.

V prípade akýchkoľvek otázok ma neváhajte kontaktovať.

Ďakujem
S pozdravom a prianím pekného dňa

Dobrý deň pani Hudecová,

Vyhovovalo by Vám stretnutie o 14:00? Zároveň zasielam krátky úvod a zdôvodnenie potreby stretnutia od pána Antala.

On 21 September 2023 the Horizon Europe project "Open Music Europe" held a stakeholder consultation in Bratislava about the possibilities for improving the current Slovak cultural satellite accounts for cultural policy implementation, and to add details for further industries currently not covered by a separate account with the example of the music industry. These proposals are based on the best practices of using privately-held data in the making of official statistics, and sharing the results of open science with open statistics.  We would like to seek a meeting on behalf of Open Music Europe (as a potential data and know-how provider), IKP (as a potential user of the improved statistical indicators) and statistical office about the possibilities of providing data via a so-called SBR satellite to the office for the improvement of its satellite accounts. On behalf of "Open Music Europe", Daniel Antal, CFA would travel to Bratislava from the Netherlands; he is the responsible task leader for data management in this project, and he is the author of the Slovak music industry report which pioneered the use of privately-held data for public policy purposes.  Mr. Antal does not speak Slovak, but we are happy to facilitate conversation in a mix of English and Slovak.

V prípade akýchkoľvek otázok ma neváhajte kontaktovať.

Ďakujem

S pozdravom a prianím pekného dňa

Ing. Marcel Čas, PhD.

Hi daniel,

Ok i see the vision now. I cannot guarantee right now the employment of this person after the end of the project unfortunately. But if he can help your project and my work at IKP, than obviously we would strongly cooperate on an informal basis. We are already working with 2 volunteer master students that are helping us clean datasets and I do want to cooperate whereever possible.

P.S. There is a long-term vision about IKP - about us being bigger and responsible not only for data interpretation, but also for data collection. This is nowhere near to being realised and right now i have to see in the short term what my relationship with the new minister will be like, but I am trying to keep an open mind about such things and look for oportunities. No guarantees though.

Best regards,

Marcel

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Tuesday, October 3, 2023 9:46 AM
To: Čas Marcel &lt;marcel.cas@culture.gov.sk&gt;
Cc: Tomas Miks &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;
Subject: Re: Data exchange with the slovak statistical authorities

Hi Marcel,

Thank you very much, it would be very helpful.

The program that I am trying to follow is very novel and the person we would have in Slovakia would ensure that you, the statistical office, and perhaps some other stakeholders are fully able to implement our software, resource, and data in practice.  It is not necessary that the person is very knowledgeable about national accounts, for example, because I will train and mentor this person for about a year. What would facilitate working together would be if she or he would get assignments from your team that would allow to place the novel data sources into real-time use.  For example, when you have a data puzzle and you do not know where to find relevant data to write a quick report, this person (with me in the background instructing him-her) would try to find relevant data in novel sources and come up with some analysis.

Our aim is to create data that can actually be used in policy analysis.  The only thing is that I cannot guarantee long-term employment for this person in Bratislava, so either the person will have to move or find local work with the accumulated knowledge locally after our project stops.   But either way I think this would allow a very useful knowledge transfer.

Best regards,
Daniel

Subject: RE: pracovné stretnutie medzi ŠÚ SR, MK SR a OPEN MUSIC EUROPE

Dobrý deň pani Hudecová,

Vyhovovalo by Vám stretnutie o 14:00? Zároveň zasielam krátky úvod a zdôvodnenie potreby stretnutia od pána Antala.

On 21 September 2023 the Horizon Europe project "Open Music Europe" held a stakeholder consultation in Bratislava about the possibilities for improving the current Slovak cultural satellite accounts for cultural policy implementation, and to add details for further industries currently not covered by a separate account with the example of the music industry. These proposals are based on the best practices of using privately-held data in the making of official statistics, and sharing the results of open science with open statistics.  We would like to seek a meeting on behalf of Open Music Europe (as a potential data and know-how provider), IKP (as a potential user of the improved statistical indicators) and statistical office about the possibilities of providing data via a so-called SBR satellite to the office for the improvement of its satellite accounts. On behalf of "Open Music Europe", Daniel Antal, CFA would travel to Bratislava from the Netherlands; he is the responsible task leader for data management in this project, and he is the author of the Slovak music industry report which pioneered the use of privately-held data for public policy purposes.  Mr. Antal does not speak Slovak, but we are happy to facilitate conversation in a mix of English and Slovak.

V prípade akýchkoľvek otázok ma neváhajte kontaktovať.

Ďakujem

S pozdravom a prianím pekného dňa

Ing. Marcel Čas, PhD.

Vyhovovalo by Vám stretnutie o 14:00? Zároveň zasielam krátky úvod a zdôvodnenie potreby stretnutia od pána Antala.&lt;http://www.culture.gov.sk/&gt;
 &lt;http://www.culture.gov.sk/&gt;
On 21 September 2023 the Horizon Europe project "Open Music Europe" held a stakeholder consultation in Bratislava about the possibilities for improving the current Slovak cultural satellite accounts for cultural policy implementation, and to add details for further industries currently not covered by a separate account with the example of the music industry. These proposals are based on the best practices of using privately-held data in the making of official statistics, and sharing the results of open science with open statistics.  We would like to seek a meeting on behalf of Open Music Europe (as a potential data and know-how provider), IKP (as a potential user of the improved statistical indicators) and statistical office about the possibilities of providing data via a so-called SBR satellite to the office for the improvement of its satellite accounts. On behalf of "Open Music Europe", Daniel Antal, CFA would travel to Bratislava from the Netherlands; he is the responsible task leader for data management in this project, and he is the author of the Slovak music industry report which pioneered the use of privately-held data for public policy purposes.  Mr. Antal does not speak Slovak, but we are happy to facilitate conversation in a mix of English and Slovak. &lt;http://www.culture.gov.sk/&gt;

For me, the 2023.10.10 in the afternoon, as earlier discussed, is possible, I will be in Bratislava on 9-10 October.   I can join anytime on on 10 October meeting, but I have to leave Slovaka in the afternoon.

I prepared a written version of the issues we discussed on the consultation based on the Memorandum o porozumení o využití výsledkov analýz otvorených politík v kontexte slovenského kultúrneho a kreatívneho priemyslu a sektorových verejných politík v spolupráci s konzorciom pre výskum a inovácie s názvom OpenMuse.

Here is the document: https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/slovakia/slovak-cult-stat-pilot.html&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/slovakia/slovak-cult-stat-pilot.html&gt; [You can download it in PDF, epub, and docx, and if you have questions, you can send us comments/questions in the docx file if you prefer.]

Sincerely yours,
Daniel Antal

Dobrý deň pani Hudecová,

Vyhovovalo by Vám stretnutie o 14:00? Zároveň zasielam krátky úvod a zdôvodnenie potreby stretnutia od pána Antala.

On 21 September 2023 the Horizon Europe project "Open Music Europe" held a stakeholder consultation in Bratislava about the possibilities for improving the current Slovak cultural satellite accounts for cultural policy implementation, and to add details for further industries currently not covered by a separate account with the example of the music industry. These proposals are based on the best practices of using privately-held data in the making of official statistics, and sharing the results of open science with open statistics.  We would like to seek a meeting on behalf of Open Music Europe (as a potential data and know-how provider), IKP (as a potential user of the improved statistical indicators) and statistical office about the possibilities of providing data via a so-called SBR satellite to the office for the improvement of its satellite accounts. On behalf of "Open Music Europe", Daniel Antal, CFA would travel to Bratislava from the Netherlands; he is the responsible task leader for data management in this project, and he is the author of the Slovak music industry report which pioneered the use of privately-held data for public policy purposes.  Mr. Antal does not speak Slovak, but we are happy to facilitate conversation in a mix of English and Slovak.

V prípade akýchkoľvek otázok ma neváhajte kontaktovať.

Ďakujem

S pozdravom a prianím pekného dňa

Ing. Marcel Čas, PhD.

Vyhovovalo by Vám stretnutie o 14:00? Zároveň zasielam krátky úvod a zdôvodnenie potreby stretnutia od pána Antala.&lt;http://www.culture.gov.sk/&gt;
 &lt;http://www.culture.gov.sk/&gt;
On 21 September 2023 the Horizon Europe project "Open Music Europe" held a stakeholder consultation in Bratislava about the possibilities for improving the current Slovak cultural satellite accounts for cultural policy implementation, and to add details for further industries currently not covered by a separate account with the example of the music industry. These proposals are based on the best practices of using privately-held data in the making of official statistics, and sharing the results of open science with open statistics.  We would like to seek a meeting on behalf of Open Music Europe (as a potential data and know-how provider), IKP (as a potential user of the improved statistical indicators) and statistical office about the possibilities of providing data via a so-called SBR satellite to the office for the improvement of its satellite accounts. On behalf of "Open Music Europe", Daniel Antal, CFA would travel to Bratislava from the Netherlands; he is the responsible task leader for data management in this project, and he is the author of the Slovak music industry report which pioneered the use of privately-held data for public policy purposes.  Mr. Antal does not speak Slovak, but we are happy to facilitate conversation in a mix of English and Slovak. &lt;http://www.culture.gov.sk/&gt;

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Thursday, October 12, 2023 1:02 PM
To: Čas Marcel &lt;marcel.cas@culture.gov.sk&gt;
Cc: Rudyjová Michaela &lt;michaela.rudyjova@culture.gov.sk&gt;
Subject: Re: KULT

Hi Marcel and Michaela,


No problem, I am sorry I had to leave so abruptly – I had a meeting about an important strategic document about the investments process in MK SR. The doors of IKP are open to you anytime, so feel free to organize your trips as it suits yourself.

Regarding the KULT surveys:

  *   I agree with starting with them, IF it suits the project – I don’t want to use you

We received public money with a mandate to make an impact with developing usable data products and software tools for public policy.  Some of my Consortium partners are eager to opportunistically spend the money on themselves, I think that spending the money on your needs is 100% aligned with the project goals.  Our mandate is to find data gaps, and use novel data science and statistical methods to fill the data gap by reusing disused open data, or setting up better data collection.


  *   The legality of giving you micro data is kinda wonky and I am trying to find a practical and legal solution. Let me ask you, does the project need the micro data as a project output? Or would the code itself be sufficient as an output? The thing is I cannot legally make the micro data publicly available – only aggregates. But I don’t consider you writing a code for us on our publicly unavailable datasets a breach of this law. If the data does not leave IKP and you, it should not be a problem. I will consult this with our lawyers.

In Europe, the Open Data Directive, which is transposed to Slovak law, allows access for public sector information for reuse at no cost, or marginal cost of provision.  Even Eurostat gives access to researchers who meet data protection rules to microdata.  However, we do not want to publish microdata at all.  I think that what we would do is exactly what we want to do with the Slovak statistical office.

The datasets will be your publicly-held datasets. However, I need to access them to write a code that can re-process them to a more usable microdata file and then to process statistical information from it.  For us, this is a worthy goal provided that the statistically processed data will be public.  (I also believe that it would be illegal to stop making them public based on the Open Data Directive.)

In a practical term, the code will eventually be run on your computer and by your colleague in RStudio. However, to write that code I need to access the data and it would be very practical to move into your office for weeks until everything is perfect. It would be good if I could get a subsample of the data to write the code that fixes it.

Working with microdata is only really problematic if the microdata identifies private persons.  I think that at least some of the KULT surveys only survey legal persons, so GDPR is not applicable to the microdata. However, any concerns can be mitigated if we simply remove the identifiers that would help identifying the responsend, say, if Hudobné centrum is named as a respondent in the file, we will give it a random identifier, for example KULT-RESPONDENT-7865.  I can also write any statement that I will not publish the data.



  *   We are talking roughly about 20 Kult questionnaires in excel (.csv format – sometimes giving us “not IT nerds” problems). Each KULT type, for example “theather” has a separate excel file for each year – roughly from 2014-2021, so 8 excel files for each of the 20 KULT types/questionnaires. Each excel file has tens of  columns (lets say about 50) with indicators and hundreds (f.e. theatres), sometimes thousands (f.e. libraries) rows with cultural institutions and their data.

In my opinion, the only possible concern with this data is the name-identifier of the respondent.  If you are concerned about this, perhaps I could spend a working day in IKP and we could select parts of at least some of the files that are of no concern. For example, visitor numbers without any reference to the size and name of the institutions become sust an abstract time series.  But again, if the respondents are not private persons, this is less of a concern, much of this data should be in their public annual report. And if they are state-public entities, I assume that most of their responses should be public, too.



  *   You can see the data at IKP anytime you want :D Actually sending you the data… I have to figure out the best way. Maybe I will get you to sign a statement that you cannot share the data with anyone else, but IKP. Or something of that sort.

Well, please check our MoU and let's sign a confidentiality agreement. SOSR would require me to work with their micordata in their premises, but it is because they have GDPR protected or business secrecy data, too, and they would monitor me that I do not try to identify the respondents (they would not give me names, but for example, in a small village, technically I could identify a person by gender, age, and occupation.)

To me, in the first round, the most interesting are the three music related surveys.  The ensembles may have private entities, but in my opinion the other two only have legal person and mainly public legal persons data.

In my opinion, this is what you would get:
- An analysis of the quality of the KULT microdata: how sampling, data recording, surveying, and data storage could be improved to avoid future data problems -- private to you, but perhaps good to discuss with SOSR, and other institutions responsible for KULT for quality improvements;
- A report and a code (that can be read, as I showed, either as a report, or just code, or both, annotated) on every problem and how it was fixed, private to you;
- The fixed dataset with every correction in log file (reproducible and reviewable, to ensure that our code works well);
- Summary statistical tables and data visualisations: you must commit to make this public and place it among your website to the EU's open repositories.  This is in my opinion is legal obligation, not a  right, which follows from the Open Data Directive and spending EU money on reprocessing bad data into usable format.  But I do not think that this would be a problem at all.

Best regards,
Daniel



  *
  *   Yeah I agree, that would be the best way forward.

Best regards,

Marcel

## European Commission study on copyright framework fit for research &lt;era2study-surveys@ppmi.lt&gt;

### Invitation to contribute to a European Commission study on copyright issues and challenges in research {#email-125}

**From:** European Commission study on copyright framework fit for research &lt;era2study-surveys@ppmi.lt&gt;  
**To:** daniel.antal@reprex.nl  
**Date:** 10/10/2023 15:17:18

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202310101517-Invitation to contribute to a European Commission -889.txt -->

Dear Daniel,

We would like to invite you to participate in an EU-wide survey of researchers on the copyright issues and challenges they currently face, particularly when accessing and reusing publicly funded R&amp;I results, publications and data for scientific purposes.

You are being invited because you have been a beneficiary of the Horizon 2020 or Horizon Europe funding programmes. Please also see a letter of support provided by the European Commission, which provides further information about the study.

The results of this survey will feed into a wider European Commission study on the effects of the EU copyright framework on research and the effects of potential interventions. The information you provide will help identify and present relevant potential provisions for research in EU data and digital legislation, focusing on rights and obligations. Ultimately, the study will be a key source of evidence for Priority Action 2 of the European Research Area Policy Agenda 2022-2024, which aims to "Propose an EU copyright and data legislative and regulatory framework fit for research."

The survey should take about 20 minutes to complete. Thank you for considering this invitation, and we very much hope that you will kindly respond to the survey.

You can complete the survey using this link: https://s-3abb10-i.sgizmo.eu/s3/i-k0qgpkCVjlWRuzevL-328600/?sguid=k0qgpkCVjlWRuzevL

We would appreciate it if you could complete your survey by 23.59 (CEST), 30 October 2023.

The study team includes the Public Policy and Management Institute (PPMI), together with the University of Amsterdam Institute for Information Law - IViR, the Centre for IT &amp; IP Law at the KU Leuven - CiTiP - and Sant&amp;#39;Anna School of Advanced Studies Pisa.

Any collected data will be treated confidentially, only used for internal purposes, and processed in line with the Privacy Statement.

Should you have any questions or require further information, please do not hesitate to contact us at era2study-surveys@ppmi.lt 

Thank you for being a part of this important study.

Sincerely,
The study team

Predmet: Follow up in Bratislava 9-10 October

Dear Colleagues,

I will be visiting Bratislava on 9 and 10 October, arriving around 12.03 to Bratislava Halavna Stanica; the aim is to follow up on our stakeholder forum

1. We would like to bring on board as a funded partner to Open Music Europe Hubobné centrum

This would effectively replacing the not successful grant proposal for Creative Europe and ensuring that SOZA and Hudobné centrum can work towards the Slovak Comprehensive Music Database as a linked open data resource for the benefit of SK music heritage (HC), better rights management (SOZA), as a statistical source (SOSR) that creates better public policy indicators (IKP).

I will send Hudobné centrum a separate email about this only and I am available on 9 October for further discussion (perhaps after lunch depending on the arrival of my train.).  I will also send more practical information about what tasks we would like to cover and with what form of contracts.  This will arrive tomorrow after consultation with the OME Coordinator.

2. With the help of IKP we are going to visit the Statistical Office of the Slovak Republic (SOSR) to discuss in technical terms what we discussed more broadly on 21 September.

I already prepared a very thorough and technical background document&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/slovakia/slovak-cult-stat-pilot.html&gt; that I can present in PowerPoint, however, I think that it would add value and be taken more seriously if all partners would accompany me with one person. So, apart from IKP, if Hudobné centrum could delegate either Anna or somebody from IT, SOZA  could delegate Marian (GDPR). On behalf of EUBA, I think it would make a good impression if Jakub as vice-rector, perhaps Katarina as vice-dean would come, and later on a technical level Maria would be the contact there. As not much input is needed from EUBA, I think that this is more of a demonstration of the strong commitment-importance locally.

We are aiming to hold this meeting on 11 October at 11.00 (huge thanks to Marcel Cas from IKP).

3. Listen Local -- educational application.

We had always dreamt of using the future SKCDMb comprehensive music database for a goal-driven, special purpose recommender application that takes the music already listened to by children-pupils, and with the help of music educators guides them on a personalised basis through local,regional, Slovak and European music (as required by the music discovery curriculum.)  What I am having in mind is a 21st century, Kodaly-inspired application that could guide teachers and pupils through the gems of the Hudonbné centrum - SKCDMb repertoire with Spotify-Deezer-Apple-YouTube connectivity and in a form that a child born after 2006 can relate to and enjoy.

We cannot move into this direction without further funding (that I may be able to secure) and a partnership from the Bratislava municipality, as we would need access to schools, which is a complicated regulatory affair. This is slightly a secondary topic, but I would like to raise this with Hudobné centrum as well, and if the Bratislava stakeholders show interest, they can also meet me, or join the meeting with the statistical office.

4. Practical cooperation with IKP, SOZA, Hudobné centrum, EUBA

As I mentioned to Tomas and Marcel, I would like to find a Reprex employee locally who would facilitate the data work among all stakeholders.  I would like to find a music-loving, quantitatively minded young researcher or future policy analyst who lives in Bratislava or in Slovakia, is a native speaker and would ensure that my work connects well with IKP, SOZA, Hudobné centrum.

I would also like to find time to visit the IKP team if I do not disturb their work or to have an informal lunch-dinner with Marcel on 10 October.

I will leave Bratislava with an early evening train on 10 October.

Best regards,

Subject: Follow-up from Bratislava: CfP, meeting with SOSK, and Polifonia

Hi James, Balazs, and Leo,

Balazs brought to my attention this conference, as a potential good platform for Open Music Europe publications.  I think that perhaps the agenda that we tried to pursue in Bratislava could fit into their   https://dcc.ac.uk/events/idcc24/call-papers Transparency and trust in research practices section.

On a substantive matter, with the help of IKP and Tomas I am trying to make a personal meeting with the relevant Slovak statistical authority heads of units possible before I go to Bologna to talk about data exchange with Polifonia.  My problem is generally that the planned PMB dates are conflicting with the dates we can offer to the statistical authority, and while I would like to be present in the PMB I also want to make this happen before the CfP deadline and more importantly the meeting with Polifonia which I see our only chance to secure data access.

The topic of how I am framing this is creating a "pilot project" and "sandbox" for data PPP on using privately-held data for official statistics.  This is the language of the relevant high-level working group in the EU data policy agenda. Currently, under these terms, MasterCard or Vodafone are sharing data with official statisticians to improve statistical products, the use of privately-held music data for improvement of cultural statistics would be in my opinion a global first.

As for the CfP, I would argue that it is a novel Transparency and trust in research practices when we create an open science project when the re-use case is improving government statistics with a data PPP. Sharing data with an official statistical authority would be probably an outlier, as this section is mainly focusing on sharing via other open science infrastructure.

As for WP4, I think that a priority would be the programing of the dataset package, which would improve the functionality of the existing eurostat, iotables, spotifyr, and retroharmonize packages with linking data and allowing not only a good download, but also a good upload/sharing with improved metadata use.  One test case would be to download, process and then share data with the Polifonia Horizon project (music data), and then with the Slovak statistical authority (privately-held data for improving government statistics with SDMX metadata.)

For further publication possibilities, I think that this fits in with two statistical policy initiatives:
- Using more and more linked open data among and for statistical offices, which has its own working groups, training, etc in the European Statistical System
- Using privately-held data for improving official statistics, and improving public-private partnership in the creation as well as use of open statistics.

The dataset package is currently in its infancy available on CRAN (it passed first peer review) and on rOpenSci.  While it will take a lot of time to mature, as I am not very sure about how to proceed with its usability, to make it able to receive from or export to Linked Open Data format would not be a huge investment, as we would need to follow up on this vignette&lt;https://dataset.dataobservatory.eu/articles/RDF.html&gt;  and connect to the existing rdflib package, which itself is a binding to the Python rdflib library, a super-standard and well functioning interface to the RDF metadata language.

Best regards,
Daniel

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202310161624-OpenMusE WP3 -- general population survey-321.txt -->

Hello OpenMusE colleagues,

I hope you are well!

I'm writing with regard to the general population survey that is planned in OpenMusE WP3 (see Slide 23 in the attached presentation). As I'm thrilled to remind you, we have enough fieldwork budget to conduct a high-quality survey in at least four countries, in either Q1 2024 or Q1 2025 (depending on your needs).

One aim of the survey is to answer research questions on music audiences: e.g., how do people interact with music, how does it contribute to their well-being, etc. However, arguably the more important aim is to fill data gaps relevant to music economics. Examples are:

  *   Valuation: how much do people report using music and spending on music in different channels?
  *   Informal employment: how many people earn some income from activities related to music?

Because the survey will be representative, the data we gather from the sample should be generalisable to the total population. We are aware that self-reported data on consumer behaviour is not as reliable as business intelligence data; however, in some cases, it may be the only data available.

ARTISJUS and SOZA: this is nothing new to you, as one purpose of the CEEMID surveys you conducted with REPREX was to provide such data. We would like to build on the foundation laid in CEEMID. I will be working with Daniel on this, and have requested from him the CEEMID survey questionnaires and relevant metadata (on universe and scope, response rate, sampling procedure, mode of collection, data collector, data collection period).

However, as Daniel's resource commitment in this WP is limited, I would like to work with you directly as well. I have experience designing and running population surveys on a high level (e.g., for German ministries and foundations), including surveys on music for the European Commission and the Max Planck Institute. However, I have not conducted a population survey specifically to answer music industry business needs. So, two opening requests for input are:

  *   What is your "survey wish list", i.e., what data needs in your organisation do you think a general population survey might help fill? Think back to CEEMID, but also give some thought beyond it.
  *   Are you aware of any dependencies that should be taken into account when deciding whether to survey your country in 2024 vs. 2025? @Rosina Petrova&lt;mailto:rosina_petrova@musicautor.org&gt;, here I am thinking of your comment in the Bratislava workshop that administrative data you will draw on in valuation are only available in Q3 of each year (and thus if we survey Bulgaria in Q1 2025, it might be too late to integrate the survey and administrative data by the time the project ends).
  *   For CEEMID partners: would you consider providing access to your CEEMID findings to the consortium, either at the aggregated level or the microdata level, and under what conditions?

My schedule this week is very flexible -- I would be happy to continue the conversation by email, phone, or both.

Thank you for your time, and best regards,
James

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Thursday, October 19, 2023 11:15 AM
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;; Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;
