Lähetetty: perjantai 20. lokakuuta 2023 12.23.12
Vastaanottaja: Leo Lahti; James Rhys Edwards; Akewak Jeba; Pyry Kantanen
Aihe: Polifonia - OME cooperation

Dear Leo, Jeba and James,

I spent three working days with another EU music project, Polifonia, that is metadata-only and computer science centered to find out synergies and ways to handle large scales of microdata for our project. I wanted to do this to avoid parallel efforts, and to find synergies; mainly towards the use of knowledge graphs and RDF, which are heavily used, for example, by Spotify, and could greatly increase our metadata handling efficiency and use.

I will write detailed suggestions of works, priorities, even with code examples next week, because I got a lot of useful advice on the [dataset] package and how it could improve the efficiency of maintaining [eurostat], [iotables], [regions] or add new functionality to [spotifyr]

If possible, first I would like to get a quick assessment from Leo about one small thing. Polifonia has a wonderful and well supported RDF tool, SPARQL-Anything&lt;https://sparql-anything.cc/&gt;. I am wondering if we could deploy this as a joint rOpenGov/Polifonia package with a quick and short effort?

This is a java application, which works with many non-RDF resources and pre-processes it much simpler than rdflib to RDF or a knowledge graph.  It could be used both for import and export or exchange our data.

https://github.com/SPARQL-Anything/sparql.anything

It could be deployed in two ways:
- Calling Java from R directly&lt;https://jozef.io/r901-primer-java-from-r-1/#calling-java-from-r-directly&gt;, we get access to the source code, and basically we have to call on only one Java object;
-  Or via packaging the latest release in .jar file and rJava&lt;https://jozef.io/r902-primer-java-from-r-2/&gt;, using the helloJavaWorld&lt;https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/helloJavaWorld/index.html&gt; template.
- They have a similar Python binding&lt;https://pypi.org/project/pysparql-anything/&gt;, which is basically perhaps 1-2 dozens of source code in Python, as we really need to pass on a resource URL to a java object and retrieve the text file it creates.

This would, in my opinion,
- significantly reduce the programming need to the [dataset] package
- create a quick win for our software ecosystem, and connect to a very well maintained community
- put as in the same language with a large music metadata project and allow accessing complex microdata sources with the same pipeline and code, but into our R ecosystem, too
- add to their projects Impact and our deliverables.

I had only worked with rJava as a user, not a developer, but if anybody in Turku has a bit of familiarity with either Java or rJava, to me this looks like 1-2 days job, not counting of course testing, documenting, releasing.

What I could offer is to create the package documentation website, rich tutorials to access relevant statistical and music sources for us, even the template of a quick publication, and of course, a concept paper on how this could improve our other package's functionality. I could do a fair amount of testing, and ask their team to provide us all files for unit testing used in other language binders, and if needed, to take care of the CRAN process.

Best regards,
Daniel Antal, CFA

Hi Daniel,

Forgot to send my notes from our call the other day


  *   General:
     *   I will request WP4 kick-off meeting minutes from Leo
     *   Recall that you must declare PM used until 2023 by December
  *   Pyry:
     *   The eurostat package can add value, if a targeted capstone is defined and assigned: getting music data from the Eurostat warehouse into the OMO
     *   Leo is framing the “ecosystem” as the sum of the interconnected packages; this is fine, but the new revision of eurostat does not interconnect with the other packages – it will have to be updated – Daniel can write specifications for this
     *   If Pyry could achieve these two goals within the next couple months, we would have a credible “baseline” for the “software ecosystem” deliverable
     *   Note that Leo and Pyry are already mentioned as authors in the other packages – this adds a bit of leverage
  *   Jeba:
     *   He cannot meaningfully contribute to R development
     *   He cannot document R packages
     *   He cannot contribute conceptual input on package development – too junior
     *   His academic writing skills are unknown, but probably limited
     *   He can manage the project on the UTU side, but this is a low-PM task
     *   He can be tasked with taking over maintenance of project-relevant packages by the project’s final quarter, but it is not realistic to expect him to contribute in the depth and scope required of a task leader
     *   The majority of PM output must lead to actual development, not learning-by-doing – the Horizon programme is designed to support research and innovation, not training (for that there is Erasmus and Marie Curie)
     *   If Leo wants to set up Jeba’s R training, and then bring him into the project in mid-2024, great – but we cannot pay for it

Regarding the SSSA data management hire:

  *   Daniel will be teaching a data management course in a Hungarian university – it may be possible to recruit from his student base
  *   Daniel also presented recently to a number of librarians in Bratislava – recruiting a Slovak speaker would be beneficial from a project standpoint
  *   Hudobne Center has tech-competent music librarians on staff, may be willing to send someone to SSSA for half a year
  *   Finally, Valentina at Polifonia teaches library scientists, and is in proximity to Pisa
  *   This could set a template for UTU as well


Best regards,
James

Hi Daniel, resending this from WhatsApp just in case.

I could have a call anytime between 12 and 16:00.

I share your concern. The possible justification is that the eurostat package is mentioned in the DoA. However, it is fishy that Leo would first say that Pyry is not working on the project, then frame his work retroactively as project work.

However, I think taking a hard line will not work well. This is based on Leo’s stubborn reaction when I stated during the call that routine maintenance work would not be accepted as project work. You know him better than I do, but I get the impression it is a matter of ego for him. We need to find a diplomatic way to pivot them.

Re: Pyry, if we could determine how the OMO can use Eurostat data in a way that adds value on top of what Eurostat themselves have done (see their updated page on cultural statistics, including a breakdown of data by domain, i.e., music: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/culture), we could give Leo / Pyry a concrete "capstone" task to rationalise that update, and then make it clear that further maintenance work should be cleared with you before being claimed as project work. This would let Leo save face.

Re: Jeba, the DoA is clear on R being the project’s working language. Hiring / selecting someone who hasn’t written an R package yet was irresponsible. But again, I don’t think we can simply enact a veto. We need to define what he *can* do, and make it clear that we won’t accept his work as project work beyond that scope.

Anyway, let me know when today between 11 and 16:00 is best for you.

Best regards,
James

Dear Daniel

Great to hear from you and very happy to connect with James as well. I had a look at the project's website: truly interesting. I do not think that there are so many advanced projects of this kind for the cultural sector (it would be excellent to go beyond music at a certain point and I guess this is what you have in mind). Congrats, also for putting together what seems to be a very relevant and competent team.

To immediately answer your question on R: difficult to say! Perhaps between beginner and intermediate level. It is really not the field where I come from, but I was so convinced that data analytics was going to become crucial, for the cultural sector as well, that at a certain point in my career I decided to invest more and more in this area, at my own pace. That's why I graduated in Statistical Analysis for the Social Sciences in 2015 (where I first learned about R, but I was mostly using SPSS at the time), then moved from KEA to the European Commission's Joint Research Centre as main researcher and project coordinator of the Cultural and Creative Cities Monitor (working alongside pure statisticians, web developers and data scientists) and very recently got the Coursera certificate "Data analysis with R programming". Actually, yesterday I also received a proposal to give a course on "Analytics for Cultural Policies" to Master-level students at the University of Bologna (still to be confirmed, but there are good chances).

As an independent researcher since June 2022, I am trying to get projects where I can keep testing and improve my data analytics skills and R knowledge. For instance, you will find attached the .R script that I wrote to propose a new way to the French Ministry of Culture to analyse different kinds of cultural variables coming from the 'ATLAS - Culture et Territoires' by groups of 'peer' departments so to facilitate comparative analysis and policy design (right now, public investments remain very (too!) much focused on Paris, as you certainly know). I am not sure the script is very advanced, but you tell me!

Last but not least: I love data analytics and am an R passionate, but I do believe that my main added value lies in the capacity of building bridges in the world of research / data analytics and policy making, as you might have understood. I am sure this is a promising profession that does not exist yet (certainly not in the field of culture), so my ultimate dream is indeed to work on data-driven projects and perfect my data skills, but having in mind the need to translate results for policy making use (notably to make sure that CCS are fully recognised and supported, especially the high majority of individual artists that make up the sector!).

I hope this gives you a better understanding of my professional path and aspirations and you are still willing to exchange.

Best regards
Valentina

Some of you have received this and some not, I received some bounce messages that this was not delivered but I did not understand from whose email.


Before/After
- Rosina, your people should describe currently how they match ISRC codes with ISWC and why; we will then write how we think this should be improved.
- James, you should describe a bit more on how you select and prepare questionnaire items for  harmonisation, and what you do with them now.
- Richard, I think you should describe how currently the work registration goes, and we will imagine how it should be slightly amended.

The before statements are important because we know which are the processes whose data we need to sample, and which are the processes that we will automate and improve. The after statements can be dreamed up by you or I will invent improvements.

Personas
I invented fictional names and ages, but they should reflect with fictional names your actual colleagues and workflows. The age and background should mildly reflect reality, because that gives an indication on the documentation and UX need.

Statements
These are coming from the Polifonia XD method, and they relate to metadata ontologies more than functional requirements, however, in both WPs we will work with both metadata and data.

The statement parts of the stories describe hypothetical but crystal clear statements that you want to be able to make in your rights management work  or your research practice.

For Rosina, just an example, we need about 5
- The ISRC of "Let It Be" ISRCXY1234 can be matched with the music work of John Lennon - Paul McCartney: Let It Be with ISWC19203943.  -&gt; this means that we solved the problem if our solution can be tested against such statements and it succeeds.  Our computer system is successful if it successfully matches a work in the CIS-Net (described with title, author, and ISWC) with a recording described by title, ISRC.
- It is important that we know how we identify music works and recordings that will be used in Listen Local Bulgaria.  While cleaning these data helps your normal working routine, it is also important that it clears up the mess and ensures that it creates new apps where the money flows to the right person. Please read on to the other example shared with Richard.

In Open Music Europe we write code to work with the data, but with Polifonia we also amend metadata ontologies to help automate the data connections.  These statements are rather metadata oriented but eventually we will tackle them first in OWL/RDF and second in R and potentially in a Shiny web application.

For @James Rhys Edwards&lt;mailto:JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;  , we need similar examples:
- The variable QA2_12 in the Eurobarometer series refers to TheSOZ concept "Occupation" / SDMX concept ("Occupation") and its data can be joined with the variable in AES X67 which equally refers to these concepts.
- The variable QA2_12 has a sufficiently similar question label to Afrobarometer Wave 5 67 and pending approval from the Principal Investigator should be seen as a harmonisation target.
- The current variable QB8 In the Eurobarometer 98.7 should be recoded with the Eurostat standard coding ESTAT 876 and its SDMX 2.1 equivalent "SEX"
- Our variable DMO2024_456 must be validated to have categories corresponding to ESTAT 679.

While these statements relate to metadata (they have ontological consequences) they also relate to functional software requirements, i.e. retroharmonize must support relabelling and concept harmonisation.

For @Demčák Richard&lt;mailto:Richard.Demcak@soza.sk&gt;, @Jankovič Marián&lt;mailto:marian.jankovic@soza.sk&gt;  , @Rosina Petrova&lt;mailto:rosina_petrova@musicautor.org&gt;
- The new registration form contains a yes/no answer if we can share the work's details with the Slovak Comprehensive Music Database and the database of Hudobne Centrum.
- The new registration form clearly states which personal details, in addition to the fields relevant for the CIS-Net legislation, can/cannot be shared with the Slovak Comprehensive Music Database and the database of Hudobne centrum.

These can be initial thoughts, and we can change them for some time, but this is the logic of a later functional testing of an automated system.

Dear Pierre, Caterina,

I looked up our correspondence from the year before, because we never acted upon it. In the meantime, we received significant funding for our plans and we are at the end of the first year of a large-scale EU research and innovation project.   Reprex has already interesting things to show to you which I think may be very relevant for MetaMusique. We would also like to review the European music diversity and circulation policy landscape a bit in Québec, which could then provide us some alignment across the Atlantic.

I am putting Dr Caterina Sganga, the Work Package leader of our Diversity and Circulation WP in CC.

I am wondering if I could set up a call with you on two topics:
1./ We would generally like to read something in English or French about the music policy landscape in Québec, which is not necessarily highly academic, but gives us an idea how music diversity policies are currently implemented on a practical level.
2./ Generally just cross-present what MetaMusique and Reprex are doing now, perhaps including some other consortium members on our side: HearDis! is a German SME providing innovative and diverse music for brands in-store, and Aloaded is a fast-growing Swedish premium digital distributor. Reprex is mainly working on knowledge/data systems related to data and metadata improvement to their needs.

Best regards,
Daniel

Our goal is to build somehting in Québec, than to expand in French Canada as a whole and ulitimatley in Canada in general.

I do not want to start negotiating a co-supervised person before agreeing on what will change in the GA if at all, and generally how will this work.

If Richard and Caterina think that they can manage the DMP, I wish them good luck. If not, we will need to talk generally about a lot of things, because there are very serious questions apart from this task with the entire WP4, and several aspects of WP1 and WP2, too.

I think that the best and easiest solution would be an SSSA-Reprex deal on the transfer of task and PMs, which is below the treshold of a Grant Agreement modification.  The transfer of the task of WP5 is not necessary if Richard makes a solmen pledge that he will no longer try to micromanage this task, or overrule me as a WP leader in any data management issues.  A co-supervised postdoc must have very tangible benefits for Reprex, because I really do not feel that I want to help SSSA to take over my know-how and reputation at the cost of my time. The observatory will be a big deal, and they will make a false claim as if this was their work. I do not like this idea at all.

Best regards,
Daniel

I have a call but please keep this in mind as you discuss with them.

### Dissemination updates from each partner required {#email-201}

**From:** Johannes Braunbruck &lt;johannes.braunbruck@synyo.com&gt;

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202311221117-Dissemination updates from each partner required-751.txt -->

Dear partners!

As we have recently added a *blog section* (https://www.openmuse.eu/blog/)
on the website: We kindly ask you to *forward all your relevant
activities *regarding
OME to us. If you are attending an event, giving a talk about the project,
or have something interesting to say about your studies or similar,
please *send
to us*:



*-a photo-relevant information about the event itself (if there is any, we
can get it online ourselves if necessary)-personal information about what
you did, why it is important, inspiring, etc. (short)*

We will then turn this into a blog post and use it for the newsletter.

provide regular updates if there are any from your side!

If you have any questions or suggestions, please email or call christoph
and me!
Many thanks and best regards!

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Wednesday, December 6, 2023 12:40 PM
To: Anna Zilkova &lt;anna.zilkova@hc.sk&gt;; Čas Marcel &lt;marcel.cas@culture.gov.sk&gt;; Demčák Richard &lt;richard.demcak@soza.sk&gt;
Cc: Igor Valentovič &lt;igor.valentovic@hc.sk&gt;; Mária Kmety Barteková | FPM EU v Bratislave &lt;maria.bartekova@euba.sk&gt;; Arianna Martinelli &lt;arianna.martinelli@santannapisa.it&gt;; James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;; Tomas Miks &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;; Felix Haaksman &lt;felix.haaksman@heardis.com&gt;
Subject: Progress with software tools

Dear Anna and Marcel,

I am wondering if we could find a joint meeting date about some practicalities involving Marcel, Anna, and Richard? It will be a very short meeting I think, as you will see, I did a lot of work but the questions are very pragmatic and simple.
https://doodle.com/meeting/participate/id/dy6qmyPe

In the following files, I reveal code how I handle the KULT data, but no KULT data is uploaded anywhere or made visible, apart from the names of a few orchestras that are obviously part of the data.

Software requirements
I made a lot of progress with our work.  First of all, based on your needs, I created certain stories. I changed your identities a bit, and sometimes invented "personas" instead of one to make the work of the developers and later testing easier. Your stories, which can be refined later, are here:
https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/open-music-europe-user-stories
(There are other ones, too that you can review here, for example, "Georg" is very relevant for Richard and Anna, but it comes from our partner HearDis!)
So, we want to develop software solutions to handle these scenarios, if you have any further ideas, tell me in the call, or write a short email.

  *   Michal, who have not used yet R, a junior assistant at a policy unit and does the work nobody wants to do. Recently, he had to reconcile dozens of PDF variable descriptions with poorly formatted CSV files and create clean Excel tables. Michal wanted to know if an R script could do this: eurostat-user2&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/dataset-development/stories/michal.html&gt; -- source stories/michal.qmd&lt;https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/dataset-development/stories/&gt;
  *   Ivana is the chief analyst of a cultural policy unit. She uses the integrated microdata files created with retroharmonize to make utilisation and budget forecasts for concert halls based on panel data. She uses Excel, where time series projections could be more convenient to assemble. ivana&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/dataset-development/stories/ivana.html&gt; -- source stories/ivana.qmd&lt;https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/dataset-development/stories/&gt;
  *   Natália is a 45-years-old engineer working in a collective rights management organisation. She has extensive experience working with relational database management systems, but only vague familiarity with knowledge graphs. natalia&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/dataset-development/stories/natalia.html&gt; -- source stories/natalia.qmd&lt;https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/dataset-development/stories/&gt;
  *   Persona: Jana, a 42-years-old librarian working in a music information center. She is experienced in library metadata, such as Dublin Core, and working with relational database management systems, but not via queries or scripts, more using a graphical interface. jana&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/dataset-development/stories/jana.html&gt; -- source stories/jana.qmd&lt;https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/dataset-development/stories/&gt;

KULT surveys
I would like to go back to the Statistical Office in January with a clear plan, and before that we create a database of the existing KULT surveys, improve the data and suggest some changes.  Here is where I am now.

KULT documentation
We will meet the research team today and talk through how we can put all the PDF files into a format that reads into a database, and can create, for example, a KULT book with all codebooks and problems.

https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/kult/kult_harmonisation.html

It is a long document, but for you, I think the end is important, this is something that I would like to discuss with Anna first, then with the National Library:
https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/kult/kult_harmonisation.html#linking-data-about-observational-units
&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/kult/kult_harmonisation.html#linking-data-about-observational-units&gt;
This problem relates to our Slovak Comprehensive Music Database, too.

KULT namespace
Here is my first take on creating a namespace. This will be a largely manual work, but not a really big deal, and we have to do this only ones.  It will also be directly usable for the Hudobné centrum website and the other new application; we must find a single, correct, unique name for the entities, for example, Bratislavské gitarové kvarteto

Now this is a software documentation so that eventually I can transfer this in a version to Marcel and his colleagues can learn to run this in the future.  Right now I have one serious issue here, that half of the files were saved with a Slovak Excel and I cannot correctly read in the Slovak characters.  This is unfortunately a known issue, and it is possible that the only solution will be that somebody at IKP has to reopen these files and save them explicitly as the country/operational system independent UTF-8 encoding.

https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/kult/kult_namespace.html

Again, you can skip most of the technical documentation and start reading at almost the end:
https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/kult/kult_namespace.html#data-linking

Marcel, you also have a colleague who knows some R, can you ask here if she can read this document, if it makes sense to her (the entire HTML file above)?


Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder
+31615058460
linkedin&lt;https://www.linkedin.com/in/antaldaniel/&gt; •  reprex bv&lt;http://reprex.nl/&gt;  • eviota&lt;https://eviota.nl/&gt;

Subject: KULT update

Hi Michalea and Marcel,

We made a lot of progress with the database, and I have a few simple things to ask and question.

1. Am I correct to assume that the -1 value in the data files means "missing"?
There are negative values in places where that makes no sense (for example, count of concerts), so I assume that this is a special value, and in such cases I would myself use a negative value for missing cases. Usually, microdata has special values for "missing", "not applicable",  "logically impossible", because if they just leave a cell empty, later it is impossible to find out why it is empty.

Is there  a codebook for special values? I am almost certain that it will explain all the small differences in the checksums and your sums.

2. I'll send you later a definitive list of missing files, but for example, in the PDF pack KULT11 is missing in 2007, 2010, 2011, 2022.

When you re-save to UTF-8, I think it is a good time to write to yourself and me a note like KULT05 = there are x files, the year y missing; and then check if the accompanying PDF file is present.

3.  I assume that the name space or entity name list is also per survey per "wave",  for example KULT05, 2007 (where 2007 is the 'wave').  If that is the case, it would be good to save again those files together with the summary PDFs.

The way I see it, we will have an almost full database by the end of the year, with Slovak and English labelling for 5 surveys. When I go to Slovakia, I think I'd like to teach the team how to do this better; with your assistance I could tidy up all surveys later, not only the five that I have now.  It would really benefit the team to gain a bit more data organisation skills, and you would be able to do a lot of the things I am doing yourself.

So far, I think that with a student there was about 30 hours going into this combined.  I do believe that with a combined effort of about 100 hours (most of which is PDF copy pasting that the most junior assistant can do) the entire work can be done, which would be a huge saving compared to your original workflow.

Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA

Subject: Progress with software tools

Dear Anna and Marcel,

I am wondering if we could find a joint meeting date about some practicalities involving Marcel, Anna, and Richard? It will be a very short meeting I think, as you will see, I did a lot of work but the questions are very pragmatic and simple.
https://doodle.com/meeting/participate/id/dy6qmyPe

In the following files, I reveal code how I handle the KULT data, but no KULT data is uploaded anywhere or made visible, apart from the names of a few orchestras that are obviously part of the data.

Software requirements
I made a lot of progress with our work.  First of all, based on your needs, I created certain stories. I changed your identities a bit, and sometimes invented "personas" instead of one to make the work of the developers and later testing easier. Your stories, which can be refined later, are here:
https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/open-music-europe-user-stories
(There are other ones, too that you can review here, for example, "Georg" is very relevant for Richard and Anna, but it comes from our partner HearDis!)
So, we want to develop software solutions to handle these scenarios, if you have any further ideas, tell me in the call, or write a short email.

  *   Michal, who have not used yet R, a junior assistant at a policy unit and does the work nobody wants to do. Recently, he had to reconcile dozens of PDF variable descriptions with poorly formatted CSV files and create clean Excel tables. Michal wanted to know if an R script could do this: eurostat-user2&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/dataset-development/stories/michal.html&gt; -- source stories/michal.qmd&lt;https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/dataset-development/stories/&gt;
  *   Ivana is the chief analyst of a cultural policy unit. She uses the integrated microdata files created with retroharmonize to make utilisation and budget forecasts for concert halls based on panel data. She uses Excel, where time series projections could be more convenient to assemble. ivana&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/dataset-development/stories/ivana.html&gt; -- source stories/ivana.qmd&lt;https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/dataset-development/stories/&gt;
  *   Natália is a 45-years-old engineer working in a collective rights management organisation. She has extensive experience working with relational database management systems, but only vague familiarity with knowledge graphs. natalia&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/dataset-development/stories/natalia.html&gt; -- source stories/natalia.qmd&lt;https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/dataset-development/stories/&gt;
  *   Persona: Jana, a 42-years-old librarian working in a music information center. She is experienced in library metadata, such as Dublin Core, and working with relational database management systems, but not via queries or scripts, more using a graphical interface. jana&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/dataset-development/stories/jana.html&gt; -- source stories/jana.qmd&lt;https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/dataset-development/stories/&gt;

KULT surveys
I would like to go back to the Statistical Office in January with a clear plan, and before that we create a database of the existing KULT surveys, improve the data and suggest some changes.  Here is where I am now.

KULT documentation
We will meet the research team today and talk through how we can put all the PDF files into a format that reads into a database, and can create, for example, a KULT book with all codebooks and problems.

https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/kult/kult_harmonisation.html

It is a long document, but for you, I think the end is important, this is something that I would like to discuss with Anna first, then with the National Library:
https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/kult/kult_harmonisation.html#linking-data-about-observational-units
&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/kult/kult_harmonisation.html#linking-data-about-observational-units&gt;
This problem relates to our Slovak Comprehensive Music Database, too.

KULT namespace
Here is my first take on creating a namespace. This will be a largely manual work, but not a really big deal, and we have to do this only ones.  It will also be directly usable for the Hudobné centrum website and the other new application; we must find a single, correct, unique name for the entities, for example, Bratislavské gitarové kvarteto

Now this is a software documentation so that eventually I can transfer this in a version to Marcel and his colleagues can learn to run this in the future.  Right now I have one serious issue here, that half of the files were saved with a Slovak Excel and I cannot correctly read in the Slovak characters.  This is unfortunately a known issue, and it is possible that the only solution will be that somebody at IKP has to reopen these files and save them explicitly as the country/operational system independent UTF-8 encoding.

https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/kult/kult_namespace.html

Again, you can skip most of the technical documentation and start reading at almost the end:
https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/kult/kult_namespace.html#data-linking

Marcel, you also have a colleague who knows some R, can you ask here if she can read this document, if it makes sense to her (the entire HTML file above)?


Best regards,

Subject: RE: Interview Invitation University of Amsterdam

Dear Fábio,

Thank you once more for your interest in our postdoc position. I am happy to let you know that we would like to invite you for a second interview.

Ideally, we would like to have this interview on Tuesday 9 January, some time between 11 AM and 2 PM. If possible, I would be great if we could make this an in person interview at our institute.

We really liked your background and the quality of your R language sample, and also your interest in business/economics issues, because after all, one of the main reasons why we want to crack a sampling problem is to provide valuation benchmarks; in other words, our research leads to intellectual property valuation and repertoire valuation, which is a hot topic in alternative investments.

In the second interview, we would like to focus more on the statistical approach on establishing a statistical value (median, mean) with observing a population’s quantitative values (play count, payout) whose underlying distribution is not known to us, and changing week to week as new songs are appearing in the service.  Think about the construction of a stock or bond index basket to measure investment performance or price movement.

We would like you to reflect on the following question in the follow up interview:

To quote common knowledge, i.e., Wikipedia, “Inverse transform sampling (also known as inversion sampling, the inverse probability integral transform, the inverse transformation method, Smirnov transform, or the golden rule) is a basic method for pseudo-random number sampling, i.e., for generating sample numbers at random from any probability distribution given its cumulative distribution function.”  Do you think that this would be an adequate method to select the songs and query their features and popularity on the Spotify API to get a representative popularity median for songs released in Italy in the year 2023?  Why? What would you do (differently) to select those songs which represent best the popularity of a “typical new release in Italy” on Spotify.

I hope this instruction for preparation is useful for you. If you have preliminary questions, please let us know.

Please also indicate if you have availability within the indicated time slot, and if an in person interview on site would be a possibility for you.

Kind regards, and wishing you a happy new year,

Joost

in the beginning because there is a lot coming after. But I think the doc
gives a great overview about the idea and the different initiatives.

our ABC_DJ project).

Betreff: Re: OpenMusE WP leader call

Dear WP Leaders,

Unfortunately the winning time is the one when I am not available, but I will try to make myself available for 60 minutes, if that is acceptable, if not, I will try to ensure that Istvan will replace me.  If it was possible to go in reverse order from WP6 to WP1 then perhaps this would be possible.

Having visited Brussels twice the last month, I think that there is an interest from the representative stakeholders and the Commission's policy unit, and it even though by now all WP1-2-3-4 is in significant delay, by the end of February when they want to hear from us, it would be still possible to present this project as a success, and to sell the project officer, if needed, with the help of the policy officer the necessary changes. In my opinion if we deliver an observatory prototype by May, with some data in it, and an appropriate data management plan, with appropriate data governance, then they will see this project as a success even if the letter of the grant grant agreement regarding research goals is not strictly followed.  As I wrote to James and Joost earlier, this would require a good sales pitch but relatively little change in the Grant Agreement.  If this is of interest to this forum, I would like to ask a few minutes in the first half of the meeting to expand on this.

Best regards,
Daniel

Dear WP leaders,

I hope you’re doing fine and are enjoying the first pre-Christmas season!

As mentioned during the last PMB meeting, we would like to schedule a monthly WP leader call for OpenMusE. It would be positive to have a meeting before the winter holidays, where at least one representative per organization is present, so we would kindly ask you to fill in the following doodle: https://doodle.com/meeting/participate/id/b4kwn5xa

The aim of the WP leader call is to go through each WP one by one, present its progress and discuss any urgent needs and issues. For the first call, we would schedule 90 minutes, for the following ones one hour should be enough.

Please let me know if you have any questions!

Subject: Access to microdata and urgent next steps

Dear Arianna and James,

I visited Slovakia again and received a lot of microdata, and I would like to go back in the 2nd or 3rd week of January which is the last possible time to actually do something meaningful (which would be very highly appreciated in Brussels) with the Statistical Office of Slovakia.

We are planning a workshop with IKP, SOSR, the Audiovisual Fund, the national library, and music stakeholders, because their contributions are all needed to reform the audiovisual (i.e. music + film + television) cultural satellite accounts.

This time it would be mission critical to get support from EUBA on time, any further delay cannot be made up by the end of 2025 because surveying has a 2-year cycle.

With IKP I think that I can do  most of the preparation, but we need to have a full documentation of the KULT surveys and its concept mapping to the data gaps identified by WP1 and WP2 withing 2 weeks.  This would require a lot of studid work first (can be done even by a Master's student), i.e., transcribing about 60 PDF documents into well-formatted Excel sheets.  Then we need to correct their labelling and match them with statistical, economic, diversity, circulation and sustainability concepts.

Because UTU could not hire, and they have not a single R programmer in the project, I do all the data harmonisation work, and I cannot find any time for the codebook and variable map creation. So I created a very detailed job description and I can assist the start of the work:

https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/data-to-policy/KULT-harmonisation.html [you can download the very detailed job description with plenty of screenshots in PDF, epub or Word.]

In my experience, the total mission critical but buring work is about 20 hours, but it is really 20 hours (the very precise translation of the PDF documentation to Excel).  Then a far more intellectual mapping should be made, which is not Master-student level, it requires a group work with Arianna, James, Maria and Katerina, because we have to understand the relevant variables in the KULT data.  The KULT is a real starting point, because it is the only culture-specific data source for the SORS; every other mixed survey is the sector-agnostic and well-known LFS, AES, and the SBS surveys ROC; they are very standard and easy to work with conceptually; the categorisation of non-music and music-employment, non-music and music-production, etc, is only possible via KULT.

Only I have a written agreement to work with the data itself, but it is not a problem, my code can be reviewed and I will run it on the actual data.  However, the documentation is public and it can be accessed by anybody.

Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder
+31615058460
linkedin&lt;https://www.linkedin.com/in/antaldaniel/&gt; •  reprex bv&lt;http://reprex.nl/&gt;  • eviota&lt;https://eviota.nl/&gt;

Subject: Access to microdata and urgent next steps



Dear Arianna and James,



I visited Slovakia again and received a lot of microdata, and I would like to go back in the 2nd or 3rd week of January which is the last possible time to actually do something meaningful (which would be very highly appreciated in Brussels) with the Statistical Office of Slovakia.



We are planning a workshop with IKP, SOSR, the Audiovisual Fund, the national library, and music stakeholders, because their contributions are all needed to reform the audiovisual (i.e. music + film + television) cultural satellite accounts.



This time it would be mission critical to get support from EUBA on time, any further delay cannot be made up by the end of 2025 because surveying has a 2-year cycle.



With IKP I think that I can do  most of the preparation, but we need to have a full documentation of the KULT surveys and its concept mapping to the data gaps identified by WP1 and WP2 withing 2 weeks.  This would require a lot of studid work first (can be done even by a Master's student), i.e., transcribing about 60 PDF documents into well-formatted Excel sheets.  Then we need to correct their labelling and match them with statistical, economic, diversity, circulation and sustainability concepts.



Because UTU could not hire, and they have not a single R programmer in the project, I do all the data harmonisation work, and I cannot find any time for the codebook and variable map creation. So I created a very detailed job description and I can assist the start of the work:



https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/data-to-policy/KULT-harmonisation.html [you can download the very detailed job description with plenty of screenshots in PDF, epub or Word.]



In my experience, the total mission critical but buring work is about 20 hours, but it is really 20 hours (the very precise translation of the PDF documentation to Excel).  Then a far more intellectual mapping should be made, which is not Master-student level, it requires a group work with Arianna, James, Maria and Katerina, because we have to understand the relevant variables in the KULT data.  The KULT is a real starting point, because it is the only culture-specific data source for the SORS; every other mixed survey is the sector-agnostic and well-known LFS, AES, and the SBS surveys ROC; they are very standard and easy to work with conceptually; the categorisation of non-music and music-employment, non-music and music-production, etc, is only possible via KULT.



Only I have a written agreement to work with the data itself, but it is not a problem, my code can be reviewed and I will run it on the actual data.  However, the documentation is public and it can be accessed by anybody.



Best regards,



Daniel Antal, CFA

co-founder

Subject: Access to microdata and urgent next steps



Dear Arianna and James,



I visited Slovakia again and received a lot of microdata, and I would like to go back in the 2nd or 3rd week of January which is the last possible time to actually do something meaningful (which would be very highly appreciated in Brussels) with the Statistical Office of Slovakia.



We are planning a workshop with IKP, SOSR, the Audiovisual Fund, the national library, and music stakeholders, because their contributions are all needed to reform the audiovisual (i.e. music + film + television) cultural satellite accounts.



This time it would be mission critical to get support from EUBA on time, any further delay cannot be made up by the end of 2025 because surveying has a 2-year cycle.



With IKP I think that I can do  most of the preparation, but we need to have a full documentation of the KULT surveys and its concept mapping to the data gaps identified by WP1 and WP2 withing 2 weeks.  This would require a lot of studid work first (can be done even by a Master's student), i.e., transcribing about 60 PDF documents into well-formatted Excel sheets.  Then we need to correct their labelling and match them with statistical, economic, diversity, circulation and sustainability concepts.



Because UTU could not hire, and they have not a single R programmer in the project, I do all the data harmonisation work, and I cannot find any time for the codebook and variable map creation. So I created a very detailed job description and I can assist the start of the work:



https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/data-to-policy/KULT-harmonisation.html [you can download the very detailed job description with plenty of screenshots in PDF, epub or Word.]



In my experience, the total mission critical but buring work is about 20 hours, but it is really 20 hours (the very precise translation of the PDF documentation to Excel).  Then a far more intellectual mapping should be made, which is not Master-student level, it requires a group work with Arianna, James, Maria and Katerina, because we have to understand the relevant variables in the KULT data.  The KULT is a real starting point, because it is the only culture-specific data source for the SORS; every other mixed survey is the sector-agnostic and well-known LFS, AES, and the SBS surveys ROC; they are very standard and easy to work with conceptually; the categorisation of non-music and music-employment, non-music and music-production, etc, is only possible via KULT.



Only I have a written agreement to work with the data itself, but it is not a problem, my code can be reviewed and I will run it on the actual data.  However, the documentation is public and it can be accessed by anybody.



Best regards,



Daniel Antal, CFA

co-founder

Subject: Access to microdata and urgent next steps



Dear Arianna and James,



I visited Slovakia again and received a lot of microdata, and I would like to go back in the 2nd or 3rd week of January which is the last possible time to actually do something meaningful (which would be very highly appreciated in Brussels) with the Statistical Office of Slovakia.



We are planning a workshop with IKP, SOSR, the Audiovisual Fund, the national library, and music stakeholders, because their contributions are all needed to reform the audiovisual (i.e. music + film + television) cultural satellite accounts.



This time it would be mission critical to get support from EUBA on time, any further delay cannot be made up by the end of 2025 because surveying has a 2-year cycle.



With IKP I think that I can do  most of the preparation, but we need to have a full documentation of the KULT surveys and its concept mapping to the data gaps identified by WP1 and WP2 withing 2 weeks.  This would require a lot of studid work first (can be done even by a Master's student), i.e., transcribing about 60 PDF documents into well-formatted Excel sheets.  Then we need to correct their labelling and match them with statistical, economic, diversity, circulation and sustainability concepts.



Because UTU could not hire, and they have not a single R programmer in the project, I do all the data harmonisation work, and I cannot find any time for the codebook and variable map creation. So I created a very detailed job description and I can assist the start of the work:



https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/data-to-policy/KULT-harmonisation.html [you can download the very detailed job description with plenty of screenshots in PDF, epub or Word.]



In my experience, the total mission critical but buring work is about 20 hours, but it is really 20 hours (the very precise translation of the PDF documentation to Excel).  Then a far more intellectual mapping should be made, which is not Master-student level, it requires a group work with Arianna, James, Maria and Katerina, because we have to understand the relevant variables in the KULT data.  The KULT is a real starting point, because it is the only culture-specific data source for the SORS; every other mixed survey is the sector-agnostic and well-known LFS, AES, and the SBS surveys ROC; they are very standard and easy to work with conceptually; the categorisation of non-music and music-employment, non-music and music-production, etc, is only possible via KULT.



Only I have a written agreement to work with the data itself, but it is not a problem, my code can be reviewed and I will run it on the actual data.  However, the documentation is public and it can be accessed by anybody.



Best regards,



Daniel Antal, CFA

Subject: Access to microdata and urgent next steps



Dear Arianna and James,



I visited Slovakia again and received a lot of microdata, and I would like to go back in the 2nd or 3rd week of January which is the last possible time to actually do something meaningful (which would be very highly appreciated in Brussels) with the Statistical Office of Slovakia.



We are planning a workshop with IKP, SOSR, the Audiovisual Fund, the national library, and music stakeholders, because their contributions are all needed to reform the audiovisual (i.e. music + film + television) cultural satellite accounts.



This time it would be mission critical to get support from EUBA on time, any further delay cannot be made up by the end of 2025 because surveying has a 2-year cycle.



With IKP I think that I can do  most of the preparation, but we need to have a full documentation of the KULT surveys and its concept mapping to the data gaps identified by WP1 and WP2 withing 2 weeks.  This would require a lot of studid work first (can be done even by a Master's student), i.e., transcribing about 60 PDF documents into well-formatted Excel sheets.  Then we need to correct their labelling and match them with statistical, economic, diversity, circulation and sustainability concepts.



Because UTU could not hire, and they have not a single R programmer in the project, I do all the data harmonisation work, and I cannot find any time for the codebook and variable map creation. So I created a very detailed job description and I can assist the start of the work:



https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/data-to-policy/KULT-harmonisation.html [you can download the very detailed job description with plenty of screenshots in PDF, epub or Word.]



In my experience, the total mission critical but buring work is about 20 hours, but it is really 20 hours (the very precise translation of the PDF documentation to Excel).  Then a far more intellectual mapping should be made, which is not Master-student level, it requires a group work with Arianna, James, Maria and Katerina, because we have to understand the relevant variables in the KULT data.  The KULT is a real starting point, because it is the only culture-specific data source for the SORS; every other mixed survey is the sector-agnostic and well-known LFS, AES, and the SBS surveys ROC; they are very standard and easy to work with conceptually; the categorisation of non-music and music-employment, non-music and music-production, etc, is only possible via KULT.



Only I have a written agreement to work with the data itself, but it is not a problem, my code can be reviewed and I will run it on the actual data.  However, the documentation is public and it can be accessed by anybody.



Best regards,



Daniel Antal, CFA

co-founder

Subject: Access to microdata and urgent next steps



Dear Arianna and James,



I visited Slovakia again and received a lot of microdata, and I would like to go back in the 2nd or 3rd week of January which is the last possible time to actually do something meaningful (which would be very highly appreciated in Brussels) with the Statistical Office of Slovakia.



We are planning a workshop with IKP, SOSR, the Audiovisual Fund, the national library, and music stakeholders, because their contributions are all needed to reform the audiovisual (i.e. music + film + television) cultural satellite accounts.



This time it would be mission critical to get support from EUBA on time, any further delay cannot be made up by the end of 2025 because surveying has a 2-year cycle.



With IKP I think that I can do  most of the preparation, but we need to have a full documentation of the KULT surveys and its concept mapping to the data gaps identified by WP1 and WP2 withing 2 weeks.  This would require a lot of studid work first (can be done even by a Master's student), i.e., transcribing about 60 PDF documents into well-formatted Excel sheets.  Then we need to correct their labelling and match them with statistical, economic, diversity, circulation and sustainability concepts.



Because UTU could not hire, and they have not a single R programmer in the project, I do all the data harmonisation work, and I cannot find any time for the codebook and variable map creation. So I created a very detailed job description and I can assist the start of the work:



https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/data-to-policy/KULT-harmonisation.html [you can download the very detailed job description with plenty of screenshots in PDF, epub or Word.]



In my experience, the total mission critical but buring work is about 20 hours, but it is really 20 hours (the very precise translation of the PDF documentation to Excel).  Then a far more intellectual mapping should be made, which is not Master-student level, it requires a group work with Arianna, James, Maria and Katerina, because we have to understand the relevant variables in the KULT data.  The KULT is a real starting point, because it is the only culture-specific data source for the SORS; every other mixed survey is the sector-agnostic and well-known LFS, AES, and the SBS surveys ROC; they are very standard and easy to work with conceptually; the categorisation of non-music and music-employment, non-music and music-production, etc, is only possible via KULT.



Only I have a written agreement to work with the data itself, but it is not a problem, my code can be reviewed and I will run it on the actual data.  However, the documentation is public and it can be accessed by anybody.



Best regards,



Daniel Antal, CFA

Subject: Access to microdata and urgent next steps



Dear Arianna and James,



I visited Slovakia again and received a lot of microdata, and I would like to go back in the 2nd or 3rd week of January which is the last possible time to actually do something meaningful (which would be very highly appreciated in Brussels) with the Statistical Office of Slovakia.



We are planning a workshop with IKP, SOSR, the Audiovisual Fund, the national library, and music stakeholders, because their contributions are all needed to reform the audiovisual (i.e. music + film + television) cultural satellite accounts.



This time it would be mission critical to get support from EUBA on time, any further delay cannot be made up by the end of 2025 because surveying has a 2-year cycle.



With IKP I think that I can do  most of the preparation, but we need to have a full documentation of the KULT surveys and its concept mapping to the data gaps identified by WP1 and WP2 withing 2 weeks.  This would require a lot of studid work first (can be done even by a Master's student), i.e., transcribing about 60 PDF documents into well-formatted Excel sheets.  Then we need to correct their labelling and match them with statistical, economic, diversity, circulation and sustainability concepts.



Because UTU could not hire, and they have not a single R programmer in the project, I do all the data harmonisation work, and I cannot find any time for the codebook and variable map creation. So I created a very detailed job description and I can assist the start of the work:



https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/data-to-policy/KULT-harmonisation.html [you can download the very detailed job description with plenty of screenshots in PDF, epub or Word.]



In my experience, the total mission critical but buring work is about 20 hours, but it is really 20 hours (the very precise translation of the PDF documentation to Excel).  Then a far more intellectual mapping should be made, which is not Master-student level, it requires a group work with Arianna, James, Maria and Katerina, because we have to understand the relevant variables in the KULT data.  The KULT is a real starting point, because it is the only culture-specific data source for the SORS; every other mixed survey is the sector-agnostic and well-known LFS, AES, and the SBS surveys ROC; they are very standard and easy to work with conceptually; the categorisation of non-music and music-employment, non-music and music-production, etc, is only possible via KULT.



Only I have a written agreement to work with the data itself, but it is not a problem, my code can be reviewed and I will run it on the actual data.  However, the documentation is public and it can be accessed by anybody.



Best regards,



Daniel Antal, CFA

Subject: Access to microdata and urgent next steps



Dear Arianna and James,



I visited Slovakia again and received a lot of microdata, and I would like to go back in the 2nd or 3rd week of January which is the last possible time to actually do something meaningful (which would be very highly appreciated in Brussels) with the Statistical Office of Slovakia.



We are planning a workshop with IKP, SOSR, the Audiovisual Fund, the national library, and music stakeholders, because their contributions are all needed to reform the audiovisual (i.e. music + film + television) cultural satellite accounts.



This time it would be mission critical to get support from EUBA on time, any further delay cannot be made up by the end of 2025 because surveying has a 2-year cycle.



With IKP I think that I can do  most of the preparation, but we need to have a full documentation of the KULT surveys and its concept mapping to the data gaps identified by WP1 and WP2 withing 2 weeks.  This would require a lot of studid work first (can be done even by a Master's student), i.e., transcribing about 60 PDF documents into well-formatted Excel sheets.  Then we need to correct their labelling and match them with statistical, economic, diversity, circulation and sustainability concepts.



Because UTU could not hire, and they have not a single R programmer in the project, I do all the data harmonisation work, and I cannot find any time for the codebook and variable map creation. So I created a very detailed job description and I can assist the start of the work:



https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/data-to-policy/KULT-harmonisation.html [you can download the very detailed job description with plenty of screenshots in PDF, epub or Word.]



In my experience, the total mission critical but buring work is about 20 hours, but it is really 20 hours (the very precise translation of the PDF documentation to Excel).  Then a far more intellectual mapping should be made, which is not Master-student level, it requires a group work with Arianna, James, Maria and Katerina, because we have to understand the relevant variables in the KULT data.  The KULT is a real starting point, because it is the only culture-specific data source for the SORS; every other mixed survey is the sector-agnostic and well-known LFS, AES, and the SBS surveys ROC; they are very standard and easy to work with conceptually; the categorisation of non-music and music-employment, non-music and music-production, etc, is only possible via KULT.



Only I have a written agreement to work with the data itself, but it is not a problem, my code can be reviewed and I will run it on the actual data.  However, the documentation is public and it can be accessed by anybody.



Best regards,



Daniel Antal, CFA

co-founder

Hi Daniel,

Thank you for your quick response. Understood, we will start tomorrow.

@Mária Kmety Barteková&lt;mailto:maria.bartekova@euba.sk&gt; revisiting my email of a couple days ago, would you and Kristian have time for a quick call tomorrow?
@Arianna Martinelli&lt;mailto:Arianna.Martinelli@santannapisa.it&gt; and @Caterina Sganga&lt;mailto:caterina.sganga@santannapisa.it&gt;, if you also have time for a 15-min call, I can go over the controlled vocabularies in question.

Re: the Slovak stakeholders, we are indeed behind in all WPs. However, WP3 at least has concrete data identification and collection goals, which I could easily elucidate for the Slovak stakeholders by early January. So, IMO we should not give up on that meeting.

For WP1, I think we are also not far away. As you mentioned in our WP3 call, much of the work we did in WP3 actually overlaps with, or even belongs more properly in WP1. If the data gap assessment schema we proposed is satisfactory, than it should not take more than 3 working days to cross-check it with: 1) Eurostat; 2) the list of data providers identified in the Feasibility Study; and 3) the list of Slovak datasets that I have also already identified in D3.1.

For WP2, we still have a bit more work to do. However, there is a recognition on the part of all deliverable authors that more attention must be paid to diversity of repertories rather than of natural persons. In this, I'm glad you identified the Polifonia ontologies as a source to work with, as I was thinking the same thing. This is also work that HEARDIS could contribute to, as they have in-house MIR and musicological metadata annotation tools developed in our prior EU project.

Specifically re: Hubodne Centrum, I do think it would be beneficial to send them the letter on Monday. We can make it clear that we do not require an answer before January, but I would like to formally initiate the conversation. Do you think that would be a mistake? If so, please let me know why.

Thank you again and best regards,
James

Subject: Re: Hudobné centrum

Hi James,

On Sun, Dec 17, 2023 at 5:11 PM James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt; wrote:
Hi Daniel,

Focusing on the two items here on which I can directly contribute, and which should not take you more than 10 minutes to respond to:

  1.  On Monday we can begin (and probably complete) the concept mapping. Please confirm that this is the current spreadsheet that we should use: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ZX4qwyJC1uNSDvROw8133CRVA9MQMotRk8r4-Yuhxk8/edit#gid=1466486711

  *
Please let me know if there is an order of preference re: the controlled vocabularies to use.

I will share the other question banks, too.


     *
For cross-domain concepts, I assume we should use the SDMX subject-matter domains when possible.

Yes, the SDMX cross-domain concepts. This should be used by Arianna, too, for designing the surveys.



     *   For topical concepts, I would argue we should use EuroVoc as it contains translations to 24 EU languages, including Slovak.
     *
However, EuroVoc contains few music-specific concepts. For music-specific concepts, I will use THESOZ, STW, UNESCO, and DBPedia, in that order of preference.

For economic concepts, I think that Arianna and Maria should decide, as the material should also be worked into T1.1, as it will be the data requirement for T1.2. I would very much suggest the use EuroVoc, and if we want to score points with GESIS, then STW, too.

I think that for music diversity and circulation issues, the task leader of T2.1 should decide which ontologies to use, because the data will be the data requirement for the subsequent task of T2.2. I do not know who is the task leader of WP2 or what is happening there.  However, the WP2 is not really covered by EU statistics at all, after all, culture is a natural competence.  My main preference would be the use of the Polifonia ontologies, whenever possible. For music diversity and circulation, the vocabularies overlap a great deal with competition law and competition economics, so that should be used from EuroVoc.

As for WP3 T3.1 and 3.2, UNESCO and THESOZ would be a great choice, whenever not covered by EuroVoc.

Generally, the use of DBpedia should be a last resource, when the researchers do not find a good description of their desired research topic  or research data needs in any other ontology.

The DMP should be updated also accordingly.  I did updates in the DMP till November, the repository has further commits, but ongoing that task, unless otherwise agreed, should be continued by SSSA, I absolutely have no more PMs in the DMPs, and generally we almost filled all hours in WP6.

Since you will be on holiday from 19 December, I guess that the retroharmonize requirement elicitation will happen only next year. As for going back to the Slovak stakeholders -- probably we should skip this now. While it would have been critical to start data collection next year, it seems that nobody was available in December to do the preparation in WP1-2-3.

Best regards,
Daniel

Betreff: Re: OpenMusE WP leader call



Dear WP Leaders,



Unfortunately the winning time is the one when I am not available, but I will try to make myself available for 60 minutes, if that is acceptable, if not, I will try to ensure that Istvan will replace me.  If it was possible to go in reverse order from WP6 to WP1 then perhaps this would be possible.



Having visited Brussels twice the last month, I think that there is an interest from the representative stakeholders and the Commission's policy unit, and it even though by now all WP1-2-3-4 is in significant delay, by the end of February when they want to hear from us, it would be still possible to present this project as a success, and to sell the project officer, if needed, with the help of the policy officer the necessary changes. In my opinion if we deliver an observatory prototype by May, with some data in it, and an appropriate data management plan, with appropriate data governance, then they will see this project as a success even if the letter of the grant grant agreement regarding research goals is not strictly followed.  As I wrote to James and Joost earlier, this would require a good sales pitch but relatively little change in the Grant Agreement.  If this is of interest to this forum, I would like to ask a few minutes in the first half of the meeting to expand on this.



Best regards,
Daniel

In our WP leader call today, we addressed the concept harmonisation. It struck me that I may have failed to stress how important this work is. So, by putting care into this now, we are killing several birds with one stone.

Would you perchance be available on 22 Dec for a follow-up call with Daniel and I? As Daniel will be traveling, we wonder if you could specify windows of availability rather than specific times at this point.

If we can prove our added value here, we may have the opportunity to take part in really state-of-the-art scientific and practical work in music statistics. Thank you in advance for your work on this important task!

Hi James,

I do not think that Paul would be ideal for UTU, unless it is well-coordinated with what we try to do with Joost and in Reprex; and it really depends on the IViR candidate if he is taking at all our offer, and it would still require a change of subtaks, PMs, etc. Paul has never written a single line of code in R, and knows nothing about statistics, so parachuting him into a statistics department without statistics is not a good move, unless I can co-supervise him with our co-supervisee in IViR. In UTU, he will land in the void, and his work would still need to be connected to R-based software. He can't figure it out alone, and I am not willing to train UTU staff for free. He would be a great asset to a functional consortium where professional work is carried out, but just parachuting him there would not do good to him, you.

To me, the WP leader's meeting was a disappointment.  We have a PMB that is not managing the project, a GA that is not an assembly, and now WP leaders where they do not show up or nothing is discussed.   And also, Richard's decision to put fake datasets in a fake way into the DMP was the most disheartening thing to hear. It goes against any principles of ethics, professionals, and integrity.  Fake software ecosystem, fake data management, ... I will distance myself from this as much as I can, and I think that I heard in the last weeks from several active Consortium members that they want to insulate themselves.

  In the last weeks, I saw some signs of hope that there is a will to save at least a part of the budget and to do something meaningful in this project, after this meeting I do not see it that way any longer.  I was expecting Leo to stand up and show some self-critique and apologize today, in a private email that is what I was asking from him--after all, he had been for years a fake co-author of my work without a single line added and I got him a lot of money. I think it would be a decent thing to say sorry that I am derailing your plans.   I hoped that Caterina would show up, and do the same -- after all, she also got a grant that she had subverted, and in the first 12 month she did not find the time to meet at least once her task leaders.  I was writing to you that if they are serious about co-supervising postdocs, I am happy to listen and give them my proposed terms.  They could have been favorable for them, and they could allow the use of the roughly 900k that goes to them into something remotely in line with the public grant that was given to us.

The same can be said about EUBA. You will be on holiday on 22nd December, I will be on holiday, and honestly, I do not think that they will make up the work not done in December over the holidays. I want to cancel the visit to Bratislava because I will not fake any longer that there is no consortium behind me and there is any kind of research.

22nd December is my mother's birthday, the first time our family from 5 countries meets, and I am rather pissed to have a work meeting.  I will do it, but I will send a task to be done from the airport tomorrow beforehand, and I will only go into the meeting if they will accomplish that before Friday.  I suggest you do the same.  I think that you should stop assisting their fake work. I certainly will not cover up for any partners any longer in 2024.

Best regards,
Daniel

Subject: A musicologist applicant for T1.1

Hi James,

As you know well, we have a candidate for IViR, a musicologist from Berlin.  We have 15 candidates, and in the original selection we eliminated him as he does not appear to have the skills required for the position, and we have at least 3 or 4 candidates who fully match it.

However, we decided to invite him to an interview, because we think that it is the candidate's interest, we think that he could be a valuable addition to several tasks in this Consortium, but this particular role.   To me, the most logical choice would be UTU, which I can explain.

It seems that we have more senior R developers applying for the IViR position than what UTU has in house at any seniority levels. However, UTU is not only supposed to develop R packages (which they currently do not do) but also Apps. I think that the musicologist's skills could be extremely useful in packaging our lower level code into visually appealing and music UX-friendly apps.

While we do not currently have a selection at all, I could imagine a scenario when all senior R/stat development would go to IViR and Reprex, and UTU would provide support activities for the Apps and the OMO (with a reduced budget.)

Generally, I think that this would be very feasible from a budget point of view.  I just finished the report on my software development task for the NL research council. I develop code about 400% faster than juniors, and about at a 400% higher PM rate than a fresh Master's level data scientist in the NL.  Because we have very good candidates to go to IViR, whose postdoc rates are comparable to UTU, I can imagine that all R work will be accomplished with half or even less PMs but at a roughly 25% higher PM rate.  It is very acceptable in Horizon Europe to report 25% lower PM use for a task at a 25% higher average PM rate.   For Paul, perhaps working with UTU where there is a musicology department in place would be even better.

At this point, I cannot imagine that UTU will contribute anything to T4.1; Pyry has no statistical knowledge and he is a junior R developer, and Jeba does not have any statistical or R background at all. I had not seen Leo writing code ever, and I do not see him involved in the project so far.

Best regards,

**From:** Richard Wages &lt;Richard.Wages@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**To:** Richard Wages &lt;Richard.Wages@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**Cc:** James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;, Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**Date:** 12/15/2023 08:43:22

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202312150843-OpenMusE __ First EC Review for our project _ plea-797.txt -->

Hello OpenMusE team,

After my vacation was slightly ‘prolonged’ by an involuntary and fascinating extra day on Miami airport and a bonus migraine attack over the past two days I am contacting you today with a request of major importance, but little surprise: our Project Officer Melpomeni has offered several options for us to pick from in the first half of March 2024 for our upcoming First Project Review. We need to answer her call without delay.

Our work, our planning and of course our deliverables so far will be evaluated by at least two external, non-EU-affiliated experts over the course of January and February. Together with the presentations we give on the review day itself this will serve as the basis for the recommendations the experts will give to our Project Officer. Obviously, we want to present ourselves in an optimal way as this full day review will also decide whether we will continue to receive EU-funding as planned for the remainder of the project runtime.

Hence, I urge you to indicate your availabilities in this doodle poll&lt;https://dud-poll.inf.tu-dresden.de/openmuse-first-EC-review-2024/&gt; asap, and by Tuesday, 19 December 23:59 the latest, so that SINUS can communicate our decision to the PO well before the Christmas break. The minimum requirements for attendence are

  *   One person per partner organisation
  *   All WP leaders
  *   Coordinator team

Looking forward to seeing all of you again soon,
Cheers,
Richard

Dear OpenMusE team,

We received some concerned emails from team members after four “For Action” / rejection emails were sent out by the European Commission’s Participant Portal today. Please be assured that there is no reason to be alarmed.

This morning I had a phone call with our Project Officer in which I asked her for permission to upload updates to the deliverables D2.1, D3.1, D5.2 and D6.3 as we had agreed upon during the PMB. The only way for her to unlock the ECAS system to allow for a re-upload is to formally reject an existing version. This however triggers an automated rejection notification to the entire consortium which is what you received today.

Everything is fine.

Cheers,
Richard

Cc: Balázs Bodó &lt;B.Bodo@uva.nl&lt;mailto:B.Bodo@uva.nl&gt;&gt;; Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&lt;mailto:daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;&gt;
Subject: RE: Interview Invitation University of Amsterdam

Dear Fábio,

Thank you once more for your interest in our postdoc position. I am happy to let you know that we would like to invite you for a second interview.

Ideally, we would like to have this interview on Tuesday 9 January, some time between 11 AM and 2 PM. If possible, I would be great if we could make this an in person interview at our institute.

We really liked your background and the quality of your R language sample, and also your interest in business/economics issues, because after all, one of the main reasons why we want to crack a sampling problem is to provide valuation benchmarks; in other words, our research leads to intellectual property valuation and repertoire valuation, which is a hot topic in alternative investments.

In the second interview, we would like to focus more on the statistical approach on establishing a statistical value (median, mean) with observing a population’s quantitative values (play count, payout) whose underlying distribution is not known to us, and changing week to week as new songs are appearing in the service.  Think about the construction of a stock or bond index basket to measure investment performance or price movement.

We would like you to reflect on the following question in the follow up interview:

To quote common knowledge, i.e., Wikipedia, “Inverse transform sampling (also known as inversion sampling, the inverse probability integral transform, the inverse transformation method, Smirnov transform, or the golden rule) is a basic method for pseudo-random number sampling, i.e., for generating sample numbers at random from any probability distribution given its cumulative distribution function.”  Do you think that this would be an adequate method to select the songs and query their features and popularity on the Spotify API to get a representative popularity median for songs released in Italy in the year 2023?  Why? What would you do (differently) to select those songs which represent best the popularity of a “typical new release in Italy” on Spotify.

I hope this instruction for preparation is useful for you. If you have preliminary questions, please let us know.

Please also indicate if you have availability within the indicated time slot, and if an in person interview on site would be a possibility for you.

Kind regards, and wishing you a happy new year,

Joost

Subject: FW: Interview Invitation University of Amsterdam

Dear Fabio Vieira,

Thank you very much for your application for the position of “Postdoctoral Research Fellow with a Quantitative Background and an Interest in Music Data”.

We have read your application with great interest, and are happy to invite you for an online interview. This interview will be held by Balázs Bodó, Daniel Antal and myself.

Your interview is planned for Monday 18 December 12:30 – 13:15 CET.

We do realize this is short notice, but hope you blocked the time slots mentioned in the vacancy, so that you are available.

In preparation of the interview, we would like to ask you two questions:


  1.  Please send us a link to a public (GitHub or other) repository where we can see samples of code that you yourself wrote and that you think is the most relevant to evaluate your preparedness for this job; or, if you do not have such code in a public repository, send us source code in R, Python or C++.  We will not keep a copy of the source file beyond the selection process.


  1.  In the interview, among other questions, we will ask you to tell us your personal approach to the following problem: how would you create random samples ISRC codes to establish typical popularities, revenues of a) music made in Slovakia b) new music released in the year 2023 in Italy c) a random sample of “new classical music”.  Please explain how you would come to such a sample, what tools you would use for sampling, where would you try to find data.  There is no one good answer to this question, but such problems will keep you busy if you work with us.

Please let us know if you can meet us at the indicated time slot, after which I will send you a Teams Link.

Looking forward to meeting you on Monday, and wishing you a great weekend,

Joost
