We have read your application with great interest, and are happy to invite you for an online interview. This interview will be held by Balázs Bodó, Daniel Antal and myself.

Your interview is planned for Monday 18 December 12:30 – 13:15 CET.

We do realize this is short notice, but hope you blocked the time slots mentioned in the vacancy, so that you are available.

In preparation of the interview, we would like to ask you two questions:


  1.  Please send us a link to a public (GitHub or other) repository where we can see samples of code that you yourself wrote and that you think is the most relevant to evaluate your preparedness for this job; or, if you do not have such code in a public repository, send us source code in R, Python or C++.  We will not keep a copy of the source file beyond the selection process.


  1.  In the interview, among other questions, we will ask you to tell us your personal approach to the following problem: how would you create random samples ISRC codes to establish typical popularities, revenues of a) music made in Slovakia b) new music released in the year 2023 in Italy c) a random sample of “new classical music”.  Please explain how you would come to such a sample, what tools you would use for sampling, where would you try to find data.  There is no one good answer to this question, but such problems will keep you busy if you work with us.

Please let us know if you can meet us at the indicated time slot, after which I will send you a Teams Link.

Looking forward to meeting you on Monday, and wishing you a great weekend,

Joost

Subject: RE: Interview Invitation University of Amsterdam



Dear Fábio,



Thank you once more for your interest in our postdoc position. I am happy to let you know that we would like to invite you for a second interview.



Ideally, we would like to have this interview on Tuesday 9 January, some time between 11 AM and 2 PM. If possible, I would be great if we could make this an in person interview at our institute.



We really liked your background and the quality of your R language sample, and also your interest in business/economics issues, because after all, one of the main reasons why we want to crack a sampling problem is to provide valuation benchmarks; in other words, our research leads to intellectual property valuation and repertoire valuation, which is a hot topic in alternative investments.



In the second interview, we would like to focus more on the statistical approach on establishing a statistical value (median, mean) with observing a population’s quantitative values (play count, payout) whose underlying distribution is not known to us, and changing week to week as new songs are appearing in the service.  Think about the construction of a stock or bond index basket to measure investment performance or price movement.



We would like you to reflect on the following question in the follow up interview:



To quote common knowledge, i.e., Wikipedia, “Inverse transform sampling (also known as inversion sampling, the inverse probability integral transform, the inverse transformation method, Smirnov transform, or the golden rule) is a basic method for pseudo-random number sampling, i.e., for generating sample numbers at random from any probability distribution given its cumulative distribution function.”  Do you think that this would be an adequate method to select the songs and query their features and popularity on the Spotify API to get a representative popularity median for songs released in Italy in the year 2023?  Why? What would you do (differently) to select those songs which represent best the popularity of a “typical new release in Italy” on Spotify.



I hope this instruction for preparation is useful for you. If you have preliminary questions, please let us know.



Please also indicate if you have availability within the indicated time slot, and if an in person interview on site would be a possibility for you.



Kind regards, and wishing you a happy new year,



Joost

Subject: RE: Interview Invitation University of Amsterdam



Dear Fábio,



Thank you once more for your interest in our postdoc position. I am happy to let you know that we would like to invite you for a second interview.



Ideally, we would like to have this interview on Tuesday 9 January, some time between 11 AM and 2 PM. If possible, I would be great if we could make this an in person interview at our institute.



We really liked your background and the quality of your R language sample, and also your interest in business/economics issues, because after all, one of the main reasons why we want to crack a sampling problem is to provide valuation benchmarks; in other words, our research leads to intellectual property valuation and repertoire valuation, which is a hot topic in alternative investments.



In the second interview, we would like to focus more on the statistical approach on establishing a statistical value (median, mean) with observing a population’s quantitative values (play count, payout) whose underlying distribution is not known to us, and changing week to week as new songs are appearing in the service.  Think about the construction of a stock or bond index basket to measure investment performance or price movement.



We would like you to reflect on the following question in the follow up interview:



To quote common knowledge, i.e., Wikipedia, “Inverse transform sampling (also known as inversion sampling, the inverse probability integral transform, the inverse transformation method, Smirnov transform, or the golden rule) is a basic method for pseudo-random number sampling, i.e., for generating sample numbers at random from any probability distribution given its cumulative distribution function.”  Do you think that this would be an adequate method to select the songs and query their features and popularity on the Spotify API to get a representative popularity median for songs released in Italy in the year 2023?  Why? What would you do (differently) to select those songs which represent best the popularity of a “typical new release in Italy” on Spotify.



I hope this instruction for preparation is useful for you. If you have preliminary questions, please let us know.



Please also indicate if you have availability within the indicated time slot, and if an in person interview on site would be a possibility for you.



Kind regards, and wishing you a happy new year,



Joost

Subject: FW: Interview Invitation University of Amsterdam



Dear Fabio Vieira,



Thank you very much for your application for the position of “Postdoctoral Research Fellow with a Quantitative Background and an Interest in Music Data”.



We have read your application with great interest, and are happy to invite you for an online interview. This interview will be held by Balázs Bodó, Daniel Antal and myself.



Your interview is planned for Monday 18 December 12:30 – 13:15 CET.



We do realize this is short notice, but hope you blocked the time slots mentioned in the vacancy, so that you are available.



In preparation of the interview, we would like to ask you two questions:



  1.  Please send us a link to a public (GitHub or other) repository where we can see samples of code that you yourself wrote and that you think is the most relevant to evaluate your preparedness for this job; or, if you do not have such code in a public repository, send us source code in R, Python or C++.  We will not keep a copy of the source file beyond the selection process.



  1.  In the interview, among other questions, we will ask you to tell us your personal approach to the following problem: how would you create random samples ISRC codes to establish typical popularities, revenues of a) music made in Slovakia b) new music released in the year 2023 in Italy c) a random sample of “new classical music”.  Please explain how you would come to such a sample, what tools you would use for sampling, where would you try to find data.  There is no one good answer to this question, but such problems will keep you busy if you work with us.



Please let us know if you can meet us at the indicated time slot, after which I will send you a Teams Link.



Looking forward to meeting you on Monday, and wishing you a great weekend,



Joost

Subject: FW: Interview Invitation University of Amsterdam



Dear Fabio Vieira,



Thank you very much for your application for the position of “Postdoctoral Research Fellow with a Quantitative Background and an Interest in Music Data”.



We have read your application with great interest, and are happy to invite you for an online interview. This interview will be held by Balázs Bodó, Daniel Antal and myself.



Your interview is planned for Monday 18 December 12:30 – 13:15 CET.



We do realize this is short notice, but hope you blocked the time slots mentioned in the vacancy, so that you are available.



In preparation of the interview, we would like to ask you two questions:



  1.  Please send us a link to a public (GitHub or other) repository where we can see samples of code that you yourself wrote and that you think is the most relevant to evaluate your preparedness for this job; or, if you do not have such code in a public repository, send us source code in R, Python or C++.  We will not keep a copy of the source file beyond the selection process.



  1.  In the interview, among other questions, we will ask you to tell us your personal approach to the following problem: how would you create random samples ISRC codes to establish typical popularities, revenues of a) music made in Slovakia b) new music released in the year 2023 in Italy c) a random sample of “new classical music”.  Please explain how you would come to such a sample, what tools you would use for sampling, where would you try to find data.  There is no one good answer to this question, but such problems will keep you busy if you work with us.



Please let us know if you can meet us at the indicated time slot, after which I will send you a Teams Link.



Looking forward to meeting you on Monday, and wishing you a great weekend,



Joost

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: dinsdag 16 januari 2024 7:54
To: Fábio Generoso Vieira &lt;F.V.GenerosoVieira@tilburguniversity.edu&gt;
Subject: Re: Interview Invitation University of Amsterdam

Hi Fábió,

I was travelling till now, and I did not have a lot of time to prepare for my return to the Netherlands but here I am.  I am wondering how much time you have on Friday, because I see two options, knowing that I have an appointment at 1100 and another one at 1300 that may be of interest to you.

At 1300 there will be a webinar of another Horizon Europe music project, i.e., Polifonia, who are a finishing stage project and they are our sister project in a way that we will use in our project their metadata results, i.e. comprehensive ontologies.  They have a 1300 webinar about how they make their 3-year data results available for further use.  While the data that they make available for further reuse is perhaps a bit alien to you -- it is more digital humanities metadata related to music -- but what they are regarding the use of the grant is exemplary. So, in a way, when we finish our work in Open Music Europe, we will have to do something similar to what they do.

One possibility would be that you join me in the office, we sit down, watch the webinar on mute, and we talk about what they do and how we could do it.  It could be a kind of an introduction to making the most out of a grant that will employ you, but it is not very directly related to our work, after all, we will work with statistical data. Polifonia has a more computer science and metadata approach, but I generally found their entire research ecosystem approach and data management approach absolutely top notch.

The other possibility is that we meet before or after the webinar, which ends around 1430, when I have all the afternoon free, or if that does not work for you, I have a slot between 1200-1300.

Best regards,
Daniel

_________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
Dear stakeholders and early adopters,

You're all invited to join a webinar on the Polifonia &lt;https://polifonia-project.eu/&gt; Research Ecosystem this friday afternoon. The webinar is co-organised by DANS&lt;https://dans.knaw.nl/en/&gt;, the Dutch national centre of expertise and repository for research data.

Polifonia Research Ecosystem – Impact of a project. A webinar on Data re-use and workflows
Where: Join Zoom Meeting
https://dariah.zoom.us/j/86468792131?pwd=X1zMFpeaAMVbaK56tnnihvVkiFuTgy.1
Meeting ID: 864 6879 2131
Passcode: 361647
January 19, 2024: 13.00-14.30 Amsterdam time

Description:
During the last project meeting, the Polifonia consortium extensively discussed how to foster the impact of the project in academia and beyond. How to make the output of Polifonia sustainable after the lifetime of the project is one important aspect. But fostering re-usability does not end by long-term preservation of certain assets (such as data and tools). In Polifonia Research Ecosystem – Impact of a project. A webinar on Data re-use and workflows, we will discuss how we ensure that more fluid assets such as interfaces, but also experiences in setting up and executing workflows via those interfaces, become reproducible and reuseable.

In this webinar the Polifonia consortium presents the specific Data Management Strategy (set up as management of research components of the type Data, Tools and Reports) Polifonia has developed. The project is presented briefly and team members  detail the Polifonia Research Ecosystem as the DMP strategy. They also summarise how the Ecosystem approach is related to usual DMP practices. In the last one-third of the webinar, we ask a round of experts to give feedback, share their own experiences with making project output sustainable by fostering reusability and to share ideas with us how to improve our impact strategy in Polifonia.
Will you join us?

Programme
13.00-13.15 Introduction into the project  and thoughts on (long-term) impact of the Polifonia project (Peter van Kranenburg) [10’ presentation 5’ questions]
13.15-13.45 The Research Ecosystem approach of the Polifonia project  (Enrico Daga) [25’ presentation 5’ questions]
13.45-14.00 The dynamic nature of Data Management in a research project (Andrea Scharnhorst) 10’ presentation 5’ questions]
14.00-14.30 Panel round with experts from other projects and ERIC’s (lead by Elena Giglia, Head of the Open Access Office at the University of Turin and Polifonia Advisory member)
· Dr. Femmy Admiraal - Senior data management expert at Leiden University Libraries
· Dr. Suzanne Dumochel - Head of International Cooperation, CNRS (Directorate of Open Research Data)
· Barbara Magagna – coauthor of the FAIR Implementation Profile (FIP) Ontology, and member of the EOSC Task Force Semantic Interoperability
· Dr. Wolmar Nyberg Åkerström - ELIXIR, and Coordinator of the EOSC TF Semantic Interoperability

Reprex has an office in Apollo 14, the impact hub of The Hague.  It is a cool place, with all the table tennis, community kitchen and garden facilities you would expect from a place where sustainability minded startups are present. And we are surrounded by the new Fokker Terminal, and the scale up hub and all in the old industrial area behind the Centraal station.

The best would be if I would show you around next Friday or the Monday after, because I will arrive back to the Netherlands only on Wednesday night. Maybe the best would be to exchange phone numbers and set up something (+31 615058460)?

Best regards,
Daniel

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Monday, January 8, 2024 5:36 PM
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Subject: Re: Further KULT suryves

Hi James,

WP2:
I will go on Wednesday to Slovakia, but I very much scaled down the visit, and focus only on Hudobné centrum; SOZA; and Wikipedia Slovensko.  I do not see the possibility of putting on a higher workload if EUBA and SSSA are not contributing to this work in a meaningful way.

WP4:
1. Today I also sent for peer review two pieces of the software ecosystem: a major upgrade of dataset and a minor update of iotables, which is just a small maintenance of the background.
2. Before Christmas, I had a one-on-one discussion with Leo before Christmas about the D4.2 and I believe that what Leo suggested to me did not meet the professional and ethical standards but in the absence of witnesses I just decided to distance myself. I declared that I am not going to work under his leadership without a clear description of the REPREX and UTU background, and a very detailed plan on how the foreground (the software ecosystem) will be developed.
3. In practice, Reprex will create software parts that a) identify data gaps, b) help filling them, c) and place them into music innovation applications for WP1,2,3,5, but I do not accept any contributions from UTU and I will not contribute to any UTU software. If Leo/Richard want to, they can deliver something that meets the definition of a software ecosystem, but Reprex's contribution must be fully attributed to Reprex.

Plans for 2024:

  *   We started last week a major new project, OpenProductions, which is currently a privately funded project (our EIT appeal is still pending, the entire grant scheme is delayed).
  *   I started hiring for Reprex and we are doing a recruitment with a new project manager.
  *   Unless Marc and you agree otherwise to redirect OpenMuse into some meaningfully different direction, I will keep contributing significantly to this project till May (maily to deliver the OMO) and will gradually withdraw personally afterwards.
  *   I am at this stage not open to shared postdocs with any university except for UvA. Such a deal would have to be initiated by EUBA, SSSA or UTU and with clear benefits to Reprex.

Best regards,
Daniel

Hi all,

Daniel is correct, we will not conduct CAP surveys in 2024. We were fortunate to receive funding for high-quality data collection, and we do not want this to suffer from rushing the set-up.

@Joost Poort&lt;mailto:j.p.poort@uva.nl&gt; and @daniel.antal@reprex.nl&lt;mailto:daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;, we should still find a time in February to start this discussion, though!

Best regards,
James

________________________________
From: daniel.antal@reprex.nl &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Friday, January 12, 2024 4:35 PM
To: Leo Lahti &lt;leo.lahti@utu.fi&gt;
Cc: Akewak Jeba &lt;akewak.k.jeba@utu.fi&gt;; Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;; James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Subject: Re: VS: Inquiry Regarding Availability of CAP Surveys for OpenMUSE WP4

Hi Leo,

All the information is on the retroharmonize website, our background
package was developed to harmonize the Hungarian, Croatian, Slovak and
EU CAPs originally.
https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/retroharmonize-publication, and
the publication repo that we set up back in 2022 to write a publication
about the background of our project to kickstart this one. Even the CAP
replication dataset with it is on GitHub and Zenodo, and the actual code
with the tutorial vignettes are actually hosted by rOpengov, i.e. UTU.

https://retroharmonize.dataobservatory.eu/articles/cap.html

I think it is important to notice that this is a background to the
project, it is already processed, the code is written, so I do not see a
huge deal of interest in working with this. Because every WP in the
project is seriously delayed, I do not think that that any CAP surveys
will be conducted in 2024.  However, the work related to creating the
data catalogue and codebook and crossswalk tables for the KULT surveys
is extremely urgent.

Best regards,
Daniel

EBAN represents a sector estimated to invest 11.4 billion Euros a year and playing a vital role in Europe’s future, notably in the funding of SMEs.

·       SIF&lt;https://solarimpulse.com/&gt; Solar Impulse Foundation. To address sustainability challenges while enabling economic growth, Bertrand Piccard and the Solar Impulse Foundation have identified 1000+ clean tech and profitable solutions.

Dear Daniel,

While I recognise the reasons for your frustration, I do think that this latest email from Leo to you was in good faith – not a further attempt at evasion.

As the deliverable resubmissions are complete, it's time for a SINUS-REPREX bilateral check-in. Is there a day/time this week that would be best for you? A brief agenda from our side follows:


  *   Walk through of the revisions to D2.1 and WP2 agenda for 2024
  *   Walk through of the revisions to D3.1 and WP3 agenda for 2024
  *   Walk through of the revisions to D6.3
  *   Request for update on WP5, specifically the OMO and stakeholder outreach (in coop. w Joost)
  *   Implications of all of the above re: WP4

Briefly, here are my thoughts on the project as a whole. It has functionally split into two:


  *
REPREX and SOZA continuing your past work in Slovakia, with forthcoming help from UVA via your joint postdoc, and transfer potential to ARTISJUS and MUSICAUTOR given their interest
  *
SINUS trying to assist everyone else in meeting the EC reviewers' baseline expectations

This is not the worst possible outcome. A peaceful separation is better than a messy divorce. However, it also sets a low bar for expected outputs. At the very least, our 'two projects' will have to cooperate on:


  *   Our stakeholder advisory board
  *   Our surveys (WP2 and WP3)
  *   The Open Music Observatory

I do not see any necessary barriers to a minimal degree of cooperation here. But hopefully we can go beyond the bare minimum.

Finally, regarding your prospective plan of ceasing all personal work in the project by May. In order for this to be workable, REPREX has to hire soon, or at least present a hiring plan. I will not be able (nor willing) to brief REPREX hires on their responsibilities in your absence. You are responsible for the handover.

Please let me know what is best for a call,

James




________________________________
From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Saturday, January 13, 2024 11:14 AM
To: Leo Lahti &lt;leo.lahti@utu.fi&gt;
Cc: Akewak Jeba &lt;akewak.k.jeba@utu.fi&gt;; James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;; Burus István &lt;istvan.burus@reprex.nl&gt;
Subject: Re: VS: Inquiry Regarding Availability of CAP Surveys for OpenMUSE WP4


Dear Leo and James,

I suggested a solution to James to break this impasse, but that will require adherence to the grant agreement (i.e. placing the backgrounds into the Consortium Agreement), and an honest and actionable task list and budget. Reprex is not going to participate in any work that deviates from our grant agreement: which is not feeling well-identified data gaps of the music industry with novel methods and code, and does not lead to the creation of indicators and datasets that the industry finds useful in filling the data gaps.

Let me quote my code of ethics and standards of professional conduct&lt;https://www.cfainstitute.org/-/media/documents/ethics-in-practice/code_of_ethics_and_standards_of_professional_conduct.pdf&gt;, which we attached to the internal by-laws of our Open Music Europe project’s ethics to let you understand why I think that adhering to the grant agreement in terms of clearly spelling out our respective background, and creating a detailed task list is inevitable for our cooperation.

 Members and Candidates have a duty of loyalty to their clients and must act with reasonable care and exercise prudent judgment. Members and Candidates must act for the benefit of their clients and place their clients’ interests before their employer’s or their own interests.

Disclose to clients and prospective clients the nature of the services provided, along with information about the costs to the client associated with those services.

Members and Candidates must not engage in any professional conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, or deceit or commit any act that reflects adversely on their professional reputation, integrity, or competence.

Members and Candidates must make reasonable efforts to ensure that anyone subject to their supervision or authority complies with applicable laws, rules, regulations, and the Code and Standards.

REPREX will continue to use its limited resources in this grant in line with the grant agreement: we will write new software pieces that form an ecosystem, and can fill the data gaps in music economy, diversity of music circulation, social and environmental sustainability, education of music, with novel data that can be demonstrated in Taskstream 3 to be useful for the music industry. We will validate our efforts in the following way:

- We will get validation of representative music industry stakeholders that our approach, software and datasets create value for them and meet the intended purpose;

- We will pass our software and its documentation independent peer review;

- We hired an independent auditor to assure that our spending on the software pieces is accounted for till the last working hour and eurocent in line with grant.

My problems with your Excel table:

I do not think that I see how the eurostat package in its current form can provide any value to this grant. Anybody can download or receive Eurostat products in the highest possible quality. Eurostat indeed has some semi-finished products, like the one that is used by the iotables package, which require further processing to be useful for the music industry, but the eurostat package per se does no such thing.  I could imagine after a careful cost-benefit analysis some COICOP or similar filtering of some data products that would create novel statistical indicators for the music industry, but downloading perfectly documented and formatted data and putting them into another data catalogue to me does not seem to be in scope with our grant.

I do not think that any work with EU-SILC is feasible without a plan in less than 6 months, and I also find it hard to believe that you have a plan to reconcile it with the objectives of this grant. I do not think that the eurostat package without a supporting package serves the needs of the music industry.   I actually do not think that you can create value with EU-SILC, an extremely complex harmonised survey program without having a statistically competent researcher with work experience with EU-SILC and strong programming skills in R.  We can provide such an expert (she is mentioned in our grant agreement) but currently I am not sure Dr Tátrai is available right now, as we never promised her full-time work, and we do not have a budget to employ her for more than 1-2 months.

Members and Candidates must act with and maintain the competence necessary to fulfill their professional responsibilities.

I think that we work with

- survey microdata for retrospective harmonisation, where the data is in different pre-exisiting formats, coding, etc,

- survey microdata for ex-ante harmonisation, where the data should be designed to be collected in suitable format to match with pre-existing data and metadata- privately-held administrative data in various music enterprises and other institutions, conforming to a wide range of forms, supports with a wide range of metadata

- publicly held administrative data in public institutions, conforming a wide range of forms, supported with a wide range of metadata

- other data that serves as metadata for various purposes, and primary data for others.  They are usually neither administrative nor survey data.



I do not think that you have an understanding of the problems that the KULT datasets pose.  There is a lot of processing needed to make them work, but of course, they are not super-specific to KULT, however, the KULT-specific work cannot be done without taking care of the retrospective harmonisation and crosswalking issues, which are only touched by our background retroharmonize package superficially. I do not think that REPREX alone can do much with it in less than 12 months and I informed the Slovak partners that we suspended this part of the project, because we did not receive any kind of resources from the academic partners. This is not our work.

Members and Candidates must avoid or make full and fair disclosure of all matters that could reasonably be expected to impair their independence and objectivity and interfere with respective duties to their clients, prospective clients, and employer. Members and Candidates must ensure that such disclosures are prominent, are delivered in plain language, and communicate the relevant information effectively.

Unfortunately we have an extremely strong conflict of interest here.  If you create a software ecosystem that does not fulfill the three objectives of our grant, my tasks, and the tasks of my longü-standing partners, particularly SOZA, Artisjus and ALOADED will fail and the blame will be on me. Therefore, I cannot participate in the creation of a software ecosystem that will not serve the purposes of the grant.

Members and Candidates must not knowingly make any misrepresentations relating to investment analysis, recommendations, actions, or other professional activities.

Reprex actually has a published code to work with Eurobarometer, which is part of the background of our grant agreement.  I would find it hard from an integrity or accountability point of view if you would submit a foreground delivery that Reprex already developed 4 years ago, and which sits in your repository with a logbook dating back to 2020.

I do not think that a "bulk download of Eurobarometer files"  serves any purpose, or if it is even legal, and certainly cannot fathom how it serves the needs of the music industry in filling its data gaps.  GESIS, the owner of the data catalogue used to have such an R package which was discontinued, because it served no real purpose. I do not think that if you contact them with the idea to restart it will be met with great enthusiasm, particularly, because much of the Eurobarometer data in different formats is now available in the Open Data Portal in pristine format.

Best regards,
Daniel Antal

Dear Daniel,

I am sorry if you found my email disappointing – that was not my intention. I actually thought that I was striking a conciliatory note, but perhaps I was tone-deaf. I want to aim for more alignment rather than less, and am very glad personally to be of help to REPREX any way I can. However, I also want to adopt realistic goals given the numerous conflicts we seem to face.

How about Thursday 18 Jan at 14:00? My schedule on Thursday is also very open, so feel free to suggest an alternate time.

I will reply in the conversation with Joost separately. I assure you based on our prior conversations that Joost has the Consortium's best interests at heart and is committed to being flexible.

In any case, hopefully I can clarify my meaning during our call.

Best regards,
James

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Monday, January 15, 2024 5:27 PM
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Subject: Re: VS: Inquiry Regarding Availability of CAP Surveys for OpenMUSE WP4

Hi James,

I wrote you several suggested dates for the week, but currently Tuesday is no longer feasible.  I can find time on Thursday almost anytime, though I would prefer sometime mid-day.  Also, I can find time on Friday but, preferably in the afternoon hours.

We have created an extremely detailed task list for WP2.2 and 2.3 the week before and a contractual task list for HUDOBNÉ CENTRUM. I think that this must be reviewed as well.

I am very disappointed by your mail, and I want to make sure that my former clients and partners will stay with me, which includes ALOADED as well.  If this divorce happens, and the consortium is no longer filling the data gaps and the OMO, obviously I will not in anyhow give my name, face to assist anything that the consortium does.  I was quoting the CFA Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct because I must distance myself from Leo; I cannot and will not work with anybody to use the grant for a different purpose than it was given for. Generally, I think that the EU Horizon unit has some baseline expectations and the policy unit has, too.  For me that will remain a credibility issue to work for the original aim of the grant, but of course, I will always make it clear that since I am not the Coordinator, I have no powers to spend the money with the original intention.

Joost emailed me about the workshop plan, which I find very unfortunate, as it is completely colliding with what we spoke with the policy unit, who want to invite us to their conference on those days for the same purpose. I think that it is certain that no serious stakeholders will meet this consortium within 2 weeks.  I also think that the stakeholder network and the advisory board will be a delicate thing because it will be soon clear that the majority of the money will not be spent for the original purpose.

I generally think that the entire OMO idea will need to be recalibrated, as it was never the intention that we will deliver an empty observatory, which is what will happen.  We'll talk about this, but I think that this is a rather difficult task, as an empty observatory will not really look like an observatory for the reviewers. Also, for the stakeholders it will be an extremely tough sale. I really will need to think through with Tomas how to manage the reputation damage following from this.

Best regards,
Daniel






On Mon, Jan 15, 2024 at 2:46 PM James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt; wrote:
Dear Daniel,

While I recognise the reasons for your frustration, I do think that this latest email from Leo to you was in good faith – not a further attempt at evasion.

As the deliverable resubmissions are complete, it's time for a SINUS-REPREX bilateral check-in. Is there a day/time this week that would be best for you? A brief agenda from our side follows:


  *   Walk through of the revisions to D2.1 and WP2 agenda for 2024
  *   Walk through of the revisions to D3.1 and WP3 agenda for 2024
  *   Walk through of the revisions to D6.3
  *   Request for update on WP5, specifically the OMO and stakeholder outreach (in coop. w Joost)
  *   Implications of all of the above re: WP4

Briefly, here are my thoughts on the project as a whole. It has functionally split into two:


  *
REPREX and SOZA continuing your past work in Slovakia, with forthcoming help from UVA via your joint postdoc, and transfer potential to ARTISJUS and MUSICAUTOR given their interest
  *
SINUS trying to assist everyone else in meeting the EC reviewers' baseline expectations

This is not the worst possible outcome. A peaceful separation is better than a messy divorce. However, it also sets a low bar for expected outputs. At the very least, our 'two projects' will have to cooperate on:


  *   Our stakeholder advisory board
  *   Our surveys (WP2 and WP3)
  *   The Open Music Observatory

I do not see any necessary barriers to a minimal degree of cooperation here. But hopefully we can go beyond the bare minimum.

Finally, regarding your prospective plan of ceasing all personal work in the project by May. In order for this to be workable, REPREX has to hire soon, or at least present a hiring plan. I will not be able (nor willing) to brief REPREX hires on their responsibilities in your absence. You are responsible for the handover.

Please let me know what is best for a call,

James

Subject: Re: VS: Inquiry Regarding Availability of CAP Surveys for OpenMUSE WP4


Dear Leo and James,

I suggested a solution to James to break this impasse, but that will require adherence to the grant agreement (i.e. placing the backgrounds into the Consortium Agreement), and an honest and actionable task list and budget. Reprex is not going to participate in any work that deviates from our grant agreement: which is not feeling well-identified data gaps of the music industry with novel methods and code, and does not lead to the creation of indicators and datasets that the industry finds useful in filling the data gaps.

Let me quote my code of ethics and standards of professional conduct&lt;https://www.cfainstitute.org/-/media/documents/ethics-in-practice/code_of_ethics_and_standards_of_professional_conduct.pdf&gt;, which we attached to the internal by-laws of our Open Music Europe project’s ethics to let you understand why I think that adhering to the grant agreement in terms of clearly spelling out our respective background, and creating a detailed task list is inevitable for our cooperation.

 Members and Candidates have a duty of loyalty to their clients and must act with reasonable care and exercise prudent judgment. Members and Candidates must act for the benefit of their clients and place their clients’ interests before their employer’s or their own interests.

Disclose to clients and prospective clients the nature of the services provided, along with information about the costs to the client associated with those services.

Members and Candidates must not engage in any professional conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, or deceit or commit any act that reflects adversely on their professional reputation, integrity, or competence.

Members and Candidates must make reasonable efforts to ensure that anyone subject to their supervision or authority complies with applicable laws, rules, regulations, and the Code and Standards.

REPREX will continue to use its limited resources in this grant in line with the grant agreement: we will write new software pieces that form an ecosystem, and can fill the data gaps in music economy, diversity of music circulation, social and environmental sustainability, education of music, with novel data that can be demonstrated in Taskstream 3 to be useful for the music industry. We will validate our efforts in the following way:

- We will get validation of representative music industry stakeholders that our approach, software and datasets create value for them and meet the intended purpose;

- We will pass our software and its documentation independent peer review;

- We hired an independent auditor to assure that our spending on the software pieces is accounted for till the last working hour and eurocent in line with grant.

My problems with your Excel table:

I do not think that I see how the eurostat package in its current form can provide any value to this grant. Anybody can download or receive Eurostat products in the highest possible quality. Eurostat indeed has some semi-finished products, like the one that is used by the iotables package, which require further processing to be useful for the music industry, but the eurostat package per se does no such thing.  I could imagine after a careful cost-benefit analysis some COICOP or similar filtering of some data products that would create novel statistical indicators for the music industry, but downloading perfectly documented and formatted data and putting them into another data catalogue to me does not seem to be in scope with our grant.

I do not think that any work with EU-SILC is feasible without a plan in less than 6 months, and I also find it hard to believe that you have a plan to reconcile it with the objectives of this grant. I do not think that the eurostat package without a supporting package serves the needs of the music industry.   I actually do not think that you can create value with EU-SILC, an extremely complex harmonised survey program without having a statistically competent researcher with work experience with EU-SILC and strong programming skills in R.  We can provide such an expert (she is mentioned in our grant agreement) but currently I am not sure Dr Tátrai is available right now, as we never promised her full-time work, and we do not have a budget to employ her for more than 1-2 months.

Members and Candidates must act with and maintain the competence necessary to fulfill their professional responsibilities.

I think that we work with

- survey microdata for retrospective harmonisation, where the data is in different pre-exisiting formats, coding, etc,

- survey microdata for ex-ante harmonisation, where the data should be designed to be collected in suitable format to match with pre-existing data and metadata- privately-held administrative data in various music enterprises and other institutions, conforming to a wide range of forms, supports with a wide range of metadata

- publicly held administrative data in public institutions, conforming a wide range of forms, supported with a wide range of metadata

- other data that serves as metadata for various purposes, and primary data for others.  They are usually neither administrative nor survey data.



I do not think that you have an understanding of the problems that the KULT datasets pose.  There is a lot of processing needed to make them work, but of course, they are not super-specific to KULT, however, the KULT-specific work cannot be done without taking care of the retrospective harmonisation and crosswalking issues, which are only touched by our background retroharmonize package superficially. I do not think that REPREX alone can do much with it in less than 12 months and I informed the Slovak partners that we suspended this part of the project, because we did not receive any kind of resources from the academic partners. This is not our work.

Members and Candidates must avoid or make full and fair disclosure of all matters that could reasonably be expected to impair their independence and objectivity and interfere with respective duties to their clients, prospective clients, and employer. Members and Candidates must ensure that such disclosures are prominent, are delivered in plain language, and communicate the relevant information effectively.

Unfortunately we have an extremely strong conflict of interest here.  If you create a software ecosystem that does not fulfill the three objectives of our grant, my tasks, and the tasks of my longü-standing partners, particularly SOZA, Artisjus and ALOADED will fail and the blame will be on me. Therefore, I cannot participate in the creation of a software ecosystem that will not serve the purposes of the grant.

Members and Candidates must not knowingly make any misrepresentations relating to investment analysis, recommendations, actions, or other professional activities.

Reprex actually has a published code to work with Eurobarometer, which is part of the background of our grant agreement.  I would find it hard from an integrity or accountability point of view if you would submit a foreground delivery that Reprex already developed 4 years ago, and which sits in your repository with a logbook dating back to 2020.

I do not think that a "bulk download of Eurobarometer files"  serves any purpose, or if it is even legal, and certainly cannot fathom how it serves the needs of the music industry in filling its data gaps.  GESIS, the owner of the data catalogue used to have such an R package which was discontinued, because it served no real purpose. I do not think that if you contact them with the idea to restart it will be met with great enthusiasm, particularly, because much of the Eurobarometer data in different formats is now available in the Open Data Portal in pristine format.

Best regards,
Daniel Antal

To: EUROPEANA-TECH@LISTSERV.EUROPEANA.EU &lt;EUROPEANA-TECH@LISTSERV.EUROPEANA.EU&gt;
Subject: Offer for Cooperation: Datasheets for Cultural Heritage Datasets


*Sorry for cross-posting*



Dear Europeana TECH Members,

the combined Europeana Tech and Research Working Group "Datasheets for digital cultural heritage datasets&lt;https://pro.europeana.eu/project/datasheets-for-digital-cultural-heritage-working-group&gt;" has written and published a paper to propose that datasheets should accompany the publication of digital cultural heritage datasets. The paper contains recommendations to incorporate information on the motivation and selection criteria, digitisation pipeline, data provenance, the use of linked open data, and version information. Furthermore, a datasheet template has been adapted for use in cultural heritage institutions.

The paper has been published in open access in the Journal of Open Humanities:

https://openhumanitiesdata.metajnl.com/articles/10.5334/johd.124

The datasheet template has been published by us on Zenodo:

https://zenodo.org/records/8375034



Cultural heritage institutions aiming to publish machine-amenable datasets are cordially invited to use this template. Several members of the Europeana Working Group are willing to support these cultural heritage institutions in establishing such datasheets by providing explanations and advice on the datasheet template. From our side, it would be interesting to receive feedback on the datasheet template and to collect experiences and best practices while using it.



If you are interested in a cooperation between your institution and the working group, you may get in touch with:

Giulia Osti, PhD researcher at the University College Dublin, eMail: giulia.osti@ucdconnect.ie

Henk Alkemade, Member of the Steering Group of Europeana TECH, eMail: henkalkemade66@gmail.com

Steven Claeyssens, Chair of the Europeana Research community, eMail: Steven.Claeyssens@KB.nl

Jörg Lehmann, postdoctoral researcher at the Berlin State Library, eMail: joerg.lehmann@sbb.spk-berlin.de



Looking forward to cooperate,

with best regards,

Giulia Osti, Henk Alkemade, Steven Claeyssens, Jörg Lehmann



--



Dr. Jörg Lehmann

IDM 4 (Data Science) · Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter · Projekt Mensch.Maschine.Kultur – Künstliche Intelligenz für das Digitale Kulturelle Erbe&lt;https://mmk.sbb.berlin/&gt;

Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin – Preußischer Kulturbesitz

+49 30 266 43 23 21

Subject: Re: VS: Inquiry Regarding Availability of CAP Surveys for OpenMUSE WP4


Dear Leo and James,

I suggested a solution to James to break this impasse, but that will require adherence to the grant agreement (i.e. placing the backgrounds into the Consortium Agreement), and an honest and actionable task list and budget. Reprex is not going to participate in any work that deviates from our grant agreement: which is not feeling well-identified data gaps of the music industry with novel methods and code, and does not lead to the creation of indicators and datasets that the industry finds useful in filling the data gaps.

Let me quote my code of ethics and standards of professional conduct&lt;https://www.cfainstitute.org/-/media/documents/ethics-in-practice/code_of_ethics_and_standards_of_professional_conduct.pdf&gt;, which we attached to the internal by-laws of our Open Music Europe project’s ethics to let you understand why I think that adhering to the grant agreement in terms of clearly spelling out our respective background, and creating a detailed task list is inevitable for our cooperation.

 Members and Candidates have a duty of loyalty to their clients and must act with reasonable care and exercise prudent judgment. Members and Candidates must act for the benefit of their clients and place their clients’ interests before their employer’s or their own interests.

Disclose to clients and prospective clients the nature of the services provided, along with information about the costs to the client associated with those services.

Members and Candidates must not engage in any professional conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, or deceit or commit any act that reflects adversely on their professional reputation, integrity, or competence.

Members and Candidates must make reasonable efforts to ensure that anyone subject to their supervision or authority complies with applicable laws, rules, regulations, and the Code and Standards.

REPREX will continue to use its limited resources in this grant in line with the grant agreement: we will write new software pieces that form an ecosystem, and can fill the data gaps in music economy, diversity of music circulation, social and environmental sustainability, education of music, with novel data that can be demonstrated in Taskstream 3 to be useful for the music industry. We will validate our efforts in the following way:

- We will get validation of representative music industry stakeholders that our approach, software and datasets create value for them and meet the intended purpose;

- We will pass our software and its documentation independent peer review;

- We hired an independent auditor to assure that our spending on the software pieces is accounted for till the last working hour and eurocent in line with grant.

My problems with your Excel table:

I do not think that I see how the eurostat package in its current form can provide any value to this grant. Anybody can download or receive Eurostat products in the highest possible quality. Eurostat indeed has some semi-finished products, like the one that is used by the iotables package, which require further processing to be useful for the music industry, but the eurostat package per se does no such thing.  I could imagine after a careful cost-benefit analysis some COICOP or similar filtering of some data products that would create novel statistical indicators for the music industry, but downloading perfectly documented and formatted data and putting them into another data catalogue to me does not seem to be in scope with our grant.

I do not think that any work with EU-SILC is feasible without a plan in less than 6 months, and I also find it hard to believe that you have a plan to reconcile it with the objectives of this grant. I do not think that the eurostat package without a supporting package serves the needs of the music industry.   I actually do not think that you can create value with EU-SILC, an extremely complex harmonised survey program without having a statistically competent researcher with work experience with EU-SILC and strong programming skills in R.  We can provide such an expert (she is mentioned in our grant agreement) but currently I am not sure Dr Tátrai is available right now, as we never promised her full-time work, and we do not have a budget to employ her for more than 1-2 months.

Members and Candidates must act with and maintain the competence necessary to fulfill their professional responsibilities.

I think that we work with

- survey microdata for retrospective harmonisation, where the data is in different pre-exisiting formats, coding, etc,

- survey microdata for ex-ante harmonisation, where the data should be designed to be collected in suitable format to match with pre-existing data and metadata- privately-held administrative data in various music enterprises and other institutions, conforming to a wide range of forms, supports with a wide range of metadata

- publicly held administrative data in public institutions, conforming a wide range of forms, supported with a wide range of metadata

- other data that serves as metadata for various purposes, and primary data for others.  They are usually neither administrative nor survey data.



I do not think that you have an understanding of the problems that the KULT datasets pose.  There is a lot of processing needed to make them work, but of course, they are not super-specific to KULT, however, the KULT-specific work cannot be done without taking care of the retrospective harmonisation and crosswalking issues, which are only touched by our background retroharmonize package superficially. I do not think that REPREX alone can do much with it in less than 12 months and I informed the Slovak partners that we suspended this part of the project, because we did not receive any kind of resources from the academic partners. This is not our work.

Members and Candidates must avoid or make full and fair disclosure of all matters that could reasonably be expected to impair their independence and objectivity and interfere with respective duties to their clients, prospective clients, and employer. Members and Candidates must ensure that such disclosures are prominent, are delivered in plain language, and communicate the relevant information effectively.

Unfortunately we have an extremely strong conflict of interest here.  If you create a software ecosystem that does not fulfill the three objectives of our grant, my tasks, and the tasks of my longü-standing partners, particularly SOZA, Artisjus and ALOADED will fail and the blame will be on me. Therefore, I cannot participate in the creation of a software ecosystem that will not serve the purposes of the grant.

Members and Candidates must not knowingly make any misrepresentations relating to investment analysis, recommendations, actions, or other professional activities.

Reprex actually has a published code to work with Eurobarometer, which is part of the background of our grant agreement.  I would find it hard from an integrity or accountability point of view if you would submit a foreground delivery that Reprex already developed 4 years ago, and which sits in your repository with a logbook dating back to 2020.

I do not think that a "bulk download of Eurobarometer files"  serves any purpose, or if it is even legal, and certainly cannot fathom how it serves the needs of the music industry in filling its data gaps.  GESIS, the owner of the data catalogue used to have such an R package which was discontinued, because it served no real purpose. I do not think that if you contact them with the idea to restart it will be met with great enthusiasm, particularly, because much of the Eurobarometer data in different formats is now available in the Open Data Portal in pristine format.

Best regards,
Daniel Antal

Hi Daniel,

Subject: Re: VS: Inquiry Regarding Availability of CAP Surveys for OpenMUSE WP4


Dear Leo and James,

I suggested a solution to James to break this impasse, but that will require adherence to the grant agreement (i.e. placing the backgrounds into the Consortium Agreement), and an honest and actionable task list and budget. Reprex is not going to participate in any work that deviates from our grant agreement: which is not feeling well-identified data gaps of the music industry with novel methods and code, and does not lead to the creation of indicators and datasets that the industry finds useful in filling the data gaps.

Let me quote my code of ethics and standards of professional conduct&lt;https://www.cfainstitute.org/-/media/documents/ethics-in-practice/code_of_ethics_and_standards_of_professional_conduct.pdf&gt;, which we attached to the internal by-laws of our Open Music Europe project’s ethics to let you understand why I think that adhering to the grant agreement in terms of clearly spelling out our respective background, and creating a detailed task list is inevitable for our cooperation.

 Members and Candidates have a duty of loyalty to their clients and must act with reasonable care and exercise prudent judgment. Members and Candidates must act for the benefit of their clients and place their clients’ interests before their employer’s or their own interests.

Disclose to clients and prospective clients the nature of the services provided, along with information about the costs to the client associated with those services.

Members and Candidates must not engage in any professional conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, or deceit or commit any act that reflects adversely on their professional reputation, integrity, or competence.

Members and Candidates must make reasonable efforts to ensure that anyone subject to their supervision or authority complies with applicable laws, rules, regulations, and the Code and Standards.

REPREX will continue to use its limited resources in this grant in line with the grant agreement: we will write new software pieces that form an ecosystem, and can fill the data gaps in music economy, diversity of music circulation, social and environmental sustainability, education of music, with novel data that can be demonstrated in Taskstream 3 to be useful for the music industry. We will validate our efforts in the following way:

- We will get validation of representative music industry stakeholders that our approach, software and datasets create value for them and meet the intended purpose;

- We will pass our software and its documentation independent peer review;

- We hired an independent auditor to assure that our spending on the software pieces is accounted for till the last working hour and eurocent in line with grant.

My problems with your Excel table:

I do not think that I see how the eurostat package in its current form can provide any value to this grant. Anybody can download or receive Eurostat products in the highest possible quality. Eurostat indeed has some semi-finished products, like the one that is used by the iotables package, which require further processing to be useful for the music industry, but the eurostat package per se does no such thing.  I could imagine after a careful cost-benefit analysis some COICOP or similar filtering of some data products that would create novel statistical indicators for the music industry, but downloading perfectly documented and formatted data and putting them into another data catalogue to me does not seem to be in scope with our grant.

I do not think that any work with EU-SILC is feasible without a plan in less than 6 months, and I also find it hard to believe that you have a plan to reconcile it with the objectives of this grant. I do not think that the eurostat package without a supporting package serves the needs of the music industry.   I actually do not think that you can create value with EU-SILC, an extremely complex harmonised survey program without having a statistically competent researcher with work experience with EU-SILC and strong programming skills in R.  We can provide such an expert (she is mentioned in our grant agreement) but currently I am not sure Dr Tátrai is available right now, as we never promised her full-time work, and we do not have a budget to employ her for more than 1-2 months.

Members and Candidates must act with and maintain the competence necessary to fulfill their professional responsibilities.

I think that we work with

- survey microdata for retrospective harmonisation, where the data is in different pre-exisiting formats, coding, etc,

- survey microdata for ex-ante harmonisation, where the data should be designed to be collected in suitable format to match with pre-existing data and metadata- privately-held administrative data in various music enterprises and other institutions, conforming to a wide range of forms, supports with a wide range of metadata

- publicly held administrative data in public institutions, conforming a wide range of forms, supported with a wide range of metadata

- other data that serves as metadata for various purposes, and primary data for others.  They are usually neither administrative nor survey data.



I do not think that you have an understanding of the problems that the KULT datasets pose.  There is a lot of processing needed to make them work, but of course, they are not super-specific to KULT, however, the KULT-specific work cannot be done without taking care of the retrospective harmonisation and crosswalking issues, which are only touched by our background retroharmonize package superficially. I do not think that REPREX alone can do much with it in less than 12 months and I informed the Slovak partners that we suspended this part of the project, because we did not receive any kind of resources from the academic partners. This is not our work.

Members and Candidates must avoid or make full and fair disclosure of all matters that could reasonably be expected to impair their independence and objectivity and interfere with respective duties to their clients, prospective clients, and employer. Members and Candidates must ensure that such disclosures are prominent, are delivered in plain language, and communicate the relevant information effectively.

Unfortunately we have an extremely strong conflict of interest here.  If you create a software ecosystem that does not fulfill the three objectives of our grant, my tasks, and the tasks of my longü-standing partners, particularly SOZA, Artisjus and ALOADED will fail and the blame will be on me. Therefore, I cannot participate in the creation of a software ecosystem that will not serve the purposes of the grant.

Members and Candidates must not knowingly make any misrepresentations relating to investment analysis, recommendations, actions, or other professional activities.

Reprex actually has a published code to work with Eurobarometer, which is part of the background of our grant agreement.  I would find it hard from an integrity or accountability point of view if you would submit a foreground delivery that Reprex already developed 4 years ago, and which sits in your repository with a logbook dating back to 2020.

I do not think that a "bulk download of Eurobarometer files"  serves any purpose, or if it is even legal, and certainly cannot fathom how it serves the needs of the music industry in filling its data gaps.  GESIS, the owner of the data catalogue used to have such an R package which was discontinued, because it served no real purpose. I do not think that if you contact them with the idea to restart it will be met with great enthusiasm, particularly, because much of the Eurobarometer data in different formats is now available in the Open Data Portal in pristine format.

Best regards,
Daniel Antal

From: Discussion list for Europeana Technical Developments &lt;EUROPEANA-TECH@LISTSERV.EUROPEANA.EU&gt; on behalf of Marloes Bontje &lt;mbontje@BEELDENGELUID.NL&gt;
Sent: Wednesday, January 17, 2024 8:38:34 AM
To: EUROPEANA-TECH@LISTSERV.EUROPEANA.EU &lt;EUROPEANA-TECH@LISTSERV.EUROPEANA.EU&gt;
Subject: #webinar: Polifonia Research Ecosystem – Impact, Data re-use and Workflows (Jan 19)

Dear all,

Polifonia &lt;https://polifonia-project.eu/&gt; is a 3M€ project funded by the EU Horizon 2020 Programme that will run from January 2021 until April 2024 to recreate the connections between music, people, places and events from the sixteenth century to the modern day. These findings will be available to everyone as an interconnected global database on the web – a knowledge graph – and will enhance our understanding of European musical heritage. The project is now in its final stages.

[image.png]

In this webinar the Polifonia consortium presents the specific Data Management Strategy (set up as management of research components of the type Data, Tools and Reports) Polifonia has developed. The project is presented briefly and team members detail the Polifonia Research Ecosystem as the DMP strategy. They also summarise how the Ecosystem approach is related to usual DMP practices. In the last one-third of the webinar, we ask a round of experts to  give feedback, share their own experiences with making project output sustainable by fostering reusability and to share ideas with us how to improve our impact strategy in Polifonia.

Polifonia Research Ecosystem – Impact of a project. A webinar on Data re-use and workflows

Hi Daniel,

I fear you are shooting yourself in the foot here, because it looks like you are the one who refuses to work with Leo. It's obvious that D4.1 will fail and I think it's quite possible that UTU will do nothing before the interim review. At that point, we can make more drastic decisions. However, for the PO to accept drastic decisions, we have to shoiw a good-faith effort at exhausting every option within the current Consortium.

I'm well aware that the proposal, and especially the software ecosystem and OMO, are based on REPREX concepts – but it is *the Consortium* that received funding. There is no way to know whether a proposal without UTU in it would have been funded: possibly not, because regardless of work quality, motivation, creativity, etc., they have prestige.

This is bullshit but we have to accept it, and it has to at least *look like* we tried to work with them. Does this make sense..?

Believe me, I am as frustrated as you.

Best regards,
James
________________________________
From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Monday, January 22, 2024 1:52 PM

Cc: Leo Lahti &lt;leo.lahti@utu.fi&gt;; Richard Wages &lt;Richard.Wages@sinus-institut.de&gt;; Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Subject: Re: OpenMusE -- disambiguating REPREX &amp; UTU background

Hi James,


Step 1 – deadline today:

@Daniel, would it be possible for you to fill in cells J4 through M8 in the spreadsheet, i.e., specify whether you want to impose conditions on the use of these REPREX R packages above and beyond the licenses currently specified in CRAN?

I already sent you the conditions.  There are no further use conditions, I set the conditions for co-development and contribution.  This is not technically required for use, but I wanted to make clear what may be the conditions that UTU contributes to these packages, should they have the capacity and vision to do so.



Step 2 – deadline Tues 23 Jan:

@Leo, does UTU wish to declare any other background at this time, or only eurostat?

@Daniel, I know that there is REPREX background in addition to the R packages in the spreadsheet. Is any of this background relevant to the current conversation on REPREX vs. UTU intellectual property and the work that will be done in WP4? If so, please track down the current descriptions so we can try to reformat them into the DESCA template.


Yes, all our backgrounds are relevant.  For example, Leo requested access to the Slovak CAP surveys, which is a joint background of SOZA and REPREX.  At this point, there is no sufficient reason to grant access.



Step 3 – deadline Thurs 25 Jan:

As mentioned separately to both of you, to reduce dependencies, the smoothest way forward might be to assign each user story to a "product owner", either REPREX or UTU. Your teams will still have to ensure interdependency, but each team will have a more or less autonomous "work order" to implement.

Here is a spreadsheet summarising the existing user stories (Story_1 to Story_8) and five additional user stories that SINUS and SSSA need to write (Story_9 to Story_13): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/12ewUQAFtDDDoz_U-TSPxPDKy1hz8f427/edit#


  *
Columns B to G are based on the Github repository. Please double-check and correct if required, esp. Column G, "Existing R packages used".
  *
Columns H and I specify whether new R packages and/or other dev work is required. Please fill these in on a best-effort basis.
  *
Columns J and K specify the OpenMusE tasks to which the story is relevant and the "client" within the consortium. Please double-check and correct if required.
  *
In Column L and M, I suggest a "product owner" for each story and give my rationale.
  *
Please add your thoughts in Columns N and O.

Note that I suggest UTU as "product owner" for the survey implementation and survey data management user stories, despite these using retroharmonize. This is because UTU has a large number of PM in WP3, which must be used (recall that UTU previously rejected the idea of hiring a postdoc/research assistant under Prof. Cloonan, which would have needed to happen in year 1 to have real value). I'll do my best to flesh out these user stories within the next couple of days.

As all code created in the project will be open source, your teams can continue to benefit from each others' work without having to directly cooperate in an intensive way, which has proven stressful for everyone.

Please let me know what you think.


@James Rhys Edwards&lt;mailto:JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt; , I cannot put it another way.  I worked for 2.5 years to get this grant, and the EU Commission recommended to me to put together this consortium to develop the European Music Observatory. UTU signed up to develop R packages that help fill up the observatory.  I do not want to participate in any work that is not aiming towards this, and I treat it a misuse of the grant if the work is not contributing directly to filling identified data gaps.

I do not want UTU to be a product owner of anything that does not start to yield publishable datasets into the OMO by late March latest.  I do not want anybody to spend the programming part of the grant for a different purpose than the grant.  There are no products that UTU could own, because there is no agreed plan even on what the product should be doing, how many products there should be, or who has the capability to develop those products in an acceptable standard.

We just hired a great developer for WP1 who will contribute to this work, and I think that he could contribute to WP4 in a meaningful way, starting in a few weeks.  One of the developers of tidyverse also reached out to me and showed interest.  So far, I do not see how Leo is going to get people who can contribute in a meaningful way to our objective, therefore I do not see the ground for any intensive or whatever cooperation.  Over 13 month, I did not even got to understand a single sub-subtask planned by UTU that would contribute to our grant.

So this is my prefered course of action:

1. Define the background of the partners.
2. Report a default on D4.1 as there is no software ecosystem that can be developed  in 9 days, and the work has not started yet.
3. Have a call with the project officer and the policy officer and recalibrate the project.
4. Come up with a realistic plan on how R code will be developed that supports T1.2, T2.2, T3.2, T4.2 and T5.1 subject to constraints set in T6.3
5. Sell this budget, timeline, etc adjustment to all stakeholders in the consortium and the EC.

Best regards,
Daniel

### DMP diverging descriptions {#email-297}

**From:** James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**To:** Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;  
**Date:** 01/30/2024 10:13:56

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202401301013-DMP diverging descriptions-401.txt -->

Description of Action T6.3. “Data management plan (lead: SSSA; contributors: REPREX, MUSICAUTOR). [Start: M1, End: M36] A data management plan (DMP) is elaborated according to the GDPR. It will address questions of privacy and data sharing, data collection and data processing, as well as questions of IPRs, ensuring the monitoring and update of all IP related questions throughout the project. Additionally, data gathered in WPs 1-4 as well as their metadata, will be compiled and deposited in OpenAIREʼs Zenodo repository to ensure discoverability, accessibility, and intelligibility, based on their usefulness for the scientific community. Furthermore, questions of intellectual property are addressed within the consortium.”

https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/software/OME_Software_Ecosystem.html
“The team of T6.3 (Data Management Plan) must reconcile the expressive, human-language and visual representation of knowledge with coded ontologies to connect them to our open-source software ecosystem. We suggest that they assist the researchers with Wikibase GUI, OpenRefine, and Protégé so that they can translate the researchers’ implicit knowledge into an explicit and coded form. We expect that the DMP will make the coded knowledge available in RDF and use and adopt, as necessary, ontologies available in OWL.”

Hi Daniel,

________________________________
From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Wednesday, January 31, 2024 8:42 PM
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Subject: Hudobné centrum contract

Hello James,

I took a day to let yesterday's two meetings, the one in private, and the one in the WP leaders to settle down, and also the previous daylight and nighttime calls.

I will avoid any further conflict with Richard and Leo, provided that they do not put REPREX's name, input, background into any false statements.  If Leo misrepresents the work in 4.1 in any way, like yesterday, I will call him out: he did not write any software, he has absolutely no right to integrate REPREX's software, and he most certainly did not collect requirements from data users or owners.


  *
I can assure you that SINUS will not permit misrepresentations of background or work performed in any official / public documents or discussions.
  *   I was also surprised by, and regret, Leo's phrasing re: the user stories ("we").
  *   However, it is our duty as coordinator to take the most charitable interpretation of each partner. In this case this means that as Leo stated in response to your protest, by "we", he meant the WP4 team. However skeptical I may be, personally, I must take on a neutral expression during the discussion.
  *
I can assure you that it is on record that REPREX initiated the usability requirements elicitation process (despite SINUS requests to UTU to do this throughout Q2 and Q3 2023). All other WP leaders know this, and if anyone implies otherwise, they will merely be embarrassing themselves.

Apart from that, I think that the fact that Richard never created a task-level resource plan is good for now, because REPREX will allocate all its resources in WP4 to T4.2 and UTU can keep T4.1 100% to its own; just the way Richard can keep the data management.


  *   To clarify, it was never Richard's job to create a task-level resource plan per WP: this is something we asked the WP leaders to initiate, and which nobody has done so far.
  *   To further clarify, Richard is not the DMP task leader, rather SSSA (Dr. Denise Amram). As noted in our bilateral call, I have assisted SSSA in putting together a list of data sources that we may utilise, however, each partner that generates data must still catalogue their data assets in compliance with DMP standards. Most partners will require technical assistance for this.
  *   Earlier, we discussed a post-Interim Review swap of T4.1 to REPREX and T4.2 to UTU; I would like to keep this on the table, depending on how the discussion goes on the proposed PM transfers within UTU (6 to 12PM to Prof. Cloonan for a Live Music Census) and from UTU to UVA (6PM for Fabio) and REPREX (2 to 4PM for yet-unspecified programming tasks).

I would like to find how we could work in a more fruitful way in this project if you remain in the Coordinator's role, and I would also like to reach out to Marc Calmbach, because in case you leave, I think that this project will sink to an even lower chance of success.


  *   I am yet undecided on this. It is a difficult decision for a number of reasons.
  *   Keep this to yourself for now. It is highly sensitive and your discretion is appreciated.
  *
Hold off on reaching out to Marc. If it becomes necessary, I will initiate this conversation and involve you when the timing is right.
  *
Trust me on this. I know the parties involved and am confident that I can frame whatever decision I take as a win-win – but it is delicate.
  *
No matter where I am based, I will continue to contribute to the project to at least the same extent as now.
  *
No matter my official title, I will remain committed to my mediating role, even if this becomes a "shadow" position.
  *
Indeed, one decision point is that a move in institutions might give me more time / energy to dedicate to the project, as well as to continuing education.
     *
Leading multiple projects on different topics simultaneously in 2022 was very taxing.
     *
My current position does not incentivise or even permit improving my data science / management skills, something I have been long interested in.

Right now I do not see that I can be of any other help than ensure that at least in Slovakia we present something presentable, and for that I would like to ask you to finalize Hudobné centrum's contract next week.  REPREX will not be anyhow involved in that, apart from 2.2 and 2.3. Whatever data must be collected or processed for the other WPs, it is up for Leo and Richard to solve that.  They have a combined warchest of 30PMs to collect, process and manage data for this project.


  *   I think that maintaining a positive relationship with our Slovak stakeholders is a top priority, and appreciate your efforts here. I fully support your dedicating yourself 100% to this in the coming weeks.
  *   We are eager to finalise the contract next week. Richard supports it fully and our financial / legal administrators are aware that it is coming.

Once we have passed the interim review, and Hudobné centrum is contracted and working, sometime in late March we can present the OMO and how the research data management team can put things in it.


  *   This sounds like a good plan to me.

Best regards,

Dear Daniel,

Last week, I visited James in Berlin, and we started planning the work about the professional and MSMEs surveys. In response to your mail below, I think there are two types of input we would need from you to make sure the collected data will be usable inputs for T5.1:

  1.  We would need an example of a survey codebook and dataset formatted and documented in compliance with all of the standards you require for use with the music observatory. A mock-up data example (and codebook) would ensure that we fully understand your requirements and that the survey data could "interoperate" with the other data to contribute to the observatory.
  2.  Concerning the MSME survey, I am trying to identify the Slovak target companies. My first option would be to use the Bureau van Dijk - Orbis database, which is searchable by NACE code (4 digits), to collect firms' names (and addresses) and then decide whether to draw a sample from these names or eventually target all of them. I wonder whether Slovak microdata could be used for a better outcome on this point. If you could help me understand this, I can consider applying for the data as well, but at the moment, I am still determining the advantages of this latter sampling method. I have two questions:
     *   Are the accessible microdata anonymised? Could I get the name, address, or other information to reach them out? I suspect not, but I am not 100% sure.
     *   In case data are not anonymised, how are firms classified? Is there a NACE code or other codes that would allow a suitable identification of the music-related firms?

I understand you have finished your budget, but I hope you can address these requests so I can work autonomously with James and possibly a new post-doc. I am adding in cc, Joost as WP1 leader under which the MSME falls.


Best Regards

Arianna
