Hi Marcel,

I was thinking about how we should go forward.  We had this meeting with the Slovak national library, which went in a weird way but with a happy ending, we will sign with them what I wanted.  So this project will go on, but under the current circumstances, I do not want to touch our grant.

I was thinking if you have a discretionary budget -- very small one, maybe 1000 euro -- that I could deliver to you, and not via the EU grant that I promised to you.  I think that it would create a re-incentive for Sinus and EUBA and UTU.  Currently, if I do what I promised to you, they will claim that it was a consortium effort, and I will receive about 15% of the money that is charged to the EU even though I do the entire work.  However, this means that for 15% of the cost, I cloud deliver to you, they would see that they cannot claim anything from the EU, and perhaps that would create a new incentive that they put their resources or at least money into this cooperation.

From a professional point of view, I think that the work would be very solid and now that even the national library is in, I think it will have prestige both in Slovakia and abroad.  I just want to avoid that  questionable EU grant management is connected to it.

Best regards,

Subject: Re: FW: Purchase laptop rules

Hi Fábió,

Unless Balázs or Joost has something in mind, I think that your laptop needs to be very standard, I would maximise built-in memory and a fast SSD drive.  This budget is more than sufficient for that purpose, particularly if you want to go back to using a Microsoft Windows laptop instead of Mac.

I always buy Lenovo, because that is my preferred brand for many years, but from any brand I can help to find you the right configuration.  At least myself, I only use open source software components, so whatever you will use for the sampling and programming will be free to download.  I generally think that people get used to the keyboard of a particular brand and get used to it, in terms of other capabilities, for programming, I think that any brand is great. I use Lenovo because I like their keyboards.

I work with a dual partition Windows laptop, which has a smaller Linux particion. Some web technologies, for example, API connectors, work better on Linux.  This means that I have actually four participations, one for Windows, one for Linux, and a shared one for data and a shared for photos that both the Windows and Linux setup can see.  This is very straightforward to set up this way.  I mainly work in Windows, but if I run into an R package or Java component that is hard to configure in Windows or does not work that well then I boot up the Linux partition.   When you start up or restart your computer you can chose if you want to see the Windows or Linux  configuration with access to your important files from both sides.

Just to check the price range, I randomly chose this&lt;https://www.bol.com/nl/nl/p/lenovo-thinkpad-l14-gen-3-intel-core-i7-1255u-16gb-512-gb-14-full-hd-ips-windows-11-pro-ir-cam/9300000161240283/?Referrer=ADVNLPPcef78e00cdbf929700d6641b2f051126362&amp;utm_source=1126362&amp;utm_medium=Affiliates&amp;utm_campaign=CPS&amp;utm_content=def&gt;:  it a rather pro Lenovo, costs 999 euros, and if you by a few software subscriptions for it (though I guess UvA has Microsoft Office), you will be still in the budget line.  What I would suggest is to either chose something similar to your previous Tilburg laptop, or try out the feel of them.

Best regards,
Daniel

To: Fábio Generoso Vieira &lt;F.V.GenerosoVieira@tilburguniversity.edu&gt;
Subject: Re: FW: Purchase laptop rules

Hi Fábio,

My laptop buying advice is this: try to go for an older model at a vendor that allows you to change the specifications. If you do not use your laptop for gaming or video editing, the latest processor is something that you do not need, but the maximum available memory and a large SSD hard disk is very useful. Usually you get the best deal with a 2 years old model with upgraded specifications.

Installing GitHub is quite straightforward on a new Windows laptop, the only hard part -- but it is always hard -- to set up 2 factor authentication, personal access tokens, and all these security layers.  But you have to do them anyway on any system.

I usually by refurbished computer with a guaranty, because I can ask them to load them up to max memory with  them: https://www.remarkt.nl/, but I think you need a new computer for UvA (though they may not mind.)  Usually you need a specialist laptop vendor that allows you to change the configuration.  If you go to one of them, and not the general stores like MediaMarkt or bol.com&lt;http://bol.com&gt;, and tell them that you are a statistician who writes code, need a large ram and large fast ssd, but no fancy video sound cards and super powerful processor, then they will know what you mean and you will get the best deal.

Few places https://www.pc070.nl/laptop-kopen-den-haag,  https://www.laptop.nl/laptops/alle-laptops/

Let me know if I can help.

Best regards,
Daniel

What I would suggest is to either chose something similar to your previous Tilburg laptop, or try out the feel of them.

Daniel

Hi Fábio,

My laptop buying advice is this: try to go for an older model at a vendor that allows you to change the specifications. If you do not use your laptop for gaming or video editing, the latest processor is something that you do not need, but the maximum available memory and a large SSD hard disk is very useful. Usually you get the best deal with a 2 years old model with upgraded specifications.

Installing GitHub is quite straightforward on a new Windows laptop, the only hard part -- but it is always hard -- to set up 2 factor authentication, personal access tokens, and all these security layers.  But you have to do them anyway on any system.

I usually by refurbished computer with a guaranty, because I can ask them to load them up to max memory with  them: https://www.remarkt.nl/, but I think you need a new computer for UvA (though they may not mind.)  Usually you need a specialist laptop vendor that allows you to change the configuration.  If you go to one of them, and not the general stores like MediaMarkt or bol.com&lt;http://bol.com&gt;, and tell them that you are a statistician who writes code, need a large ram and large fast ssd, but no fancy video sound cards and super powerful processor, then they will know what you mean and you will get the best deal.

Few places https://www.pc070.nl/laptop-kopen-den-haag,  https://www.laptop.nl/laptops/alle-laptops/

Let me know if I can help.

Best regards,
Daniel

## Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;

### OpenMusE short videos {#email-319}

**From:** Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**To:** Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;  
**Cc:** James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;, Ferdinand Hintz &lt;ferdinand.hintz@sinus-institut.de&gt;, Johannes Braunbruck &lt;johannes.braunbruck@synyo.com&gt;, Christoph Steiner &lt;christoph.steiner@synyo.com&gt;  
**Date:** 02/15/2024 13:59:35

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202402151359-OpenMusE short videos-245.txt -->

Hi Daniel,

I hope you're doing fine!

I wanted to contact you concerning an idea for a WP5 activity, that SINUS wanted to explore to counterbalance our previous underspending in WP5.
In a previous project, COVINFORM, we created a series of short videos to highlight best practice examples on how civil society organizations (CSOs) were able to support their communities during the COVID-19 pandemic. The aim of the videos was to reach a different audience (individuals, people that work at CSOs, or NGOs), to complement the series of white papers and policy briefs that we had already published. The videos made quite a positive impression with the EC, which is why we believe that a similar project could be interesting for OpenMusE. To get a first impression on the Covinform videos you can watch them here: Project Videos | COVINFORM&lt;https://www.covinform.eu/project-outputs/project-videos/&gt; (the six videos at the bottom).

For OpenMusE, the idea would be to start with four videos centered around the four goals of our project to support the European music industry in becoming:

  *   More competitive
  *   Fairer
  *   More sustainable
  *   More transparent

We would produce one short video for each topic, highlight the importance of these aspects, and draw attention to our project and the music industry experts within our consortium. To achieve the latter points, we would like to film the videos with some of our partners. As a start, we were thinking about Alona (MEU), Felix (Heardis!), Tomas (SOZA) and Balasz or Ester (Artisjus) but have not contacted them yet.
The videos will be made in a format adapted to current social media practices, i.e. short videos (max 90 Sec.) in a vertical format. This format is especially interesting for social media as it allows us to reach a broad audience outside of your existing followers.

We've briefly discussed the idea with Synyo, who liked it, and would distribute the work as follows: We would produce and cut the videos, and Synyo would create an intro- and/or outro-clip with our logo, help with cutting if needed, and publish the videos. We aim to finish the videos before April and publish them after Easter. All in all, we (SINUS) estimate to spend about 1-2 PMs on this project (the first videos should probably not take more than 1PM).

What do you think about this idea? Does that fit into your plan for the work package and our PM-spend?

We're always happy about constructive feedback and ideas!

Best regards,

Isabella Tautscher

### AW: OpenMusE short videos {#email-320}

**From:** Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**To:** Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;  
**Cc:** James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;, Ferdinand Hintz &lt;ferdinand.hintz@sinus-institut.de&gt;, Johannes Braunbruck &lt;johannes.braunbruck@synyo.com&gt;, Christoph Steiner &lt;christoph.steiner@synyo.com&gt;, Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;, Dr. Kabai Eszter &lt;ekabai@artisjus.com&gt;, Alona Dmukhovska &lt;alona.dmukhovska@gmail.com&gt;, Felix Haaksman &lt;felix.haaksman@heardis.com&gt;  
**Date:** 02/16/2024 09:18:05

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202402160918-AW_ OpenMusE short videos-246.txt -->

Hi Daniel,

Thanks for the quick reply! I understand your concerns, so here’s my suggestion:
Our colleague Ferdinand, who’s currently doing an internship with us, has a background in producing documentary films, which is why we would like to use this extraordinary resource as long as he’s working with us, which would be until end of March 😊

In order to not overpromise, my idea would be to first focus on the “Why”, why should the European music industry become more competitive/fairer/sustainable/transparent? Why is this so important?
This way, we could start a first awareness campaign, without overpromising, and at the same time make sure that we meet our communication goals with the EC.

The other point is, that we can start filming now, but we can choose when we’ll publish the videos. I.e. if in April you believe that it is not yet the right time, we can delay publishing a bit (although preferably only for a couple of weeks, not months).

What do you think? I’d especially like to hear from you, Tomas, Eszter, Alona and Felix, since you’re already in cc 😊 What do you think of this idea?

Thank you very much in advance!

Best regards,

Isabella Tautscher
Research &amp; Consulting
T. +49 175 7661558
&lt;https://www.sinus-institut.de/&gt;
www.sinus-institut.de&lt;https://www.sinus-institut.de/&gt;

Teil der INTEGRAL-SINUS-OPINION Gruppe
Berlin, Heidelberg, Nürnberg, Wien, Singapur

Von: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Gesendet: Donnerstag, 15. Februar 2024 17:01
An: Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Cc: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;; Ferdinand Hintz &lt;ferdinand.hintz@sinus-institut.de&gt;; Johannes Braunbruck &lt;johannes.braunbruck@synyo.com&gt;; Christoph Steiner &lt;christoph.steiner@synyo.com&gt;; Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;; Dr. Kabai Eszter &lt;ekabai@artisjus.com&gt;; Alona Dmukhovska &lt;alona.dmukhovska@gmail.com&gt;; Felix Haaksman &lt;felix.haaksman@heardis.com&gt;
Betreff: Re: OpenMusE short videos

Dear Isabella,

I think that this is a very good idea, and I am putting Alona, Eszter, Tomas, and Felix in CC in my reply.   In my opinion, once this consortium is back on track, we should modify our communication plan to accommodate videos.

At this point, I think we should avoid to get into the same credibility gap that we are now facing in Slovakia, where we signed a ceremonial MoU with the ministry of culture, the statistical office, we held an event of what we will do, we signed up to an international conference to report later the results, and today we are making apology visits to this partners  because the work has not yet started yet.  We have also important stakeholders, whom we contacted when we got the grant, and keep them waiting when this consortium will actually start the work it has a grant agreement for.

In my opinion, we need to find answers why the responsible university did not show up for T1.1.  I indeed took over this work, and did  not yet get compensated, however, by now, I had to just apologies with the ministry and other stakeholders why it is not happening.  Luckily, we did not get that far with T2.1, which also did not happen, but we did not start to communicate it.  Its open policy analysis folder is still open, not a single music organisation has an idea -- even within this consortium -- what kind of data will be collected in terms of diversity and circulation.  The T3.1 folder is also empty and no stakeholder was consulted.  And, as you know, the other univeristy partner for T4.1, which was supposed to write the software that would be collecting the data for this years work, did not show up for task and did not even record a single system requirement, let alone write a line of software code by the deadline in January.  The same university that did not show up for T1.1 failed the Data Management Plan.  I jumped in, too, and delivered it.  Because Sinus accidentally made in sensitive, and did not want to invoke the grant agreement to release this public document, our Consortium actually voted to make it public and start discussing data collection with industry partners. 7 months later, in spite of the Horizon Europe guidelines, the grant agreement and the assembly decision, it is still a secret how we will handle data.

All in all, I would like to protect the professional integrity and standing of the aforementioned people, and suggest that they will be put out in videos when we actually know what this Consortium will do for music, how, and they will not face those awkward situation that we are facing now in Slovakia.

In my opinion, in the next PMB, we should discuss what went down in D1.1, D2.1, D3.1, D4.1, D6.3, and how we can continue the work, and what we will say in the interim review.  Then, when we have actual, actionable proposals, and some results in our open respositories, we can start crafitng messages and find out who is willing to represent them. This way we protect the professional integrity of Felix, Eszter, Tomas, and Alona, and we will not find ourselves in the same credibility gap that we are facing now on Slovakia.

Let's bring this up in the conversation in the PMB!

Best  regards,
Daniel

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;

Subject: Re: Hudobné centrum contract

Hi James,

I appreciate that you are sharing all this with me.  However, I would really like to ask you to think a bit about it from my perspective? Why would I agree to receiving 0.3% of the grant, where currently about 60-70% of all output is Reprex's but only 15% of the money?  Yesterday we made our financial calculation, this project is massively loss making for us.  We do not want more of it, we want less of it.  Last year I would have taken on research data management for 15k, but I already paid out more than that for Istvan to sit in pointless meetings. I took on Fabio's co-supervision for free, and I will try to somehow stay in this after my exit from WP4.1, but we will not enter into any deals that does not increase our share in the grant to 20%. Which would be still a steal for the rest of the consortium seeing our share in the work.

I checked the evaluators profile. Richard and Leo make a gamble.  Though one of the evaluators has a computer science / database expert and music policy degree, they will try to send a non-software as a deliverable. If they get away with this, there will be no deal anyways. If they don't, we will talk about me taking over WP4 with the DMP, and leaving WP5 to Felix or Istvan or Johannes.

I would like to stop any haggling in this project for good, and if there is a deal to be made, I would like to make it with Marc. I think that I could still make this project successful for SINUS as a company and REPREX as a company (and you as a music researcher) but that would require a reset, and dropping all dubious deals.    Because Richard is gambling on this interim review, I think that the time for this will be after the review.

Let us focus on getting things done in Slovakia, that is our only place where we actually do something that brings unquestionable results.

Best regards, Daniel

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&lt;mailto:daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;&gt;
Sent: Wednesday, January 31, 2024 8:42 PM
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt;
Subject: Hudobné centrum contract

Hello James,

I took a day to let yesterday's two meetings, the one in private, and the one in the WP leaders to settle down, and also the previous daylight and nighttime calls.

I will avoid any further conflict with Richard and Leo, provided that they do not put REPREX's name, input, background into any false statements.  If Leo misrepresents the work in 4.1 in any way, like yesterday, I will call him out: he did not write any software, he has absolutely no right to integrate REPREX's software, and he most certainly did not collect requirements from data users or owners.


  *
I can assure you that SINUS will not permit misrepresentations of background or work performed in any official / public documents or discussions.
  *   I was also surprised by, and regret, Leo's phrasing re: the user stories ("we").
  *   However, it is our duty as coordinator to take the most charitable interpretation of each partner. In this case this means that as Leo stated in response to your protest, by "we", he meant the WP4 team. However skeptical I may be, personally, I must take on a neutral expression during the discussion.
  *
I can assure you that it is on record that REPREX initiated the usability requirements elicitation process (despite SINUS requests to UTU to do this throughout Q2 and Q3 2023). All other WP leaders know this, and if anyone implies otherwise, they will merely be embarrassing themselves.

Apart from that, I think that the fact that Richard never created a task-level resource plan is good for now, because REPREX will allocate all its resources in WP4 to T4.2 and UTU can keep T4.1 100% to its own; just the way Richard can keep the data management.


  *   To clarify, it was never Richard's job to create a task-level resource plan per WP: this is something we asked the WP leaders to initiate, and which nobody has done so far.
  *   To further clarify, Richard is not the DMP task leader, rather SSSA (Dr. Denise Amram). As noted in our bilateral call, I have assisted SSSA in putting together a list of data sources that we may utilise, however, each partner that generates data must still catalogue their data assets in compliance with DMP standards. Most partners will require technical assistance for this.
  *   Earlier, we discussed a post-Interim Review swap of T4.1 to REPREX and T4.2 to UTU; I would like to keep this on the table, depending on how the discussion goes on the proposed PM transfers within UTU (6 to 12PM to Prof. Cloonan for a Live Music Census) and from UTU to UVA (6PM for Fabio) and REPREX (2 to 4PM for yet-unspecified programming tasks).

I would like to find how we could work in a more fruitful way in this project if you remain in the Coordinator's role, and I would also like to reach out to Marc Calmbach, because in case you leave, I think that this project will sink to an even lower chance of success.


  *   I am yet undecided on this. It is a difficult decision for a number of reasons.
  *   Keep this to yourself for now. It is highly sensitive and your discretion is appreciated.
  *
Hold off on reaching out to Marc. If it becomes necessary, I will initiate this conversation and involve you when the timing is right.
  *
Trust me on this. I know the parties involved and am confident that I can frame whatever decision I take as a win-win – but it is delicate.
  *
No matter where I am based, I will continue to contribute to the project to at least the same extent as now.
  *

The Balkam Museum Network is organizing a webinar on Metadata in Museum Collections on Tuesday 13th February, 14:00 - 16:30 CET.

From: Andreas Schönrock &lt;andreas.schoenrock@heardis.com&gt;

Subject: CfP IASPM D-A-CH Conference 2024

Dear OpenMusE Consortium,

please have a look at the Call for Papers for the upcoming biennial conference of the IASPM D-A-CH-branch in Zurich. It might be of interest for disseminating your activities within the OpenMusE project or your other academic ventures. Either way, the Call is open until February 15.

Many thanks and my best,

Andreas

The German-speaking branch of the International Association for the Study of Popular Music is pleased to announce its biennial conference, which will take place at the University of Zurich from 07-09 November 2024.

Call for Papers
Metadata | Meta information
Popular Music and its Metamorphoses.

In recent years, the term metadata has evolved from a technical IT term to a commonplace and buzzword referring to fundamental cultural semantics and technological dynamics of the present - also and particularly regarding popular music. In the context of digital systems, machine learning (AI), ubiquitous internet availability in the global North, streaming possibilities, etc., “data about data” and the labelling of other data are of considerable importance for the infrastructures of popular music. At the same time, they also affect the production side because genre boundaries and other conventions are shifting - and act as a heuristic starting point for attempts to intellectually explore and criticise respective processes. Streaming services and their music recommendation algorithms are a prime example for the current significance of metadata. Musicologists and scholars of cultural studies have recently increasingly studied such digital systems and their effects. Both ethnographically and using quantitative methods, substantial insights have been gained into the technical (infra)structures, ideologies, and redistribution effects in the environment of platform capitalism - although many (research) questions remain unanswered.

Given the conjuncture of metadata - as a phenomenon, as a term - and, more generally, of those phenomena labelled as “meta”, socio-technical constellations, shaping the current production, circulation, and reception of popular music in a particular way, become tangible. Labelling as “meta” (metadata - but also, for example, metatags, metatrend, metamaterial or even the renaming of the Facebook umbrella company to meta) also evokes a zeitgeisty ambiguity and vagueness. “Meta-” is therefore at least as much a phenomenon of the cultural imaginary as of technological materiality. As the leitmotif of the conference, "meta" (in the sense of the ambiguous Greek prefix μετά) refers to that which lies beyond the audible aspects of popular music, that which accompanies it, that which exists in the spaces in between.

The conference will therefore focus not only on metadata and metatags in digital systems, but also on other meta information of popular music: although audible materiality - referring to affordance theory - offers reference points for extra-musical attributions of meaning, the conference will focus on aspects of popular music that go beyond sound. Popular music is inevitably linked to its spatio-temporal context; it unfolds in the coordinate system of socio-cultural, economic, ecological, media, technological and political axes. It is characterised by the multidirectional flow between different sources of information. Popular music's meta information such as artist images, genre classifications, performative qualities, fashion, design, charts positions, marketing-related communication, social symbols, lifestyle-related codes etc. therefore also enables us to explore the current expansion and concentration of the multi-layered reference system surrounding popular music cultures. The prefix additionally describes change, the alteration of a state, e.g. in the sense of metamorphosis. It references the constant flux of the content labelled as popular music, but also the fundamentally dynamic nature of its forms and the fluidity of its production and reception.

We look forward to contributions from academics, artists, journalists, and practitioners on the conference theme and welcome both thematically and formally free submissions dealing with relevant questions on popular music cultures. The latter will be considered within the time frame of the conference.

Exemplary topics

Metadata

  *   Metadata in music platforms (streaming, alternative platforms, shops)
  *   Classification of popular music in digital systems (genre classifications, moods, contextual classification, classification methods, etc.)
  *   Copyright in digital systems (royalty assignment, CMO’s, General Data Protection Regulations, systematics etc.)
  *   Findability of music in digital systems and recommendation algorithms
  *   Bias in digital systems (gender and race imbalance, success parameters, etc.)
  *   MIR (Music Information Retrieval) and AI in digital systems
  *   Power relationships in digital systems (Who has the power to decide on terminology? Who defines methods? Who possesses respective tools?)
  *   Data management and transparency (Who has access to which data? Who has the power of disposal over metadata?)
  *   Digital humanities topics in the context of music-related metadata
  *   Metadata in and from popular music studies (e.g. coding interviews, dealing with AI, MIR, ML etc.)
  *   …

Meta information

  *   Interconnections between popular music and fashion, design etc.
  *   Memes, TikTok and their non-musical reference systems
  *   Artist images, music press and magazines, blogs, websites etc.
  *   Advertising industry, brands and music industry (music in commercials, brand collaborations with artists, brand presence at music events, artist communication and marketing, etc.)
  *   Genre classifications and further categorisation of popular music forms (e.g. context-related playlists)
  *   Physicality/corporality in popular music (e.g. communication through performative qualities)
  *   Social symbols and lifestyle-related codes (subcultures, distinction from others, layers of meaning)
  *   Interactions of meta information and content transfer by recipients (e.g. influencing variables on image generation, categorisation of recipients, transfer of non-musical qualities to musical content, etc.)
  *   Hierarchies and relationships between human and non-human entities and information
  *   …


Metamorphoses

  *   Production and texture of popular music forms
  *   Influence of metadata and meta information on the construction of meaning in the reception of popular music and changing reception environments
  *   Changes in the audible content subsumed under the term popular music over time and reflection with regard to associated meta information and holistic contextual variables
  *   Artistic research (e.g. exploring the influence of meta information on the production processes of popular music or critical reflection on its production and communication)
  *   Critical evaluation of established paradigms in popular music cultures and popular music studies
  *   Changes in the medial functionality of popular music within the context of predominantly digital reference systems
  *   …

We particularly encourage contributions on all these topics addressing power structures and effects and, for example, questions of transnational inequality research, gender and sexuality studies or racism research. As an explicitly interdisciplinary conference, researchers from all disciplines working in the broad field of popular music studies are invited to present current research.

Contributions can be submitted in German or English in the following formats:

  *   Individual papers (30 minutes presentation &amp; 15 minutes discussion),
  *   Panels (min. three presentations on a common topic, total 60 minutes presentations &amp; 30 minutes discussion).

Participation in the conference is free for members of all IASPM branches and students/lecturers of the University of Zurich and the University of Bern. The following participation fees apply to all other participants (to be paid by invoice/bank transfer after registration):

  *   Full conference: 100.00 CHF
  *   Thursday, 07.11.2024: 40.00 CHF
  *   Friday, 08.11.2024: 40.00 CHF
  *   Saturday, 09.11.2024: 30.00 CHF

IASPM membership is not required to submit a paper or panel.

The publication of individual contributions as part of the IASPM D-A-CH ~Vibes series is intended.

Submissions must contain the following information:

  *   Paper and/or panel title
  *   Abstract (or individual papers max. 300 words, excluding references to the authors of the abstracts; for panels max. 300 words on the panel topic and max. 200 each on the papers)
  *   Five Keywords
  *   Name, contact information and institutional affiliation if applicable
  *   Short biography (max. 150 words)
  *   Apply for travel grant yes/no (see below)

Please submit your proposals online using our form&lt;https://forms.gle/pAT4AxNSXwCMfE3f6&gt; by 15 February 2024 at the latest.

The evaluation and selection of the anonymised contributions will be carried out by the executive committee and advisory board of IASPM D-A-CH as well as the conference steering committee. We will endeavour to provide you with feedback by April 2024 at the latest.

Contacts: Andreas Schoenrock&lt;mailto:andreas.schoenrock@hkb.bfh.ch&gt;; Moritz Ege&lt;mailto:moritz.ege@uzh.ch&gt;

We are planning to provide travel and accommodation reimbursement or grants for presenting IASPM-D-A-CH members, provided that third-party funding is available. We furthermore intend to reimburse students for travel and accommodation expenses if they produce a conference report (text and/or audio/visual/audiovisual formats are possible).

Looking forward to your submissions and fruitful discussions in Zurich,

Andreas Schoenrock (MAS Popular Music, University of the Arts Bern)
Britta Sweers (Institute of Musicology, University of Bern)
Inga Mai Groote (Institute of Musicology, University of Zurich)
Moritz Ege (Department of Social Anthropology and Cultural Studies, University of Zurich)

Hello OpenMusE colleagues,

I hope you are well!

I'm writing with regard to the general population survey that is planned in OpenMusE WP3 (see Slide 23 in the attached presentation). As I'm thrilled to remind you, we have enough fieldwork budget to conduct a high-quality survey in at least four countries, in either Q1 2024 or Q1 2025 (depending on your needs).

One aim of the survey is to answer research questions on music audiences: e.g., how do people interact with music, how does it contribute to their well-being, etc. However, arguably the more important aim is to fill data gaps relevant to music economics. Examples are:

  *   Valuation: how much do people report using music and spending on music in different channels?
  *   Informal employment: how many people earn some income from activities related to music?
Because the survey will be representative, the data we gather from the sample should be generalisable to the total population. We are aware that self-reported data on consumer behaviour is not as reliable as business intelligence data; however, in some cases, it may be the only data available.

ARTISJUS and SOZA: this is nothing new to you, as one purpose of the CEEMID surveys you conducted with REPREX was to provide such data. We would like to build on the foundation laid in CEEMID. I will be working with Daniel on this, and have requested from him the CEEMID survey questionnaires and relevant metadata (on universe and scope, response rate, sampling procedure, mode of collection, data collector, data collection period).

However, as Daniel's resource commitment in this WP is limited, I would like to work with you directly as well. I have experience designing and running population surveys on a high level (e.g., for German ministries and foundations), including surveys on music for the European Commission and the Max Planck Institute. However, I have not conducted a population survey specifically to answer music industry business needs. So, two opening requests for input are:

  *   What is your "survey wish list", i.e., what data needs in your organisation do you think a general population survey might help fill? Think back to CEEMID, but also give some thought beyond it.
  *   Are you aware of any dependencies that should be taken into account when deciding whether to survey your country in 2024 vs. 2025? @Rosina Petrova&lt;mailto:rosina_petrova@musicautor.org&gt;, here I am thinking of your comment in the Bratislava workshop that administrative data you will draw on in valuation are only available in Q3 of each year (and thus if we survey Bulgaria in Q1 2025, it might be too late to integrate the survey and administrative data by the time the project ends).
  *   For CEEMID partners: would you consider providing access to your CEEMID findings to the consortium, either at the aggregated level or the microdata level, and under what conditions?
My schedule this week is very flexible -- I would be happy to continue the conversation by email, phone, or both.

Thank you for your time, and best regards,
James

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202402211951-Re_ OpenMUSE D4.1 reporting plan-420.txt -->

Hi Daniel,

I am 100% agnostic on the use of the term "ecosystem" in the deliverable or any reporting.

In fact, I deeply dislike the use of this word in contexts other than systems ecology and social-ecological systems analysis. It has become so widely used as to be meaningless.

Dropping this word would not solve the bigger problem of ensuring we have software that can concretely benefit our data providers and data users. However, if minimising its use in the deliverable would ease tension, I will not object.

Best regards,
James

Hi James,



@Daniel Antal&lt;mailto:daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;, I assume it is OK if your name appears as "aut" / "cre" on references to packages you have authored and "ctb" on references to packages to which you have contributed..?

I did not contribute to any UTU packages since 2022, nor have they.  There is not ctb to report. The work I did in this project was solely attributed to me.


Regarding the "software ecosystem" as a whole: given the way the work has unfolded, our "software ecosystem" is not an entity per se, but a set of affordances and potential interactions (much like a natural ecosystem). It has no single "author" or "creator". Only the individual packages do.

I do not recall if you were present in the call when Leo advised Richard and me to add this phrase to the task list to keep pesky deliverable evaluators at bay, but in retrospect I also made a mistake that I did not protest. I think that this was a highly unethical framing of the work, and I will present a GA modification suggestion to the PMB to remove these words from the task list.

In the meantime, as I have earlier stated, there is a conflict of interest between UTU, REPREX, and other consortium members who would need to use the software in 1.2, 2.2, 3.2, 4.2, 5.1, because the software does not exists, and that negatively affects the deliveries, costs, and success of other consortium members. In my opinion, the ecosystem you mention is purely fictitious, it does not exist, and does not fulfill the aims of the grant agreement. If I am wrong, I need to be persuaded.

My work is visible for the PO because all my contributions follow the OPA, the Horizon Guidelines and the DMP, and they are on OpenAIRE. So there is no problem with that. However, it would be a misrepresentation of my work if it would be added to an "ecosystem" in a way that exaggerates the connection of these software elements, or their relevance to this project, or anyhow deceives the evaluators or other consortium members. My work, either in the foreground or the background, is not part of any UTU-defined software ecosystem, and I will object to any such misrepresentation.

Regarding the submitted PDF, the decision as to whether to appear on the author list is entirely yours. Let us know on the day of submission and we can add or remove your name.

Depending on how much the PDF resolves my earlier ethical complaint and the conflict of interests, my name may appear as author, or may be omitted. However, I will formalise my ethical complaint if there is any misrepresentation of my work in the PDF.

Daniel

We have both run dozens of surveys before and are used to the process of client alignment.

However, the above two points would be incredibly helpful.

I do not know how specific Istvan eventually was with Richard, but we think that we seriously overspent last year by working on other organisations tasks, and we also have a risk that we have to create a new data management plan to make the OMO work. I suggested for Istvan to indicate a 100-120,000 budgetary adjustment request for Richard, and this is what we want to take to the PMB as well.

If we see that the partners we helped out are acknowledging or help and we get a compensation for stepping in – and frankly saving a grant that anyways mainly we got for them – then we are happy to help with tasks to some degree.

Arianna is planning to write you an email that elaborates on the Orbis contents (as I have seen it on her screen but personally don't have access).

I think that we have already given up on T2.1 but pro forma the WP2 should exist and should do something towards the grant agreement.  Regarding the DMP, I will put it on the agenda of the PMB again, because the General Assembly decisions were never implemented, and the current state of the data management of the consortium is not satisfactory.

Currently, Reprex has access to data - for example, microdata in Slovakia - but the Consortium does not have access to data. The consortium has a DMP that nobody uses, and Reprex started to build its own data management plan, because it will actually manage data, but at this point, not for the consortium. It would be a win-win if we could work on behalf of the consortium, because in that case the consortium would have data access.



Thank you and best regards,
James


I was on the IDCC24 this week and  it was extremely useful – I think that the Digital Music Observatory will be recognised as a platform that works together with some statistical authorities, the EU Open Data portal, music organisations, libraries, and Wikipedia. We will have a machine-actionable data plan that will allow OpenAIRE, the Open Data portal to automatically retrieve our datasets or recommend them on their platforms. We will be officially a research repository, and will now longer rely on Zenodo. And we will have a governance model that follows the latest EU recommendations and perhaps even the large players like CISAC will come around. Yet, at this point, I do not see how anything will get into the OMO part of the DMO, i.e., the pillars that are supposed to financed from this grant.

The D5.1 will be a presentable and successful deliverable, but when we will send it to review for the EU, it will be also empty. The DMO itself will at one point it will have data, but not from OpenMuse partners, and often without even access for OpenMuse partners.  I hope that the PMB will understand that this is less then optimal: we received 3 million euros to fill up an observatory and it will be filled up by others.

Reprex is hiring 4 new team members this week, and we are building parallel to our music observatory a film observatory, too. To me, it would be sensible to take over at least the data management of the consortium from SSSA, and perhaps a part of UTUs work to actually write some code that will process some data for the consortium. At this point, I cannot imagine that UTU will ever be allowed to process music data, or to create any dataset that meets the requirements of the observatory. However, with a small budgetary allocation Reprex could fill up the OMO with actual data that meets the requirements set by actual international stakeholders. If we would get the 6.3 budget and a half of the T1.1 budget you would have a very successful project. Of course, it could have some surveys, too, both retrospectively processed and new ones. To me, processing the KULT surveys would not be such a great cost, I already have a microdata agreement, and a survey harmonisation program.

Best regards,
Daniel

Please indicate your availabilities in this doodle poll&lt;https://dud-poll.inf.tu-dresden.de/openmuse-pmb05/&gt; until Thursday, 22 February the latest.

I am aware that the week from 11 March to 15 March will be densely packed for some of us, since UVA is also running the project’s stakeholder workshop on the 14th, but this is simply the challenge we have to deal with.


  *   Attendance for the PMB meeting is compulsory for all task and WP leaders (UVA, SSSA, MIH, SOZA, UTU, REPREX, SYNYO, HEARDIS, SINUS) and this time I would also ask EUBA to be present. For all other partners this meeting is voluntary, but highly recommended.
WP leaders please have your Review Meeting slides ready (15mins + 10m Q&amp;A per WP), because this meeting will for the most part consist of a test run for the meeting with the EC (Mon, 18 March)


  *   Attendance for the EC Review meeting on 18 March is compulsory for all partners (one person per partner minimum, all WP and task leaders, coordinator team).

Looking forward to seeing you all soon.

Cheers,
Richard

Dear Richard,

I would like to know what is the cut off date for PMB agenda point suggestions. Given that the last PMB did not make a single decision, and the General Assembly decisions were not implemented, I think that apart from the review meeting, there will be a lot of agenda points that have piled up since June.  My first suggestion will be procedural, I will ask to agree on a procedure that every agenda point ends with a formal vote.  If there is no decision taken, then the PMB members explicitly vote if they received satisfactory information under that agenda point or not.

I would like to suggest agenda points to the tasks where I am involved, either because I had to take them over from somebody, or because my next task cannot start because of the delay of another task. In these cases,  I will ask for a decision from the PMB, or a vote if they agree with the explanation heard.

I think it would be also more efficient and professional if each agenda point would have a half page or a page of written information received before the meeting, so that notetaking is easier, and people can ask their questions more pointedly.

Please let me know what is the deadline for these agenda points.

Best regards,
Daniel

Hi Istvan,

Heike and I were not available on Friday (and Heike will be back in office tomorrow only) which is why we originally asked to talk to you last Wednesday or Thursday. Unfortunately, your email only came in past that window on Thursday evening.

For clarification as you asked: my text talked about the PM budget, i.e., 62 PMs in REPREX’ case. Obviously, project work cannot be expected to be distributed a hundred percent evenly over the three years, but a default expectation of a reviewer might nevertheless well be the consumption of something closer to 21 PMs for REPREX during the first year. Hence my request for a clarifying statement to avoid such impression of underspending from the get-go.

As for the argumentation of the 68% labour cost increase, I personally find the currently given reason from your email not convincing enough and I doubt the PO and the reviewers (and ultimately the auditor at project end) will be satisfied with it. I therefore want to renew my former request and urge you that REPREX either bring down for the Periodic Report their monthly average to something somehow close to the 5790 EUR rate that went into the project calculation or come up with a sufficiently convincing argument.

Thanks and cheers,
Richard

From: Istvan Burus &lt;istvan.burus@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Thursday, 22 February 2024 18:19
To: Richard Wages &lt;Richard.Wages@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Cc: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;; Heike Kuchheuser &lt;Heike.Kuchheuser@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Subject: Re: OpenMusE // ECAS entries for Review, please finish by Fri, 23. February the latest


Hi Richard,


Please find our replies below along with a reiteration of some of our concerns in this matter that haven't been properly addressed at least since early August. I am available to discuss this tomorrow.


I.) For the periodic report


1) Financial statement.


·     REPREX has used LESS than 1/3 of their PM budget in 2023 which might be interpreted as underspending by the EC. Please prepare a short statement on whether or not this actually is to be seen as underspending (eg, bulk of work towards 2nd half of project) and send it to Richard for the Periodic Report until 23 February the latest.

Reprex used 34.6% of its budget allocated to personnel costs in 2023, that's slightly more than 1/3 of our budget. Please clarify what you mean by underspending and what's required from us in this regard.

Furthermore, according to our resource plan, we overspend heavily, considering we took over tasks originally planned to be performed by others. Therefore in the period we were mainly working on tasks of other partners, not on our own tasks. This means that we are in fact considerably above our originally planned budget.

·     The stated numbers of PMs and labour costs currently yield an average monthly rate which is some 68% higher than the proposal estimate. Given REPREX’ large budget share the PO and the reviewers will see this as unsustainable

·     Hence, we will either need a decrease of the monthly rate or a REPREX-internal statement which explains why this rate is (a) justified and (b) how REPREX plans to be able to fulfill their contractual workload of 62 PMs by the end of the project.


The work carried out by Reprex in the first reporting period required the involvement of senior colleagues with a relatively low person month total. It must be recognised that it requires seniority to take over entire tasks from other organisations, like we did in 6.3 and 1.1, or to leapfrog 2.2 because 2.1 is late or missing. Similarly, working out the exploitation pathways of the project for D5.2 required senior involvement as well.

Reprex's activities in the second and third year of the project, however, will also require the involvement of junior colleagues in particular in data related tasks with a lower monthly rate. This will result in a decrease of the average monthly rate of Reprex for the remainder of the project, the degree of which will depend on to what extent involvement of senior colleagues will still be required. As in our understanding Daniel will be expected to supervise junior staff outside of Reprex as well, some further overspending of senior hours can still be expected.

Generally, at this point we estimate that Reprex will require more than 62 PMs in total to finish the tasks that were originally planned to be carried out by us, after devoting more time than expected on other tasks .


2)      Researchers involved in the project


The list of researchers is up to date as of now. As for Gabija, Reprex has not allocated any of her hours to OpenMuse. As for the other colleagues, Reprex still plans to involve them in later project activities. We are also in the process of contracting other new people not yet included, but they can be only released to this project if the tasks are properly managed and their involvement (together with their supervisor's time commitments) can be well planned.
_ _



It is important to note that we have repeatedly indicated the misalignment of Reprex's budget with the tasks that have shifted to Reprex in the first reporting period. I've sent a detailed breakdown and forecast of Reprex's efforts dedicated to the project to James on August 7. This email explained clearly how Daniel's larger than planned involvement in Tasks 1.1 and 6.3 in particular results in a higher average monthly rate for Reprex for the reporting period, as well as a delay in the involvement of junior colleagues.


This misalignment will still have to be addressed to ensure that carrying out all planned project tasks are sustainable. However, this requires corrective action on the consortium level. We are looking forward to increasing the Reprex budget by about 20%, understanding the current skills gaps of our consortium and that we had to spend in 2023 mainly on unplanned activities. Based on Reprex’s deliveries to the Sinus Cloud and to OpenAIRE, we believe that it should be clear that our workload is higher than the ~15% budget allocation to Reprex.


Best regards,


Istvan

&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; music organisations who are contemplating to leave the consortium, because
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; they feel left out and they think that the university partners who fail to
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; whatever they promised to backroom deals with Sinus, while the General
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; Assembly decisions are not implemented and the last PMB did not even take
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; decisions. I.e., the decision-making bodies of the consortium are empted.
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; Unfortunately, I think that Richard has similar plans, i.e,  he
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; placed the PMB as close to the interim review as possible and wants to
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; spend the time instead of a PMB with a practice of presentations.  I will
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; speak up against this, because this is not the role of the PMB.  What made
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; me decide to go into this direction is the latest D4.1 deliverable of the
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; software ecosystem. It misrepresented Reprex's pre--grant work as if it was
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; UTU's software ecosystem, which consists of exactly zero software elements,
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; and reported ready -- meaning that all the subsequents tasks would have to
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; work with no software even though they should have data collection software
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; ready.  Also, the consortium currently manages zero data, even though it is
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; supposed to be a data collection and dissemination consortium.  I will try
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; to press the coordinator into the direction that they take aside the
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; unspent money from last year for these granted goals, because in the
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; absence of data and data management tools, we can only pretend that this
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; consortium does anything -- no results can be disseminated or communicated,
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; and no subsequent tasks can be implemented.
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt; Best regards,
&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;&gt;

Dear all,

Thank you very much for filling in the doodle. The date and time, where most PMB members are present, is March 28th, from 14:00 to 17:00. I will send out a teams invitation after this e-mail.

Following Caterina’s suggestion, the aim of this meeting is to go through each work package, and each task within each WP, and discuss:

  *   what were the task objectives,
  *   what has been achieved so far, and how this complies with the task objectives,
  *   what should have been done by other partners, but was covered/taken over by someone else,
  *   and what still needs to be done, and by whom?

In order to prepare for this meeting, it was further agreed that:

  *   SINUS will send the current draft version of the technical report with the inputs by the partners and the PM distribution per WP (see attachments),
  *   each task leader will prepare a written summary for their task and coordinates with their WP leaders,
  *   all WP leaders will share a final summary of their WP with the consortium. This should happen min. 2-3 working days before the meeting on March 28 to give the other partners time to react.
  *   each WP leader will present their WP summary during the next PMB meeting; the presentations should not take more than 15 minutes per WP to leave time for discussion.

Please note that the current version still describes ongoing disagreements. However, we are hopeful that they will be solved by the involved partners before the GA, and that the technical report will be modified accordingly.

We are looking forward to a productive meeting!

Best regards,

Hi Isabella,

1. I would like you to add for the record the fact that this was an extraordinary PMB requested by REPREX, and the agenda suggested by REPREX was not followed or even allowed to the vote.  This part of the memo is missing.

2. I would also like to add that we have requested access to Richard's accusatory presentation, the names of the EC officers who were allegedly consulted, and the fact that we disagreed with the presentation.

3. Istvan's words about consortium agreement;  "Istvan: it is not reasonable to do it now and not fair; REPREX already submitted in February" , for clarity, please add that we are referring to February 2023, as the work should not have started without the background declaration. [Since that time we have tried to have our background added several times, including this year.]

4. The part about 4.1 is completely confusing and does not follow what happened.

This part omits I think several minutes and it is confusing  Daniel: REPREX needs to leave the Call (no reason mentioned) and questions can be asked; Richard: I recommend to take 4.1 off the net; Daniel: Content

The fact is that Reprex never saw the D4.1 which was delivered with a significant delay and I have no recollection of seeing it online, although it should be online, so this whole take down of 4.1 is a misunderstanding, this was not the document that Richard wanted off.

The document that Richard wanted to take off, but it was not possible, was Reprex's submission was discussed in the WP leader's meeting, and after being criticized for not having the consortium logos, was uploaded with the consortium logos. This is what Richard called in the missing part of the memo a "surprise deliverable".  Because UTU was not ready with any submissible document by the deadline, Reprex prepared a document that could have been submitted. When the decision was taken by the Coordinator not to submit Reprex's 4.1 document, it was uploaded as Reprex's contribution to the then non-existing deliverable. A new version - upon request now - was uploaded this time without the consortium logos.   https://zenodo.org/records/10804036

The text also incorrectly mentions that there was no funding information on the document, which I explained why was a misunderstanding, as all our artefacts have a machine-readable and human readable form of the official funding statement, in fact, they are linked to the grant agreement automatically.  If you want to rework this part, please let me know if I can help.

We will send a revised background version of the many times submitted background agian on Monday.

Have a nice weekend,
Daniel

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202403211609-Re_ 2nd extraordinary meeting of the PMB - PMB06-424.txt -->

Dear Consortium partners,



I hope you are well. I am writing to pass along our suggested agenda for the second extraordinary PMB called for on Thursday 28 March 2024:

  1.  SINUS will open the PMB and present the agenda (15 min).
  2.  WP presentations on tasks and their status quo (15 min per WP -- 90 min total).
  3.  REPREX will present ideas to reshape the work plan incl. discussion (30 min).
  4.  Discussion on steps to be taken leading to General Assembly on April 4th (30 min).
  5.  Closing notes by the coordinator (15 min).

We expect all partners to remain in the meeting for its full duration. We place the WP presentations prior to the REPREX presentation because our communications with partners suggest that there is still no common understanding of where each WP is and what each WP leader hopes to do. Without such a common understanding, suggestions for how to pivot would likely just provoke more confusion. As Richard is sick, I will moderate the meeting and Marc will act as SINUS representative.



I will close this brief email by putting to rest an allegation. Hopefully you have all read the Interim Report. It is a purely technical document. Assuming all partner inputs are credible and imply a feasible path forward for the project, it is not hard to write.



The allegation that SINUS reached out to the Project Officer and postponed the Interim Report and Review because our team could not string together this simple document is fantasy. We did so because in our assessment, the last-minute inputs provided by REPREX were not credible, and roadblocked the feasible path forward that the Report and Review must present.



The REPREX inputs furthermore implied that unless SINUS somehow magically resolved tensions between REPREX and other partners by 3 March, these tensions would be aired in front of the EC officers and experts. Anyone with a modicum of experience in EU projects could tell you that this would have been a disaster.



In summation: I was there during SINUS preparations for the interim review, while REPREX was not. Anyone can speculate about how these preparations went down, but such idle speculations will not be entertained during the meeting, nor in future emails. This is our last word on the matter.



Hopefully, we can take this as a pivot point toward a more constructive and meaningful discussion on 28 March.



Thank you all, and best regards,

James

### OpenMusE conduct {#email-358}

**From:** James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**To:** Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;  
**Date:** 03/21/2024 16:10:50

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202403211610-OpenMusE conduct-425.txt -->

Daniel,



I returned to work yesterday and went through the PMB minutes, as well as the record of communications leading up to the PMB. I am disappointed and embarrassed. I will here note that Marc was also disappointed and embarrassed, particularly by your attempt to shift blame for the project delay, as well as for your conflicts with other partners, to our team. Such distraction manouevers can only further poison the REPREX-SINUS relationship going forward. Do not engage in them again.



A personal note. It was ludicrous of you to ask SINUS to resolve your conflicts with SSSA and UTU within a few days, and to do so on the day after my last working day prior to three weeks of personal leave. You were well aware that this leave was not a normal holiday, but rather a long-planned trip to deal with my parents' estate. You were well aware that I would be dealing with intensive logistical and emotional burdens immediately upon arrival. You nevertheless implied that I should set everything aside and help you mediate your frankly childish conflicts, with partners that you onboarded to the project in the first place, from a different time zone, while jet-lagged.



To be frank: I have gotten used to unprofessional and disrespectful behaviour by you, but this set a new low bar. I will not tolerate such behaviour going forward.



These topics will not be discussed on 28 March. The meeting will focus solely on building a credible path forward on which all impacted partners can reach consensus, and which can be presented to the General Assembly on 4 April.



In closing: apparently you have been working behind the scenes with UVA and the CMOs to develop a "solution" to the WP4 problems without involving Leo. When planning your proposed amendments, do involve all impacted partners. Otherwise, there is unlikely to be consensus and the amendments are likely to fail the vote in the GA, and/or to be rejected by the Project Officer. This is a recipe for disaster and wasted time by all, not least you.



James

He refused to the documents with the PMB members, then, as if this was his original PMB, neglected the extraordinary PMB agenda, and went out on highly personal rant against Reprex in front of about 10 perplexed people.  With Istvan we hardly spoke in the entire process. Given that I called the extraordinary PMB for 75 minutes, and even my agenda points were not allowed on the vote, they were neglected, and I did not even get the word in 75 minutes, I left, and Istvan took notes.  We received the document that would have been discussed on the extraordinary PMB 3 days after the PMB.

After this terrible PMB, where I was not the only one to find the conduct of the coordinator unacceptable, I sat down with Joost, Tomas and Eszter to discuss next steps.   Perhaps it would be wise to join in that conversation after the next PMB.  I do not wish to have any further conversation outside of the PMB, because I think that the way this project is managed is way off the Grant and Consortium Agreement.  In the PMB,

Best regards,
Daniel

Hello James,

Perhaps one thing that everybody agrees is that currently there is no trust in the consortium to go on with business as usual.  I think that it would be a good idea to plan this forthcoming PMB a bit differently and allow time first of all for me to reflect off the record to the long lists of accusations from the last one and offer my apologies where it is due, and then to open the discussion with a much broader canvas.  We can no longer pretend that these work packages are on track, or will necessarily pass an interim review, therefore a more productive meeting would be needed than the business as usual.

If there would be a short call about just making the next PMB more productive after the last one, I would try to make time for it.

Best regards

Daniel

On Thu, Mar 21, 2024 at 4:09 PM James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt; wrote:

Dear Consortium partners,



I hope you are well. I am writing to pass along our suggested agenda for the second extraordinary PMB called for on Thursday 28 March 2024:

  1.  SINUS will open the PMB and present the agenda (15 min).
  2.  WP presentations on tasks and their status quo (15 min per WP -- 90 min total).
  3.  REPREX will present ideas to reshape the work plan incl. discussion (30 min).
  4.  Discussion on steps to be taken leading to General Assembly on April 4th (30 min).
  5.  Closing notes by the coordinator (15 min).

We expect all partners to remain in the meeting for its full duration. We place the WP presentations prior to the REPREX presentation because our communications with partners suggest that there is still no common understanding of where each WP is and what each WP leader hopes to do. Without such a common understanding, suggestions for how to pivot would likely just provoke more confusion. As Richard is sick, I will moderate the meeting and Marc will act as SINUS representative.



I will close this brief email by putting to rest an allegation. Hopefully you have all read the Interim Report. It is a purely technical document. Assuming all partner inputs are credible and imply a feasible path forward for the project, it is not hard to write.



The allegation that SINUS reached out to the Project Officer and postponed the Interim Report and Review because our team could not string together this simple document is fantasy. We did so because in our assessment, the last-minute inputs provided by REPREX were not credible, and roadblocked the feasible path forward that the Report and Review must present.



The REPREX inputs furthermore implied that unless SINUS somehow magically resolved tensions between REPREX and other partners by 3 March, these tensions would be aired in front of the EC officers and experts. Anyone with a modicum of experience in EU projects could tell you that this would have been a disaster.



In summation: I was there during SINUS preparations for the interim review, while REPREX was not. Anyone can speculate about how these preparations went down, but such idle speculations will not be entertained during the meeting, nor in future emails. This is our last word on the matter.



Hopefully, we can take this as a pivot point toward a more constructive and meaningful discussion on 28 March.



Thank you all, and best regards,

James

I think that it would be a good idea to plan this forthcoming PMB a bit differently and allow time first of all for me to reflect off the record to the long lists of accusations from the last one and offer my apologies where it is due, and then to open the discussion with a much broader canvas.  We can no longer pretend that these work packages are on track, or will necessarily pass an interim review, therefore a more productive meeting would be needed than the business as usual.

If there would be a short call about just making the next PMB more productive after the last one, I would try to make time for it.

Best regards

Daniel



On Thu, Mar 21, 2024 at 4:09 PM James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt; wrote:

Dear Consortium partners,



I hope you are well. I am writing to pass along our suggested agenda for the second extraordinary PMB called for on Thursday 28 March 2024:

  1.  SINUS will open the PMB and present the agenda (15 min).
  2.  WP presentations on tasks and their status quo (15 min per WP -- 90 min total).
  3.  REPREX will present ideas to reshape the work plan incl. discussion (30 min).
  4.  Discussion on steps to be taken leading to General Assembly on April 4th (30 min).
  5.  Closing notes by the coordinator (15 min).

We expect all partners to remain in the meeting for its full duration. We place the WP presentations prior to the REPREX presentation because our communications with partners suggest that there is still no common understanding of where each WP is and what each WP leader hopes to do. Without such a common understanding, suggestions for how to pivot would likely just provoke more confusion. As Richard is sick, I will moderate the meeting and Marc will act as SINUS representative.



I will close this brief email by putting to rest an allegation. Hopefully you have all read the Interim Report. It is a purely technical document. Assuming all partner inputs are credible and imply a feasible path forward for the project, it is not hard to write.



The allegation that SINUS reached out to the Project Officer and postponed the Interim Report and Review because our team could not string together this simple document is fantasy. We did so because in our assessment, the last-minute inputs provided by REPREX were not credible, and roadblocked the feasible path forward that the Report and Review must present.



The REPREX inputs furthermore implied that unless SINUS somehow magically resolved tensions between REPREX and other partners by 3 March, these tensions would be aired in front of the EC officers and experts. Anyone with a modicum of experience in EU projects could tell you that this would have been a disaster.



In summation: I was there during SINUS preparations for the interim review, while REPREX was not. Anyone can speculate about how these preparations went down, but such idle speculations will not be entertained during the meeting, nor in future emails. This is our last word on the matter.



Hopefully, we can take this as a pivot point toward a more constructive and meaningful discussion on 28 March.



Thank you all, and best regards,

James

Hi all,

Here are my meeting notes. As the recording started late and was cut off early, I'd suggest using these notes as the official record. Please let me know you have any comments or concerns.

I want to take this opportunity to revisit SINUS' duties as Coordinator. They are described in clear terms in the Consortium Agreement (Section 6.4), as are my own duties as Project Director (Section 6.4.2, line 8). These duties are largely administrative and procedural.

From day 1 of the project, I have stressed that amendments should be drafted jointly by the partners involved. They should then be brought to the PMB and/or GA as consensus proposals, with the consent of the impacted partners. If a proposal is made in this way, it is likely to pass. On the other hand, if a proposal is made to restructure the work plan and/or budget WITHOUT the consent of the impacted partners, it is in our experience likely to fail. In either case, we will give our assessment and vote like any other partner, and if the amendment does pass, we will execute it.

So: please engage in whatever behind-the-scenes horse-trading is needed to ensure that amendments reach the PMB and GA with the consent of all impacted partners. If you think having me in the room can be helpful, I'll make that call on a case-by-case basis. However, the days of "marriage counselling" via meandering bilateral conversations and "he said, she said" sessions are over. It's a losing game and I'm no longer inclined to play it.

Thank you and best regards,
James

________________________________
From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Monday, March 18, 2024 7:44 AM
To: Leo Lahti &lt;leo.lahti@utu.fi&gt;; Burus István &lt;istvan.burus@reprex.nl&gt;; Richard Wages &lt;Richard.Wages@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Cc: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Subject: Background statement / Reprex

Dear Richard, Leo, István

I am returning the background statement in the form that we approved a bit more than a year ago based on Richard's initial comments and suggestions.  There are only two significant changes.

1. Following Richard's remark:
Each Reprex R package has a separate description, and we have new exploitation statements, which mainly follow the best practices of rOpenSci. When there are no planned further developments at this stage, we accept co-authors and co-developers,pending approval from Reprex, with various requirements.

- In the case of packages that are not difficult to extend but we have no plans to do so, we require a development plan.
- In the case of package when extension would require significant oversight from Reprex we also require an approved exploitation plan (for the package, of course.)
- In the case we have active development plans or development guidelines (iotables and dataset) we also ask compliance with them.

2. Following James' remark:
SureyHarmonies is added as a Reprex background, with the blanket statement originally written by Richard for other elements.  While we used to work on this together with James, we do not have further development plans at this stage and I did not add any specifics.

Use of our background

As a matter of principle, without a development plan I do not agree to include packages that are not actively developed in Open Music Europe to be included in an anyhow defined "Open Music Europe Software Ecosystem". The term 'software ecosystem' has multiple, contested meanings, but none of them is standardised, and it must not be used to confuse or deceive reviewers or users.  We do not agree with the inclusion of any package that cannot be connected directly to the data needs identified by the consortium for the future European Music Observatory.

At this point, in my opinion, only the dataset and tuRtle packages have any plans to bring data into the consortium and then into the observatory, should such an ecosystem be formed. I have made a long, detailed description on how I see their role in a future software ecosystem. Even if they can form the nucleus of a software ecosystem, they are currently developed solely by myself. If we will not find a way to develop them with this grant, then we will develop them from other funds.

The iotables package has a potential to be used by the Consortium.  But at this point there are no described use cases, requirements, or anything to connect it to the work of tte Consortium or the future observatory.

Regarding the packages statcodelists, it is likely to be superseded with a new package. The regions package is not currently under development; it could be used potentially by the Consortium, but it would require a very special use case, and so far there are no plans to include it in the software ecosystem.

The retroharmonize package would require a very significant investment to be used in the ecosystem and without any plans to do so we do not allow their inclusion into the ecosystem, because Reprex has no budget to coordinate that work.

The spotifyr package was included in the background statement for clarity, but it is a background that is co-owned with other IP holders, and Reprex will not make any plans unilaterally for this package. If there will be further developments around it, it is likely that it will be in cooperation with IViR, but given that Spotify has significantly changed the data available on the API, this is undecided at this stage.

All packages are listed as they should have been added in the beginning of the work as background.  In most cases, there had not been any significant changes, except for the dataset package, which had only a prototype in the background and it was further developed in 2023.

Further discussions on WP4

I think that futher discussions should be based on a written proposal made by the WP leader, or on the PMB.  Reprex allocates all its PMs in the WP to T4.2 that it leads and plans no further PM allocation in T4.1

Best regards,
Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder

Subject: Call with Joost

Dear Joost and James,

I appreciate the time that Joost took this morning to speak with me.  I think I was very unprepared for this call, which was 15 minutes in the invitation, and I think that our conversation went in a bad direction.

I would like to speak for myself on the PMB, and stick to the agenda that we agreed on earlier. What we will communicate with Istvan, to avoid a surprise, is that we have been blamed for the lack of interim review, and we are willing to step aside, but we have no formal suggestion in any way.  We did not make any decision, we just indicated that we want to get out of this conflict zone and we are willing to make financial sacrifices to a reasonable extent.

We think that the Consortium must focus on how it will deliver the end results and not lose the grant, and if the Consortium sees a path forward without Reprex, we encourage it to take ownership of that path, because that will also create an incentive to come to an agreement with us. We do not want to hijack the agenda that we want to be subcontractors or whatever.  Subcontracting has as many pitfalls as being a consortium member with ill-designed tasks and responsibilities, it is only a contractual form. We are open to any contractual form that helps the consortium to better reach its goals, be it consortium membership, subcontracting, licensing, accelerated delivery, whatever is necessary.  We need to have an end of tasks and a payment in sight.

I am ready to make an apology for what is in my opinion my responsibility, and to contribute to my best ability to the stock-taking exercise that was suggested by Tomas on the PMB. Reprex will not put forward any proposals other than what we think is helpful for the interim review.  We will indicate in my apologetic intervention that we are willing to step aside, and we mean it.

I think that the best way forward is to take stock of what we have and what we are missing, and not to start another contractual or formalistic exercise.

Best regards,


Daniel Antal, CFA
