### OpenMusE // IMPORTANT / PMB meeting called off {#email-370}

**From:** Richard Wages &lt;Richard.Wages@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**To:** Richard Wages &lt;Richard.Wages@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**Cc:** James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;, Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;, Heike Kuchheuser &lt;Heike.Kuchheuser@sinus-institut.de&gt;, Marc Calmbach &lt;Marc.Calmbach@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**Date:** 03/03/2024 19:26:52

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202403031926-OpenMusE __ IMPORTANT _ PMB meeting called off-811.txt -->

Dear OpenMusE team,

Some two weeks ago I sent out a doodle poll for our next PMB meeting.
“For that reason I am calling for an in advance PMB meeting which this time shall first and foremost include a test run of the presentations each WP leader will have to give during the review (15m + 10m Q&amp;A). Please indicate your availabilities in this doodle poll&lt;https://dud-poll.inf.tu-dresden.de/openmuse-pmb05/&gt; until Thursday, 22 February the latest.”

As mentioned in my email this particular meeting was originally designed foremost to be an important test run for the planned EC review one week later. Today I am calling this PMB meeting off until further notice.

Reason: over the past two weeks there have been developments within the project which affect the orderly continuation of OpenMusE. In particular:

  *   REPREX has withdrawn permission to use their software components in a music data software ecosystem as planned in the Grant Agreement (i.e., under the lead of UTU)
  *   REPREX demands a considerable restructuring of the project plan as well as respective changes to responsibilities and budget distribution
  *   Drafts for this restructuring have been sent out by REPREX to a few selected other partners together with the request to decide on these suggestions during the now cancelled PMB and one week ahead of the EC review
  *   Plus, several other events which shall not be listed here today for brevity

Under these circumstances the planned PMB has lost its original meaning.

As clearly stated numerous times in the past, the PMB is not a project body which could legally make such decisions. The only decision body in such cases is the General Assembly. The GA is headed by James. Calling for a General Assembly needs a three week in advance notification. Furthermore, and as many of you know, James is currently in the US dealing with important family issues which do not allow for any delay.

In a separate email (Monday or Tuesday) James will call for a GA meeting (or he will ask me to do so on proxy). On a practical level, this means that the General  Assembly meeting can take place on March, 25 the earliest – most likely though in the very beginning of April.

Any GA decisions regarding changes in project and/or budget structure must then be forwarded to the EC for approval or denial (so-called amendment process). This process usually lasts about two months before becoming contractually valid. This too, had been communicated by SINUS on several occasions in the past.

That means, we have a time conflict, since the EC review was planned for 18 March.

James and I have spoken to our Project Officer to inform her on the current impasse. With her approval we will for the moment not submit the Periodic Report, as major parts may become obsolete depending on the outcome of the GA. She is currently considering several options regarding the EC Review meeting and will come back to us very soon.

We are on it and will keep you posted.

Kind regards&lt;
Richard

Procedural proposal:
Every agenda point in the PMB must be followed by an explicit vote.  There should be no agenda points without decisions.
Justification: The former GA and PMB meetings were not, or not in full implemented.  The last PMB did not make any decisions. Some members may come to the wrong conclusion that the real decisions are made in the backroom, and not in the decision making bodies of the consortium.
Resolution: in agreement / against.
A revision of all General Assembly and Project Management Board decisions.
Suggestions for quicker resolution:  material handed out in writing before the meeting, and discussion is only as needed.
Resolution:  PMB is

a)      in approval of the implementation of past decisions

b)      not in approval and suggests changes.

Procedural proposal
The PMB should only allow items on the agenda that have a written, informative documentation, i.e., the PMB members can read the basic facts, problems, review spending about a topic.  The PMB should not discuss any agenda points and should not make decisions without written submissions.
Justification: It cannot be reasonable expected that organisations which were not actively managing WPs or Tasks can make an informed decision from an oral presentation.

A revision of the T1.1, T2.1, T3.1 task from the point of the view of the T1.2, T2.2, T3.2 tasks.
Justification: According to original plan, the first year should have seen the creation of a DMP, and research into the important data gaps and novel methods to fill them for the benefit of the music sector of Europe.  This must result in clearly identified gaps and methods, which are discussed in iteration with the target groups of the grant, and based on the iterated gaps and methods, data collection should have started in the data collection window January-February 2024.  There were several problems during the last year, and the PMB members should be informed about them in writing, so that the vote on the resolutions should be made quickly.
The following issues should be put on a vote based on a proposal of the Coordinator and after considerations of the PMB.

-          Which task were not completed on time?

-          Which tasks needed a change of task leadership and execution (for example, T2.1)?

-          How much money was spent on each of the task?

-          How much money was not spent on organisations who did not, or not fully implement their task (for example, what happened with the SSSA budget for T1.1)?

-          How did the planned/vs actual budget  and spending change in the organisations that took over tasks and in those that did not fulfil the task.  For example, Reprex operates at a much higher PM rate due to these changes, the PMB should be informed about both the reasons and consequences to make an informed suggestion for the General Assembly for changes.

-          How much budget should be reollacated to the organisations that took over tasks, and implemented, or will implement the tasks?

-          How should the responsibilities, such a task leadership, supervision change.

Suggestion for quicker resolutions:  material handed out in writing before the meeting, listing the data gaps identified, methods to fill described in open materials, and stakeholders who were consulted, summarising the data collection task handover to the new tasks.
A revision of the research data management of the Consortium and the Data Management Plan.
Justification:  The project should have a living research data management function, well documented in a public and machine-actionable plan. Even though the General Assembly has voted to on this, the consortium has no such plan.   Even though the grant agreement specifically mentions that this consortium must collect data from external stakeholder, so far it has not collected any data. This also disables the continuation of the task stream 3 that requires data.
A revision of the D4.1 and preparation of change of the Grant Agreement
The Grant Agreement specifically states that open-source software should be developed for collecting data that fills the data gaps identified in the T1.1, T2.1, T3.1 in a way that it can be placed into the T5.1 observatory, subject to machine actionable reusability in T6.3. However, the task list of T4.1 erroneously does not specify these tasks, instead describes a software ecosystem referring to some R packages that were developed years before the grant and not for music data collection. This created a conflict of interest between the participants of the WP4 in the first place, and the task leader and the rest of the Consortium, because technically the software ecosystem can be delivered without a single line of music data collection software being developed.  The conflict of interest arises that other tasks and their leaders must execute tasks using software that does not exist.
The PMB should be informed about the fact that the task leader did not deliver on time, and after an extended time, created a “paper deliverable” without any new software or software plan for music data collection.
The PMB should make the necessary timing, re-scheduling, re-budgeting decisions and changes of responsibilities, because the original granted tasks, not only T4.1, but also T1.2, T2.2, T3.2, T4.2, T5.1 and T6.3 cannot be implemented without software the currently does not exist or has been planned.

Subject: PMB agenda proposals

Dear Marc and Richard,

I would like to go to the PMB with a consensual agenda and as much as possible consensual suggestions.  Unfortunately, this week I will have very limited time after tonight to deal with this, and the deadline for the agenda setting is Sunday.

Therefore, I am sending my proposals, which, of course, can be refined according to your wishes before the actual PMB.

Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder
+31615058460
linkedin&lt;https://www.linkedin.com/in/antaldaniel/&gt; •  reprex bv&lt;http://reprex.nl/&gt;

Procedural proposal:
Every agenda point in the PMB must be followed by an explicit vote.  There should be no agenda points without decisions.
Justification: The former GA and PMB meetings were not, or not in full implemented.  The last PMB did not make any decisions. Some members may come to the wrong conclusion that the real decisions are made in the backroom, and not in the decision making bodies of the consortium.
Resolution: in agreement / against.
A revision of all General Assembly and Project Management Board decisions.
Suggestions for quicker resolution:  material handed out in writing before the meeting, and discussion is only as needed.
Resolution:  PMB is

a)      in approval of the implementation of past decisions

b)      not in approval and suggests changes.

Procedural proposal
The PMB should only allow items on the agenda that have a written, informative documentation, i.e., the PMB members can read the basic facts, problems, review spending about a topic.  The PMB should not discuss any agenda points and should not make decisions without written submissions.
Justification: It cannot be reasonable expected that organisations which were not actively managing WPs or Tasks can make an informed decision from an oral presentation.

A revision of the T1.1, T2.1, T3.1 task from the point of the view of the T1.2, T2.2, T3.2 tasks.
Justification: According to original plan, the first year should have seen the creation of a DMP, and research into the important data gaps and novel methods to fill them for the benefit of the music sector of Europe.  This must result in clearly identified gaps and methods, which are discussed in iteration with the target groups of the grant, and based on the iterated gaps and methods, data collection should have started in the data collection window January-February 2024.  There were several problems during the last year, and the PMB members should be informed about them in writing, so that the vote on the resolutions should be made quickly.
The following issues should be put on a vote based on a proposal of the Coordinator and after considerations of the PMB.

-          Which task were not completed on time?

-          Which tasks needed a change of task leadership and execution (for example, T2.1)?

-          How much money was spent on each of the task?

-          How much money was not spent on organisations who did not, or not fully implement their task (for example, what happened with the SSSA budget for T1.1)?

-          How did the planned/vs actual budget  and spending change in the organisations that took over tasks and in those that did not fulfil the task.  For example, Reprex operates at a much higher PM rate due to these changes, the PMB should be informed about both the reasons and consequences to make an informed suggestion for the General Assembly for changes.

-          How much budget should be reollacated to the organisations that took over tasks, and implemented, or will implement the tasks?

-          How should the responsibilities, such a task leadership, supervision change.

Suggestion for quicker resolutions:  material handed out in writing before the meeting, listing the data gaps identified, methods to fill described in open materials, and stakeholders who were consulted, summarising the data collection task handover to the new tasks.
A revision of the research data management of the Consortium and the Data Management Plan.
Justification:  The project should have a living research data management function, well documented in a public and machine-actionable plan. Even though the General Assembly has voted to on this, the consortium has no such plan.   Even though the grant agreement specifically mentions that this consortium must collect data from external stakeholder, so far it has not collected any data. This also disables the continuation of the task stream 3 that requires data.
A revision of the D4.1 and preparation of change of the Grant Agreement
The Grant Agreement specifically states that open-source software should be developed for collecting data that fills the data gaps identified in the T1.1, T2.1, T3.1 in a way that it can be placed into the T5.1 observatory, subject to machine actionable reusability in T6.3. However, the task list of T4.1 erroneously does not specify these tasks, instead describes a software ecosystem referring to some R packages that were developed years before the grant and not for music data collection. This created a conflict of interest between the participants of the WP4 in the first place, and the task leader and the rest of the Consortium, because technically the software ecosystem can be delivered without a single line of music data collection software being developed.  The conflict of interest arises that other tasks and their leaders must execute tasks using software that does not exist.
The PMB should be informed about the fact that the task leader did not deliver on time, and after an extended time, created a “paper deliverable” without any new software or software plan for music data collection.
The PMB should make the necessary timing, re-scheduling, re-budgeting decisions and changes of responsibilities, because the original granted tasks, not only T4.1, but also T1.2, T2.2, T3.2, T4.2, T5.1 and T6.3 cannot be implemented without software the currently does not exist or has been planned.

Dear OpenMusE team,

As mentioned in my email last Sunday, James in his function as chair is calling for an extraordinary Meeting of the General Assembly. For practical reasons he asked me to send out this email to all of you. After 15 of the 16 GA Members cast their vote until the deadline three hours ago, and 14 of them indicated availability in the same time slot, we now have the date for the upcoming extraordinary Meeting of the General Assembly on Thursday, 4 April, 09:00 – 13:00 CET. Please mark your calendars.

Note: in recent days the coordinator was asked to postpone the GA to a much later date (e.g., end of May). This request is understandable but not we can’t do that. Our Project Officer at the EC has been made aware of our open questions in the financial statements and the gridlock in software development for the music data software ecosystem (D4.1) which make a meaningful project presentation at an EC review meeting currently implausible. She expects us to solve this impasse in our highest project body, the GA, asap. I will give further details during our extraordinary PMB meeting on 11 March.

For the meeting on the fourth of April, we can now also offer a hybrid event, i.e., if you have the chance you can join in person on the premises of SINUS in Berlin (details to come). An online option will of course be available too. In case you are a voting Member and can neither attend online nor in person, please make sure to delegate your vote.

We expect that in the upcoming days and weeks numerous suggestions for GA agenda points will be made. Please keep in mind that they should foremost be concerned with finding a sustainable solution for the remaining 22 months of our project. Suggestions can be sent to the coordinator and the final agenda will be distributed by James no later than 25 March, i.e., the deadline for handing in agenda items is Monday, 25 March 10:00 CET.

A Teams invitation for online attendance will follow shortly.

Looking forward to seeing you soon, hopefully in Berlin.

Kind regards,
Richard

-          How much money was not spent on organisations who did not, or not fully implement their task (for example, what happened with the SSSA budget for T1.1)?

-          How did the planned/vs actual budget  and spending change in the organisations that took over tasks and in those that did not fulfil the task.  For example, Reprex operates at a much higher PM rate due to these changes, the PMB should be informed about both the reasons and consequences to make an informed suggestion for the General Assembly for changes.

-          How much budget should be reollacated to the organisations that took over tasks, and implemented, or will implement the tasks?

-          How should the responsibilities, such a task leadership, supervision change.

Suggestion for quicker resolutions:  material handed out in writing before the meeting, listing the data gaps identified, methods to fill described in open materials, and stakeholders who were consulted, summarising the data collection task handover to the new tasks.
A revision of the research data management of the Consortium and the Data Management Plan.
Justification:  The project should have a living research data management function, well documented in a public and machine-actionable plan. Even though the General Assembly has voted to on this, the consortium has no such plan.   Even though the grant agreement specifically mentions that this consortium must collect data from external stakeholder, so far it has not collected any data. This also disables the continuation of the task stream 3 that requires data.
A revision of the D4.1 and preparation of change of the Grant Agreement
The Grant Agreement specifically states that open-source software should be developed for collecting data that fills the data gaps identified in the T1.1, T2.1, T3.1 in a way that it can be placed into the T5.1 observatory, subject to machine actionable reusability in T6.3. However, the task list of T4.1 erroneously does not specify these tasks, instead describes a software ecosystem referring to some R packages that were developed years before the grant and not for music data collection. This created a conflict of interest between the participants of the WP4 in the first place, and the task leader and the rest of the Consortium, because technically the software ecosystem can be delivered without a single line of music data collection software being developed.  The conflict of interest arises that other tasks and their leaders must execute tasks using software that does not exist.
The PMB should be informed about the fact that the task leader did not deliver on time, and after an extended time, created a “paper deliverable” without any new software or software plan for music data collection.
The PMB should make the necessary timing, re-scheduling, re-budgeting decisions and changes of responsibilities, because the original granted tasks, not only T4.1, but also T1.2, T2.2, T3.2, T4.2, T5.1 and T6.3 cannot be implemented without software the currently does not exist or has been planned.

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Monday, April 15, 2024 9:59 AM
To: Fábio Generoso Vieira &lt;F.V.GenerosoVieira@tilburguniversity.edu&gt;
Cc: Poort, Joost &lt;J.P.Poort@uva.nl&gt;
Subject: Warming in up in R development and ISRC codes

Dear Fábió,

Welcome on your first working day in IViR.  I woud like to ask you to review the following material from the book I had recommended to you in our last meeting, Advanced R.  These parts focus on your ability to work in a team of developers and to publish. Most of this we have talked about in Apollo 14, but at that time you were still focused on your PhD so we did not follow up.

The most important would be that you can create a much higher quality and inviting documentation of your work. One practice could be to put your existing packages into a format that it makes easier to download, try out, and learn by examples.  Or, you can get involved in one of my packages and gain practical experience.
This is now part of a new manual: https://r-pkgs.org/man.html  &lt;https://r-pkgs.org/man.html&gt;  (The entire manual is very useful: https://r-pkgs.org/man.html)

This is one package that I am actively developing for this project on rOpenSci – which is an organisation that ensures both scientific peer review and CRAN computer science peer review (that you are familiar with) and that your package will be published in methodological journal papers, too. https://dataset.dataobservatory.eu/   What you can do is at least to fork on GitHub the package, and to review with me how it is documented and presented.

There is one important aspect of programming that you should review from a programming point of view.  In the same book, there are five chapters about object-oriented programming (OOP).  You should read the chapter, but only focus on the S3 system, which is the simplest. You should have a reading familiarity with the R6 system, which is used in open science for publishing, but you only have to understand that unlike the S3 system, R6 objects are ephemeral and only stay in the memory.
https://adv-r.hadley.nz/oo.html
Last, but not least, we use these collaboration tools. If you use Keybase, you can always ask questions from me or my two co-developers, it is similar to Slack but free and open-source.  And I think that it would benefit you greatly if you would do the practice lessons of GitHub. All co-developed code is usually managed on GitHub, and I realised that you work mostly on your own and not experienced with it. On rOpenSci or other platforms you are expected to communicate in GitHub issues, to ask help on GitHub, and that it what we will use for work.
https://contributors.dataobservatory.eu/collaboration-tools.html
If you connect on Keybase and GitHub I can review your practice material and give almost instant feedback.

From a content perspective, I still find the original challenge the most relevant.  How can you create a sequence of valid ISRC codes that are truly random? For this, I would start to study the manual of the ISRC code itself, and the history of the code, to understand its intrinsic biases: that far more codes have a 2022 year code than 1989, that the US and Brazilian space is basically fully but small countries like SK are sparce, etc.
https://www.ifpi.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/ISRC_Handbook.pdf

Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder
+31615058460
linkedin&lt;https://www.linkedin.com/in/antaldaniel/&gt; •  reprex bv&lt;http://reprex.nl/&gt;  • eviota&lt;https://eviota.nl/&gt;

### Re: OpenMusE -- DISCO-10M dataset {#email-391}

**From:** Fábio Generoso Vieira &lt;f.v.vieira@uva.nl&gt;  
**To:** Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;  
**Date:** 04/24/2024 09:07:10

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202404240907-Re_ OpenMusE -- DISCO-10M dataset-114.txt -->

Hi Daniel,

Interesting! I will check that out. And indeed, you are right, finding the ISRCs is not an easy task. After our meeting on Tuesday, I started following Joost’s suggestion of looking for ISRCs of the format UK---2300001. Basically, checking all the possible combinations of those three characters after the first two in the prefix code, the so-called registrant code.

Out of the nearly 46,000 possible combinations, I found only 1024 that were valid (only about 2.2%). Interestingly, when I checked for the codes ending 00002 all of them pop up. So, you could repeat this process until you exhaust all of them. Though that would not be a computationally efficient task. Especially since that’s just one country and one year. And there’s also the fact that Spotify locks you out of the API after about 25,000 queries. So, the question is: is it worth continuing this? I think to check a few countries it is going to take months (or probably the whole time of my contract).

Another question I have is, should I be saving the results of those queries? If so, I am going to have to find and efficient way, otherwise, I will run out of physical memory in my computer in about 2 months. Do you know whether UvA has something like a cloud service (at Tilburg we used SurfDrive) that I can save all these data? Also, I haven’t designed a SQL database before, but it seems like it would be nice to have that data in this format.

Finally, I found a package (not on CRAN) that extracts data from MusicBrainz. I don’t know if you have seen it before. This is the link &lt; https://github.com/mikkelkrogsholm/musicbrainz&gt;. I tried a few searches, and it seems reliable. The only problem is that it seems like the data on MusicBrainz are not standardized. So, not all tracks have an ISRC code, even when the code does exist. So, it seems to me, at this point, that the Spotify API is by far the most reliable source of data.

Best,
Fabio

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Tuesday, 23 April 2024 22:03
To: Fábio Generoso Vieira &lt;f.v.vieira@uva.nl&gt;
Subject: Re: OpenMusE -- DISCO-10M dataset

Hi Fábio,

I think that I have a different idea that perhaps you could think of and pursue.  So, we have no way of randomly finding ISRC codes, however, I think that we can find randomly artists on Spotify.  So, imagine that you are searching for the most frequent words and names in English, Spanish, Slovak, Dutch, etc, and it gives you a few artists with artist ID. Then you querry the 5 or 10 or 50 most popular songs of these artists.

https://www.rcharlie.com/spotifyr/reference/search_spotify, for example aritst="fabio"  or album="cloud", I think that it will give you a near and not exact search.
it will return an artist id or many artist ids

Then use get_artist_top_tracks()&lt;https://www.rcharlie.com/spotifyr/reference/get_artist_top_tracks&gt;
it will give you a lot of artist.

While directly searching for isrc codes may be difficult (and I may need to change the search_spotify() function for that, finding random artists and then randomly selecting their songs should not really be correlated much with how the ISRC codes are assigned.  If you look for an artists named "Fred" or "Guilo" could be an artist from any decade, and the songs can be any editions, releases, etc.

Finding random aritsts may be simpler than random ISRC codes!

 Best regards,
Daniel

Hi all,

First off, please excuse the late email – the Coordinator and Project Management Board have been busy in the background. In brief, we have been restructuring the project:


  *   To ensure that those partners who work together well can continue to do so, without interpersonal tension getting in the way.

  *   To make tasks, expectations, and timelines more streamlined and concrete.

Tomorrow's meeting was called as a General Assembly, and we appreciate that all of you made time for it.

The first 1.5 hours will be dedicated to filling in the entire Consortium on where we are now. We'd like all partners to be present, and will ask for approval of the following agenda:


  *   09:00: debrief on the past two weeks (SINUS)

  *   09:15: update on WP1 (UVA)

  *   09:25: update on WP2 (SSSA)

  *   09:35: update on WP3 (SINUS)

  *   09:45: Q&amp;A

  *   10:15-10:30: next steps = what to expect in the coming weeks

The following 2.5 hours will be recast as a PMB meeting, i.e., WP leaders (UVA, SSSA, SINUS, UTU) and task leaders (SOZA, MIH, HEARDIS, SYNYO). We gladly gift the others the rest of their day back – although you are welcome to join if you want. The agenda here will be more fluid, but we will ask for approval of the following:


  *   10:30-10:45: break

  *   10:45: debrief on the past two weeks, pt. II (SINUS)

  *   11:00: breakout rooms

     *   WP1 &amp; WP2 – hybrid

     *   WP4 – in person at SINUS

  *   12:00: reconvene and discuss

  *   12:30-13:00: next steps = what we must do in the coming weeks

We are happy to consider additional items.

Thank you, and best regards,
James

Il giorno ven 29 mar 2024 alle ore 11:59 Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&lt;mailto:daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;&gt; ha scritto:
Dear Sarah and Anna,

After you left this extraordinary-extraordinary PMB, we went on for an hour and agreed that on 04 April everybody will be requested to fill in a form (that will come from James) about what they really want to do with their remaining grant. I think that this is a very good idea, and as I contacted you earlier, we see that we have a critical ingredient to your task (which is in James's WP.)

We are working on a banking sustainability project in Hungary, and a film sustainability project in Hungary and France, and we would be doing something similar with you. As we have four projects, not only OpenMuse, we can allocate a large and efficient team, but only if the projects are more  or less aligned in time.  Also, if the timeline does not fit, you can reuse our other project's results.

In France we currently work with a business school and their incubator, and I am sending along the slides for their professors and finishing year students, which in many ways could be copied by MiH.

In all our projects we work with EFRS E1 greenhouse gases, because that is the most developed need. I understand that in WP3 to utilize harmonised surveys, perhaps ESRS S2 would be more desirable, but that would be also more work.

My practical suggestion woudl be this:

- To mitigate the risk that there will be further problems and delays in OpenMuse, participate in our existing projects and create an ESRS E1 calculator for music in the coming 3-4 months.  This would require relatively little work commitment because we have a large team working on this.  Then, there would be something to show to evaluators, stakeholders, with little time and resource commitment already this year.

- In 2025, as resources permit in OpenMuse, use this framework to try to build an ESRS S2 social sustainability measurement tool which requires surveying and more input.

- In either case, we would know by June or July that the task is certain that can report something that may be acceptable overall.

What would be needed:

If you do not do ESRS S2 but E1, we would need a little assistance to gather enough data from music stakeholders (internally in the consortium and externally) that we can use for prototyping.

- communication with stakeholders, requesting data, sending them explanations

- we would essentially follow up with the work from the MusicAire project where I did some calculations with MiH data, we would refine that add more companies.

- the timeframe shoudl be April-June 2023, but with very limited MiH resource

- we could evaluate later how much it is feasible to add social indicators to the same reporting tool.

I am attaching a validation project presentation that is adapted from our banking and HU Hungarian film project to French film. We would do something similar to greenhouse gases in music.

Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA

________________________________
From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Tuesday, April 2, 2024 9:05 PM
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Cc: Burus István &lt;istvan.burus@reprex.nl&gt;
Subject: Fwd: PMB preparation (WP2)

Hi James,

We tried to put into a spreadsheet the essence of my presentation today (Adam will create a cleaner version of it, and we will send it to you as you saw it today). You may find it useful that we tried to put the WP1 and WP2 into the same format, which is a work in progress, by no means final and could be shared with Caterina or Joost, but this is how we are thinking along our preparation for Thursday.

https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1Sj7S9p1ekByk8cW9RfmlamOznQvmufPpbwHZofV9-kU/edit?usp=sharing

I think that a part of my presentation on Thursday went a bit unnoticed, when I tried to explain that the work done in Slovakia is punching above its weight.  I think that SOZA, Reprex and HC are doing work in Slovakia that has the potential to be excepted in some ways as European best practice (in WP1 and WP2, too), and could carry both WP1 and WP2 through not only an interim but a final report, too.  However, there is a big caveat here.  If you look at SOZA's and Reprex's task definition (T2.3 and T1.3 respecitvely) we would need to scale up the work with SOZA and Artisjus to a European level.  I am most certain that neither Artisjus nor SOZA, even with the help of Reprex can do that.

To me, the most worrying intervention from Caterina was during the PMB that she is expected help from SOZA, MusicAutor, Aloaded and Reprex to her work in her WP where she has far-far-far the most resources. However, the original work plan suggests that Artisjus, SOZA, Reprex, ALOADED will get help from SSSA and IViR to scale up our work to a European level (with data collectors programmed by UTU).  What I tried to say on the PMB and on earlier occasions is that SOZA and Artisjus are not research organisations, nor is MusicAutor. SOZA with Reprex can create a wonderful report on the Slovak music diversity, Artisjus with Reprex on the Hungarian music economy (we have been there, done that before), but our expectation from this project was that IViR, SSSA, EUBA and UTU will generalize and scale this up to a European level, not the other way around.

To ask a European report from SOZA or Reprex and Artisjus is not realistic. Neither Artisjus, SOZA or Reprex has the capacity and ambition to do so.

We can suggest a different solution, but in my opinion, this would require resource shift from the universities towards Artisjus, SOZA and Reprex, i.e., that we try to create the T1.3 and T2.3 reports in a way that they have a European relevance and with a bit modified description, they can carry the day towards the EU. I think that the T1.3 report could do so if it meets the expectatios of DG EAC and Eurostat and the T2.3 if we can add a bit of replication from other countries. But this would require extra motivation and resources for the parties involved, I think currently the stake of Artisjus and SOZA is so small in this consortium and they see so many problems that this would be a difficult sell without offering something important for all parties concerned.

The reason why I see it this way, because if you follow a reductio ad absurdum argument, you can claim that UvA, EUBA, and SSSA are basically done with their tasks, so is UTU, and the WP leaders can do freely whatever they want in the rest of the project, however, Reprex, SOZA, MiH, and HearDis have to carry through the project in the last 2 years, potentially without any investment from the universities.  This is most certainly not what these four organisations were prepared for.

So, overall, I think that you have to balance the following:

WP1 &gt; do you want to have something that the DC EAC/Eurostat like -- perhaps Artisjus, SOZA, and Reprex can do this, but this would be way beyond what can reasonably be expected from these organisations, and would require a careful balaced rebudgeting and replanning; you also must beware that this deliverable in T1.3 is depending on surveys that you have the budget for.
WP2 &gt; do you want that SOZA, HC, and Reprex creates something that has a European relevance without SSSA/EUBA/UTU significant input; we can probably do this, but it require extra budget and a redefinition of the task, and would require a careful balaced rebudgeting and replanning involving at least SOZA, HC, and Reprex.
WP3 &gt; I think that we have a plan of action and it is good

WP4 &gt; A complex issue, and we have no ideas at this point
WP5 &gt; The question is deliverable timing.  I think that Reprex can only deliver in May if it is not involved in these other issues. It would be better to deliver in June. It is more difficult to deliver an empty observatory than an observatory with some good looking data, because we need a lot more effort to dress up an empty database than an interesting one. Or by the interim review.
WP6 &gt; Reprex does not want to be involved in anyway.

Best regards,
Daniel

Daniel

### OpenMusE -- agenda for 3 April 2024 meeting {#email-401}

**From:** James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202404031813-OpenMusE -- agenda for 3 April 2024 meeting-442.txt -->

Hi all,

First off, please excuse the late email – the Coordinator and Project Management Board have been busy in the background. In brief, we have been restructuring the project:


  *
To ensure that those partners who work together well can continue to do so, without interpersonal tension getting in the way.
  *
To make tasks, expectations, and timelines more streamlined and concrete.

Tomorrow's meeting was called as a General Assembly, and we appreciate that all of you made time for it.

The first 1.5 hours will be dedicated to filling in the entire Consortium on where we are now. We'd like all partners to be present, and will ask for approval of the following agenda:


  *
09:00: debrief on the past two weeks (SINUS)
  *
09:15: update on WP1 (UVA)
  *

________________________________
From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Thursday, April 4, 2024 2:27 PM
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Subject: Reprex PM, financial

Hi James,

I wanted to give a quick update on other Reprex issues.

PM rate.
We understand that our rate is high, but it will significantly decrease in the coming months and come to the range that Richard presented to be the Dutch startup benchmark rate. There is a fundamental misunderstanding: our rate, in the absence of history in 2022, is based on the 2022 Marie Curie rate for NL (per EU guideline). In itself, the MC rate is adjusted annually, and the NL had the highest inflation in the period since WW2. Even if the Marie Curie rate would be our benchmark it would increase, so I think that our technical PM rate is by definition not a hard benchmark. But the practice is that you use the MC rate until you have a true wage history. I cannot predict what will be our end rate, but well within the expected range. I was actually hired from Hungary, because the super gross rate of the Dutch minimum wage for university educated people is in itself almost the same as the Marie Curie rate (postdocs hardly earn more than the minimum living wage.)

We also believe that IViR would be a benchmark for us that the PO must be accepted. We employ people on the same market, similarly qualified people for similar tasks, and in NL it is illegal to have more than 30% wage difference. In my opinion IViR -30% should be easy to communicate, because we can only go below that if we outsource to Hungary, which we will practically do, but nobody can force a Dutch startup to do that.  Per Dutch law, I should receive no less than -30% that IViR pays for a WP leader or task leader. My team members should receive no less than -30% that IViR pays, and the only way I can go below this is to hire from abroad on a freelance basis.

Our hires in Hungary have a similar PM to Artisjus, but it will not really level us out to 5000. But we will not use all our PMs and will claim that we used less but more senior human resources. However, we believe that this is a non-issue, our PM rate will fall significantly but not exactly to the Marie Curie rate.

Advance and revenue
Our interest is to make our advance a revenue, and it would be beneficial if the interim review would be a review of not the first 12M but 13 or 14 (D4.1 was anyways shifted to M14)
We also expect that Sinus will release the remaining advance after the interim review, in which case a part of our earlier advance will become earned revenue, and some more advance will be added to the not earned but incurred costs of M12?M14?  to M18 (or whatever will be the interim review cutoff point)

We exepct more clarity by the end of the month when our final task list and budget and purchase costs will be all planned.

Best regards,
Daniel

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202404120859-Re_ email for WP2 partners to elicit contributions-451.txt -->

Hi Daniel,

A note from the coordination side:


  *
One purpose of the restructuring is to support everyone in working primarily with those partners, with whom they already have effective and trusting relationships.
  *
Another purpose is to minimise dependencies and clarify those remaining (as well as the responsibility of all involved). We will chart out the dependencies in visual form once the WP and task leaders have tentatively approved the task structure.
  *
The original task list is available in the Grant Agreement and on EMDesk. PM were not assigned on the task level within the Grant Agreement. To my knowledge, WP3 is the only WP that proposed a task-level assignment of PM. However, the PM *spent* per task are available in the Excel breakdown sent by Isabella in the lead-up to the extraordinary PMBs.

In the third extraordinary meeting, it was proposed that WP1-3 would be less problematic to restructure than WP4-5, and that we should thus start with them. I was under the impression that you agreed and were willing to work with the rest of the Consortium here. You and I have a call on Thursday 18 April to discuss the software and data management issues, but I doubt we will solve them in that single call. If we put WP1-3 on hold until after 18 April, we will miss our proposed internal deadlines.

This will put us on track to be forced to delay our interim review yet again, as well as probably to ask for a formal delay or extension. I was under the impression REPREX *did not* want further delays. I thus urge you to make time to work out these issues with us on schedule, or find someone else in the REPREX team who is capable of representing the company's position.

We do have some momentum here, but it is fragile. The alternatives to this restructuring are more dramatic, more effort- and cost-intensive, and in nobody's interest.

Thank you and best regards,
James


________________________________
From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Friday, April 12, 2024 12:08 AM
To: Caterina Sganga &lt;caterina.sganga@santannapisa.it&gt;
Cc: Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;; James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Subject: Re: email for WP2 partners to elicit contributions

Hi Caterina,

I do not understand the text of T2.1 and T2.3, and I find some of the wording confusing, (how can ontologies be streamlined) but I will not comment on them if I see that the SOZA-Reprex task is well resourced, and I understand what inputs it gets and if anything depends on it.  I want to make sure that I do not have to contribute to any tasks that I do not understand.

I would like to see an  original task list with PMs attached to it and how they are going into the new tasks and PMs.  I would also like to know if the SOZA-Reprex task has any dependencies, and if anything depends on our work.  I do not want to see that T2.1 and T2.3 draws away the resources of our partners from our tasks. I am particularly against losing any resources of ALOADED, SOZA, who are critically important to our work.  I would like to see all their resources committed to our task.  I also want more clarity on how T2.2 is referred to in T2.3.  I do not see the T2.4 task, and I am a bit concerned about the missing music policy competences in the music policy task.

I think that the task leaders meeting would be much needed before we ask for any contributions from partners. This is not the originally planned task list, I see that the data collection task disappeared.  Last, but not least, we are still not finished with the software and data management issues, and until those are cleared, I would not like to proceed with this one.

All in all, I do not think that we should ask from smaller partners contributions until we have clear tasks and we see what resources are available for those tasks, including inputs from other WPs.

Best regards,
Daniel
















On Thu, Apr 11, 2024 at 12:33 PM Caterina Sganga &lt;Caterina.Sganga@santannapisa.it&lt;mailto:Caterina.Sganga@santannapisa.it&gt;&gt; wrote:

Dear Tomas and Daniel,

As just agreed during the WP2 meeting, here’s a very simple/short email template we can share with other WP2 members to solicit their contributions. Just let me know if you would like to send a separate email on your own or we can do it together so that people don’t get bombed.



Many thanks – best

Caterina







Dear WP2 members,



Many thanks for your participation to our meeting last Thursday. As agreed, below you can find short details on the new proposed tasks, the contributions we would like to receive, and the expertise/competence needed from your side to offer such a contribution. We would be grateful if you could answer to this email with your proposal to the respective task leaders no later than next Wednesday 17 April EOB.



Best wishes,

XXXXXX



Task 2.1 Mapping of legal, policy and economic domains on music diversity and circulation and development of economic indicators (SSSA). [Start: M3, End: M32]

The first 4 actions of this task have already been completed and described in D2.1. The next and last phase (SSSA-UVA-SINUS) will transform the legal and policy domains on music diversity and circulation in actionable economic indicators at the EU level. Terminologies and ontologies will be streamlined in order to allow the implementation of the indicator frameworks on single Member States. T2.1 will act in conjunction with T1.1 and T3.1 in order to provide a comprehensive framework covering the economic, social and cultural implications of music and its diversity and circulation aspects, which will be all channeled in D3.X.



DESIRED CONTRIBUTIONS FROM OTHER PARTNERS

  *   Help to adapt EU-level and general indicators to your country contexts and data sources (statistical, CMOs, other sources)



EXPERTISE/COMPETENCE NEEDED

  *   Awareness of national statistical (or other official) data sources
  *   Being or having contact with national CMOs having a list of indicators/data they commonly collect and use



T2.2: Pilot study on music diversity and circulation in Europe (SOZA-REPREX). Implementation of a pilot study in Slovakia and Bulgaria as a second target country. The pilot study will demonstrate the feasibility of increasing local artist representation in radio and streaming, via using previously generated AI on a company-internal and human-checked level and evidence-based regulatory policy. A GDPR-compliant reference database to measure the market share of Slovak music within Slovak radio play, using SOZA’s collective management system for public performance – as well as within streaming, using the big data sampling software contained within the OpenMusE music data software ecosystem. The pilot study will culminate in the co-creation of guidelines and recommendations for scaling and transfer to selected markets.



DESIRED CONTRIBUTIONS FROM OTHER PARTNERS

  *   ….
  *   …
  *   …



EXPERTISE/COMPETENCE NEEDED

  *   …
  *   …
  *   …





T2.3. Stakeholders’ engagement and policy recommendations (lead: SSSA). [Start:M28, End:M36] Legal and policy domains and economic indicators for music diversity and circulation, developed under T2.2, will be tested with local stakeholders in a pilot interview program, with the aim of prioritizing the most important indicators for different actors in the music industry and filling in eventual gaps. On this basis, T2.4 will build on the current legislative framework – in cooperation with T1.4, to draft policy recommendations on the legislative and non-legislative measures to be implemented in order to ensure the availability of and access to data sources responding to the economic indicators identified in D3.X to measure the full economic value of music, the sustainability of the music industry, the social value-adds of music, and music diversity and circulation.



DESIRED CONTRIBUTIONS FROM OTHER PARTNERS

  *   Availability to identify and contact local stakeholders in your country (selected, limited number) to be interviewed in order to validate the indicators, fill in gaps and define priorities. Note that the interview text will be provided by SSSA-SINUS-UVA



EXPERTISE/COMPETENCE NEEDED

  *   Contacts and leverage on local stakeholders
  *   Time availability to carry out the interviews

Hi Daniel,

Ahead of the call, details on T5.1 as it stands would be appreciated. Talking to the other WP leaders, it became clear that nobody has a clear idea of how exactly you envision the "Open Music Observatory", beyond the very top-level task description in the Grant Agreement.

Some notes from my side that will need to be discussed, based on your document "Open Music Europe Software Ecosystem: Functional requirements elicitation and release timeline":


  *
Pg. 6-7: WP2 use cases are clear. WP1 and WP3 use cases are still under-elaborated. Joost and I can commit to working with REPREX and/or UTU on this.
  *
Pg. 9: RDF, OWL, Wikidata, Wikibase GUI, OpenRefine, and Protege were not discussed during the proposal or Grant Agreement processes, and don't appear in the GA.
  *
Pg. 9: Fluency with controlled vocabularies and ontologies, Wikibase GUI, OpenRefine, and Protege was not an expectation communicated to the research partners during the proposal or Grant Agreement processes.
  *
Pg. 9: Making coded knowledge available in RDF is not a sub-activity mentioned in the T6.3 description.
  *
Pg. 10-13: for clarification, is it the case that:
     *
The new packages dataset (&amp; datacube?) and crosswalk are intended to take over / surpass functions currently performed by iotables, regions, statcodelists, retroharmonize..? If so, many sections in the existing Methodology text will have to be amended.
     *
The REPREX package tuRtle and non-REPREX package ontologics will be used to make harmonised music industry data interoperable with the semantic web..? This is not part of the current GA and would have to be added, and the cost/benefit analysis would have to be discussed/approved with the PO.
  *
Pg. 15: The KULT package also doesn't appear in the GA, but this is justifiable as the KULT harmonisation work arose unexpectedly out of the cooperation with IKP. I still hope a way can be found to continue this work.
  *
Pg. 17: Re: SDMX, the GA states that "OpenMusE data are documented with SDMX compatible codebooks, and DublinCore and DataCite metadata, ensuring full interoperability, and are available in tidy format". UTU is familiar with these standards and can assist partners responsible for data collection (SSSA, SINUS) that their datasets comply.
  *
Pg. 17: The requirement that T4.1 involve OWL interoperability packages was not discussed at the proposal or GA stage, is not in the GA, and must be cleared with UTU.
  *
Pg. 17: The requirement that the DMP be machine readable or actionable was not discussed at the proposal or GA stage, and is not in the GA.
  *
Pg. 19: The reconciliation of existing music database schemas with coded ontologies is highly interesting and in my opinion, relevant, but also is not anywhere in the GA.
  *
Pg. 22: Harmonisation of the SKCMDb with Wikidata is mentioned in the WP2 pilot project sub-section of the "Methodology" section, but if it is a core sub-activity, should be added to the formal task description.

In brief: some time in 2023, REPREX appears to have made a hard pivot toward semantic web technologies as a core business and scientific interest. This pivot has been retroactively written into your vision for the OMO and the OME project.

This may make sense from a state-of-the-art perspective, but it also imposes requirements on the non-REPREX partners that are *not* in the contracts they signed. This is problematic.

We will work with REPREX to resolve this problem. For instance, having explored Wikibase GUI, OpenRefine, and Protege, I believe I could learn to use the latter to further formalise the systematic assessment of data gaps that I developed in WP3 (currently linked to Eurovoc). I could then support WP1 and WP2 in doing so.

However, expecting T6.3 to make this coded knowledge available in RDF format is out of scope. Put simply: if you envisioned this, you should have written it into the GA and invited a partner with the requisite competence to the Consortium.

So: compromises will be required. The research partners will have to be persuaded to meet new and sometimes challenging expectations. I commit to supporting them in this. But these expectations must be realistic: Joost and Caterina cannot be asked to become, or to supervise, database managers. So, REPREX will also have to compromise. If REPREX wants to *exceed* the specifications for data management or the OMO that are laid out in the GA, it will be contingent upon REPREX to fund the work required using its existing budget.

Otherwise, we must retain the lower standard of SDMX, DublinCore, and DataCite compliance for datasets, and (to be retroactively implemented to the best degree possible) Open Policy Analysis compliance for documents, etc.

Thank you and best regards,
James

Dear James,

 Hello James,

I read your feedback with interest and I want to avoid a lot of misunderstandings with giving a few general remarks.  Reprex did not pivot from the project that it had developed for years, and the grant agreement supports our understanding of the tasks.
I am very sad that Leo in the last minute put the „software ecosystem” term into the task list, as he said then, to manage what reviewers can expect, which turned out to avoid actually writing software.  We do not have the terms „semantic technologies” or other buzzwords in the text, however, there are literally more than hundred of mentions of „metadata”, „open data”, „interoperability”, „standards”.  These are the places that refer to data semantics.
Another sadly missing or infrequently used term is the „database”, however, we have countless mentions of „data collection”, „data processing”, data reprocessing”, „data dissemination”.  Since the 1970s this is done in databases.  While anybody can challenge the EU publication offices recommendation to use Wikibase, which is completely free, open source, and sutaibale from citizen scientist to archvist and statistician, you must acknowedge that we must use some sort of database management system to fulfill the grant agreement.
The grant agreement is in the lower level of the legal hierarchy, it is not repeating laws, regulations, but adheress that you stick to them. The laws governing data interoperability and data access, or data governance, in the European Interoperability Act, the Open Data Directive, the Data Governance Act and other legal instruments mandate data interoperability and within that semantic interoperability. You don ot find the definition of the machine actionable DMP in the grant agreement because it is regulated in the higher legal norms about the conduct of publicly funded (open science.)
I do not think that it will be constructive if we start to challenge the need to use interoperable databases in this project, and software that can work not only with data and metadata, because this is written into almost every second sentence of our grant agreement.

Best regards,
Daniel

Subject: WP2 issues

Dear Caterina, James,

We were invited with Tomas last minute to a Hackathon by the Cultural and the Innovation Ministries to Bratislava the weekend, so I had really little time because I got the news in Portugal.   We discussed the WP2 with Tomas, too.

We do not want to hold up the separation of the tasks and I think that perhaps we do not need to wait till Friday until we could go in a call, because we can clear up the tasks in an email exchange.  For us, there was some unclarity in the new task descriptions, even in the numbering.

What we see more problematic is that perhaps nobody will replicate SOZA's work. We sent some specification to MusicAutor but I find their organisational capacity rather weak and they are surrounded by very weak organisations -- Bulgaria does not have a music information center or an association of music libraries.

Assuming your task stream receives the UTU funding and UVA spends half of its PM in each task stream, the breakdown of existing resources is:

University stream (50% of UVA, 100% of SSSA, EUBA): €169594
Ex-CEEMID stream (50% of UVA, 100% of REPREX, SOZA, ALOADED, ARTISJUS, MUSICAUTOR) plus reallocated UTU: €160887

Additionally, UVA will receive 6 PM (€18198) from SSSA for Fabian's work in this WP, giving the ex-CEEMID stream €179085 total.

In my view as Coordinator:


  *
€169594 for the university stream is justified and sufficient as they must design and implement a multinational survey, as well as taking over all of the policy analysis and policymaker-oriented writing.
  *
€179085 for the ex-CEEMID stream is justified and sufficient, given the value-add to the industry of the market comparator model.

Dependencies between the task streams are:
     *
Uni task stream requires industry registers from ex-CEEMID task stream to plan survey sampling.
     *
Uni task stream requires survey background from ex-CEEMID task stream, to ensure proper inputs for market comparator model.
     *
Ex-CEEMID task stream requires cleaned final survey data from uni task stream as inputs for market comparator model.

Otherwise, the two task streams should be autonomous.

Dear Joost,

I was able to open but not edit on your server, so I created a new version.  Changes:

- In the survey task, Reprex remains involved as you will use the Artisjus/SOZA/Reprex surveying background, but the role is limited to provide access to the background / i.e. the music professional MSME survey
- Reprex will be the task leader not Artisjus in 1.6.  If Eszter has no further comments on this, perhaps the meeting is not necessary for this reason.

There are two issues that I do not think that we can close this week.  The text makes reference to UTU contributions, this is very unclear now how that will be, and if that is the case, I want to make it very explicit. I will talk with James tomorrow and hopefully there will be more light.

Artisjus, MusicAutor, and Aloaded must contribute to the T1.2 and T1.6 tasks, too. For @Dr. Kabai Eszter&lt;mailto:ekabai@artisjus.com&gt; and @Rosina Petrova&lt;mailto:rosina_petrova@musicautor.org&gt; , T1.2 is the data collection for the valuations, and T1.6 is the valuation study itself.  While formally Reprex can be the leader in terms of making sure that the EU deliverable is made, but the work on the CMO side must be coordinated with Rosina by Eszter.  Reprex cannot directly access the CMO and CISAC databases, let alone figure out what data is available and in what format in MusicAutor.  Reprex can be responsible for the EU deliverable and any publication or the OPA files, but we cannot be responsible for the actual valuation that has to be made with Reprex assistance by Artisjus and MusicAutor.

Given that Tomas and Rosina are in the CISAC meeting now, and perhaps Eszter is there, the best would be if they would coordinate among themselves, as they are doing this now with the WP2 CMO tasks, too.

Best regards,
Daniel

- In the survey task, Reprex remains involved as you will use the Artisjus/SOZA/Reprex surveying background, but the role is limited to provide access to the background / i.e. the music professional MSME survey
- Reprex will be the task leader not Artisjus in 1.6.  If Eszter has no further comments on this, perhaps the meeting is not necessary for this reason.

Artisjus, MusicAutor, and Aloaded must contribute to the T1.2 and T1.6 tasks, too. For @Dr. Kabai Eszter&lt;mailto:ekabai@artisjus.com&gt; and @Rosina Petrova&lt;mailto:rosina_petrova@musicautor.org&gt; , T1.2 is the data collection for the valuations, and T1.6 is the valuation study itself.  While formally Reprex can be the leader in terms of making sure that the EU deliverable is made, but the work on the CMO side must be coordinated with Rosina by Eszter.  Reprex cannot directly access the CMO and CISAC databases, let alone figure out what data is available and in what format in MusicAutor.  Reprex can be responsible for the EU deliverable and any publication or the OPA files, but we cannot be responsible for the actual valuation that has to be made with Reprex assistance by Artisjus and MusicAutor.

Given that Tomas and Rosina are in the CISAC meeting now, and perhaps Eszter is there, the best would be if they would coordinate among themselves, as they are doing this now with the WP2 CMO tasks, too.

Best regards,
Daniel

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202405011605-Re_ Updates-115.txt -->

Hi Daniel,

Thanks for your answer.

Indeed, I agree that there are some technical and methodological issues with this approach. But as I first try, I would say it’s decent.

Yes, I can come to Apollo 14 on Friday. Let me know when you have time.

I need to check again the download of the MusicBrainz data base. I checked the documentation and I confess I didn’t understand how it works, it flew way over my head.

I will think about this suggestion. At a first glance, I would say, if I understood it correctly, this would result in the same issue we have with creating random codes following the ISRC format. The space of possible options would be way too large. For instance, I tried these two changes you suggested here:

My idea would be to "dial" something like 5rQEom98vgByjAZ4kIw2kL to 6rQEom98vgByjAZ4kIw2kL or 7MoIc5s9KXolCBH1fy9kkw to 7NoIc5s9KXolCBH1fy9kkw.

And none of them resulted in a valid Spotify page. Maybe I am missing something, but I think then the question would be, what digits would we need to change?

Regarding the ‘dialing’ idea you described, I think there might be something there. It looks like there is a disproportionately larger number of codes where the 5 final digits start with 0000 and 000. For instance, the plots below represent the distribution of digits of samples I got for NL and IT. In the x-axis, the left most side starts with 00001, which is the first number there and represents the highest spike on both plots. After that it goes down significantly. I believe most registrants start by 00001, then 00002 and so on...So the beginning of the sequence will be significantly denser than the remaining. We might be a lot more likely to find a code that ends with 00005 than one that ends with 09999.

[cid:image003.png@01DA9BDF.EC90B610][cid:image004.png@01DA9BE1.564D3BE0]

Regarding the data base for Slovakia, that really sounds amazing. It will facilitate our work a lot if we have that. I don’t know how this data base will look like, but it doesn’t hurt to dream that they will be kind enough to have the Spotify ID there too (haha).

Best,
Fabio

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Wednesday, 1 May 2024 13:16
To: Fábio Generoso Vieira &lt;f.v.vieira@uva.nl&gt;
Cc: Joost Poort &lt;j.p.poort@uva.nl&gt;
Subject: Re: Updates

Hi Fabio,

I think that this is really good work and it shows that the ideas were more or less good: we start with "random" names and look up their ISRC codes; while you should think about how truly random this approach is, I think it is a good way forward and can be improved in many ways.

Share not send source code
I would first suggest assisting you to move your work to GitHub, because then we do not need to send source code files and can gradually improve and document the code. If you come in to Apollo 14, perhaps on Friday afternoon or whenever you are not in IViR, we could spend an hour making sure that you know how to do this, how to make sure that your Spotify secret key credentials remain secret, etc.

MusicBrainz -&gt; more efficent through direct database dump
Second, I think that this approach can be scaled up with MusicBrainz to a next level -- though maybe still not very satisfactory --, because MusicBrainz allows users to download their entire database. This means that you can avoid querying their APIs.  We just need to make sure that we download the large database and then select and streamline only the tables we need: artist names and tracks.

A few potential improvements on randomness following the "random" name querry
A third idea could be to find a dense part of an ID, which can be the MusicBrainz ID or the Spotify ID and "dial"  a few digits. So, the idea is the same as masking hopefully uncorrelated ISRC numbers with the name; for example, moving from "Japanese Breakfast"  to the search term "Breakfast" only gives a bunch of really unrelated artists, but still, I am concerned that using an English-language word will leave us in a certain geographical and genre space.
 For example, here is
- a Spotify Track ID https://open.spotify.com/track/5rQEom98vgByjAZ4kIw2kL
- with the artist ID https://open.spotify.com/artist/7MoIc5s9KXolCBH1fy9kkw  [stage name: Japanese Breakfast]
- the tracks's ISRC is  USJ5G1713302

My idea would be to "dial" something like 5rQEom98vgByjAZ4kIw2kL to 6rQEom98vgByjAZ4kIw2kL
or 7MoIc5s9KXolCBH1fy9kkw to 7NoIc5s9KXolCBH1fy9kkw

Just to recap, if you "dial" the USJ5G1713302  to 3301 there is no randomness at all:  3302 is the 2nd track on the album where the song was released and 3301 is the first (i.e. same artist, same label, same released album, just different track.)  Dialing US to BR is likely to result in no track, because the rest of the code is differently managed by the BR and US registrars, etc  . I am just guessing that 33 was the 33rd release of this particular label in the "US" registry in the year 2017.

Unfortunately, these IDs are designed to be sparse (i.e. that Spotify will not run out of them for a very long time), so it is a bit tricky to know what may be a dense element in it.  But if we find such a "dial", I am almost certain that unlike "dialing" the ISRC, it will be random, because I am 99.9% certain that Spotify's engineers use random hash generators for the IDs.

Scale up on Slovakia
In Slovakia we have a near-complete database  that I will have access to in May.  That database is only 15% filled with ISRC codes, however, I think it is a near complete name database of every artists who has something to do with Slovakia. This means that randomly picking a name from that name table will almost certainly cover extremely well the Slovak space.  So your approach can be very well scaled to one of our target countries, and I think that we can replicate this in Bulgaria and Hungary, too.  While the CMOs will not give you a full name list, I think we can arrange that we can get repeated random samples of their full name lists.

Best regards,
Daniel





On Tue, Apr 30, 2024 at 3:08 PM Fábio Generoso Vieira &lt;f.v.vieira@uva.nl&lt;mailto:f.v.vieira@uva.nl&gt;&gt; wrote:
Dear guys,

Firstly, sorry if this email is too long.

I think I figured out a way to get some random samples from ISRCs stratified by country as we discussed in our last meeting.

After the meeting, Daniel sent me an email with an idea. So, just to recap, the idea was basically to randomly get some artists names and then look for songs of those artists. This way, instead of creating a random sample of ISRCs, we create a random sample of artists, and getting some tracks of these artists would be the same as getting random ISRCs. However, given that Spotify does not associate artists to any country, the problem of country-wise stratification would persist.

Thus, what I am doing is basically integrating the Spotify data base (which seems to be by far the best source of ISRCs) with the MusicBrainz data base (which is a decent source for artist data and contains the country). So, I can randomly get artists from a particular country from MusicBrainz and then look for tracks of those artists on Spotify.

Just as an example, I ran this algorithm for Italy and Slovakia. Below you can see plots with the distribution of the frequencies in the country code of the ISRCs extracted.

[cid:image001.png@01DA9BDC.1C83EFD0][cid:image002.png@01DA9BDC.1C83EFD0]

I am sending the code I used to generate the samples and make this plots. The file random_samples.R contains the function I wrote and the file sampling_SK_and_IT.R generates the above plots (which might slightly change every time you run). All you need is the Spotify’s API credentials to make it work.

Anyway, I have tried a bunch of other stuff and I am not sure what could be useful at this point. Maybe we could schedule a new meeting (maybe next week?) to see whether I have anything useful or not for now.

Thanks!

Best,
Fabio

Firstly, sorry if this email is too long.

I think I figured out a way to get some random samples from ISRCs stratified by country as we discussed in our last meeting.

After the meeting, Daniel sent me an email with an idea. So, just to recap, the idea was basically to randomly get some artists names and then look for songs of those artists. This way, instead of creating a random sample of ISRCs, we create a random sample of artists, and getting some tracks of these artists would be the same as getting random ISRCs. However, given that Spotify does not associate artists to any country, the problem of country-wise stratification would persist.

Thus, what I am doing is basically integrating the Spotify data base (which seems to be by far the best source of ISRCs) with the MusicBrainz data base (which is a decent source for artist data and contains the country). So, I can randomly get artists from a particular country from MusicBrainz and then look for tracks of those artists on Spotify.

Just as an example, I ran this algorithm for Italy and Slovakia. Below you can see plots with the distribution of the frequencies in the country code of the ISRCs extracted.

[cid:image003.png@01DA9C7B.EB893840][cid:image004.png@01DA9C7B.EB893840]

I am sending the code I used to generate the samples and make this plots. The file random_samples.R contains the function I wrote and the file sampling_SK_and_IT.R generates the above plots (which might slightly change every time you run). All you need is the Spotify’s API credentials to make it work.

Anyway, I have tried a bunch of other stuff and I am not sure what could be useful at this point. Maybe we could schedule a new meeting (maybe next week?) to see whether I have anything useful or not for now.

Thanks!

Best,
Fabio

### Re: Deliverable 5.1 due this week - and start planning for exploitation with SOZA, ALOADED and HearDis {#email-433}

**From:** Felix Haaksman [HearDis!] &lt;felix.haaksman@heardis.com&gt;  
**To:** Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;  
**Cc:** Istvan Burus &lt;istvan.burus@reprex.nl&gt;, adam.lazar@openproduction.eu  
**Date:** 05/30/2024 14:35:08

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202405301435-Re_ Deliverable 5.1 due this week - and start plan-206.txt -->

Hi Daniel,

we briefly described what we want to do in the DMO Personas document:

*Creating reports for different CMOs*
*HearDis! wants to submit playlists with accurate metadata to PROs to make
sure the composer(s) and music publisher(s) get paid for the public
performance of their musical works in the In-Store Music domain. HearDis!
uses an elaborated audio content management platform to manage the metadata
of the music and to schedule the music into playlists for In-Store music
usage. To date, the platform focused on the description of tracks from the
musical perspective, while information about the artists who worked on it
had only a marginal role. The platform is already using external data
sources (such as Discogs) to import metadata via API. Via an API the
recordings should be matched with a publicly available database to retrieve
the metadata of composer(s) and music publisher(s). The metadata should be
stored in the metadata dataset of each recording. *


*Boutique Hotel Hamburg*



*The music curator accesses the HearDis! platform, navigates to the library
and specifies a city/region in the search criteria. The system then returns
all the relevant tracks that have one of the following criteria matching: -
lyrics mention the requested city/region- artist is from the requested
city/region- label is from the requested city/region- album/song title is
from the requested city/regionThe HearDis! music curator can go through the
results further refining the criteria based on the client’s briefing.
Additionally, she e can get inspired to acquire new music via standard web
stores for HearDis! based on artists and collabs. Having reliable, updated
and automatic metadata of artists, labels, songs etc. that are based in a
certain city or area to easily fulfil such wishes of clients with more
efficiency and especially with way less manual labour/research involved.
This would also create a foolproof method for such cases because manual
research can also lead to easier mistakes all the time, whereas a reliable
external data catalogue is usually always more accurate and the information
is easier to interpret and to handle.*

Does this help?
Anything more technical needs to come from Stefano.

To put it in a nutshell: we already have an audio CMS platform where we
store the metadata of the music recordings we need for the instore music
curation.
Currently we cannot automatically fetch the metadata for the above
mentioned scenarios.

Best,
Felix

Dear Daniel,

Thank you for this. A correct question bank of the former CEEMID CAP and MSME questions and answer items would be tremendously helpful. UTU has made a commitment to support our surveying teams in creating DDI-compliant

I've created a Wikibase account and am exploring. Do you think it would be sufficient to learn to use Wikibase cloud, or are there significant advantages to running it locally using Docker? I am familiar with Docker from personal work, but our IT lead doesn't really like to let us use it.

I think that SOEP is very easy to work with: both the questionnaire repository and question bank (https://paneldata.org/soep-core/) and the help site, which includes a section on working with SOEP documentation (https://companion.soep.de/index.html#). I'm pretty sure everything they do is DDI compliant. The only thing I could not find was the option to export into different formats, which would be an immediate value-add!

James




________________________________
From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Wednesday, May 8, 2024 6:52 PM
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Cc: Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;; Arianna Martinelli &lt;Arianna.Martinelli@santannapisa.it&gt;
Subject: Background survey question banks

Hi James,

Regardless of whether UTU will work with it or not, I would like to create a correct question bank of the former CEEMID CAP - MSME questions and answer items in a format that can be placed into the OMO. It can be published on the EOSC Cloud and the EU Open Data portal.

I must admit that the DDI documentation is challenging to read, and if you can find a peer-reviewer for our work, it may help, but I think that we will crack it because we do not need to be compliant with the entire DDI; only with a small part of it. We will adequately describe Questions, Question Blocks, etc (these are required for the survey) and Variables (for the data representation), disregarding analysis, processing, archiving, etc. As a further improvement, we will synchronise label translation properly and map the resulting Variables into standard thesauri and vocabularies.

We will upload the multi-language questionnaire used for SurveyHarmonies into a Wikibase instance (the same software that manages Wikidata) to be exported into a DDI-C compliant XML, JSON, RDF/XML, or TTL file. It should work with almost any survey fieldwork software. It would be good if you and your colleagues learned to use this system because it is very easy to use and fulfils all FAIR, EOSC, DDI, etc., requirements.

If you agree with this approach, then I would like you to show me a few question bank descriptions (not technical ones, but instances of questionnaire item documentation) that you think you can efficiently work with or that you find useful. We would use them as reference documents for tutorials and checking if our system works well. We want to place the question bank into the OMO by 31 May.

Best regards,

### OpenMusE -- MUSICAUTOR pilot study "gap analysis" {#email-440}

**From:** James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**To:** Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;, Burus István &lt;istvan.burus@reprex.nl&gt;, Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;  
**Date:** 05/13/2024 17:21:41

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202405131721-OpenMusE -- MUSICAUTOR pilot study _gap analysis_-468.txt -->

Hi all,

I pitched to Rosina the idea of MUSICAUTOR taking part in the WP2 and/or WP1 pilot study in a reduced manner by producing a "gap analysis" – i.e., a policy brief on what barriers prevent full replication in Bulgaria and how they could be overcome.

She was initially sceptical, but warmed up to the idea under certain conditions, such as:


  *
No intensive involvement or decisions required by senior management or the board (e.g., no new legal agreements)
  *
The work would be mostly doable by her and her immediate colleagues (e.g., nothing too technical)
  *
The work could be done *after* the release of significant outputs from the main pilot study countries, that she and her colleagues could review
  *
The primary target audience would be stakeholders that MUSICAUTOR wants to engage (e.g., national-level policymakers)
  *
The primary outputs would be standard (human-readable) documents in Bulgarian

IMO, getting her to buy into this would be a good backup for checking the "transfer potential" box (though obviously no substitute for actual replication, which we should still make our #1 goal).

What do you think? @Tomas, you mentioned that in the Slovak case, an preliminary, low-barrier step such as this was actually taken before SOZA committed to the full valuation study...? I didn't fully understand the details, maybe we could go through them. If SOZA also began this "journey" with a step-by-step approach, this could help us convince Rosina.

Best regards,
James
