**Date:** 05/13/2024 17:34:00

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202405131734-Re_ OpenMusE PMB -- amendment draft and discussion-469.txt -->

Dear OpenMusE PMB members,

Thank you all again for last week's productive meeting. I'm writing to let you know of a request by our Project Officer to add an extension of two to three months into our amendment. This means that the project would end on Feb 28 or Mar 31 2026.

As the amendment process itself has cost us two to three months, I think this would be beneficial. My suggestion is:


  *
Retain all current task and deliverable timeframes for WP1-4 (e.g., these tasks end in M36)
  *
Extend the WP5 and WP6 timeframes to M39 (March 2026)
  *
Revise only the following two deliverable deadlines to M39 (March 2026):
     *
D5.4 Final communication, dissemination, exploitation plan
     *
D5.7 Policy brief 2

This incentivises us to finish our scientific work "on time" according to the original plan, and ensures that nobody has to worry about hiring beyond 2025.

However, we gain three months at the end for dissemination and exploitation. This could help us squeeze through the submission deadlines for journals, conferences, industry showcases, etc. It also puts us in a good position to showcase final results alongside our sister projects, who started later.

If all PMB members or at least WP leaders can let us know what you think by Wednesday, we can consider adding this to the GA agenda on Friday.

Thank you and best regards,
James

**To:** Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;, Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;  
**Cc:** Burus István &lt;istvan.burus@reprex.nl&gt;  
**Date:** 05/14/2024 08:57:06

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202405140857-Re_ OpenMusE -- MUSICAUTOR pilot study _gap analys-471.txt -->

Hi Daniel,

Thanks for your quick response.

Re: the WP1 pilot study, I understand your point re: impact on the ARTISJUS case.

We cannot try to compel MUSICAUTOR to participate without the risk of pushing them out completely. However, we *can* produce meaningful outputs in Hungary and Slovakia by mid-2025, and demonstrate proof of a smooth cooperation. This could change their mind. A data-sharing MoU signed by project close would not count as "replication", but it would be a positive result we could share in our final review.

Re: the WP2 pilot study, @Mikš Tomáš&lt;mailto:tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt; would you be available for a 15-minute call with me within the coming days to prepare a pitch, and then a 30-minute call with Rosina at some point to explain what would be expected of her?

Thanks again and best regards,
James
________________________________
From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Monday, May 13, 2024 7:48 PM
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Cc: Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;; Burus István &lt;istvan.burus@reprex.nl&gt;
Subject: Re: OpenMusE -- MUSICAUTOR pilot study "gap analysis"

Hi James,

I think that this is a very good approach for WP2 and it is a very bad approach for WP1. There is a big legal difference between the two works. In WP1, we claim that we have a solution that correctly applies binding international and EU law, and it is applicable everywhere in Europe.  They cannot do a gap analysis showing that this is not the case, that would undermine Artisjus's legal use case. What we do in WP1 is fully replicable in Bulgaria, and in fact, I think that the management and the board of Musicautor has a fiduciary duty to its members to create valuations. Also, I think that it is implicitly their duty as a CISAC and GESAC member society, because they have to provide proper representation to the foreign repertoires that they represent in Bulgaria.

In WP2, we do something that is not expected from a collective management organisation, and it is something of an extra that they can do for their members, or to perform their core tasks better.  So I think that the gap analysis argument is very problematic in the case of WP1, but it is a valid argument for WP2.

Best regards,
Daniel

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;

Subject: Background survey question banks

Hi James,

Regardless of whether UTU will work with it or not, I would like to create a correct question bank of the former CEEMID CAP - MSME questions and answer items in a format that can be placed into the OMO. It can be published on the EOSC Cloud and the EU Open Data portal.

I must admit that the DDI documentation is challenging to read, and if you can find a peer-reviewer for our work, it may help, but I think that we will crack it because we do not need to be compliant with the entire DDI; only with a small part of it. We will adequately describe Questions, Question Blocks, etc (these are required for the survey) and Variables (for the data representation), disregarding analysis, processing, archiving, etc. As a further improvement, we will synchronise label translation properly and map the resulting Variables into standard thesauri and vocabularies.

We will upload the multi-language questionnaire used for SurveyHarmonies into a Wikibase instance (the same software that manages Wikidata) to be exported into a DDI-C compliant XML, JSON, RDF/XML, or TTL file. It should work with almost any survey fieldwork software. It would be good if you and your colleagues learned to use this system because it is very easy to use and fulfils all FAIR, EOSC, DDI, etc., requirements.

If you agree with this approach, then I would like you to show me a few question bank descriptions (not technical ones, but instances of questionnaire item documentation) that you think you can efficiently work with or that you find useful. We would use them as reference documents for tutorials and checking if our system works well. We want to place the question bank into the OMO by 31 May.

Best regards,

Subject: Replication cases - WP1

Hi James and Tomas,

I had a conversation with the economist of Music Sweden. There is a very slight chance that they would do the full market valuation model in Sweden, but they would be very keen on a partial replication with our surveys.

@Poort, Joost&lt;mailto:J.P.Poort@uva.nl&gt; @Arianna Martinelli&lt;mailto:arianna.martinelli@santannapisa.it&gt;  I did not include you in all the conversations, we are frantically trying to find with Tomas a country where we can replace MusicAutor who want to leave the consortium and will not do the case study in WP1.

They anyway want to do a music production survey to get consistent valuation of live and recorded music (what is our model is about) and they are particularly interested in measuring the gross value added of live music, and live music exports.  There is a slight chance that they would even bring into the question UK Music, because they are working with them as well.

The original idea of "valuation" in the grant agreement is a microeconomic valuation and is meant for valuing the royalty streams of Artisjus, SOZA, Musicautor, but I am inclined to think that we could twist the words to use it for a macro-level valuation.  They want to have figures on the GVA (part of GDP) of recorded and live music in Sweden, but not the particular value and price of say, public performance in television (what MusicAutor originally wanted and what is far more close to what we promised to do.)

I still believe that ZAIKS and perhaps SABAM are or main targets, because they are far more similar in needs to Artisjus, but having Music Sweden on board will probably not cost as anything and can be a fallback option.

I did not yet mention to them the work we are doing with Fabio and ALOADED, so there is a slight chance that we can go one step further, but I did not want to go all in and at least to have them on board for the MSME survey would be a great plus.

Best regards,

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;

Cc: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Subject: Re: Replication of valuations

Dear Tomas,
I wrote an page of summary about our work and its benefits, and copied the short document we wrote with Eszter Kabai that started our fruitful cooperation with the EU.
In 2014, Artisjus, SOZA and HDS started cooperation to measure together the value of music. In this cooperation, we have tried out all music valuation methods recognized by WIPO in practice. We developed a data model and a methodology to use data harmonized by CISAC and harmonized statistical questionnaires to consolidate data from CISAC member societies' own databases (the CISAC Financial database), public financial statements, and missing data that can be collected with questionnaires.

As a result, societies were able to correctly measure the value of their music in use, including private copying and the earlier contentious "value gap." This helped both SOZA and Artisjus revalue parts of their rights, adjust their collection targets and tariffs, and significantly increase revenues.

The DG EAC, cultural policy unit, recognized our methodology as a best practice and encouraged us to apply for a Horizon Europe grant to provide a further scientific underpinning to these models and create tools that allow the repeated, easier, cheaper repetition of these valuations.

Based on this work, the following reports were made:

-          First public Hungarian music industry report&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/publication/hungary_music_industry_2014/&gt;, for advocacy, tax changes in 2014, repeated many times.

-          Five non-public Artisjus valuation reports in 2014, 2015, 2017, 2018, 2019.

-          First non-public SOZA music industry report for advocacy, and first pubic Slovak music industry&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/publication/slovak_music_industry_2019/&gt; report for advocacy, better pricing and better taxation, 2019.  Non-public SOZA/SLOVGRAM/LITA valuation reports in 2018 and 2021.

-          Croatian PCR report&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/publication/private_copying_croatia_2019/&gt;, 2019.

-          Comparative Central European Music Industry Report, deemed as best practice by DG EAC, 2020.

In 2025, Artisjus will create a new, further enhanced valuation with the Horizon Europe grant, providing an opportunity for Zaiks to do the same. We need a "replication" case in a country that has not done these valuations before. We can provide financial support for the work by paying for the two surveys necessary to carry out the valuations (50,000 euros).

As a result, we can offer ZAIKS both an advocacy report (which must be public but contains information that does not jeopardize any royalty negotiations) and a private version that can be used, like in Slovakia, Hungary, and Croatia, to revalue underperforming royalty streams.

Our project also includes various data enrichment and data improvement tasks that can benefit ZAIKS and its members, too. We started to take effective measures to understand the low metadata quality on online platforms and ways how we could reduce the costs and error rates of such data. Participation in these project elements would be also possible free of charge.

Further information: Tomas Miks, member of the SOZA management team, Eszter Kabai dr, head of legal at Artisjus, Daniel Antal CFA, the economist who developed the models together with Aritsjus, SOZA and HDS colleagues.



Best regards,
Daniel Antal, CFA

### Re: Submission of D5.1 - AI REVIEW questions {#email-458}

**From:** Richard Wages &lt;Richard.Wages@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**To:** Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;, James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;

**Date:** 05/24/2024 21:14:26

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202405242114-Re_ Submission of D5.1 - AI REVIEW questions-823.txt -->

Hi Daniel,

I suggest the following procedure which I expect to find the approval of the PO and the external reviewers:

The upcoming deliverable: D5.1 should contain:

  1.  A statement that the consortium is aware that AI is used. No extra mentioning/discussion of past ‘statements on the non-use of AI’ is necessary at all at this point.
  2.  A short description of the AI systems used, their capabilities, how the are used and the advantages to do so.
  3.  A self-assessment on the potential entailed dangers of this AI use, plus measures taken to minimise these.
  4.  A statement that this use will be brought to the attention to and be discussed with the Ethics Advisor (Ms. Bauer), eg, during an upcoming meeting of the Ethics Board (second half of 2024)
Optimally, make this entire part its own (short) chapter “Use of AI Systems” in D5.1.

As soon as D5.1 has been greenlit by the external reviewers @James Rhys Edwards&lt;mailto:JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt; as the chair of the Ethics Board will inform Ms. Bauer and forward D5.1 to her to make her aware of this AI use.

After meetings of the Ethics Board Ms. Bauer will reflect on the project’s use of AI and assess the potential dangers and our handling of the matter in her annual report (OEI Requirement 3) which in return will be included in deliverable D7.4 in M24. The PO and the external reviewers will thus be provided with an Ethics expert’s assessment of the situation. I can hardly see any scenario in which they would diverge from this assessment.

And all should be fine.

Cheers,
Richard

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Friday, 24 May 2024 18:17
To: Richard Wages &lt;Richard.Wages@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Cc: Burus István &lt;istvan.burus@reprex.nl&gt;; James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;; Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Subject: Re: Submission of D5.1 - AI REVIEW questions

Hi Richard,

I have one not question regarding the deliverable, and I would like to know when we are supposed to turn for advice to our ethic reviewer, Dr. Bauer.  The document that you will get on Thursday after in-house reviews by several partners will describe the  OMO how it will function. Some of these functions will be working from that day and can be tried out, others will only work if we will get more data. The report will describe what is immediately usable and what will be turned on later (as in the grant agreement, which states that the OMO will be updated til M36.)

Earlier I stated that we will not apply AI, but two partners had data needs that are best supplied with AI. One of the functionalities is the so-called "identity alignment", which is a requirement that was indicated by HearDis and SOZA. In layman terms this means that we try to find out what is the ISRC code of a music work identified with an ISWC code or vica versa.  This is important for the management of different rights. For this procedure, we will apply various algorithms that fall under the scope of the new AI Act.

At this point, we do not have enough data to start to do "identity alignment", so we have not used AI without control. But we plan to do it, even though this is certainly "low risk" AI. I would like to state in the report the procedure correctly.  So, my questions in:

- Do we need to send this part to Dr Bauer?
- If not, shall we indicate when she will review what we are doing in this aspect?

I want to avoid technical reviewers saying, hey, this is AI, do these guys have the correct procedure?

Best regards,
Daniel

Hi Adam,

Sorry, but I didn’t track the changes while editing. However, all is not lost: you can generate a side-by-side document comparison in Word automatically.


  *   Open a new document in Word.
  *   In the upper menu, click Review.
  *   Click Compare, and then click Compare Documents.
  *   Choose your document as ‘original’ and mine as ‘revision’.
  *   Click OK.

Hope this does the trick for you.

Note: the document I received was set to ‘English US’, thus a vast number of non-UK spellings will not be indicated. Also, a recurring error was ‘feasibilty’. But please do not worry – compared to other deliverables I received this one meant rather low effort for me.

Cheers,
Richard

Dear all,

We have received a request for a presentation template for the review meeting on June 21st, so we quickly set one up, which you can find attached.
The template is our normal presentation template, with additional information on what is expected on slide 2. The presentations should follow the structure of each WP chapter in the periodic report. We will send you the WP3 presentation as an example by the end of the week.

As you might have already seen in the meeting agenda (see attachment), one presentation is needed per WP. The only exception is WP5, which we divided into one presentation about the OMO and one about communication, dissemination, and exploitation in general. Each presentation should last 20 minutes, plus 10 minutes of Q&amp;A by the EC.

Please send us your presentations by June 14th and feel free to contact us if you have any questions.

Thank you very much in advance!

Before last week's PMB, I briefly suggested a meeting in Budapest to plan our forthcoming surveys. This is because one major aim of all of our surveys (music MSME, music professional, music audience / cultural access and participation) is to provide data inputs for the music valuation pilot study conducted by REPREX on behalf of ARTISJUS.



Now that the revised work plan has been approved, we should begin to follow up on that. As we must finalise the questionnaires in Autumn, we should do this before the summer holiday.



@ARTISJUS team, are there particular windows in June or July, during which you are / are not available? I think it should be possible for the other partners to plan around your schedules.



One idea, if it works for you and for Arianna and Daniel, is to come to Budapest some time during the week preceding the project's interim review meeting on 21 June. Please let me know what you think.



Thank you and best regards,

James



PS. Attached for everyone's reference are a summary of the surveys and survey-type data collection we'll conduct, and a summary Daniel created of issues that arose during the CEEMID CAP surveys.

Subject: Re: submitted - RE: D5.1 Deliverable

Hi James,

Regarding the issue of double funding/financing, it is on one hand (and most importantly) an accounting issue - we have to make sure that the same expenditure (e.g. someone's working hours) are not reported towards two grants - it's a very clear-cut issue, and I don't think there is such risk.
The other way double funding/financing is often meant is that the same "action" cannot be financed by two grants. This is much less clear cut in general, however, I think this can also be neatly laid out in the spreadsheet you mentioned (can you share with me the previous version please).
What we are doing within Task 5.1 on the level of activities is presented in the periodic reports. I think what we provided for the first periodic report works well in this regard, and I think it can be a basis for updating the spreadsheet. As for activities beyond 2023 (and work on the observatory very much accelerated in 2024), this will be presented in the second periodic report. If you believe that a summary of activities carried out in 2024 is something that will have to be done for the review meeting covering 2023, please let us know.

As for presenting previous and/or non-project-funded work/results on the website of the Observatory, I think it is fully in line with how the observatory has been presented both in the GA and in subsequent project documents. The previous version of the observatory was always presented as a background to the current version. Also, the observatory has always been presented as a dissemination channel presenting work that is relevant to its topic beyond the project as well (for an example see https://music.dataobservatory.eu/publication/sustainability_guide_enterprising_musicians/)

As for the 3.3.4 and 3.3.5 of the deliverable, that's indeed an unfortunate clerical error, however fortunately it does not affect the comprehensibility of the deliverable greatly - the reviewers can and probably will visit the website itself instead of looking at screenshots only. However, we may indicate this to the PO and ask her to allow the upload of an updated deliverable version.

Best,

Istvan

Hi James,

We will think it through. This is a website, not the observatory, and we have not even had the review of the last year.

To me it is a greater concern that we do not have data. Right now we are trying to integrate with the EU Open Data Portal and Europeana, and those are clearly EU digital services. They have their rules on how they give attribution to everything. The data will be there, provided that we get them from partners (we are already testing placing and publishing on the EU Open Data Portal, but we have not yet got data to place on Europeana).

In my view, the biggest problem of this observatory is that there are no stakeholders and no data present. We are working on this, as much as our WP is concerned. So, if you want to make it look better, perhaps making sure that the other WPs invite representative stakeholders and provide us data to publish is a higher priority. An empty website will not be reviewed positively.  So far, we are only receiving data from Slovakia, and I am nudging A38 to give me something before their contract is made. (Can I already make a contract with them?)

I'll discuss this with Istvan and we will figure out what is EU funded and what is not and what needs to be attributed to how. If we need to present this in the interim review (do we?) then it will be thoroughly reviewed.

Best regards,
Daniel

### Re: submitted - RE: D5.1 Deliverable {#email-508}

**From:** James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;

**Date:** 06/06/2024 09:32:25

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202406060932-Re_ submitted - RE_ D5.1 Deliverable-493.txt -->

Hi Daniel,

Tuesday 11 works for me. You're correct that nominally, the OMO shouldn't be part of the review – however, in my experience it is not uncommon to "informally" introduce work done in early year two. We should choreograph it as the natural culmination of work done in year one. In this case, that's true: even though most of the actual programming work was done in year two (to my knowledge), the conceptual foundations for the data coordination model were refined in year one through your various interactions with the Slovak stakeholders on the one hand, and the linked open data community on the other (as you describe in your inputs to the periodic report). If we clearly present those interactions in a simple, more-or-less chronological form (with visuals, as done for Slovakia on pg. 23 of the PDF deliverable), then walk through the repositories, it will make sense. In my opinion we don't necessarily even have to show the website yet: just the repositories themselves. But it's 100% your call.

Re: the distinction between the "Open Music Observatory" and the website, this is clear now and of course you're correct. However, note that I made this slip despite having read the Feasibility Study multiple times and being very familiar with the fact that an Observatory is a technical and institutional infrastructure rather than just a dashboard. I think when many lay persons hear the words "data observatory", they imagine a dashboard: a place where with a few clicks, they can "observe data", as it were. Hopefully the reviewers will have read up on the concept and not make this mistake, but based on past experience, it is equally possible they come into the meeting without having done any homework at all.

The difference is clearly explained on the "About" page of the current website, but maybe we should make it even more evident via a very short text in the header...? This is just something to consider. To this end, even though it's not "software", it might make sense to add the final website to the applications we UX / UI test in WP4.

Finally, while the PDF is full of helpful visuals, I didn't see a single visual mapping the dimensions and functions of the Open Music Observatory as a gesamt technical and institutional infrastructure – pg. 22 and pg. 70 are close... if it would be helpful, I could try to create such a visual and we could workshop it on Tuesday. This would also be a litmus test of how clearly I understand the concept, as I must have a crystal clear understanding by the time of the review meeting.

Thanks and best regards,
James

Subject: Re: submitted - RE: D5.1 Deliverable

Hi James,

Let's do then Tuesday 11.00 because that day later I have some difficult meetings.  What I meant with the other consortium members and all this conversation is that nominally the OMO should not be part of the interim review, but I think it can actually partly save the day if it is presented correctly. After all, this consortium got 3 million euros to create a prototype of a European Music Observatory.  If you try to see it as a website, it will be a failure, and if you isolate it from the consortium it will also not look good.

As a data project it is very successful and invited to all conferences and data people love it. But non-data people will miss the data from it, and rightly.  Because we are still not in a contract with Hudobne centrum and A38 who could have filled cool data in it, it does not look as good as I would like it to look at this point, but we can make it promise a lot, and look quite good by 21 June.  However, this will also require a correct choreography of the presentations. If it will be obvious that the OMO is empty and the rest of the consortium is not even pretending to work on music data, then it will just look odd.

I believe that we can make a good and promising presentation, and it will improve a lot in the next weeks, but it must not be seen as a website.  I can tell you that the had DG EAC liked what I do a lot, now the DC Connect also liked it, the data people love, but for music people you need to have music data in  it to look good. We at least have to promise that we are on it.

Best regards,
Daniel

Subject: Re: submitted - RE: D5.1 Deliverable

Hi James,

As soon as Hudobne centrum and A38 are onboard, we will have more and more data visible in the system, also on Europeana. We will also bring in some data. But I think that especially if you want an early presentation on the interim review about the OMO, there should be a clear understanding on what the OMO is and what it is not.

I think that we should have a proper call sometime soon. The observatory is supposed to be an organisation, a consortium of data owners and users who share data through us, or to be precise, via our data sharing space. The website is not an observatory, it is just a website. The website had always been there. SOZA and Artisjus have been always sharing data via this system, and we see that we will have some ALOADED data soon. There are 12 consortium members who never shared any data with us, or brought any data owner or user into this project.

I am presenting the OMO now in the Dataweek of DG Connect, and try to find potential members in the observatory stakeholder network. I will be more available next week, and hopefully by that time at least we have sorted things out with the EU Publications Office.

Best regards,
 Daniel

Hi James,

We will think it through. This is a website, not the observatory, and we have not even had the review of the last year.

To me it is a greater concern that we do not have data. Right now we are trying to integrate with the EU Open Data Portal and Europeana, and those are clearly EU digital services. They have their rules on how they give attribution to everything. The data will be there, provided that we get them from partners (we are already testing placing and publishing on the EU Open Data Portal, but we have not yet got data to place on Europeana).

In my view, the biggest problem of this observatory is that there are no stakeholders and no data present. We are working on this, as much as our WP is concerned. So, if you want to make it look better, perhaps making sure that the other WPs invite representative stakeholders and provide us data to publish is a higher priority. An empty website will not be reviewed positively.  So far, we are only receiving data from Slovakia, and I am nudging A38 to give me something before their contract is made. (Can I already make a contract with them?)

I'll discuss this with Istvan and we will figure out what is EU funded and what is not and what needs to be attributed to how. If we need to present this in the interim review (do we?) then it will be thoroughly reviewed.

Best regards,
Daniel

Subject: Re: submitted - RE: D5.1 Deliverable

Hi Daniel,

Tuesday 11 works for me. You're correct that nominally, the OMO shouldn't be part of the review – however, in my experience it is not uncommon to "informally" introduce work done in early year two. We should choreograph it as the natural culmination of work done in year one. In this case, that's true: even though most of the actual programming work was done in year two (to my knowledge), the conceptual foundations for the data coordination model were refined in year one through your various interactions with the Slovak stakeholders on the one hand, and the linked open data community on the other (as you describe in your inputs to the periodic report). If we clearly present those interactions in a simple, more-or-less chronological form (with visuals, as done for Slovakia on pg. 23 of the PDF deliverable), then walk through the repositories, it will make sense. In my opinion we don't necessarily even have to show the website yet: just the repositories themselves. But it's 100% your call.

Re: the distinction between the "Open Music Observatory" and the website, this is clear now and of course you're correct. However, note that I made this slip despite having read the Feasibility Study multiple times and being very familiar with the fact that an Observatory is a technical and institutional infrastructure rather than just a dashboard. I think when many lay persons hear the words "data observatory", they imagine a dashboard: a place where with a few clicks, they can "observe data", as it were. Hopefully the reviewers will have read up on the concept and not make this mistake, but based on past experience, it is equally possible they come into the meeting without having done any homework at all.

The difference is clearly explained on the "About" page of the current website, but maybe we should make it even more evident via a very short text in the header...? This is just something to consider. To this end, even though it's not "software", it might make sense to add the final website to the applications we UX / UI test in WP4.

Finally, while the PDF is full of helpful visuals, I didn't see a single visual mapping the dimensions and functions of the Open Music Observatory as a gesamt technical and institutional infrastructure – pg. 22 and pg. 70 are close... if it would be helpful, I could try to create such a visual and we could workshop it on Tuesday. This would also be a litmus test of how clearly I understand the concept, as I must have a crystal clear understanding by the time of the review meeting.

Thanks and best regards,
James

Subject: Re: submitted - RE: D5.1 Deliverable

Hi James,

Let's do then Tuesday 11.00 because that day later I have some difficult meetings.  What I meant with the other consortium members and all this conversation is that nominally the OMO should not be part of the interim review, but I think it can actually partly save the day if it is presented correctly. After all, this consortium got 3 million euros to create a prototype of a European Music Observatory.  If you try to see it as a website, it will be a failure, and if you isolate it from the consortium it will also not look good.

As a data project it is very successful and invited to all conferences and data people love it. But non-data people will miss the data from it, and rightly.  Because we are still not in a contract with Hudobne centrum and A38 who could have filled cool data in it, it does not look as good as I would like it to look at this point, but we can make it promise a lot, and look quite good by 21 June.  However, this will also require a correct choreography of the presentations. If it will be obvious that the OMO is empty and the rest of the consortium is not even pretending to work on music data, then it will just look odd.

I believe that we can make a good and promising presentation, and it will improve a lot in the next weeks, but it must not be seen as a website.  I can tell you that the had DG EAC liked what I do a lot, now the DC Connect also liked it, the data people love, but for music people you need to have music data in  it to look good. We at least have to promise that we are on it.

Best regards,
Daniel

Subject: Re: submitted - RE: D5.1 Deliverable

Hi James,

As soon as Hudobne centrum and A38 are onboard, we will have more and more data visible in the system, also on Europeana. We will also bring in some data. But I think that especially if you want an early presentation on the interim review about the OMO, there should be a clear understanding on what the OMO is and what it is not.

I think that we should have a proper call sometime soon. The observatory is supposed to be an organisation, a consortium of data owners and users who share data through us, or to be precise, via our data sharing space. The website is not an observatory, it is just a website. The website had always been there. SOZA and Artisjus have been always sharing data via this system, and we see that we will have some ALOADED data soon. There are 12 consortium members who never shared any data with us, or brought any data owner or user into this project.

I am presenting the OMO now in the Dataweek of DG Connect, and try to find potential members in the observatory stakeholder network. I will be more available next week, and hopefully by that time at least we have sorted things out with the EU Publications Office.

Best regards,
 Daniel

Subject: Re: submitted - RE: D5.1 Deliverable

Hi James,

We will think it through. This is a website, not the observatory, and we have not even had the review of the last year.

To me it is a greater concern that we do not have data. Right now we are trying to integrate with the EU Open Data Portal and Europeana, and those are clearly EU digital services. They have their rules on how they give attribution to everything. The data will be there, provided that we get them from partners (we are already testing placing and publishing on the EU Open Data Portal, but we have not yet got data to place on Europeana).

In my view, the biggest problem of this observatory is that there are no stakeholders and no data present. We are working on this, as much as our WP is concerned. So, if you want to make it look better, perhaps making sure that the other WPs invite representative stakeholders and provide us data to publish is a higher priority. An empty website will not be reviewed positively.  So far, we are only receiving data from Slovakia, and I am nudging A38 to give me something before their contract is made. (Can I already make a contract with them?)

I'll discuss this with Istvan and we will figure out what is EU funded and what is not and what needs to be attributed to how. If we need to present this in the interim review (do we?) then it will be thoroughly reviewed.

Best regards,
Daniel

________________________________
From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: 10 June 2024 17:22
To: Dominika Semanakova &lt;Dominika.Semanakova@soza.sk&gt;; Alona Dmukhovska &lt;alona.dmukhovska@gmail.com&gt;; Richard Demčák &lt;richard.demcak@soza.sk&gt;; James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;; Anna Zilkova &lt;anna.zilkova@hc.sk&gt;; Stefan Kragh &lt;stefan@aloaded.com&gt;
Cc: Adam Lazar &lt;adam.lazar@reprex.nl&gt;
Subject: Europeana publishing

Dear Colleagues,

I would like to send a first, test batch of content to Europeana, which is a very high-value platform, particularly in classical music, old music, jazz, authentic folk music, and established artists.  At this point, we want to test the publishing workflow; however, this is a very desirable service for music information centers, cultural centers, and I think for folk/jazz/classical repertoire owners, concert promoters or artists.

Unfortunately the Hudobné centrum does not have much such content, and we would like to find some of the "ambassadors" to provide us content, or some labels, or associations of old music, or any similar organisations. I would need about 50-100 assets, to start experimenting about the service workflow with the British Library and Europeana.

I think that this is a valuable service and it really requires nothing from the content owners and provides them free traffic and high value visibility.

This is a FAQ about how we can put things on Europeana, and what it is at all:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Odhe-cWbQw7Y9L-yriLlJU8aPA-E-OOawUzJv2KpSFk/edit#heading=h.lnij483rqhpg

And this is an example of the minimum information we need about an asset (sound recording, video, photo or music sheet.)
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1c0bTcUpeWyNZ8JGsmpFcbT2jU9Gki-ioTlmYrxPtdlQ/edit?usp=sharing

We will have more than enough content from A38, but because of their collection size it takes some time till we put it in order. However, they are a very atypical user, as they are professional music TV producers, and I would like to find some Slovak or other content too, and less professional content owners to prepare for all possible hickups.

https://music.dataobservatory.eu/data/europeana/

Can you help with giving me a some music, perhaps a musician with whom we could do a Data &amp; Lyrics interview and start the testing process a.s.a.p? (See for example: https://dataandlyrics.com/post/2023-02-24_airu/)

Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder
+31615058460
linkedin&lt;https://www.linkedin.com/in/antaldaniel/&gt; •  reprex bv&lt;http://reprex.nl/&gt;  • eviota&lt;https://eviota.nl/&gt;

I think that unless we get such a catalogue by tomorrow night we should let this go because it is not feasible to do it in less than a week.

Daniel

Subject: OpenMusE -- SOZA background declaration



Dear Tomáš and Richard,



In preparation for our meeting on surveying, we should revisit the issue of SOZA background. With regard to surveying, this should include as separate items:



1.                 Questionnaires, codebooks, documentation, etc. of surveys conducted by SOZA (music professional; music MSME; cultural access and participation)

  1.  The survey findings on an aggregated level (e.g., cross-tabulations)

  1.  The survey microdata



To fulfil the GA aim of harmonising survey questions, we only *need* access to item 1. Access to item 2 would be indispensable while eventually writing our reports on the music economy and on music, society, and citizenship. Access to item 3 would be helpful for more technical reasons, but not critical.



Of course, the declaration should also cover other background such as SKCMBd and Listen Local, but we need restrictions/conditions for access of survey-related background more critically, so we can make the formal requests.



Attached is the (nearly final) ARTISJUS background declaration for reference!



Thank you and best regards,

James

From: Marc Calmbach &lt;Marc.Calmbach@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:Marc.Calmbach@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt;
Sent: Monday, February 6, 2023 9:26 PM
To: OpenMusE Consortium &lt;openmuseconsortium@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:openmuseconsortium@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt;
Subject: CA version 1.6, ready for final approval





Dear partners,



SINUS is glad to announce that we have finalised the CA version 1.6 tonight.  We would kindly ask you to check the following sections:



  1.  Section 3.3 (survival of rights and obligations): a new closing sentence was added that explicitly states the survival of IPRs (intellectual property rights), as requested by ARTISJUS. We consider this addition helpful because it spells out that this section is also valid for IPRs.
  2.  Section 5.2 (liability): this section was in discussion during the Kick-Off, during which UVA expressed concerns. In dialogue with Joost (UVA – thank you very much for your input) we now have a text which leaves no place for ambiguity. It was fused together from the (clearer formulated) DESCA 1.2.4 for Horizon 2020 and the (more cautious) formulation of the new DESCA for Horizon Europe, i.e., in our view, the best of both worlds.
  3.  Section 6.1 (general structure): “Executive Board” changed to “Project Management Board”, as this is not an executive body in the governance sense of the term, but rather, a representative body charged with day-to-day project management.
  4.  Section 6.3 (governance): in consultation with Caterina (SSSA), Sections 6.3.1.1.2 and 6.3.2.1 (on the body chairs) have been approved by both the SINUS and REPREX teams. Caterina has our gratitude for sharing her expertise as a legal academic and experienced coordinator (as well as for her time).
  5.  Section 6.4.2 (management/directorial team): here, we have changed “Project Management Team” to “Directorial Team” to reflect the leadership roles of our internal experts. And we have changed the individual titles in accordance. The role of the ‘Project Ambassador’ (formerly ‘Evangelist’) was furthermore added. This addition found unanimous support among the project members who were still present at the last discussions in Bratislava on the 27th of January (Mark asked us to change the title from Evangelist to Ambassador).
  6.  Section 6.5.2 (external stakeholder representative bodies): here, we have changed “Observatory Stakeholder Network” to “Music Observatory Network” to pave a clearer pathway to the project’s hoped-for adoption as a European Music Observatory.



So: the differences between v1.5 and v1.6 are not dramatic, but they are meaningful. We would thus appreciate your immediate attention to the edits. If you are OK with the edits, send us an ‘OK with us’ by this Wednesday, 8th of February, 24:00. Once we have an OK from each partner, we will send out a clean version 1.7 right away.



In the meantime, we are working hard to define Background, which is critical to the implementation of the project. It would be beneficial to both the project and the interests of individual partners to declare Background ASAP.



We would like to finish this process, and get a signature on the CA v1.7 (including Background for each partner who chooses to declare) at best by this Wednesday, but no later than Friday, 17th February 18:00.



We would like to extend our thanks to all of the partners involved in this revision process, especially SSSA, UVA, UTU, and REPREX.



Thank you to everybody! Best regards,



Marc

Managing Director

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: 18 June 2024 11:59
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Cc: Balázs Huszák &lt;bhuszak@artisjus.com&gt;; Dr. Kabai Eszter &lt;ekabai@artisjus.com&gt;; Arianna Martinelli &lt;Arianna.Martinelli@santannapisa.it&gt;; Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;; Richard Demčák &lt;richard.demcak@soza.sk&gt;; marian.jankovic@soza.sk &lt;Marian.Jankovic@soza.sk&gt;; Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;; Burus István &lt;istvan.burus@reprex.nl&gt;
Subject: Re: Aligning ARTISJUS, SOZA, REPREX background access applications

Hello,

I think that the real question is really what we will do, so in several cases the background is referring to pending my approval. As neither Artisjus or SOZA or I have given a blanket permission for re-use, eventually we are back to what we wanted to discuss: exactly who wants to do what with this background.

So there are different aspects of this background.  First and foremost, we developed these questionnaires for the valuations, and this relates to the new WP1 that we want to do new valuations (if I am not mistaken, in Hungary and Poland.)  So the know-how on how to use the codebooks, questionbank, questionnaires and the resulting variables in valuations relates to that issue. I think that here we will decide case-by-case with Eszter and Balazs what we want to make public from the past to justify and improve the new model.

Then, there is the issue of being able to create harmonised surveys in WP3.  I do not think that this requires the re-use of the entire questionbank (questionnaires and codebooks.) However, when this is justified, I would like to put this into a standard, DDI and DCAT compliant, question bank for reuse. This question bank will have a Creative Commons license for reuses. One of the reasons why we give access to this background is that SINUS and the partners can translate the question, and SSSA and SINUS can develop further questions following the ICET methodology and hierarchy. These new items (i.e., new language versions and modified questions, or new questions) can be added to our questionbank, as a foreground of this project.

The questionbank as a linked, open dataset will be also a foreground from a technical point of view, but its background contents will be the items that Artisjus, SOZA and Reprex allows to put there. I think that these will be the questionnaire parts that are directly relevant for the valuations, or some general use cases, like sustainability, demography, that have nothing to do with royalty calculations.

If there are further uses envisioned, then we should discuss them at 16.00.

Best regards,
Daniel

### Re: GANTT presented {#email-543}

**From:** James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;

**Date:** 06/25/2024 10:25:24

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202406251025-Re_ GANTT presented-528.txt -->

Hi Daniel,

Thank you for the update.

Note here on the topic of communication style, I draw attention again to comments such as "it is a pity that the consortium did not come up so far with any data". I already know this, and you know I know it. The comment does not serve any purpose, other than to irritate me. Is this your intention? This does not have to be a discussion, the question is rhetorical. I merely want you to know that if your intended effect is to motivate me, you're achieving the opposite: "you catch more flies with honey than vinegar".

Returning to the topic at hand: the reviewers' concern was not that the web presence is under-engaging. Rather, they were confused by the co-existence of multiple websites/domains hosting overlapping and sometimes-identical content, sometimes labelled "open music observatory" (e.g., https://music.dataobservatory.eu/), other times labelled "digital music observatory" (e.g., https://dataobservatory.eu/observatories/music/), etc. One question: does REPREX intend to continue hosting and updating sites using the "digital music observatory" brand, or will you subsume everything into the "open music observatory" brand?

If you wish to keep using "digital music observatory", one idea would be to try amending D5.1 to "open music data space". This could constitute a unique project innovation, which you then subsume into the "digital music observatory" as an exploitation measure.

There is no guarantee that the reviewers will accept this, as delivering a data space is less substantial than delivering an "observatory". However, it's arguable that the latter was not well understood by either the reviewers or even the Consortium anyway.

We could have a call on this in the coming days if you have time.

Thanks and best regards,
James




[https://music.dataobservatory.eu/media/icon_hucb5a98ddbc2b506d08aa42cee80f29c1_33038_512x512_fill_lanczos_center_3.png]&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/&gt;

An open knowledge platform for the music industry
music.dataobservatory.eu

Digital Music Observatory | Automated Data Observatories&lt;https://dataobservatory.eu/observatories/music/&gt;
The Digital Music Observatory is a fully automated, open source, open data observatory that links public datasets in order to provide a comprehensive view of the European music industry.
dataobservatory.eu

From: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Sent: 25 June 2024 10:25
To: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Cc: Burus István &lt;istvan.burus@reprex.nl&gt;; Richard Wages &lt;Richard.Wages@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Subject: Re: GANTT presented

Hi Daniel,

Thank you for the update.

Note here on the topic of communication style, I draw attention again to comments such as "it is a pity that the consortium did not come up so far with any data". I already know this, and you know I know it. The comment does not serve any purpose, other than to irritate me. Is this your intention? This does not have to be a discussion, the question is rhetorical. I merely want you to know that if your intended effect is to motivate me, you're achieving the opposite: "you catch more flies with honey than vinegar".

Returning to the topic at hand: the reviewers' concern was not that the web presence is under-engaging. Rather, they were confused by the co-existence of multiple websites/domains hosting overlapping and sometimes-identical content, sometimes labelled "open music observatory" (e.g., https://music.dataobservatory.eu/), other times labelled "digital music observatory" (e.g., https://dataobservatory.eu/observatories/music/), etc. One question: does REPREX intend to continue hosting and updating sites using the "digital music observatory" brand, or will you subsume everything into the "open music observatory" brand?

If you wish to keep using "digital music observatory", one idea would be to try amending D5.1 to "open music data space". This could constitute a unique project innovation, which you then subsume into the "digital music observatory" as an exploitation measure.

There is no guarantee that the reviewers will accept this, as delivering a data space is less substantial than delivering an "observatory". However, it's arguable that the latter was not well understood by either the reviewers or even the Consortium anyway.

We could have a call on this in the coming days if you have time.

Thanks and best regards,
James

Regarding the communication, we will discuss these days with Chrisoph how we can integrate the new services well into the openmuse.eu&lt;http://openmuse.eu&gt; website.  However, this is still an issue because without data it is very difficult to have an engaging and captivating demonstration of what we can do with the data. It is a pity that the consortium did not come up so far with any data, because the CMO data is the most cumbersome to work with -- I already have quite some data in our system but it will take weeks to get through all checks and legal controls to release anything out of it.  But we will soon have things to show and then integrating their display to the project website will not be difficult.

Best regards,
Daniel

From: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt;
Sent: 25 June 2024 10:25

Cc: Burus István &lt;istvan.burus@reprex.nl&lt;mailto:istvan.burus@reprex.nl&gt;&gt;; Richard Wages &lt;Richard.Wages@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:Richard.Wages@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt;
Subject: Re: GANTT presented

Hi Daniel,

Thank you for the update.

Note here on the topic of communication style, I draw attention again to comments such as "it is a pity that the consortium did not come up so far with any data". I already know this, and you know I know it. The comment does not serve any purpose, other than to irritate me. Is this your intention? This does not have to be a discussion, the question is rhetorical. I merely want you to know that if your intended effect is to motivate me, you're achieving the opposite: "you catch more flies with honey than vinegar".

Returning to the topic at hand: the reviewers' concern was not that the web presence is under-engaging. Rather, they were confused by the co-existence of multiple websites/domains hosting overlapping and sometimes-identical content, sometimes labelled "open music observatory" (e.g., https://music.dataobservatory.eu/), other times labelled "digital music observatory" (e.g., https://dataobservatory.eu/observatories/music/), etc. One question: does REPREX intend to continue hosting and updating sites using the "digital music observatory" brand, or will you subsume everything into the "open music observatory" brand?

If you wish to keep using "digital music observatory", one idea would be to try amending D5.1 to "open music data space". This could constitute a unique project innovation, which you then subsume into the "digital music observatory" as an exploitation measure.

There is no guarantee that the reviewers will accept this, as delivering a data space is less substantial than delivering an "observatory". However, it's arguable that the latter was not well understood by either the reviewers or even the Consortium anyway.

We could have a call on this in the coming days if you have time.

Thanks and best regards,
James

Digital Music Observatory | Automated Data Observatories&lt;https://dataobservatory.eu/observatories/music/&gt;
The Digital Music Observatory is a fully automated, open source, open data observatory that links public datasets in order to provide a comprehensive view of the European music industry.
dataobservatory.eu&lt;http://dataobservatory.eu&gt;

Regarding the communication, we will discuss these days with Chrisoph how we can integrate the new services well into the openmuse.eu&lt;http://openmuse.eu&gt; website. It is a pity that the consortium did not come up so far with any data, because the CMO data is the most cumbersome to work with -- I already have quite some data in our system but it will take weeks to get through all checks and legal controls to release anything out of it.  But we will soon have things to show and then integrating their display to the project website will not be difficult.

Best regards,
Daniel

Subject: Re: Update on T3.4

Hi Anna,

To me it is still an open question what kind of sustainability indicators we are going to measure. If it is a social indicator, then this topic connects to the next meeting, because social data is mainly collected via surveys.  If it is an environmental indicator, then do not necessarily connect to that. We have collected all (or almost all, because in few cases the descriptions are ambiguous) indicators that the European Sustainability Reporting Standards have so far defined in the five environmental and four social matter areas. We have counted (not considering the ambiguities) so far 163 indicators, give or take, with some interesting social matters not having been defined yet (I enclose them in an Excel sheet.)

In my opinion, we can do sustainability reporting in a credible way if we measure a handful of these indicators with music organisations. We should be realistic, and find a focus, out of the 163 indicators if we can produce like 4 I think that is an achievement.

Best regards,
Daniel

Hi Daniel,

Yes, you are right! Album_release_date refers to the date in which the album was first released. There are some values for this variable that date before the internet. I don’t think Spotify existed at the time yet. Did I write something else there?

I understand. That makes sense. I will have a look. I didn’t know where to find this music ontology. Hopefully, they have all the descriptions there.

Do you know how to find these variables? I just checked and the pages all have a review history, with all the reviews ever made in that page. Is this what you’re talking about?

Also, regarding the variables I want to work with, it’s really hard to tell at this stage. I will think about what we have spoken so far, regarding estimating general popularity and income of a song and I’ll just come up with some variables like that. But I don’t know how realistic would be to get those data, that’s why I didn’t want to just define some variables out of the blue (I assumed this is not what you wanted me to do). Moreover, I think ideally we should keep everything that has a potential to be useful, right? If you have some recommendations about variables that we would want to use, that would be much appreciated.

Best,
Fabio

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Monday, July 8, 2024 3:47 PM
To: Fábio Generoso Vieira &lt;f.v.vieira@uva.nl&gt;
Subject: Comment on the variables

Hi Fabio,

This caught my eye:

spotify_album_release_date Spotify API album_release_date The date the album was first released.

I think this should be double checked: is this the release date on Spotify or the release date overall? I think it is the latter.

I think that your variables are well described from Spotify, now it would be important to start to look for a standard description. What is the more general version of the spotify_track_time_signature_value for example, if there is?

For standard descriptions, start with the Music Ontology, it is reliable, and cross check with Polifonia Music Match ontology. For example, Duration has a description in the Music Ontology http://purl.org/ontology/mo/duration (ontological_uri_1), just as well as "lablel" and many other things. The ontological definition is "The duration of a track or a signal in ms",
which is exactly the spotify definition, so in this case, spotify_track_duration_ms
will be immediately convertible to a duration_ms or simply duration variable.

Regarding Wikipedia, I think you can also look into variables like how many times a page was visited or modified.   I also made a comment about three of your entries.

Generally, I think taht you should be defining variables that you want to work with.

Best regards,




Daniel Antal, CFA

Best, Joost

Dear Mr.

With Fábio Generoso Vieira, on behalf of the University of Amsterdam, Danie Antal (the author of the Slovak Music Industry Report) and SOZA are working on an EU Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Action with creating better statistical data about European music. The focus of our work is randomly selecting sound recordings that were registered in Slovakia.
We would like to ask your assistance to understand better the way the CS (isn’t is CZ?) and SK ISRC codes have been assigned.
To our knowledge, the Slovak ISRC codes should take the following form:
SK-AAA-YY-NNNNN, like SK-K29-16-00101
Year of reference: YY part
- We sometimes see that the YY (16) part differs from the officially announced or coded release date (in the case of this song, Slnko Records officially released it in ’17)
- Are we correct to assume that the reason for this is that the range of codes given out to Slnko Records in 2016 is not yet filled, and they decided to put the recording later on the market?
- In your opinion, what is the longest possible difference between the release year signalled by the ISRC code and the actual release date?
- Is it possible that we find ISRC codes that are not in the range of 86-24, i.e., 1986 and 2024. Is it possible that earlier recordings were retroactively filled with, for example, a YY year code of 76?
Registrant code: AAA part (like K29)
- Can we assume that an identical AAA part, like K29 always relates to the same registering entity?
- Is the list of registering entities confidential or can we find it somewhere?
- If the names of the registering entities are confidential, can we get a list of valid AAA codes?
- Our aim is to create a “lottery” algorithm that randomly selects a song registered with the SK country code, we do not want to reveal trade secrets.
Changes over time
- Were there any changes when the ISRC code changed in 2001, or when the CZ and SK registrars separated in the way this is managed?
- Is it possible to know what is the total number of filled (assigned) ISRC codes starting with SK for each year? For example, if we know that there are 2x more recordings with YY=22 than with YY=08, than a random sample of songs should have twice as many 2022 recordings.

### OpenMusE Bergfest {#email-581}

**From:** Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;

**Date:** 07/08/2024 10:54:57

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202407081054-OpenMusE Bergfest-262.txt -->

Dear all,

As mentioned briefly during the interim review meeting, we would like to organize a "Bergfest" in fall to celebrate the half-time of our project!

We believe that this would be a great occasion to kick-off the project after the summer and the amendment, which will hopefully have passed by then! And since we know how important in-person meetings are for the team spirit within the consortium, we hope that all partners will be present! We would like to organize this meeting in Vienna (tbc), which should be rather easy for most partners.

The Bergfest will be planned over two days, including a GA meeting, smaller workshops to resolve lingering questions and generate ideas, and some time to connect and get to know Vienna! We would like to organize this meeting in late September (after EPIP and the Reeperbahn festival), or the first week of October. To find a date that works for as many people as possible, please fill in the following doodle: https://doodle.com/meeting/participate/id/dR53NJOb

Thank you very much in advance!

Best regards,

Isabella Tautscher

Hi Istvan,

We have to do both. As you know, the periodic report consists of two parts, the financial part, i.e. the partners' financial statements directly added into the ECAS, and the technical part, i.e. the written report on objectives, progress, deviations etc.

Concerning the financial requests made to the partners, SINUS cannot make any changes to your financial statements. So, if for example REPREX needs to change to unit costs, you will have to do this through the ECAS. Your explanations should also be made through the ECAS, as this is not only a request directed to the coordinator, but also to each partner mentioned on the first page of the EC's letter.

On top of this, SINUS will add the explanations to the technical part B under deviations, as you correctly observed, together with other minor changes, e.g. add the new gantt chart.

Once all changes to the financial part and the technical part are made, SINUS will resubmit the periodic report through the ECAS, i.e. click the submit button.

If you can send us the texts by Monday, that would be perfect!

Thank you very much and have a great weekend!

Best regards,

### OpenMusE Bergfest {#email-587}

**From:** Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**To:** OpenMusE Consortium &lt;openmuseconsortium@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**Cc:** James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;, Marc Calmbach &lt;Marc.Calmbach@sinus-institut.de&gt;, Christoph Steiner &lt;christoph.steiner@synyo.com&gt;  
**Date:** 07/23/2024 17:50:57

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202407231750-OpenMusE Bergfest-268.txt -->

Dear all,

Our project is halfway through, which we would like to celebrate with you at our Bergfest from September 30th to October 1st.
Indeed, the last year and a half have often felt like a tough hike up a steep mountain. We’ve finally arrived at a point in the project where we can enjoy the view before taking the (hopefully) easier path until the end of our hike 😊

Working with this symbolic, Synyo and Sinus will organize the Bergfest in the mountains surrounding Vienna, in Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;. It’s quite close to the city and can be reached by train&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt; in ca. 1 ½ hours from Vienna airport (see attachment) or 1 hour from the main train station (Hauptbahnhof).

The Bergfest will take place in the “Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt;”, a historic, old-school Austrian hotel in Reichenau.
We have blocked rooms for the consortium at a reduced price, which you need to book directly with the hotel! Please contact hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; and mention the “OpenMusE seminar”. Please also let them know if you need a shuttle from the train station in Reichenau (13€ p.p.).


We’re currently working on the agenda, which we will send out once it’s finalized with the WP leaders. On the program so far:

  *   Several workshops to boost the second half of our project
  *   A General Assembly
  *   A voluntary hike on Sept. 29th for all early birds
  *   Time to relax, enjoy the view, and make some noise


All details at a glance:

  *   Date: September 30th to October 1st (arrival on September 29th)
  *   Place: Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;
  *   Hotel: Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt; --&gt; please book your room directly with the hotel: hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; !
  *   Room prices:
     *   Sept. 29th to 30th: 100€ p.p. in an individual room including breakfast
     *   Sept. 30th to Oct. 1st: 165€ p.p. in an individual room, including breakfast lunch and dinner on Sept. 30th
     *   Any additional night: 100€ p.p. in an individual room including breakfast
  *   To plan your train ride, use the ÖBB website Home - ÖBB (oebb.at)&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt;, not Google Maps! The closest train station is “Payerbach-Reichenau” (see attachment)

To make this a proper team event, it would be great if 1-2 people could join per partner. Please fill in the following form to RSVP: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1JSlzhVlQzIE8rT-5_9K1IZyIDM6diwQzkZKIty8mQgg/edit?usp=sharing
Reminder: You have travel budgets for in-person meetings, which for most partners remain largely untouched. It would help neither the EC, nor your organization, to return unused budgets.


We are looking forward to celebrating with you!

Best regards,

Marc, James &amp; Isabella

## James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;

### OpenMusE -- replacing MUSICAUTOR in T1.1 {#email-588}

**From:** James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**To:** Joost Poort &lt;j.p.poort@uva.nl&gt;, Caterina Sganga &lt;caterina.sganga@santannapisa.it&gt;, Leo Lahti &lt;leo.lahti@utu.fi&gt;, Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;  
**Cc:** Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;, Marc Calmbach &lt;Marc.Calmbach@sinus-institut.de&gt;, Richard Wages &lt;Richard.Wages@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**Date:** 07/01/2024 16:47:55

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202407011647-OpenMusE -- replacing MUSICAUTOR in T1.1-540.txt -->

Dear WP leaders,

First off, many thanks again for your excellent contributions to our interim review. Thanks to our joint efforts, the result was a constructive meeting that credibly sets the stage for a renewal of the project.

I have excellent follow-up news: thanks to Tomas' efforts, the Polish Society of Authors ZAiKS is considering joining our project. This would solve the most significant problem facing the Consortium right now, which is how to replace MUSICAUTOR in the WP1 pilot study on valuation. Indeed, it would level it up significantly. Poland is a top-5 EU country by population and top-10 by GDP. Real, active participation by the dominant Polish rights management organisation would greatly magnify our project's impact.

Of course, there is a potential trade-off, which we would like to discuss openly. During our interim review, our PO stated a clear preference for replacing MUSICAUTOR with a new full partner rather than a subcontractor. Currently, due to MUSICAUTOR's low PM rate, we only have €13000 in the budget to offer ZAiKS. This is not enough to justify onboarding as a partner. Furthermore, both the low budget and the contractual description of the subcontractor / service provider roles would limit ZAiKS' scope of action in the project to replication of the pilot study. In principle, they could offer much more.

To that end, we are asking the major partners (those with over 200k in personnel costs) to sacrifice 1 PM each, thus freeing up budget for ZAiKS and/or our WP2 replication partner. This would allow us to offer them nearly 30k each  rather than just 13k each, *in case* they are open to an expanded role in the project. I firmly believe that the collective benefit to all of our institutions would greatly outweigh the budgetary impact for any one of us.

This will be on the agenda to discuss during our WP leader call on Friday at 9am. In the meantime, please give it thought and feel free to write or call with any questions.

Thank you, and best regards,
James







---

### Re: OpenMusE -- replacing MUSICAUTOR in T1.1 {#email-589}

**From:** James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**To:** Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;, Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;  
**Date:** 07/02/2024 11:31:46

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202407021131-Re_ OpenMusE -- replacing MUSICAUTOR in T1.1-541.txt -->

Hi Daniel,

Thank you for your response.

The revised work plan has already been approved by the Consortium and praised by the project officer and reviewers. I will not reopen the topic of task or resource transfers between current partners.

So, I will take this as a simple "no." That is within your rights and we accept it.

Best regards,
James
________________________________
From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: 02 July 2024 10:00
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;; Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;
Subject: Re: OpenMusE -- replacing MUSICAUTOR in T1.1

Hi James,

You already know my point of view, but I want to place it here, and find a better solution than taking 6250 euros from Reprex.

- I have made at least 7 presentations so far to make a credible, shoe-string budget replication of MusicAutor in WP2, and assisted Tomas with Zaiks
- Cultivate for Hudobne centrum as a subcontractor for over a year, with a lot of unbudgeted travel.
- I am holding back a scene with Fabio who wants to get in touch directly with the data manager of the project, because he does not understand why he has to write data exchange documentations as a statistical algorithm researcher
- In the review meeting, the WP1 passed with my work, WP4 presented a 14 years old software and my work.
- Replacing MusicAutor with two organisations in two countries will double my costs, because I will onboard them, serve them, manage them.

So my principled answer is the following:  I am willing to give up 1 PM in return for the official handover of the DMP.  Currently there is nobody working on data management on the project, and I am going to spend from my own money, I mean what I brought in from home, to hire a librarian, and assist, for example, UvA's postdoc.

The other reason why I find your proposal extremely unjust is that the other people who have to give up money are not only responsible for the lack of replication, but in fact, their salaries will not change. Their universities will not charge that few thousand euros against them. They do not have to bring it in from home.

So, my short reply is no, my long reply is that I am willing to give up 1 PM for replication in return for the DMP that I do unpaid.

The other thing to mention is that we do not have a replication budget at this point, either in Poland or Hungary. So how do you know that giving up 1 PM is sufficient? Currently this entire project is relying on credible output on these "case studies" that the lowest budget partners have to pull through with Reprex in all cases.  Giving instead of 0.5% maybe 0.7% to a new partner will really make a difference?

I do not want to start a bad mouthed discussion at the WP leaders meeting but if this proposal comes up I will demand the name of the data manager librarian in SSA and I will transfer all work that I do for about 5 partners in data management to them.

Best regards,
Daniel

Hi Daniel,

Then we are at an impasse.

In early 2023, you offered to take over the DMP task. At that time, you didn't ask for additional PM. You then rescinded this offer, causing me a lot of trouble in the process.

Afterwards, I tried to negotiate a model in which you would assist SSSA in hiring a library scientist competent to do technical data management work. I thought that we were at the verge of an agreement, but you then backed out, once more causing me a lot of trouble.

Your alternative "suggestion" or rather demand – more money and more work for REPREX – is simply not feasible. You already have the largest personnel budget in the project, and after the revision it will be even larger. To my knowledge, your technical team consists of you and Adam.

You tell me that you cannot hire without more finances or forward guidance. That is not credible. You were transferred half of your budget at project start. Was that insufficient to hire? Ridiculous.

So, I suppose that Fabio will not get the data he needs, and your task will fail. What a shame.

Best regards,
James

________________________________
From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: 02 July 2024 14:05
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Subject: Re: OpenMusE -- replacing MUSICAUTOR in T1.1

Hi James,

Fabio presented a wish list of data that he wants to use.  And then I explained to him what level of data description is required just to pass on such a data request anywhere, i..e, IFPI, IFPI CZ, CISAC, etc.  And he, as a statistician, said that this is not our work, and he wants to talk with the person who will put this together.  And indeed, like in Polifonia or other projects, that is the data steward who is in charge of the DMP and does this meticulous work. Such data requests indeed require many days or weeks of hard work, usually performed by a librarian.

I will provide Fabio with some data, but I obviously will not assign my librarian to do this work for him for exploratory work, because, indeed, there is an organisation that is actually receiving pay for this.

No, James, Fabio himself brought up this topic, because he realised that normally there is a person for this type of work and he wants to get in touch with that person.

Best regards,
Daniel

Hi Daniel,

I am confused as nobody asked Fabio to "do the work of a data manager". Unless of course you did.

Of course, you are free to reach out to SSSA for whatever reason, or to suggest that Fabio do so. If you do, CC me as I am standing in for Richard as WP6 leader. I want to keep on top of whatever impacts the WP.

Best regards,
James
