From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&lt;mailto:daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;&gt;
Sent: 02 July 2024 10:00
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt;; Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&lt;mailto:tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;&gt;
Subject: Re: OpenMusE -- replacing MUSICAUTOR in T1.1

Hi James,

You already know my point of view, but I want to place it here, and find a better solution than taking 6250 euros from Reprex.

- I have made at least 7 presentations so far to make a credible, shoe-string budget replication of MusicAutor in WP2, and assisted Tomas with Zaiks
- Cultivate for Hudobne centrum as a subcontractor for over a year, with a lot of unbudgeted travel.
- I am holding back a scene with Fabio who wants to get in touch directly with the data manager of the project, because he does not understand why he has to write data exchange documentations as a statistical algorithm researcher
- In the review meeting, the WP1 passed with my work, WP4 presented a 14 years old software and my work.
- Replacing MusicAutor with two organisations in two countries will double my costs, because I will onboard them, serve them, manage them.

So my principled answer is the following:  I am willing to give up 1 PM in return for the official handover of the DMP.  Currently there is nobody working on data management on the project, and I am going to spend from my own money, I mean what I brought in from home, to hire a librarian, and assist, for example, UvA's postdoc.

The other reason why I find your proposal extremely unjust is that the other people who have to give up money are not only responsible for the lack of replication, but in fact, their salaries will not change. Their universities will not charge that few thousand euros against them. They do not have to bring it in from home.

So, my short reply is no, my long reply is that I am willing to give up 1 PM for replication in return for the DMP that I do unpaid.

The other thing to mention is that we do not have a replication budget at this point, either in Poland or Hungary. So how do you know that giving up 1 PM is sufficient? Currently this entire project is relying on credible output on these "case studies" that the lowest budget partners have to pull through with Reprex in all cases.  Giving instead of 0.5% maybe 0.7% to a new partner will really make a difference?

I do not want to start a bad mouthed discussion at the WP leaders meeting but if this proposal comes up I will demand the name of the data manager librarian in SSA and I will transfer all work that I do for about 5 partners in data management to them.

Best regards,
Daniel


On Mon, Jul 1, 2024 at 4:47 PM James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt; wrote:
Dear WP leaders,

First off, many thanks again for your excellent contributions to our interim review. Thanks to our joint efforts, the result was a constructive meeting that credibly sets the stage for a renewal of the project.

I have excellent follow-up news: thanks to Tomas' efforts, the Polish Society of Authors ZAiKS is considering joining our project. This would solve the most significant problem facing the Consortium right now, which is how to replace MUSICAUTOR in the WP1 pilot study on valuation. Indeed, it would level it up significantly. Poland is a top-5 EU country by population and top-10 by GDP. Real, active participation by the dominant Polish rights management organisation would greatly magnify our project's impact.

Of course, there is a potential trade-off, which we would like to discuss openly. During our interim review, our PO stated a clear preference for replacing MUSICAUTOR with a new full partner rather than a subcontractor. Currently, due to MUSICAUTOR's low PM rate, we only have €13000 in the budget to offer ZAiKS. This is not enough to justify onboarding as a partner. Furthermore, both the low budget and the contractual description of the subcontractor / service provider roles would limit ZAiKS' scope of action in the project to replication of the pilot study. In principle, they could offer much more.

To that end, we are asking the major partners (those with over 200k in personnel costs) to sacrifice 1 PM each, thus freeing up budget for ZAiKS and/or our WP2 replication partner. This would allow us to offer them nearly 30k each  rather than just 13k each, *in case* they are open to an expanded role in the project. I firmly believe that the collective benefit to all of our institutions would greatly outweigh the budgetary impact for any one of us.

This will be on the agenda to discuss during our WP leader call on Friday at 9am. In the meantime, please give it thought and feel free to write or call with any questions.

Thank you, and best regards,
James

This would allow us to offer them nearly 30k each  rather than just 13k each, *in case* they are open to an expanded role in the project. I firmly believe that the collective benefit to all of our institutions would greatly outweigh the budgetary impact for any one of us.

James

Dear Eszter and Balazs, Tomas, Daniel, and Arianna,



I hope everyone is well!



Before last week's PMB, I briefly suggested a meeting in Budapest to plan our forthcoming surveys. This is because one major aim of all of our surveys (music MSME, music professional, music audience / cultural access and participation) is to provide data inputs for the music valuation pilot study conducted by REPREX on behalf of ARTISJUS.



Now that the revised work plan has been approved, we should begin to follow up on that. As we must finalise the questionnaires in Autumn, we should do this before the summer holiday.



@ARTISJUS team, are there particular windows in June or July, during which you are / are not available? I think it should be possible for the other partners to plan around your schedules.



One idea, if it works for you and for Arianna and Daniel, is to come to Budapest some time during the week preceding the project's interim review meeting on 21 June. Please let me know what you think.



Thank you and best regards,

James



PS. Attached for everyone's reference are a summary of the surveys and survey-type data collection we'll conduct, and a summary Daniel created of issues that arose during the CEEMID CAP surveys.

Dear Eszter and Balazs, Tomas, Daniel, and Arianna,



I hope everyone is well!



Before last week's PMB, I briefly suggested a meeting in Budapest to plan our forthcoming surveys. This is because one major aim of all of our surveys (music MSME, music professional, music audience / cultural access and participation) is to provide data inputs for the music valuation pilot study conducted by REPREX on behalf of ARTISJUS.



Now that the revised work plan has been approved, we should begin to follow up on that. As we must finalise the questionnaires in Autumn, we should do this before the summer holiday.



@ARTISJUS team, are there particular windows in June or July, during which you are / are not available? I think it should be possible for the other partners to plan around your schedules.



One idea, if it works for you and for Arianna and Daniel, is to come to Budapest some time during the week preceding the project's interim review meeting on 21 June. Please let me know what you think.



Thank you and best regards,

James



PS. Attached for everyone's reference are a summary of the surveys and survey-type data collection we'll conduct, and a summary Daniel created of issues that arose during the CEEMID CAP surveys.

Dear Eszter and Balazs, Tomas, Daniel, and Arianna,



I hope everyone is well!



Before last week's PMB, I briefly suggested a meeting in Budapest to plan our forthcoming surveys. This is because one major aim of all of our surveys (music MSME, music professional, music audience / cultural access and participation) is to provide data inputs for the music valuation pilot study conducted by REPREX on behalf of ARTISJUS.



Now that the revised work plan has been approved, we should begin to follow up on that. As we must finalise the questionnaires in Autumn, we should do this before the summer holiday.



@ARTISJUS team, are there particular windows in June or July, during which you are / are not available? I think it should be possible for the other partners to plan around your schedules.



One idea, if it works for you and for Arianna and Daniel, is to come to Budapest some time during the week preceding the project's interim review meeting on 21 June. Please let me know what you think.



Thank you and best regards,

James



PS. Attached for everyone's reference are a summary of the surveys and survey-type data collection we'll conduct, and a summary Daniel created of issues that arose during the CEEMID CAP surveys.

James

Hi James,



Let me just include the people in our next call and Arianna. In my understanding we agreed in March that the work plan is rescheduled by an exact 12 months, because our survey (time) frame requires January fieldwork. This means that it is totally fine to have a first draft of the questionnaire on 1 October and a final on 15 November. This frame is necessary for methodological reasons to align with the time frame of business data.



I think that the summer should be spent to get back to those tasks that should have been done before the surveying tasks

-  A revised valuation model, which is not yet known by anybody in-depth but Eszter and I

-  The conceptualisation of the data needs of Artisjus, SOZA, ZAiKS  in WP1, MiH in WP3, and any other data user

- A critical review of the background - what is available and what needs to be developed, including the vast KULT material that we received from the IKP and Hudobne centrum 78months ago.



We will introduce our question bank tool in the call, and it will be prepopulated with a part of our background for WP1, WP2, WP3. But then, in the summer, the researchers really must work on their modeling needs (including Fabio in WP1) and conceptualise the data needs so that we can define the data inputs, and define what will be collected by one of the surveys.



So, all in all, I think that your indicated timeline it is realistic that you and Ariana can get familiar with our background and start to work on some blocks of the questionnaires, but knowing how much time it took to do the annual valuations in SK and HU, I would find it impossible to arrive to a first draft questionnaire before 1 October.



Best regards,
Daniel

On 5 Jul 2024, at 14:15, Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt; wrote:

Hi James,

We have created a presentation and a tutorial for the previous Wednesday about the questionnaires, and I would like to present it to you (and Arianna) next week if you feel better.  We loaded some questionnaire items into the system, and if you agree, we will import the SurveyHarmonies entire set into it.

The tool allows mass import and export, and can be queried with standard SPARQL queries (we will create for the most used cases sample queries that can only be clicked.) This means that with a predefined querry you will be able to export into a CSV for SurveyMonkey Export, or any defined tabular form that your fieldwork software needs.  It also has a graphical user interface that makes it easy to edit elements and translations.

We will add the relevant part of the CEEMID background into this system.  We already loaded some items in it, but we would like to get some UX feedback before we mass upload all the questionnaires, because we want to make it as useful and easy to use as possible.

The tool is 98% DDI compatible, we added some features that are not well covered by DDI.  If you can make UTU write some actual code, it can also work in R with retroharmonize, i.e., it can harmonise different language labels, numeric coding, etc.  But if we have some budget left, perhaps we will do this, because it is a small connection to make it work, the heavy lifting of structuring is already done.

Adam and I had some correspondence on and off with GESIS, I think that we can cover almost everything that they can do.

The features and data coverage go far beyond the requirement of OpenMuse and we also used non-openmuse funding, too, so at one point we have to declare a cut off point what is available for reporting and use for the consortium, and what becomes a newer Reprex background (that the consortium can still use, but we will not claim costs for it, and not all data that we create will be automatically open.)

Would it be possible that we present this in 5 minutes in the WP1 meeting, and after the WP1 in 20 minutes maybe only to you, Isabella, Arianna, or whoever will work with surveys?  It would be also good to have the EUBA PhD Student use it, because this would be the tool to work with the KULT surveys.

Best regards,

Hi James,



Let me just include the people in our next call and Arianna. In my understanding we agreed in March that the work plan is rescheduled by an exact 12 months, because our survey (time) frame requires January fieldwork. This means that it is totally fine to have a first draft of the questionnaire on 1 October and a final on 15 November. This frame is necessary for methodological reasons to align with the time frame of business data.



I think that the summer should be spent to get back to those tasks that should have been done before the surveying tasks

-  A revised valuation model, which is not yet known by anybody in-depth but Eszter and I

-  The conceptualisation of the data needs of Artisjus, SOZA, ZAiKS  in WP1, MiH in WP3, and any other data user

- A critical review of the background - what is available and what needs to be developed, including the vast KULT material that we received from the IKP and Hudobne centrum 78months ago.



We will introduce our question bank tool in the call, and it will be prepopulated with a part of our background for WP1, WP2, WP3. But then, in the summer, the researchers really must work on their modeling needs (including Fabio in WP1) and conceptualise the data needs so that we can define the data inputs, and define what will be collected by one of the surveys.



So, all in all, I think that your indicated timeline it is realistic that you and Ariana can get familiar with our background and start to work on some blocks of the questionnaires, but knowing how much time it took to do the annual valuations in SK and HU, I would find it impossible to arrive to a first draft questionnaire before 1 October.



Best regards,
Daniel

Hi James,

As a custodian to the background, Reprex created a tutorial and a tool to access the questions, their translations, and all necessary metadata to include them in a questionnaire. It is compliant, when possible, with the DDI-Discovery Vocabulary (2024) which does not cover the entire DDI, in other cases we subjectively implement DDI-Lifecycle 3.3.

Our API will be able to export the questionnaire into an Excel sheet or your preferred format.  The most efficient way forward would be if Arianna and you would use the same tool to write the remaining questions, because then it will be fully interoperable via DDI with statistical or GESIS surveys, and they can be exported in any language without a hassle.

We have started to fill in to this Question Bank tool the some of the question items, question grids, blocks from the former CEEMID surveys, Eurobarometer, and SurveyHarmonies, prioritising those items that have English description, or are likely to be used.

In  my opinion, the best way forward would be if we would provide you and Arianna a login to the questionbank , and provide you a walkthrough before giving you a presentation and tutorial on how to use it. Perhaps we could do this walkthrough next week, before we have the more general call with our partners?

Best regards,
Daniel

Subject: Re: OpenMusE -- survey planning

Hi James,

Let me just include the people in our next call and Arianna. In my understanding we agreed in March that the work plan is rescheduled by an exact 12 months, because our survey (time) frame requires January fieldwork. This means that it is totally fine to have a first draft of the questionnaire on 1 October and a final on 15 November. This frame is necessary for methodological reasons to align with the time frame of business data.

I think that the summer should be spent to get back to those tasks that should have been done before the surveying tasks
-  A revised valuation model, which is not yet known by anybody in-depth but Eszter and I
-  The conceptualisation of the data needs of Artisjus, SOZA, ZAiKS  in WP1, MiH in WP3, and any other data user
- A critical review of the background - what is available and what needs to be developed, including the vast KULT material that we received from the IKP and Hudobne centrum 78months ago.

We will introduce our question bank tool in the call, and it will be prepopulated with a part of our background for WP1, WP2, WP3. But then, in the summer, the researchers really must work on their modeling needs (including Fabio in WP1) and conceptualise the data needs so that we can define the data inputs, and define what will be collected by one of the surveys.

So, all in all, I think that your indicated timeline it is realistic that you and Ariana can get familiar with our background and start to work on some blocks of the questionnaires, but knowing how much time it took to do the annual valuations in SK and HU, I would find it impossible to arrive to a first draft questionnaire before 1 October.

Best regards,
Daniel

Dear Eszter and Balazs, Tomas, Daniel, and Arianna,



I hope everyone is well!



Before last week's PMB, I briefly suggested a meeting in Budapest to plan our forthcoming surveys. This is because one major aim of all of our surveys (music MSME, music professional, music audience / cultural access and participation) is to provide data inputs for the music valuation pilot study conducted by REPREX on behalf of ARTISJUS.



Now that the revised work plan has been approved, we should begin to follow up on that. As we must finalise the questionnaires in Autumn, we should do this before the summer holiday.



@ARTISJUS team, are there particular windows in June or July, during which you are / are not available? I think it should be possible for the other partners to plan around your schedules.



One idea, if it works for you and for Arianna and Daniel, is to come to Budapest some time during the week preceding the project's interim review meeting on 21 June. Please let me know what you think.



Thank you and best regards,

James



PS. Attached for everyone's reference are a summary of the surveys and survey-type data collection we'll conduct, and a summary Daniel created of issues that arose during the CEEMID CAP surveys.

Hi James,

As a custodian to the background, Reprex created a tutorial and a tool to access the questions, their translations, and all necessary metadata to include them in a questionnaire. It is compliant, when possible, with the DDI-Discovery Vocabulary (2024) which does not cover the entire DDI, in other cases we subjectively implement DDI-Lifecycle 3.3.

Our API will be able to export the questionnaire into an Excel sheet or your preferred format.  The most efficient way forward would be if Arianna and you would use the same tool to write the remaining questions, because then it will be fully interoperable via DDI with statistical or GESIS surveys, and they can be exported in any language without a hassle.

We have started to fill in to this Question Bank tool the some of the question items, question grids, blocks from the former CEEMID surveys, Eurobarometer, and SurveyHarmonies, prioritising those items that have English description, or are likely to be used.

In  my opinion, the best way forward would be if we would provide you and Arianna a login to the questionbank , and provide you a walkthrough before giving you a presentation and tutorial on how to use it. Perhaps we could do this walkthrough next week, before we have the more general call with our partners?

Best regards,
Daniel

Hi James,

Let me just include the people in our next call and Arianna. In my understanding we agreed in March that the work plan is rescheduled by an exact 12 months, because our survey (time) frame requires January fieldwork. This means that it is totally fine to have a first draft of the questionnaire on 1 October and a final on 15 November. This frame is necessary for methodological reasons to align with the time frame of business data.

I think that the summer should be spent to get back to those tasks that should have been done before the surveying tasks
-  A revised valuation model, which is not yet known by anybody in-depth but Eszter and I
-  The conceptualisation of the data needs of Artisjus, SOZA, ZAiKS  in WP1, MiH in WP3, and any other data user
- A critical review of the background - what is available and what needs to be developed, including the vast KULT material that we received from the IKP and Hudobne centrum 78months ago.

We will introduce our question bank tool in the call, and it will be prepopulated with a part of our background for WP1, WP2, WP3. But then, in the summer, the researchers really must work on their modeling needs (including Fabio in WP1) and conceptualise the data needs so that we can define the data inputs, and define what will be collected by one of the surveys.

So, all in all, I think that your indicated timeline it is realistic that you and Ariana can get familiar with our background and start to work on some blocks of the questionnaires, but knowing how much time it took to do the annual valuations in SK and HU, I would find it impossible to arrive to a first draft questionnaire before 1 October.

Best regards,
Daniel

Hi James,

As a custodian to the background, Reprex created a tutorial and a tool to access the questions, their translations, and all necessary metadata to include them in a questionnaire. It is compliant, when possible, with the DDI-Discovery Vocabulary (2024) which does not cover the entire DDI, in other cases we subjectively implement DDI-Lifecycle 3.3.

Our API will be able to export the questionnaire into an Excel sheet or your preferred format.  The most efficient way forward would be if Arianna and you would use the same tool to write the remaining questions, because then it will be fully interoperable via DDI with statistical or GESIS surveys, and they can be exported in any language without a hassle.

We have started to fill in to this Question Bank tool the some of the question items, question grids, blocks from the former CEEMID surveys, Eurobarometer, and SurveyHarmonies, prioritising those items that have English description, or are likely to be used.

In  my opinion, the best way forward would be if we would provide you and Arianna a login to the questionbank , and provide you a walkthrough before giving you a presentation and tutorial on how to use it. Perhaps we could do this walkthrough next week, before we have the more general call with our partners?

Best regards,
Daniel

Hi James,

Let me just include the people in our next call and Arianna. In my understanding we agreed in March that the work plan is rescheduled by an exact 12 months, because our survey (time) frame requires January fieldwork. This means that it is totally fine to have a first draft of the questionnaire on 1 October and a final on 15 November. This frame is necessary for methodological reasons to align with the time frame of business data.

I think that the summer should be spent to get back to those tasks that should have been done before the surveying tasks
-  A revised valuation model, which is not yet known by anybody in-depth but Eszter and I
-  The conceptualisation of the data needs of Artisjus, SOZA, ZAiKS  in WP1, MiH in WP3, and any other data user
- A critical review of the background - what is available and what needs to be developed, including the vast KULT material that we received from the IKP and Hudobne centrum 78months ago.

We will introduce our question bank tool in the call, and it will be prepopulated with a part of our background for WP1, WP2, WP3. But then, in the summer, the researchers really must work on their modeling needs (including Fabio in WP1) and conceptualise the data needs so that we can define the data inputs, and define what will be collected by one of the surveys.

So, all in all, I think that your indicated timeline it is realistic that you and Ariana can get familiar with our background and start to work on some blocks of the questionnaires, but knowing how much time it took to do the annual valuations in SK and HU, I would find it impossible to arrive to a first draft questionnaire before 1 October.

Best regards,
Daniel

Hi James,

As a custodian to the background, Reprex created a tutorial and a tool to access the questions, their translations, and all necessary metadata to include them in a questionnaire. It is compliant, when possible, with the DDI-Discovery Vocabulary (2024) which does not cover the entire DDI, in other cases we subjectively implement DDI-Lifecycle 3.3.

Our API will be able to export the questionnaire into an Excel sheet or your preferred format.  The most efficient way forward would be if Arianna and you would use the same tool to write the remaining questions, because then it will be fully interoperable via DDI with statistical or GESIS surveys, and they can be exported in any language without a hassle.

We have started to fill in to this Question Bank tool the some of the question items, question grids, blocks from the former CEEMID surveys, Eurobarometer, and SurveyHarmonies, prioritising those items that have English description, or are likely to be used.

In  my opinion, the best way forward would be if we would provide you and Arianna a login to the questionbank , and provide you a walkthrough before giving you a presentation and tutorial on how to use it. Perhaps we could do this walkthrough next week, before we have the more general call with our partners?

Best regards,
Daniel

Hi James,

Let me just include the people in our next call and Arianna. In my understanding we agreed in March that the work plan is rescheduled by an exact 12 months, because our survey (time) frame requires January fieldwork. This means that it is totally fine to have a first draft of the questionnaire on 1 October and a final on 15 November. This frame is necessary for methodological reasons to align with the time frame of business data.

I think that the summer should be spent to get back to those tasks that should have been done before the surveying tasks
-  A revised valuation model, which is not yet known by anybody in-depth but Eszter and I
-  The conceptualisation of the data needs of Artisjus, SOZA, ZAiKS  in WP1, MiH in WP3, and any other data user
- A critical review of the background - what is available and what needs to be developed, including the vast KULT material that we received from the IKP and Hudobne centrum 78months ago.

We will introduce our question bank tool in the call, and it will be prepopulated with a part of our background for WP1, WP2, WP3. But then, in the summer, the researchers really must work on their modeling needs (including Fabio in WP1) and conceptualise the data needs so that we can define the data inputs, and define what will be collected by one of the surveys.

So, all in all, I think that your indicated timeline it is realistic that you and Ariana can get familiar with our background and start to work on some blocks of the questionnaires, but knowing how much time it took to do the annual valuations in SK and HU, I would find it impossible to arrive to a first draft questionnaire before 1 October.

Best regards,
Daniel

This is because one major aim of all of our surveys (music MSME, music professional, music audience / cultural access and participation) is to provide data inputs for the music valuation pilot study conducted by REPREX on behalf of ARTISJUS.

Now that the revised work plan has been approved, we should begin to follow up on that. As we must finalise the questionnaires in Autumn, we should do this before the summer holiday.

@ARTISJUS team, are there particular windows in June or July, during which you are / are not available? I think it should be possible for the other partners to plan around your schedules.

One idea, if it works for you and for Arianna and Daniel, is to come to Budapest some time during the week preceding the project's interim review meeting on 21 June. Please let me know what you think.

Thank you and best regards,
James

Dear Daniel,



Thank you very much for the presentation and for taking time to reformulate the project assumptions, which now seem to allay some concerns that were on our side. And thank you @Dr. Kabai Eszter&lt;mailto:ekabai@artisjus.com&gt; for the sound advice on the CMOs’ position.



After our internal meeting on Friday, we can declare that we are definitely interested in taking part in the project we just have to figure out how to provide as much useful and reliable data from Poland as possible. Various studies of the music market and music consumption have been conducted so far in Poland (e.g. for the purposes of the division of remuneration from private copying), but never on a similar scale. We have several partners whose contribution we can rely on, such as The Polish Music Council, the National Institute of Music and Dance and our own Polish Music Export Foundation. We will reach to all those institutions to check how they can engage in the project.



But for the final declaration on the form and the scope of our cooperation we will need the decision of our Board, which, due to holiday season will not meet until August 6th. For this meeting we would like to provide our Board members with all the necessary information, including the full list of our rights and obligations related to the project, which, according to my legal intuition, should be included in the contracts for formal partnership and direct subcontracting. Would it be possible for you to provide us with drafts of such contracts or, at least, comprehensive summary of the rights and obligations? Any piece of information, as much detailed as possible, would be very much welcomed.



I am sorry, that it takes a bit longer that our initial schedule predicted, but most of the people, who will be engaged in the project on our site are out of office right now or planning to be on holidays in the upcoming weeks, but we will do our best to kick off once the final decision is made at the beginning of August.



Best regards

Anna

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Monday, July 15, 2024 9:37 AM
To: Jerzy Łabuda &lt;Jerzy.Labuda@zaiks.org.pl&gt;; Poort, Joost &lt;J.P.Poort@uva.nl&gt;; James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Cc: Anna Misiewicz &lt;Anna.Misiewicz@zaiks.org.pl&gt;; Demčák Richard &lt;richard.demcak@soza.sk&gt;; Dr. Kabai Eszter &lt;ekabai@artisjus.com&gt;; Arianna Martinelli &lt;arianna.martinelli@santannapisa.it&gt;
Subject: Re: The OpenMusE project



Dear Jerzy and Anna,

Dear Colleagues,



After our conversation with Eszter I have updated the presentation thoroughly from the previous Wednesday. We critically reviewed the former CEEMID background, and Eszter gave very sound advice on how to separate the research project, the innovation elements, and exploitation pathways. I think that this separation is very sound, it is in line with the general concept that the grant should be used for generally exploitable results, and individual exploitation of knowledge should be in the "exploitation pathway" a separate use of the intellectual property. It would also alleviate all kinds of data confidentiality or conflict of interest issues.



- I made some definitions of research outputs that we can expect, and I will discuss the relevant parts with Joost and Fabio on Monday afternoon; we should also discuss it with Arianna and James about the surveying.

- Eszter suggests to separate the general valuation model and methodology, and even the survey as research outputs, and she suggests that any particular valuations that will go into active use, and may end up as evidence in copyright tribunal, litigation, dispute with the royalty payers should be the "exploitation of results" based on separate contract between the CMOs and Reprex.



https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/wp1.html/&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/wp1.html#/researchoutput&gt;



In practice, this would mean that we will fill up the evaluation models with partly real data, and partly realistic but randomised data, and try to get scientific validation for the method, but not particular valuations. It is completely up to the management team or board of a CMO if they agree with an expert valuation, and if they act on it (for example, they change a tariff, they enter into a dispute with a royalty payer.)  That should be completely left out of the picture here.



This approach would also leave more room for research and rely less on a simple replication of the CEEMID background.



Best regards,
Daniel

Hi Daniel and all,

@Daniel Antal&lt;mailto:daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;, thank you for this! Please keep us updated and/or in CC where appropriate.

Tangentially: Daniel and @Joost Poort&lt;mailto:j.p.poort@uva.nl&gt;, prior to your call with Fabio today, it might be useful to take a look at Section 5 of the Measuring CCS project final report (https://www.measuring-ccs.eu/the-measuring-ccs-consortium-publishes-the-final-report/), which discusses methods for integration of platform data into CCSI statistics.
[https://www.measuring-ccs.eu/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/BANNER-EXAMPLE.png]&lt;https://www.measuring-ccs.eu/the-measuring-ccs-consortium-publishes-the-final-report/&gt;
The Measuring CCS Consortium publishes the Final Report - Measuring the Cultural and Creative Sectors in the EU&lt;https://www.measuring-ccs.eu/the-measuring-ccs-consortium-publishes-the-final-report/&gt;
This event aims to present and discuss the results of the project. The final outputs and outcomes will be delivered by the researchers led by Professor Manuel Villares of Qmetrics.
www.measuring-ccs.eu


We have reached out to the Measuring CCS team to request access to their more detailed methodology reports. If access is granted, I could see these being interesting / useful to ARTISJUS, SOZA, and ZAiKS as well.

Best regards,
James

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: 12 July 2024 15:09
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;; Arianna Martinelli &lt;Arianna.Martinelli@santannapisa.it&gt;
Cc: Joost Poort &lt;j.p.poort@uva.nl&gt;; Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;; Anna.Misiewicz@zaiks.org.pl &lt;Anna.Misiewicz@zaiks.org.pl&gt;; Dr. Kabai Eszter &lt;ekabai@artisjus.com&gt;
Subject: Valuation + register + survey background

Dear James and Joost,

To avoid much cross-posting, I send a separate letter to the three CMOs based on a very long conversation with Eszter about the valuation project element.  We think that we should have a realistic expectation from all three societies (Artisjus, SOZA, ZAiKS) what they want to achieve as a shared and open result in this project, and what are their particular business sensitivities that they want to keep as SENSITIVE in the exploitation pathways, and perhaps further issues that they do not even want to bring into the consortium.

This is not related to the integrity of the data collection and methodology, it is strictly related to how Artisjus, ZAiKS, SOZA will utilise the results, but it is an important first step to come up with a realistic survey and valuation program.

We agreed with Eszter that the work in our background is in many ways obsolete, it answered questions of the 2010s, and it was very much related to national and international controversies  of that decade. We do not think that our background should be very directly used.

I have a clearer understanding of Artijus's needs and expectations, and will try to align this with SOZA and ZAIKS in the coming days, while also transferring the relevant part of the background to SSSA and SINUS. Our aim is to clear off unnecessary business considerations and focus only on methodology that requires scientific corroboration.

Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder

Dear OpenMusE team,

According to our original workplan we reached half-time a few days ago with the submission of D5.3. In my personal view this is a good moment for a small stocktaking as well as re-considering the team setup. Insofar, this email will also be one of the last ones I will send around to all of you.


  1.  In spite of the diverse problems we faced during the first project half the OpenMusE team has indeed produced some strong output in terms of documents/deliverables. Recently I was made aware of the fact that not all partners know that ALL official output so far is stored for and accessible to the entire project team on the SINUS Cloud in form of PDFs and Excel annex files. So, in case you feel that you want to know more on specific project aspects in preparation for upcoming tasks I would like to encourage you to log into this repository, download away and enjoy the read.
In case you lost your credentials, please just contact me.

Here is a list of the official project documents so far:
https://cloud.sinus-institut.de/ws-OpenMusE/


  *   D1.1_OpenMusE_economy-of-music-in-europe-methods-and-indicators.pdf
+ Annexes
  *   D2.1_OpenMusE_v2.0_music-diversity-and-circulation.pdf
+ Annexes
  *   D3.1_OpenMusE_v1.1_music-society-citizenship-methods-and-indicators.pdf
+ Annexes
  *   D4.1_OpenMusE_open-source-music-data-software-ecosystem.pdf
  *   D5.1_OpenMusE_open-music-observatory.pdf
  *   D5.2_OpenMusE_v1.5_communication-dissemination-exploitation-plan.pdf
  *   D5.3_OpenMusE-updated-communication-dissemination-and-exploitation-plan.pdf
  *   D5.6-policy-brief-1-music-metadata-mainstreaming-and-EU-law.pdf
  *   D6.1_OpenMusE_v1.1-project-management-handbook.pdf
  *   D6.2_OpenMusE_ethics-framework.pdf
  *   D6.3_OpenMusE_v1.2-data-management-plan.pdf
+ Annex
  *   D7.1-OEI-Requirement-1.pdf
  *   D7.2_OpenMusE-OEI-Requirement-2.pdf



  1.  Half-time also is a good opportunity to reconsider team setup and to reflect on personal goals. In my own case, I would like to put a stronger focus on slightly different professional areas and want to considerably decrease my involvement in OpenMusE. Therefore, I asked the SINUS management to accept my resignation as project manager by the end of this month and was glad with their understanding reaction. Also, I am glad to announce that Isabella will pick up the torch both as project manager and WP6 leader. Personally, I am very happy with her decision to do so and see these two project functions in very good hands with her.

That’s it from my side, a goodbye for now and a big thank you to all of you. But as they say – you always meet twice in life ...

Cheers,
Richard

Dear Fábió and Joost,

You were not in CC in the correspondence, so I am forwarding this to you. I find the answer extremely useful.   As I thought, some of the perceived irregularities have a perfectly sensible explanation due to the registration workflow, however, the workflow itself is very outdated and begs for many questions.

In  my opinion, for tFábió problem statement article - blogspot, the best way forward would be to lay out the process of release workflow and the potential pitfalls.  What we could do, and I gladly help there, to ask further IFPI registrants for similar outputs. Because ISRC is a very old system, it is decentralised (pre-Internet, so simultaneous coordination was not possible), and I can imagine that various national registrars have different practices. For example, the answer below suggests local fixes, too.

In my opinion, this would be a straightforward way ahead:
- Fabio goes on with a public blogpost based on this answers
- We sent that blogpost for further input to Hungary, Lithuania, Belgium, Netherlands, Bulgaria, where I have direct contacts for futher input and comment
- Then try to write it into an article.

I would be also interested in writing an article, with anybody interested, about modelling this process in standard information - data models, or incorporating these approaches. More about this tomorrow.

I would also suggest another small exercise for Fabio.

- Organise our your data treasure trove into easy to access folders.
- Create scripts (and commit them to the joint repo) that collect out all country - registrant code - year pairs, for example, SK- K29 - 15, SK - K29 - 16, etc. These are registration years by label and national registrar country .
- A further script to add the name of the label, when you have it, by the  SK- K29 parts.

Then create subsets for SK, HU, PL, LT, BG, NL, BE [these are countries where we can ask questions, and  just sufficient to understand what is going on with the data, for example, SK was established only in 1993]

min Year, max year for each country - label pair
country_code, regsitrant_code, min_year, max_year, label_name
SK, K29, 13, 22, Example label
SK, K30,  22, 23, &lt;label name missing&gt;
...
SK, K31, 23, 23 Example label2
...
PL,  AAA, 11,21, Polish label
PL,  ABA, 12,14, &lt;label name missing&gt;

This would provide us a much more interesting review than your earlier histograms of registrar country code and year code.

Just provide me with the country tables, i.e., I do not need access to the many gigabytes of raw data.

Best regards,
Daniel

Subject: ISRC codes question

Hi Tomas,
I wonder if you can forward this email to IFPI CZ and SLOVGRAM, or advise me to whom to address it.
Daniel

Dear Mr.

With Fábio Generoso Vieira, on behalf of the University of Amsterdam, Daniel Antal (the author of the Slovak Music Industry Report) and SOZA are working on an EU Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Action with creating better statistical data about European music. The focus of our work is randomly selecting sound recordings that were registered in Slovakia.
We would like to ask your assistance to understand the former CS and SK ISRC codes that have been assigned.

To our knowledge, the Slovak ISRC codes should take the following form:
SK-AAA-YY-NNNNN, like SK-K29-16-00101

Year of reference: YY part
- We sometimes see that the YY (16) part differs from the officially announced or coded release date (in the case of this song, Slnko Records officially released it in ’17)
- Are we correct to assume that the reason for this is that the range of codes given out to Slnko Records in 2016 is not yet filled, and they decided to put the recording later on the market?
- In your opinion, what is the longest possible difference between the release year signalled by the ISRC code and the actual release date?
- Is it possible that we find ISRC codes that are not in the range of 86-24, i.e., 1986 and 2024. Is it possible that earlier recordings were retroactively filled with, for example, a YY year code of 76?

Facts about the composition SK-K29-16-00101

- The owner of the registration code SKK29 is InnoSense, s.r.o.
- Sun Records only provides distribution of sales of the CD in question.
- The track is called "Orange"
- The first publication of the record was in 2016 in radio or digital environment
- It was also subsequently published in 2017 on the album "Stredovek" by InnoSense, s.r.o. along with other tracks published in the same year. https://www.discogs.com/release/10579920-Korben-Dallas-Stredovek
- Some tracks were not to be the first time published on an album.
- They may have been first published on radio or digital portals

ISRC does not indicate when an album is released.
Rather, ISRC denotes the first publication of a record by any means.
It is perfectly fine if the year in the ISRC is less than the year the album was released.

The difference between the year in the ISRC and the year when the ISRC was assigned can be very large.

Tracks made in 1965 can have a year in the ISRC of 1965 or even 2024. The release years can be 1965 and 2024 and all the years in between.
The ISRC manual talks about assigning the year according to when the ISRC is assigned, not according to the year the record is released on the carrier.
We prefer to assign the year in the ISRC according to the first publication of the record, by whatever means.
The big problem is that some subsequent releases or distributions assign new ISRCs to the same records.

It is better and clearer for some companies if they assign ISRCs by the year the records were produced, not by the year the ISRC was assigned. For example, if Slovak Radio were to retroactively assign several hundred thousand ISRCs to its records in a given year, the range of ISRCs would not be sufficient. It is certainly clearer if they indicate the year of production of the record in the ISRC. Their records could be dated from 1923. They could theoretically use that year in the ISRC as the oldest.

We are seeing misreported ISRCs with a year of manufacture of, for example, 33.

It is quite common for a manufacturer to indicate in the ISRC the year the record was first published and not the year the ISRC was assigned.


Registrant code: AAA part (like K29)
- Can we assume that an identical AAA part, like K29 always relates to the same registering entity?
- Is the list of registering entities confidential or can we find it somewhere?
- If the names of the registering entities are confidential, can we get a list of valid AAA codes?
- Our aim is to create a “lottery” algorithm that randomly selects a song registered with the SK country code, we do not want to reveal trade secrets.

K29, AAA are unique codes assigned to a specific entity.
SLOVGRAM sends a list of registered entities to IFPI headquarters every year. The list of registered entities is sent to IFPI headquarters and is not publicly available.
The list of valid codes is in order but some entities have ceased to exist and do not continue to be assigned ISRCs. In many cases we no longer know the current owners of the records. Rights may have been transferred or inherited. And some entities do not report ISRCs to us, so we have no ISRCs for some assigned registration codes.

We will provide you with a list of valid AAA registration codes. However, some entities have 2 codes and some have only one. This is one of the reasons why the data is not suitable for the lottery.

We can only supply the number of ISRCs assigned for each year for the records we have on file. So there are missing ones that we have not reported. It is also the case that we can only extract this data by the year of the production of the tracks or by the year contained in the ISRC. We are unable to produce a given list according to when the ISRCs were assigned because we do not record the year of the ISRC assignment. And, as mentioned earlier, we prefer the year of the record's production in the ISRC to the year the ISRC was assigned. So decide by which year you want the data and we can make the appropriate select for that.

Changes over time
- Were there any changes when the ISRC code changed in 2001, or when the CZ and SK registrars separated in the way this is managed?

- Is it possible to know what is the total number of filled (assigned) ISRC codes starting with SK for each year? For example, if we know that there are 2x more recordings with YY=22 than with YY=08, then a random sample of songs should have twice as many 2022 recordings.

We do not have information on how many ISRCs are assigned to tracks annually because not all records and ISRCs are reported to us by rights owners.
We cannot know how many recordings exist from 2008 or 2022. We should know best but we don't have enough information either. Many older tracks are not yet in the digital environment and may never get there, and many do not yet have ISRCs assigned.

We have doubts about the lottery mechanism because we don't know the details and because the tracks and producers are very different and in many cases have not reported ISRCs to us.

There are a number of Slovak tracks that have ISRCs that do not start with SK and are mainly allocated by digital distribution portals. It is therefore also not entirely appropriate to select only tracks starting with SK and consider only these as Slovak.


Best regards,
Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder

Dear all,

Our project is halfway through, which we would like to celebrate with you at our Bergfest from September 30th to October 1st.
Indeed, the last year and a half have often felt like a tough hike up a steep mountain. We’ve finally arrived at a point in the project where we can enjoy the view before taking the (hopefully) easier path until the end of our hike 😊

Working with this symbolic, Synyo and Sinus will organize the Bergfest in the mountains surrounding Vienna, in Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;. It’s quite close to the city and can be reached by train&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt; in ca. 1 ½ hours from Vienna airport (see attachment) or 1 hour from the main train station (Hauptbahnhof).

The Bergfest will take place in the “Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt;”, a historic, old-school Austrian hotel in Reichenau.
We have blocked rooms for the consortium at a reduced price, which you need to book directly with the hotel! Please contact hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; and mention the “OpenMusE seminar”. Please also let them know if you need a shuttle from the train station in Reichenau (13€ p.p.).


We’re currently working on the agenda, which we will send out once it’s finalized with the WP leaders. On the program so far:

  *   Several workshops to boost the second half of our project
  *   A General Assembly
  *   A voluntary hike on Sept. 29th for all early birds
  *   Time to relax, enjoy the view, and make some noise


All details at a glance:

  *   Date: September 30th to October 1st (arrival on September 29th)
  *   Place: Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;
  *   Hotel: Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt; --&gt; please book your room directly with the hotel: hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; !
  *   Room prices:
     *   Sept. 29th to 30th: 100€ p.p. in an individual room including breakfast
     *   Sept. 30th to Oct. 1st: 165€ p.p. in an individual room, including breakfast lunch and dinner on Sept. 30th

### OpenMusE Interim Payment {#email-630}

**From:** Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**To:** OpenMusE Consortium &lt;openmuseconsortium@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**Cc:** James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**Date:** 08/14/2024 09:30:02

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202408140930-OpenMusE Interim Payment-270.txt -->

Dear all,



After receiving the feedback on our technical report, the EC has now also finalized the financial review. We are happy to announce that they have accepted all financial reports and will now proceed to pay out the interim prepayment.



According to the CA, the second payment distributed to all partners amounts to 35% of the total budget.

However, as you all know, we are currently working on an amendment, and there will be significant budget changes for some partners. This leads us to the following issue:

On one hand, we cannot and don't want to delay payments until after the amendment, because an amendment is a rather lengthy process, that might take several weeks to months. On the other hand, we also must avoid having to request partners, that will receive a decreased budget under the new grant, for refunds after the amendment.



We would thus propose to split the second payment into two, pay out the first half immediately after receiving the EC's payment, and the rest after the amendment has been accepted. Such a decision cannot be made unilaterally by the coordinator, which is why we are calling for an e-mail vote.



For each partner, please reply if you:

  *   Agree with this proposed change in payments
  *   Or disagree



As stated in the CA the deadline for an e-mail vote is within 10 calendar days after receipt by a party and needs a minimum of 51% to pass.

I will be on a short vacation from tomorrow until August 25th and will only check my e-mails sporadically. James will be here in the meantime to collect the votes and answer any questions!



Thank you very much!

Best regards,

Dear all,

Our project is halfway through, which we would like to celebrate with you at our Bergfest from September 30th to October 1st.
Indeed, the last year and a half have often felt like a tough hike up a steep mountain. We’ve finally arrived at a point in the project where we can enjoy the view before taking the (hopefully) easier path until the end of our hike 😊

Working with this symbolic, Synyo and Sinus will organize the Bergfest in the mountains surrounding Vienna, in Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;. It’s quite close to the city and can be reached by train&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt; in ca. 1 ½ hours from Vienna airport (see attachment) or 1 hour from the main train station (Hauptbahnhof).

The Bergfest will take place in the “Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt;”, a historic, old-school Austrian hotel in Reichenau.
We have blocked rooms for the consortium at a reduced price, which you need to book directly with the hotel! Please contact hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; and mention the “OpenMusE seminar”. Please also let them know if you need a shuttle from the train station in Reichenau (13€ p.p.).


We’re currently working on the agenda, which we will send out once it’s finalized with the WP leaders. On the program so far:

  *   Several workshops to boost the second half of our project
  *   A General Assembly
  *   A voluntary hike on Sept. 29th for all early birds
  *   Time to relax, enjoy the view, and make some noise


All details at a glance:

  *   Date: September 30th to October 1st (arrival on September 29th)
  *   Place: Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;
  *   Hotel: Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt; --&gt; please book your room directly with the hotel: hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; !
  *   Room prices:
     *   Sept. 29th to 30th: 100€ p.p. in an individual room including breakfast
     *   Sept. 30th to Oct. 1st: 165€ p.p. in an individual room, including breakfast lunch and dinner on Sept. 30th
     *   Any additional night: 100€ p.p. in an individual room including breakfast
  *   To plan your train ride, use the ÖBB website Home - ÖBB (oebb.at)&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt;, not Google Maps! The closest train station is “Payerbach-Reichenau” (see attachment)

To make this a proper team event, it would be great if 1-2 people could join per partner. Please fill in the following form to RSVP: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1JSlzhVlQzIE8rT-5_9K1IZyIDM6diwQzkZKIty8mQgg/edit?usp=sharing
Reminder: You have travel budgets for in-person meetings, which for most partners remain largely untouched. It would help neither the EC, nor your organization, to return unused budgets.


We are looking forward to celebrating with you!

Marc, James &amp; Isabella

An: OpenMusE Consortium &lt;openmuseconsortium@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:openmuseconsortium@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt;
Cc: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt;; Marc Calmbach &lt;Marc.Calmbach@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:Marc.Calmbach@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt;; Christoph Steiner &lt;christoph.steiner@synyo.com&lt;mailto:christoph.steiner@synyo.com&gt;&gt;
Betreff: OpenMusE Bergfest

Dear all,

Our project is halfway through, which we would like to celebrate with you at our Bergfest from September 30th to October 1st.
Indeed, the last year and a half have often felt like a tough hike up a steep mountain. We’ve finally arrived at a point in the project where we can enjoy the view before taking the (hopefully) easier path until the end of our hike 😊

Working with this symbolic, Synyo and Sinus will organize the Bergfest in the mountains surrounding Vienna, in Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;. It’s quite close to the city and can be reached by train&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt; in ca. 1 ½ hours from Vienna airport (see attachment) or 1 hour from the main train station (Hauptbahnhof).

The Bergfest will take place in the “Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt;”, a historic, old-school Austrian hotel in Reichenau.
We have blocked rooms for the consortium at a reduced price, which you need to book directly with the hotel! Please contact hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; and mention the “OpenMusE seminar”. Please also let them know if you need a shuttle from the train station in Reichenau (13€ p.p.).


We’re currently working on the agenda, which we will send out once it’s finalized with the WP leaders. On the program so far:

  *   Several workshops to boost the second half of our project
  *   A General Assembly
  *   A voluntary hike on Sept. 29th for all early birds
  *   Time to relax, enjoy the view, and make some noise


All details at a glance:

  *   Date: September 30th to October 1st (arrival on September 29th)
  *   Place: Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;
  *   Hotel: Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt; --&gt; please book your room directly with the hotel: hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; !
  *   Room prices:
     *   Sept. 29th to 30th: 100€ p.p. in an individual room including breakfast
     *   Sept. 30th to Oct. 1st: 165€ p.p. in an individual room, including breakfast lunch and dinner on Sept. 30th
     *   Any additional night: 100€ p.p. in an individual room including breakfast
  *   To plan your train ride, use the ÖBB website Home - ÖBB (oebb.at)&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt;, not Google Maps! The closest train station is “Payerbach-Reichenau” (see attachment)

To make this a proper team event, it would be great if 1-2 people could join per partner. Please fill in the following form to RSVP: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1JSlzhVlQzIE8rT-5_9K1IZyIDM6diwQzkZKIty8mQgg/edit?usp=sharing
Reminder: You have travel budgets for in-person meetings, which for most partners remain largely untouched. It would help neither the EC, nor your organization, to return unused budgets.


We are looking forward to celebrating with you!

Best regards,

Marc, James &amp; Isabella

Cc: Anna Misiewicz &lt;Anna.Misiewicz@zaiks.org.pl&gt;; Demčák Richard &lt;richard.demcak@soza.sk&gt;; Dr. Kabai Eszter &lt;ekabai@artisjus.com&gt;; Arianna Martinelli &lt;arianna.martinelli@santannapisa.it&gt;
Subject: Re: The OpenMusE project



Dear Jerzy and Anna,

Dear Colleagues,



After our conversation with Eszter I have updated the presentation thoroughly from the previous Wednesday. We critically reviewed the former CEEMID background, and Eszter gave very sound advice on how to separate the research project, the innovation elements, and exploitation pathways. I think that this separation is very sound, it is in line with the general concept that the grant should be used for generally exploitable results, and individual exploitation of knowledge should be in the "exploitation pathway" a separate use of the intellectual property. It would also alleviate all kinds of data confidentiality or conflict of interest issues.



- I made some definitions of research outputs that we can expect, and I will discuss the relevant parts with Joost and Fabio on Monday afternoon; we should also discuss it with Arianna and James about the surveying.

- Eszter suggests to separate the general valuation model and methodology, and even the survey as research outputs, and she suggests that any particular valuations that will go into active use, and may end up as evidence in copyright tribunal, litigation, dispute with the royalty payers should be the "exploitation of results" based on separate contract between the CMOs and Reprex.



https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/wp1.html/&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/wp1.html#/researchoutput&gt;



In practice, this would mean that we will fill up the evaluation models with partly real data, and partly realistic but randomised data, and try to get scientific validation for the method, but not particular valuations. It is completely up to the management team or board of a CMO if they agree with an expert valuation, and if they act on it (for example, they change a tariff, they enter into a dispute with a royalty payer.)  That should be completely left out of the picture here.



This approach would also leave more room for research and rely less on a simple replication of the CEEMID background.



Best regards,
Daniel

Subject: Replication WP2 in Hungary

Hi James,

I had a few more conversations in Budapest and I think that we can replicate the WP2 in Hungary, though we do not know how we will avoid the censorship.  I made an extra effort, because building up such a network and workflow in a third country would be extremely time consuming.

In Hungary, nobody wants to be very much associated with the EU flag, so they do not want to become consortium partners or subcontractors, I would be paying as necessary on the purchase cost lines.

The material that we would make visible and connect via the data sharing space is scattered but spectacular.
- the entire collection of the Bartok Archive, with full English translation of letters, descriptions, captions, copies of original scores, letters, manuscripts, photographs
- the Hungarian pop music archive, and a catalogue of actual music videos,
- a few Hungarian indie labels catalogue.

We also found a new angle to work with Artisjus in a less visible role: we will use the data sharing space to report music use (according to the license terms) automatically to Artisjus;  I think that data-driven copyright law compliance was not our idea but it is an interesting case study and a good legal basis to handle metadata that would require otherwise difficult licenses.

All payments would be made via Reprex, mainly to the subcontractors of the music organisations; this way the institution directors have less visible political risk. For example, if they outsourced IT (like Hudobne centrum does) than we pay their IT freelancer directly, who does the work relevant for as a bonus task at the institutions.  We will have legal access to the content, but the cultural institutions will not touch EU money directly.

I think that this is a good compromise, because ZAiKS aims to have a visible role, and we can say that we replaced MUSIAUTOR with ZAiKS when a CMO was needed, and for WP2 we can claim that Slovakia's diverse musical heritage overlaps with Hungary, given that the two countries were one country for 900 years.

There is interest for WP2 Listen Local in several places, which are interesting avenues for exploitation, but I think that chasing them will create a time pressure, with this Hungarian material I can start working as of today, and by November we will surely have something to show in the IAML/IMIC conferences.

I hope that this is a good solution, it is actually the solution we had in mind with A38, with the exception that A38 will arrange for us to get the data and content but will not touch the money directly.  As we are talking about 12,000 euros and I will need to pay a few people, I think that these are very small payments anyways. I can even imagine that some of them can be converted to Reprex PMs if necessary.

Best regards,
Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder

Subject: Re: The OpenMusE project



Dear Jerzy and Anna,

Dear Colleagues,



After our conversation with Eszter I have updated the presentation thoroughly from the previous Wednesday. We critically reviewed the former CEEMID background, and Eszter gave very sound advice on how to separate the research project, the innovation elements, and exploitation pathways. I think that this separation is very sound, it is in line with the general concept that the grant should be used for generally exploitable results, and individual exploitation of knowledge should be in the "exploitation pathway" a separate use of the intellectual property. It would also alleviate all kinds of data confidentiality or conflict of interest issues.



- I made some definitions of research outputs that we can expect, and I will discuss the relevant parts with Joost and Fabio on Monday afternoon; we should also discuss it with Arianna and James about the surveying.

- Eszter suggests to separate the general valuation model and methodology, and even the survey as research outputs, and she suggests that any particular valuations that will go into active use, and may end up as evidence in copyright tribunal, litigation, dispute with the royalty payers should be the "exploitation of results" based on separate contract between the CMOs and Reprex.



https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/wp1.html/&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/wp1.html#/researchoutput&gt;



In practice, this would mean that we will fill up the evaluation models with partly real data, and partly realistic but randomised data, and try to get scientific validation for the method, but not particular valuations. It is completely up to the management team or board of a CMO if they agree with an expert valuation, and if they act on it (for example, they change a tariff, they enter into a dispute with a royalty payer.)  That should be completely left out of the picture here.



This approach would also leave more room for research and rely less on a simple replication of the CEEMID background.



Best regards,
Daniel

**From:** James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;

**Cc:** Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;, Anna.Misiewicz@zaiks.org.pl &lt;Anna.Misiewicz@zaiks.org.pl&gt;, Dr. Kabai Eszter &lt;ekabai@artisjus.com&gt;  
**Date:** 08/15/2024 13:20:47

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202408151320-Re_ Valuation + register + survey background-577.txt -->

Hi Joost and Daniel,

I hope you both enjoyed your holidays! Mine are upcoming from 22 to 30 August.

In the meantime I have been liaising with several other EU project teams. Two recently-concluded projects of potential interest to WP1 are Measuring CCS (https://www.measuring-ccs.eu/) and Cicerone (https://cicerone-project.eu/). I requested their non-public reports and uploaded them here:

https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1wYbk0oZ4NKwVyg9Cno0Ennd8y2SneEYn?usp=sharing

Please do not share these further.

Anyway, Measuring CCS has done an extensive review of EU and MS-level schemes for categorising, collecting data, and putting together statistics on the CCSIs (including cultural participation), and has prepared recommendations for a revision of the ESSNet-Culture framework. Please take a look at the "MeasuringCCS_Report on Inventory of Sources - Final_v1.3" and "MeasuringCCS_Analysis Report_Final_v3.0".

@Daniel, of particular interest to you might be Section 3 of the Analysis Report on "Using administrative sources for measuring CCS". We should take account of the Measuring CCS team's work in your final policy brief deliverable, D5.7, which we discussed using as a platform to critique and update the Feasibility Study.

Meanwhile, Cicerone has developed a data collection matrix very similar to the matrix we proposed in D3.1 – see "CICERONE D4.3 Everything you always wanted to know... Part II (plus Annex)". We should go through their ideas in detail prior to our revised indicators deliverable (D3.2 in the new work plan).

Finally: any thoughts on a WP1 meeting soon? Arianna and I are curious about the progress of T1.2 Defining sampling frame via CMOs , as it is prerequisite to our surveying tasks.

I am available Monday through Wednesday for a call.

Thank you and best regards,
James


________________________________

Cc: Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;; Anna.Misiewicz@zaiks.org.pl &lt;Anna.Misiewicz@zaiks.org.pl&gt;; Dr. Kabai Eszter &lt;ekabai@artisjus.com&gt;

Hi Daniel and all,

@Daniel Antal&lt;mailto:daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;, thank you for this! Please keep us updated and/or in CC where appropriate.

Tangentially: Daniel and @Joost Poort&lt;mailto:j.p.poort@uva.nl&gt;, prior to your call with Fabio today, it might be useful to take a look at Section 5 of the Measuring CCS project final report (https://www.measuring-ccs.eu/the-measuring-ccs-consortium-publishes-the-final-report/), which discusses methods for integration of platform data into CCSI statistics.
[https://www.measuring-ccs.eu/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/BANNER-EXAMPLE.png]&lt;https://www.measuring-ccs.eu/the-measuring-ccs-consortium-publishes-the-final-report/&gt;
The Measuring CCS Consortium publishes the Final Report - Measuring the Cultural and Creative Sectors in the EU&lt;https://www.measuring-ccs.eu/the-measuring-ccs-consortium-publishes-the-final-report/&gt;
This event aims to present and discuss the results of the project. The final outputs and outcomes will be delivered by the researchers led by Professor Manuel Villares of Qmetrics.
www.measuring-ccs.eu


We have reached out to the Measuring CCS team to request access to their more detailed methodology reports. If access is granted, I could see these being interesting / useful to ARTISJUS, SOZA, and ZAiKS as well.

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: 12 July 2024 15:09
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;; Arianna Martinelli &lt;Arianna.Martinelli@santannapisa.it&gt;
Cc: Joost Poort &lt;j.p.poort@uva.nl&gt;; Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;; Anna.Misiewicz@zaiks.org.pl &lt;Anna.Misiewicz@zaiks.org.pl&gt;; Dr. Kabai Eszter &lt;ekabai@artisjus.com&gt;
Subject: Valuation + register + survey background

Dear James and Joost,

To avoid much cross-posting, I send a separate letter to the three CMOs based on a very long conversation with Eszter about the valuation project element.  We think that we should have a realistic expectation from all three societies (Artisjus, SOZA, ZAiKS) what they want to achieve as a shared and open result in this project, and what are their particular business sensitivities that they want to keep as SENSITIVE in the exploitation pathways, and perhaps further issues that they do not even want to bring into the consortium.

This is not related to the integrity of the data collection and methodology, it is strictly related to how Artisjus, ZAiKS, SOZA will utilise the results, but it is an important first step to come up with a realistic survey and valuation program.

We agreed with Eszter that the work in our background is in many ways obsolete, it answered questions of the 2010s, and it was very much related to national and international controversies  of that decade. We do not think that our background should be very directly used.

I have a clearer understanding of Artijus's needs and expectations, and will try to align this with SOZA and ZAIKS in the coming days, while also transferring the relevant part of the background to SSSA and SINUS. Our aim is to clear off unnecessary business considerations and focus only on methodology that requires scientific corroboration.

Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder

HI Fabio,

So I think that when you work programmatically, you should work on GitHub in our repos, and make your code available with explanations.
1. I wrote quickly a function that combines our spotifyr functions and using a search term "Jana",  which is a very popular female name in Slovakia, returns about 2000 track in one go, in about 5 minutes.  Please customise this function to save the IRSC code, probably even delineated to country registrar, unique registrar, year.

It is in the https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/openmusesampling  repository. There are many popular female and male name lists per country available, most use family names lists, etc, you can iterate on them.

2. When you describe a problem, connect it to your code and documentation.  In R/Rtudio this is what the vignette is for. So, what I would like to see is that you include in this repository your functions and code, and then you put the problem with explanations into a vignette.  The vignette serves to explain parts of the code.  This way I can review your thinking and review your code at the same time, run it myself, and understand where you are trying to get at.

In spring we started to work like this, and I think we should take it more seriously, because as time lapses, it will become less and less easy for me to track your work.

Best regards,


search_tracks_by_term &lt;- function(search_term, wasAssociatedWith) {
  startedAtTime &lt;- Sys.time()

  uri_to_id &lt;- function(uri) gsub("spotify:artist:|spotify:album:", "", uri)
  potential_artists &lt;- search_spotify(q=search_term, type="artist") %&gt;%
    select ( uri, popularity )

  spotify_artist_ids &lt;- gsub("spotify:artist:", "", potential_artists$uri)

  potential_artists_albums  &lt;- lapply(spotify_artist_ids, get_artist_albums)
  albums_df &lt;- purrr::reduce(potential_artists_albums, rbind)
  tracks    &lt;- lapply(albums_df$id,  get_album_tracks)
  tracks_df &lt;- purrr::reduce(lapply ( tracks, function(x) x %&gt;% select (name, duration_ms, id, uri)), rbind)

  get_track_data &lt;- function(id) {

    df &lt;- get_track(id)
    data.frame (
      spotify_track_id = df$id,
      spotify_track_uri=  df$uri,
      popularity      =  df$popularity,
      duration_ms     =  df$duration_ms,
      time_query     = Sys.time()) %&gt;%
      bind_cols(df$artists %&gt;% select (spotify_artist_name = name, spotify_artist_id = id, spotify_artist_uri = uri)
      )
  }

  all_tracks &lt;- lapply(tracks_df$id, get_track_data)
  all_tracks_df &lt;- purrr::reduce(all_tracks, rbind)

  prov &lt;- provenance_statement(startedAtTime = startedAtTime, endedAtTime = Sys.time(), wasAssociatedWith = )

  attr(all_tracks_df, "provenance") &lt;- prov

  all_tracks_df
}

Hi Fabio,

I suggest that we make an online meeting either at 10.00 or at 12.00 on Thursday, if it works for you. I will review what you wrote, and I have a good assignment for you.

This worksheet has two sheets. One has all the names of the music publishers registered in Slovakia for royalty collection.  Music publishers are not equal to labels, but almost always they also manage a same-named label.

So what I would suggest is to try to find them as labels on Spotify, and try to retrieve all the records that they released. Alternatively, look for their names in your treasure trove if you identify at least one of their ISRC, because likely they register under the same registrant details.

The other parts is more straightforward, all the classical and jazz orchestras of Slovakia. You can search for them as artist names. Try to create a CSV table that links the spotify artist id to their names, and then all tracks you find.  We will also be able to find their other releases.

Unfortunately I do not have this yet in a good CSV form, but probably you can put it with hand to a simple table&gt; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Slovak_feminine_given_names
and just search for them in artists names.

I will have a similar male version in CSV, hopefully still today.

Hi Fabio,

I suggest that we make an online meeting either at 10.00 or at 12.00 on Thursday, if it works for you. I will review what you wrote, and I have a good assignment for you.

This worksheet has two sheets. One has all the names of the music publishers registered in Slovakia for royalty collection.  Music publishers are not equal to labels, but almost always they also manage a same-named label.

So what I would suggest is to try to find them as labels on Spotify, and try to retrieve all the records that they released. Alternatively, look for their names in your treasure trove if you identify at least one of their ISRC, because likely they register under the same registrant details.

The other parts is more straightforward, all the classical and jazz orchestras of Slovakia. You can search for them as artist names. Try to create a CSV table that links the spotify artist id to their names, and then all tracks you find.  We will also be able to find their other releases.
