Betreff: OpenMusE Bergfest

Dear all,

Our project is halfway through, which we would like to celebrate with you at our Bergfest from September 30th to October 1st.
Indeed, the last year and a half have often felt like a tough hike up a steep mountain. We’ve finally arrived at a point in the project where we can enjoy the view before taking the (hopefully) easier path until the end of our hike 😊

Working with this symbolic, Synyo and Sinus will organize the Bergfest in the mountains surrounding Vienna, in Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;. It’s quite close to the city and can be reached by train&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt; in ca. 1 ½ hours from Vienna airport (see attachment) or 1 hour from the main train station (Hauptbahnhof).

The Bergfest will take place in the “Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt;”, a historic, old-school Austrian hotel in Reichenau.
We have blocked rooms for the consortium at a reduced price, which you need to book directly with the hotel! Please contact hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; and mention the “OpenMusE seminar”. Please also let them know if you need a shuttle from the train station in Reichenau (13€ p.p.).


We’re currently working on the agenda, which we will send out once it’s finalized with the WP leaders. On the program so far:

  *   Several workshops to boost the second half of our project
  *   A General Assembly
  *   A voluntary hike on Sept. 29th for all early birds
  *   Time to relax, enjoy the view, and make some noise


All details at a glance:

  *   Date: September 30th to October 1st (arrival on September 29th)
  *   Place: Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;
  *   Hotel: Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt; --&gt; please book your room directly with the hotel: hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; !
  *   Room prices:
     *   Sept. 29th to 30th: 100€ p.p. in an individual room including breakfast
     *   Sept. 30th to Oct. 1st: 165€ p.p. in an individual room, including breakfast lunch and dinner on Sept. 30th
     *   Any additional night: 100€ p.p. in an individual room including breakfast
  *   To plan your train ride, use the ÖBB website Home - ÖBB (oebb.at)&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt;, not Google Maps! The closest train station is “Payerbach-Reichenau” (see attachment)

To make this a proper team event, it would be great if 1-2 people could join per partner. Please fill in the following form to RSVP: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1JSlzhVlQzIE8rT-5_9K1IZyIDM6diwQzkZKIty8mQgg/edit?usp=sharing
Reminder: You have travel budgets for in-person meetings, which for most partners remain largely untouched. It would help neither the EC, nor your organization, to return unused budgets.


We are looking forward to celebrating with you!

Best regards,

Marc, James &amp; Isabella

Indeed, the last year and a half have often felt like a tough hike up a steep mountain. We’ve finally arrived at a point in the project where we can enjoy the view before taking the (hopefully) easier path until the end of our hike 😊

Working with this symbolic, Synyo and Sinus will organize the Bergfest in the mountains surrounding Vienna, in Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;. It’s quite close to the city and can be reached by train&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt; in ca. 1 ½ hours from Vienna airport (see attachment) or 1 hour from the main train station (Hauptbahnhof).

The Bergfest will take place in the “Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt;”, a historic, old-school Austrian hotel in Reichenau.
We have blocked rooms for the consortium at a reduced price, which you need to book directly with the hotel! Please contact hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; and mention the “OpenMusE seminar”. Please also let them know if you need a shuttle from the train station in Reichenau (13€ p.p.).


We’re currently working on the agenda, which we will send out once it’s finalized with the WP leaders. On the program so far:

  *   Several workshops to boost the second half of our project
  *   A General Assembly
  *   A voluntary hike on Sept. 29th for all early birds
  *   Time to relax, enjoy the view, and make some noise


All details at a glance:

  *   Date: September 30th to October 1st (arrival on September 29th)
  *   Place: Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;
  *   Hotel: Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt; --&gt; please book your room directly with the hotel: hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; !
  *   Room prices:
     *   Sept. 29th to 30th: 100€ p.p. in an individual room including breakfast
     *   Sept. 30th to Oct. 1st: 165€ p.p. in an individual room, including breakfast lunch and dinner on Sept. 30th
     *   Any additional night: 100€ p.p. in an individual room including breakfast
  *   To plan your train ride, use the ÖBB website Home - ÖBB (oebb.at)&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt;, not Google Maps! The closest train station is “Payerbach-Reichenau” (see attachment)

To make this a proper team event, it would be great if 1-2 people could join per partner. Please fill in the following form to RSVP: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1JSlzhVlQzIE8rT-5_9K1IZyIDM6diwQzkZKIty8mQgg/edit?usp=sharing
Reminder: You have travel budgets for in-person meetings, which for most partners remain largely untouched. It would help neither the EC, nor your organization, to return unused budgets.


We are looking forward to celebrating with you!

Best regards,

Marc, James &amp; Isabella

Betreff: OpenMusE Bergfest

Dear all,

Our project is halfway through, which we would like to celebrate with you at our Bergfest from September 30th to October 1st.
Indeed, the last year and a half have often felt like a tough hike up a steep mountain. We’ve finally arrived at a point in the project where we can enjoy the view before taking the (hopefully) easier path until the end of our hike 😊

Working with this symbolic, Synyo and Sinus will organize the Bergfest in the mountains surrounding Vienna, in Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;. It’s quite close to the city and can be reached by train&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt; in ca. 1 ½ hours from Vienna airport (see attachment) or 1 hour from the main train station (Hauptbahnhof).

The Bergfest will take place in the “Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt;”, a historic, old-school Austrian hotel in Reichenau.
We have blocked rooms for the consortium at a reduced price, which you need to book directly with the hotel! Please contact hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; and mention the “OpenMusE seminar”. Please also let them know if you need a shuttle from the train station in Reichenau (13€ p.p.).


We’re currently working on the agenda, which we will send out once it’s finalized with the WP leaders. On the program so far:

  *   Several workshops to boost the second half of our project
  *   A General Assembly
  *   A voluntary hike on Sept. 29th for all early birds
  *   Time to relax, enjoy the view, and make some noise


All details at a glance:

  *   Date: September 30th to October 1st (arrival on September 29th)
  *   Place: Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;
  *   Hotel: Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt; --&gt; please book your room directly with the hotel: hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; !
  *   Room prices:

     *   Sept. 29th to 30th: 100€ p.p. in an individual room including breakfast
     *   Sept. 30th to Oct. 1st: 165€ p.p. in an individual room, including breakfast lunch and dinner on Sept. 30th
     *   Any additional night: 100€ p.p. in an individual room including breakfast

  *   To plan your train ride, use the ÖBB website Home - ÖBB (oebb.at)&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt;, not Google Maps! The closest train station is “Payerbach-Reichenau” (see attachment)

To make this a proper team event, it would be great if 1-2 people could join per partner. Please fill in the following form to RSVP: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1JSlzhVlQzIE8rT-5_9K1IZyIDM6diwQzkZKIty8mQgg/edit?usp=sharing
Reminder: You have travel budgets for in-person meetings, which for most partners remain largely untouched. It would help neither the EC, nor your organization, to return unused budgets.


We are looking forward to celebrating with you!

Best regards,

Marc, James &amp; Isabella

Betreff: OpenMusE Bergfest

Dear all,

Our project is halfway through, which we would like to celebrate with you at our Bergfest from September 30th to October 1st.
Indeed, the last year and a half have often felt like a tough hike up a steep mountain. We’ve finally arrived at a point in the project where we can enjoy the view before taking the (hopefully) easier path until the end of our hike 😊

Working with this symbolic, Synyo and Sinus will organize the Bergfest in the mountains surrounding Vienna, in Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;. It’s quite close to the city and can be reached by train&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt; in ca. 1 ½ hours from Vienna airport (see attachment) or 1 hour from the main train station (Hauptbahnhof).

The Bergfest will take place in the “Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt;”, a historic, old-school Austrian hotel in Reichenau.
We have blocked rooms for the consortium at a reduced price, which you need to book directly with the hotel! Please contact hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; and mention the “OpenMusE seminar”. Please also let them know if you need a shuttle from the train station in Reichenau (13€ p.p.).


We’re currently working on the agenda, which we will send out once it’s finalized with the WP leaders. On the program so far:

  1.  Several workshops to boost the second half of our project
  2.  A General Assembly
  3.  A voluntary hike on Sept. 29th for all early birds
  4.  Time to relax, enjoy the view, and make some noise


All details at a glance:

  1.  Date: September 30th to October 1st (arrival on September 29th)
  2.  Place: Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;
  3.  Hotel: Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt; --&gt; please book your room directly with the hotel: hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; !
  4.  Room prices:

     *   Sept. 29th to 30th: 100€ p.p. in an individual room including breakfast
     *   Sept. 30th to Oct. 1st: 165€ p.p. in an individual room, including breakfast lunch and dinner on Sept. 30th
     *   Any additional night: 100€ p.p. in an individual room including breakfast

  1.  To plan your train ride, use the ÖBB website Home - ÖBB (oebb.at)&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt;, not Google Maps! The closest train station is “Payerbach-Reichenau” (see attachment)

To make this a proper team event, it would be great if 1-2 people could join per partner. Please fill in the following form to RSVP: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1JSlzhVlQzIE8rT-5_9K1IZyIDM6diwQzkZKIty8mQgg/edit?usp=sharing
Reminder: You have travel budgets for in-person meetings, which for most partners remain largely untouched. It would help neither the EC, nor your organization, to return unused budgets.


We are looking forward to celebrating with you!

Best regards,

Marc, James &amp; Isabella

### OpenMusE Bergfest Agenda &amp; Information {#email-665}

**From:** Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**To:** OpenMusE Consortium &lt;openmuseconsortium@sinus-institut.de&gt;  
**Cc:** James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;, Marc Calmbach &lt;Marc.Calmbach@sinus-institut.de&gt;, Christoph Steiner &lt;christoph.steiner@synyo.com&gt;  
**Date:** 09/25/2024 15:57:26

<!-- source: OpenMuse_20261009-2156/OpenMuse/messages/202409251557-OpenMusE Bergfest Agenda & Information-283.txt -->

Dear all,

Please find the Bergfest agenda attached! We had to restructure the agenda quite a bit in the last days to accommodate for partners’ arrival times.
Smaller changes might still occur and will be communicated promptly.

Please find some further information below:

Day 0 – Voluntary hike
We will meet at the hotel at 10:30 and take a train to Semmering, from where we will hike back to Reichenau. This is an easy and scenic hike, and completely voluntary for everyone who will get to Austria early and would like to join!
To the people that have indicated that they want to join, I will contact you individually and create a whatsapp group to coordinate the hike!
The weather forecast is sunny but cold, so please bring stable shoes and appropriate clothing. I have attached a packing list with everything you need to bring.

Day 1 – Seminar day
There will be several workshops to discuss &amp; brainstorm open questions within the consortium, take in all opinions from within the team and kick-start the remaining months of the project.

Day 2 – General assembly
In the morning of day two, we will have a short general assembly, to take advantage of the rare opportunity of having everyone under one roof. We will send out a separate agenda for this.
Here are the most important topics that we plan to discuss (not necessarily in this order):

  *   Amendment update
  *   Zaiks &amp; further replacements for Musicautor
  *   IKP’s dissolvement and its impact on the project
  *   Cooperation with sister projects
  *   Upcoming delvierables &amp; quality check

Please let us know if there are any additional topics that you want to discuss, and we will add them to the list.

Day 2 – Team building
In the true spirit of Bergfest, Christoph has organized an excursion to the mountains next to Reichenau on Tuesday afternoon! We will take the cable car “Raxseilbahn&lt;https://www.raxalpe.com/&gt;” up the mountain and go for a short hike to Ottohaus&lt;https://www.wieneralpen.at/en/ottohaus&gt;, where we will have lunch. This is a very easy hike that is doable at all fitness levels. The weather forecast for Tuesday is sunny but cold, so please bring stable shoes and appropriate clothing. I have attached a packing list with everything you need to bring.
We will return to the hotel at 5pm latest, probably slightly earlier.

Transportation
Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt; is quite close to Vienna and can be reached by train&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt; in ca. 1 ½ hours from Vienna airport (see attachment) or 1 hour from the main train station (Hauptbahnhof). The hotel can organize a shuttle for you from Payerbach-Reichenau station, otherwise it’s 30 minutes walking. Please contact the hotel directly to organize the shuttle.

Costs
SINUS will cover the costs for:

  *   the seminar rooms on Monday and Tuesday
  *   non-alcoholic beverages on Monday during lunch and dinner
  *   The train tickets on Sunday for the voluntary hike
SYNYO will cover the teambuilding on Tuesday:

  *   The transportation to the Rax Seilbahn and back to the hotel
  *   The cable car tickets
  *   The lunch at Ottohaus
PARTNERS will have to pay as part of their travel budget:

  *   their rooms
  *   Meals outside the seminar days (Lunch and dinner on Monday, as well as daily breakfast are already included and do not have to be paid separately).
  *   Any alcoholic beverages
  *   Any further costs occurring on the voluntary hike on Sunday (Food &amp; beverages etc.)

Please let me know if you have any questions!

Best regards,

SINUS &amp; SYNYO

Betreff: OpenMusE Bergfest

Dear all,

Our project is halfway through, which we would like to celebrate with you at our Bergfest from September 30th to October 1st.
Indeed, the last year and a half have often felt like a tough hike up a steep mountain. We’ve finally arrived at a point in the project where we can enjoy the view before taking the (hopefully) easier path until the end of our hike 😊

Working with this symbolic, Synyo and Sinus will organize the Bergfest in the mountains surrounding Vienna, in Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;. It’s quite close to the city and can be reached by train&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt; in ca. 1 ½ hours from Vienna airport (see attachment) or 1 hour from the main train station (Hauptbahnhof).

The Bergfest will take place in the “Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt;”, a historic, old-school Austrian hotel in Reichenau.
We have blocked rooms for the consortium at a reduced price, which you need to book directly with the hotel! Please contact hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; and mention the “OpenMusE seminar”. Please also let them know if you need a shuttle from the train station in Reichenau (13€ p.p.).


We’re currently working on the agenda, which we will send out once it’s finalized with the WP leaders. On the program so far:

  *   Several workshops to boost the second half of our project
  *   A General Assembly
  *   A voluntary hike on Sept. 29th for all early birds
  *   Time to relax, enjoy the view, and make some noise


All details at a glance:

  *   Date: September 30th to October 1st (arrival on September 29th)
  *   Place: Reichenau an der Rax&lt;https://maps.app.goo.gl/EjG8io2sLEYnFup2A&gt;
  *   Hotel: Hotel Marienhof&lt;https://www.marienhof.at/en/&gt; --&gt; please book your room directly with the hotel: hotel@marienhof.at&lt;mailto:hotel@marienhof.at&gt; !
  *   Room prices:

     *   Sept. 29th to 30th: 100€ p.p. in an individual room including breakfast
     *   Sept. 30th to Oct. 1st: 165€ p.p. in an individual room, including breakfast lunch and dinner on Sept. 30th
     *   Any additional night: 100€ p.p. in an individual room including breakfast

  *   To plan your train ride, use the ÖBB website Home - ÖBB (oebb.at)&lt;https://www.oebb.at/en/&gt;, not Google Maps! The closest train station is “Payerbach-Reichenau” (see attachment)

To make this a proper team event, it would be great if 1-2 people could join per partner. Please fill in the following form to RSVP: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1JSlzhVlQzIE8rT-5_9K1IZyIDM6diwQzkZKIty8mQgg/edit?usp=sharing
Reminder: You have travel budgets for in-person meetings, which for most partners remain largely untouched. It would help neither the EC, nor your organization, to return unused budgets.


We are looking forward to celebrating with you!

Best regards,

Marc, James &amp; Isabella

Dear Daniel and all,

This is very unfortunate news. For us as a project, and perhaps more importantly for the Slovak music ecosystem.

For me, this underscores the potential value of producing some kind of written output that highlights the political factors involved in music data access. I think these factors are not well understood by researchers, and are consequently underestimated (if not necessarily by industry practitioners, who are undoubtedly familiar). Of course, using IKP as an example would be contingent on their consent / cooperation. We do not want to kick the hornet's nest, and even if we were to "pseudonymise" our account, it would be evident to anyone with Google immediately who we were talking about. Something to consider / discuss.

Switching topics: @Joost, looks good to me, thank you very much. Looking forward to the call.

Best regards,
James

Subject: Re: WP1 Meeting



Dear Colleagues,



I must pass on some very sad news that will affect our work, and make the work that we originally planned for the previous year partly impossible. In the very beginning of the project, Tomas and I worked hard to write a MoU with the Slovak Ministry of Culture. The IKP policy unit of the ministry was instrumental to make this work, provide us access to register data, etc. The ministry disbanded the entire unit and laid off all its members, which is something not unexpected after Slovakia started to follow Hungary.



For our work, this means that we will have less impact, less data access, and we will have to work harder to achieve things that we could have taken for granted in the previous 20 months.



I think that this is important to keep in mind for the entire WP1 and WP2.



Best regards,
Daniel

Subject: Re: WP1 Meeting



Dear Colleagues,



I must pass on some very sad news that will affect our work, and make the work that we originally planned for the previous year partly impossible. In the very beginning of the project, Tomas and I worked hard to write a MoU with the Slovak Ministry of Culture. The IKP policy unit of the ministry was instrumental to make this work, provide us access to register data, etc. The ministry disbanded the entire unit and laid off all its members, which is something not unexpected after Slovakia started to follow Hungary.



For our work, this means that we will have less impact, less data access, and we will have to work harder to achieve things that we could have taken for granted in the previous 20 months.



I think that this is important to keep in mind for the entire WP1 and WP2.



Best regards,
Daniel

We've used Qualtrics for this mini-survey project for expediency – we're not committed to using it for the CAP survey (as you noted, our fieldwork partners might prefer to program it themselves, using whatever proprietary system they use).

________________________________
From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: 16 August 2024 18:00
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Cc: Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Subject: Re: Question bank presentation

Hi James,

What I programmed for the questionbank follows the GESIS DDI data model; and to be very honest, I am not very happy with the way GESIS is handling this, it seems to me rather impractical and it is acknowledged to be work in progress. Collectica is supposed to use the same specification with a lot more details, but I have never seen an output from Collectica.

In my opinion, the most straightforward would be to create the questionbank in a Google Spreadsheet that we set up for you. Collectica is a very expensive proprietary software so that its native files are not necessarily useful for an open question bank. I may be able to read in a Collectica XML, but I am not sure that I can make sense of it without a technical documentation, and I am sure that we do not want to utilise all the functionality of Collectica.

With the number of questions you mention either way this is not a very big deal, even if we do it two different ways manually it is not a big amount of work.

To me what is unclear what you want to achieve with the question bank?
1. One use would be to import from an existing question bank to your survey (if I understand correctly, this is not the case);
2. the other that we make your work replicable for future users.

In either case I would not stick to the Collectica XML, because it is an expensive and heavy-weight application; and I know of now open question banks where you can obtain Collectica XML files, and we also cannot use it for publishing.

In my understanding we would just make sure that we make your questionbank easy-to-replicate in  Qualtrics, SurveyMonkey, Google Forms, or any simple application with little pain. In my opinion, we are actually still treading on a new path, so far what I saw from GESIS, for example, was not very user friendly. So we anyway need to experiment a bit on how to present your questions.

I would only put into the questionbank the following information:

- the concept that the question is targetting;
- the expected type of variable that should be the question output;
- a name of the variable,
- a description of the variable;
- a label of the question text in any given language;
- in case of categorical variables, the labels, codes of the answer options in all used languages;
- for other variables, codes for various missing values (declined, filtered, etc.)

&lt;if Collectica has anything else that you may want to implement, we can talk about it&gt;

With this amount of information this is best done in a spreadsheet, then it is easy to put it into Collectica and Qualtrics, or any other software.  I would suggest the spreadsheet because it also allows the independent checking of whatever is pasted into Qualtrics or Collectica.



Best regards,
Daniel

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&lt;mailto:daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;&gt;

Cc: Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt;
Subject: Re: Question bank presentation

Hi James,

What I programmed for the questionbank follows the GESIS DDI data model; and to be very honest, I am not very happy with the way GESIS is handling this, it seems to me rather impractical and it is acknowledged to be work in progress. Collectica is supposed to use the same specification with a lot more details, but I have never seen an output from Collectica.

In my opinion, the most straightforward would be to create the questionbank in a Google Spreadsheet that we set up for you. Collectica is a very expensive proprietary software so that its native files are not necessarily useful for an open question bank. I may be able to read in a Collectica XML, but I am not sure that I can make sense of it without a technical documentation, and I am sure that we do not want to utilise all the functionality of Collectica.

With the number of questions you mention either way this is not a very big deal, even if we do it two different ways manually it is not a big amount of work.

To me what is unclear what you want to achieve with the question bank?
1. One use would be to import from an existing question bank to your survey (if I understand correctly, this is not the case);
2. the other that we make your work replicable for future users.

In either case I would not stick to the Collectica XML, because it is an expensive and heavy-weight application; and I know of now open question banks where you can obtain Collectica XML files, and we also cannot use it for publishing.

In my understanding we would just make sure that we make your questionbank easy-to-replicate in  Qualtrics, SurveyMonkey, Google Forms, or any simple application with little pain. In my opinion, we are actually still treading on a new path, so far what I saw from GESIS, for example, was not very user friendly. So we anyway need to experiment a bit on how to present your questions.

I would only put into the questionbank the following information:

- the concept that the question is targetting;
- the expected type of variable that should be the question output;
- a name of the variable,
- a description of the variable;
- a label of the question text in any given language;
- in case of categorical variables, the labels, codes of the answer options in all used languages;
- for other variables, codes for various missing values (declined, filtered, etc.)

&lt;if Collectica has anything else that you may want to implement, we can talk about it&gt;

With this amount of information this is best done in a spreadsheet, then it is easy to put it into Collectica and Qualtrics, or any other software.  I would suggest the spreadsheet because it also allows the independent checking of whatever is pasted into Qualtrics or Collectica.



Best regards,
Daniel

Hi Daniel,

Thank you for your consideration here, your points make total sense. IMO the purpose is still to build a novel solution that is actually usable for our target groups, rather than simply to tick a box.

Showing off for GESIS isn't a priority as based on my interactions, they have their own DDI compliance agenda and aren't going to pay much attention to what anyone else does (regardless of whether it might be done more efficiently or provide better usability for actual survey practitioners).

I agree that combining the question label with the answer options is a confusing solution. As you note it blocks concept harmonisation and could yield thousands of combinations of very similar items covering the same set of concepts. This defeats the purpose of a question bank! And the confusion would become yet greater when multiple languages are added.

I agree with your proposed solution. I'm happy to have a short call today. I'm observing focus groups this morning, but am free from 13-15:00 and then again from 16-17:30. My schedule tomorrow is also pretty flexible. On Wednesday I leave for another short holiday (but will be off the bike, so available for audio calls).

Thank you again and best regards,
James

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: 08 September 2024 10:12
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;
Subject: Questionbank question

Hello James,

Before we go on with the questionbank, I would like to ask you, perhaps in a short audio call simply, if you have time to ring me, what is the purpose here?

To me, it is not clear if we want to show off to the EU evaluators, want to build a novel solution, or show off for GESIS, or tick a box.

The reason why I am asking is that we started to implement a rather new ontological solution from GESIS, in the absence of anything else found. However, I am not very happy with the GESIS solution.  I do not know if it is compatible with Collectica or not (do you use it?), but to me it is rather impractical. They are concatenating the question label with the answer options into a single text, which is unambiguous, but also necessitates a lot of duplications, and some kind of preprocessing before reuse.

Their solution looks like this:

Which fruit do you like? [ ] orange [ ] apple [ ] pear

Now, if you have a second question with different options

Which fruit do you like? [ ] orange [ ] apple [ ] apricot

it becomes a new item. This is very problematic with scaled categorical variables, like agreement which has 2, 3, 4, 5 options, or with item lists when the items are similar (of the same "class")

To me, it would be far more logical to do it like this&gt;

Question Q567&gt; Which fruit do you like? [ ] fruit options list

Fruit options list &gt; may contain [ ] orange [ ] apple [ ] pear [ ] apricot [ ] plum
&lt;any item from the class of fruit, in this case we can also make sure easily that they are connected to a controlled vocabulary authority!  A curator may even add further fruits&gt;

Of course, this would also require post processing, but rather simple. For example, I would create a simple code for querying Question Q567 that would produce

a) all possibilities Which fruit do you like?  [ ] orange [ ] apple [ ] pear [ ] apricot [ ] plum

b) or, if the user asks for Q567 with apples and oranges only Which fruit do you like?  [ ] orange [ ] apple [ ]

To sum up, we need to know the use case in mind. If we ever want to further use this, I would recommend to break a bit from the GESIS practice, and utilise their disco ontology with a bit of critical attitude.  If we just want to report something that we did it and make it available, we can continue as it is now, and our data dissemination will be fully compliant with the GESIS practice, easy to report ... but unlikely that many people will use it, as GESIS's technical solution is very user unfriendly.

Best regards,


Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder

Dear Anna,



Thank you for your patience as we prepared these documents. Attached is a draft Statement of Work, subject to your edits and approval. This would apply in both participation cases: either as a partner, or as a service provider.



As a partner, you would accede to the Grant Agreement Core and Consortium Agreement, both of which are attached. They are long, but appear more complex than they are. We would be happy to walk you through them in a call.



As a service provider, you would sign a contract with the contracting entity. A potential draft is attached (note that the contracting entity may be a partner other than SINUS – this should not impact the substance of the contract).



From the Consortium's perspective, having ZAiKS onboard as a partner would be highly preferable. Your formal participation would greatly elevate the visibility and significance of our project and outputs. We also believe that partnership could bring benefits to ZAiKS – for instance, the opportunity to participate in EU-level policy events and make your voices and interests directly heard by policymakers and industry stakeholders alike. The Consortium could make funding available for your travel to relevant high-level events.



On a bureaucratic level, our Project Officer has also indicated that signing on an additional Service Provider might entail difficulties. However, if this is the only feasible option for participation, we will find a way to make it work.



Please write or call anytime with questions or comments. I am at your disposal this afternoon or any day next week – with the exception of the 16th, which I'm taking off to celebrate my birthday.



Thank you again, and best regards,

James

To: Jerzy Łabuda &lt;Jerzy.Labuda@zaiks.org.pl&lt;mailto:Jerzy.Labuda@zaiks.org.pl&gt;&gt;; Poort, Joost &lt;J.P.Poort@uva.nl&lt;mailto:J.P.Poort@uva.nl&gt;&gt;; James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt;
Cc: Anna Misiewicz &lt;Anna.Misiewicz@zaiks.org.pl&lt;mailto:Anna.Misiewicz@zaiks.org.pl&gt;&gt;; Demčák Richard &lt;richard.demcak@soza.sk&lt;mailto:richard.demcak@soza.sk&gt;&gt;; Dr. Kabai Eszter &lt;ekabai@artisjus.com&lt;mailto:ekabai@artisjus.com&gt;&gt;; Arianna Martinelli &lt;arianna.martinelli@santannapisa.it&lt;mailto:arianna.martinelli@santannapisa.it&gt;&gt;
Subject: Re: The OpenMusE project



Dear Jerzy and Anna,

Dear Colleagues,



After our conversation with Eszter I have updated the presentation thoroughly from the previous Wednesday. We critically reviewed the former CEEMID background, and Eszter gave very sound advice on how to separate the research project, the innovation elements, and exploitation pathways. I think that this separation is very sound, it is in line with the general concept that the grant should be used for generally exploitable results, and individual exploitation of knowledge should be in the "exploitation pathway" a separate use of the intellectual property. It would also alleviate all kinds of data confidentiality or conflict of interest issues.



- I made some definitions of research outputs that we can expect, and I will discuss the relevant parts with Joost and Fabio on Monday afternoon; we should also discuss it with Arianna and James about the surveying.

- Eszter suggests to separate the general valuation model and methodology, and even the survey as research outputs, and she suggests that any particular valuations that will go into active use, and may end up as evidence in copyright tribunal, litigation, dispute with the royalty payers should be the "exploitation of results" based on separate contract between the CMOs and Reprex.



https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/wp1.html/&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/wp1.html#/researchoutput&gt;



In practice, this would mean that we will fill up the evaluation models with partly real data, and partly realistic but randomised data, and try to get scientific validation for the method, but not particular valuations. It is completely up to the management team or board of a CMO if they agree with an expert valuation, and if they act on it (for example, they change a tariff, they enter into a dispute with a royalty payer.)  That should be completely left out of the picture here.



This approach would also leave more room for research and rely less on a simple replication of the CEEMID background.



Best regards,
Daniel

James

Subject: A basic task we did in Slovakia - for the Bergfest

Dear Anna, Jerzy,

I did not know who will participate and in which parts of our project on your behalf, so I would like to forward you this. Not all features may be interesting to you (though I think they should!) but we will talk about this on the Bergfest!

Best regards,

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&lt;mailto:daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;&gt;



Dear Colleagues,

Before the Bergfest, let me introduce our public register demo (which has a much bigger non-public version in Slovakia.) I also want to thank the work of @Demčák Richard&lt;mailto:Richard.Demcak@soza.sk&gt; , @Jankovič Marián&lt;mailto:marian.jankovic@soza.sk&gt; , @Anna Zilkova&lt;mailto:anna.zilkova@hc.sk&gt; , @AnnA Mester&lt;mailto:anna.mester@reprex.nl&gt; , and the SOZA/HC IT teams and everybody who helped!

(I add everybody else in BCC who did not directly contribute to this, or is not a WP leader.)

It is a statistical frame, register and backbone of our future services, the SKCMDb.  This is real, tested data, but very few at this point.This is a critical input for the finalisation of WP1, WP2 and WP3 tasks, and the OMO observatory in WP5.

The SKCMDb has a public and a non-public layer; the public layer contains information that is not business sensitive or requires GDPR consent that we have.  The non-public layer has all the other data that we need for our work.

The SKCMDb public demo&lt;https://reprexbase.eu/demo/index.php?title=Item:Q200&gt;

What do we do with the music publishers in Slovakia dataset&lt;https://reprexbase.eu/demo/index.php?title=Item:Q201&gt;?

- This is a continuously updated dataset (synchronized with data from the national company registers, and that of Open Corporates, which is a register of registers by the World Bank.)
- It is the basis of the satellite structural business register for statistical data collection: this is the part of these companies that was active in 2024 in the Slovak Republic (i.e., they received royalties via SOZA or else.)  Only those publishers contribute to the GDP and employment of Slovakia that had income in 2024.
- It is also a useful tool to keep CMO registers up to date.

What do we do with the Slovak composers’ dataset&lt;https://reprexbase.eu/demo/index.php?title=Item:Q203&gt;?

- You only see here data with GDPR consent with the public interface!
- We help NERD name entity resolution and disambiguation with name versions and other data to help to sort out name duplications and spelling errors for rights management and library/collection management.
- We connect them, if they consent, to Google Knowledge Graph, Wikidata, Spoitfy, etc, so that algorithms that recommend music or search engines find authoritative information about them, and this will increase their visibility, page rank, etc.
- This is also the basis of the SSBR (informal enterprises) and LFS (labor force surveying), because those need to be surveyed for our valuation/market research who were active in the year before.
- We will work with the Slovak National Library to ensure that these people are in the authoritative global ISNI and VIAF systems, similar to the experimental project of Teosto, and hope to showcase this in the CISAC Good Governance seminar.
- We want to measure if the resolved NERD issues lead to less royalty loss, and royalty payments @Fábio Generoso Vieira&lt;mailto:f.v.vieira@uva.nl&gt;
- We aim to create similar performers, conductors, etc. collections and datasets.


What do we do with the Slovak musical groups &lt;https://reprexbase.eu/demo/index.php?title=Item:Q204&gt; dataset?

- Musical groups are the hardest to identify entities, because they usually have no legal personality, registration, or membership changes, but they release music.
- We aim to give them global, permanent identifiers on VIAF, ISNI, and Wikidata, which will help to keep their recordings (ISRCs) and ISWC connected.
- We connect them, if they consent, to Google Knowledge Graph, Wikidata, Spoitfy, etc, so that algorithms that recommend music or search engines find authoritative information about them, and this will increase their visibility, page rank, etc.

Exploitation pathways

We are looking for self-releasing artists, labels, publishers, who are willing to try out our Unlabel services with ALOADED.
- ALOADED becomes their non-exclusive or exclusive distributor (in the latter case, we have a welcome package)
- ALOADED distributes them on digital platforms with high care.
- We ensure that their data gets into the global knowledge graphs of Google, Spotify, Wikidata, etc, and we measure the impact of improving metadata.
- We ensure that their music is listed on Europeana, MusicBrainz, Wikipedia, etc.
- We want to measure in % of income, % followers, %plays, %playlist selections after 1,2,3,6 month of metadata improvements, i.e., to put a negative price of wrong metadata, missing metadata, and a positive price tag on correctly disseminated metadata (@Fábio Generoso Vieira&lt;mailto:f.v.vieira@uva.nl&gt;  and the ALOADED team)

We hope to conclude an agreement with A38 who will report with the help of our system to Artisjus, i.e, pre-cleaned user data on their web channels, which will be also listed on Europeana, MusicBrainz, Wikipedia, etc.


We are looking for locations where we can test HEAR!DISs background music service, which will increase the amount of music played that is relevant in a location, or keeps royalties and visibility in town -- i.e., in a Slovak restaurant or gallery, more Slovak music, in Bratislava, more music made in Bratislava.

Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder

Hi Daniel,

I got back yesterday and had quite some emails, so I am still going through them.

What I can tell you for now is that it has been taking an enormous amount of time to extract the data from Spotify with the orchestras’ names. I have a code that has been running during the whole time I was away, and I basically just got to half of the names. I will still need to recover the ISRCs later on. So, it will take some time.

Regarding the labels, I created a table with the artists I could recover from Spotify. But I haven’t had the change to get any ISRC yet. I either work on the orchestras or I work on the labels’ names. I can stop with the orchestras if the labels are more important at this moment. Though I think it’ll take some time until I could provide you with registrant codes, earliest and latest ISRCs, I would need the entire data base in my computer first. So far, I have been working for two weeks on the orchestras only and I just got the half of the names. Just to give you an idea, I am pasting a table below that summarizes the number of artists extracted per label. The first 7 labels, I can extract more artists I think, though Spotify was breaking the connection after 1000 artists were extracted. So I am not sure whether that is possible. Anyway, in the labels table I have almost 8200 artists. It’ll probably take a year to extract data from all of them, given how slow things have been going.

[cid:image001.png@01DB13F1.3A08E870]


It would be nice if I could somehow filter for the ones that are actually from Slovakia. Any thoughts on how to do that?

Let me know if you think it’s better to stop working on the orchestras and work on the labels. If I don’t hear from you, I will just keep working on the labels. Also, if you have an idea about how to better do this data extract, please let me know.

Best,
Fabio

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Saturday, September 21, 2024 11:24 AM
To: Joost Poort &lt;j.p.poort@uva.nl&gt;
Cc: Fábio Generoso Vieira &lt;f.v.vieira@uva.nl&gt;
Subject: Re: Meeting next week

Hi All,

I understand that Fabio will be on holiday, and if you can, please, before you go, send me the data you describe in your mail about labels/distributors in a CSV file. If not, please send me this after your holidays.

Actually, I would like to get two CSV files:
- all labels with label names, registrant numbers that you think are relevant in a Slovak context -- the name you recorded it, the ISRC part for them, if possible, by simply adding the earliest and latest known ISRC recording per label:  label_name, isrc_registrant_code, earliest_isrc, latest_isrc.
- all the names, and spotify artist id of artist/performers who you think are relevant in a Slovak context:  spotify_artist_name, spotify_artist_id,  isrc_registrant_code, earliest_isrc, latest_isrc.

In the meantime, I wanted to add a few developments:

- it seems that we have now entire catalogues where Fabio can set up experiments with full control; I will have the conversation in Fabio's absence with access to these data;

- my librarian went after ISO standards, to me it is not intuitive that a standard is secret, we found out that you can access them in national standardisation bodies and some parts of them are free, we will actually create an annotated compiled document for Fabio with all music-related standards, not only the ones he bought; so far we spent more on investigating than just buying, but we wanted to scan inconsistencies with IT and library etc standards, and that would have cost thousands.

However, I may have to take a day off on 7 October, I will try to arrange this so that it will not affect our meeting.  With Joost we will catch up in Vienna and with Fabio I will arrange a separate call when he is back from holidays.

Best regards,
Daniel

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Friday, October 4, 2024 8:01 PM
To: Fábio Generoso Vieira &lt;f.v.vieira@uva.nl&gt;
Cc: Joost Poort &lt;j.p.poort@uva.nl&gt;
Subject: Re: Meeting next week

Hi Fábió,

Thank you for this.  I think that you misunderstood me.  In my opinion, you have a few million ISRC codes in your database, out of which perhaps 10-20,000 may be under the SK domain.  Now I would like to sort those per label, because the ISRC code is made of country, label, year, and then a serial number. So we would be able to go beyond the country and the year part and match the companies with companies.

I do not really understand what you mean by extracting orchestras over a year.  Slovakia has perhaps 200 known orchestras, it must be possible to find out if they are on Spotify with at most 200 queries, which can be made in about 150 seconds, without being kicked out of the API.

Of course, having the artists per label is useful, though perhaps not for Universal Music, which has more than 30% global market share. But ordering the 17 Hudobné centrum artists into a table would certainly help, and to find at least one ISRC to them in your system would not be a very massive query. I am sure that you can query your database per artist, and 17 artist's all ISRC numbers is not a very huge table either.

Like I said earlier, because I will be on holiday on Monday, I am not 100% sure that I can join in on Monday to the call, but if I can make it happen, I will. But I think it would be essential that I see some Slovakia-related data, I mean, not on an aggregated level, but actually what you have collected.  We are aiming to come to an algorithm that selects tracks by ISRC, so it would be good to systematically review what do you know about the SK IRSC's, which are not that numerous in your system. If we would be able to see all your Slovak ISRCs with an artist name, artist Spotify ID, and a label name, that would be hugely helpful.

Best regards,
Daniel

Hi Joost and Daniel,

I have finally spoken to Etienne last week and he showed me the process of selecting your own ISRC in the distributor website.

So, basically what I understood is: you upload your music in the distributor platform and in case you have never registered your music in the past, they generate a random ISRC for you that is obtained via their own registrant. However, if you have already registered your music, in case you are changing distributors, for instance, you are allowed to provide your existing ISRC by hand. So, you should not be choosing it anyway, but that opens the back door for somebody coming in a just creating their own code that does not follow the ISO or ISRC handbook guidelines.

I want to include this as an extra bullet point in section 5 with the additional issues. I think this fits much better than your suggestion to include it in the designation code subsection 4.4.

Hi Fábió,

Thank you for this.  I think that you misunderstood me.  In my opinion, you have a few million ISRC codes in your database, out of which perhaps 10-20,000 may be under the SK domain.  Now I would like to sort those per label, because the ISRC code is made of country, label, year, and then a serial number. So we would be able to go beyond the country and the year part and match the companies with companies.

I do not really understand what you mean by extracting orchestras over a year.  Slovakia has perhaps 200 known orchestras, it must be possible to find out if they are on Spotify with at most 200 queries, which can be made in about 150 seconds, without being kicked out of the API.

Of course, having the artists per label is useful, though perhaps not for Universal Music, which has more than 30% global market share. But ordering the 17 Hudobné centrum artists into a table would certainly help, and to find at least one ISRC to them in your system would not be a very massive query. I am sure that you can query your database per artist, and 17 artist's all ISRC numbers is not a very huge table either.

Like I said earlier, because I will be on holiday on Monday, I am not 100% sure that I can join in on Monday to the call, but if I can make it happen, I will. But I think it would be essential that I see some Slovakia-related data, I mean, not on an aggregated level, but actually what you have collected.  We are aiming to come to an algorithm that selects tracks by ISRC, so it would be good to systematically review what do you know about the SK IRSC's, which are not that numerous in your system. If we would be able to see all your Slovak ISRCs with an artist name, artist Spotify ID, and a label name, that would be hugely helpful.

Best regards,
Daniel

Subject: Re: Meeting next week

Hi Fábió,

I can add the following workflow suggestions.

- If you would be willing to work in RStudio in markdown (and create your LaTex from that, not from another LaTex editor) we could review with Anna your future work, provide you with further bibliographical references, etc. You can also generate a DOC version from RStudio.
- Generally I think that Eszter or James would prefer to have a Word file for revision and not a PDF.

I think that it would be beneficial if you read an introductory book on how the music business works, for example this one&lt;https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/20744933-take-care-of-your-music-business&gt;, which is also available in an excellent online course, because without this the music metadata standards, the ISRC codebook makes little sense. For example, very few distributors (for example, TuneCore) register ISRC codes. However, even small distributors like ALOADED may work with hundreds of entities who can register ISRC (i.e., labels).  So the fact that a distributor can point you to different legal entities with different ISRC ranges is not surprising.

But how relevant is this for our work? I think that would really require a revision of the known Slovak or whatever repertoire.  In my opinion, such misregistration, while technically possible, for most musicians is not desirable. The commercially valuable part of the repertoire is managed by labels, who will not register their recordings to the domain of another label.

Best regards,
Daniel

I have finally spoken to Etienne last week and he showed me the process of selecting your own ISRC in the distributor website.

So, basically what I understood is: you upload your music in the distributor platform and in case you have never registered your music in the past, they generate a random ISRC for you that is obtained via their own registrant. However, if you have already registered your music, in case you are changing distributors, for instance, you are allowed to provide your existing ISRC by hand. So, you should not be choosing it anyway, but that opens the back door for somebody coming in a just creating their own code that does not follow the ISO or ISRC handbook guidelines.

Hi Fábió,

Thank you for this.  I think that you misunderstood me.  In my opinion, you have a few million ISRC codes in your database, out of which perhaps 10-20,000 may be under the SK domain.  Now I would like to sort those per label, because the ISRC code is made of country, label, year, and then a serial number. So we would be able to go beyond the country and the year part and match the companies with companies.

I do not really understand what you mean by extracting orchestras over a year.  Slovakia has perhaps 200 known orchestras, it must be possible to find out if they are on Spotify with at most 200 queries, which can be made in about 150 seconds, without being kicked out of the API.

Of course, having the artists per label is useful, though perhaps not for Universal Music, which has more than 30% global market share. But ordering the 17 Hudobné centrum artists into a table would certainly help, and to find at least one ISRC to them in your system would not be a very massive query. I am sure that you can query your database per artist, and 17 artist's all ISRC numbers is not a very huge table either.

Like I said earlier, because I will be on holiday on Monday, I am not 100% sure that I can join in on Monday to the call, but if I can make it happen, I will. But I think it would be essential that I see some Slovakia-related data, I mean, not on an aggregated level, but actually what you have collected.  We are aiming to come to an algorithm that selects tracks by ISRC, so it would be good to systematically review what do you know about the SK IRSC's, which are not that numerous in your system. If we would be able to see all your Slovak ISRCs with an artist name, artist Spotify ID, and a label name, that would be hugely helpful.

Best regards,
Daniel

Hi Fábió,

Thank you for this.  I think that you misunderstood me.  In my opinion, you have a few million ISRC codes in your database, out of which perhaps 10-20,000 may be under the SK domain.  Now I would like to sort those per label, because the ISRC code is made of country, label, year, and then a serial number. So we would be able to go beyond the country and the year part and match the companies with companies.

I do not really understand what you mean by extracting orchestras over a year.  Slovakia has perhaps 200 known orchestras, it must be possible to find out if they are on Spotify with at most 200 queries, which can be made in about 150 seconds, without being kicked out of the API.

Of course, having the artists per label is useful, though perhaps not for Universal Music, which has more than 30% global market share. But ordering the 17 Hudobné centrum artists into a table would certainly help, and to find at least one ISRC to them in your system would not be a very massive query. I am sure that you can query your database per artist, and 17 artist's all ISRC numbers is not a very huge table either.

Like I said earlier, because I will be on holiday on Monday, I am not 100% sure that I can join in on Monday to the call, but if I can make it happen, I will. But I think it would be essential that I see some Slovakia-related data, I mean, not on an aggregated level, but actually what you have collected.  We are aiming to come to an algorithm that selects tracks by ISRC, so it would be good to systematically review what do you know about the SK IRSC's, which are not that numerous in your system. If we would be able to see all your Slovak ISRCs with an artist name, artist Spotify ID, and a label name, that would be hugely helpful.

Best regards,
Daniel

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: Monday, October 21, 2024 2:38 PM

Cc: Joost Poort &lt;j.p.poort@uva.nl&gt;
Subject: Re: Orchestras data set

Hi Fábio,

The topic of conceptualisation is related to computer science, library/information science, and also to statistical production of an indicator. To measure performer royalty income, we must come up with a concept (abstract term) “music performer”, “royalty”, and “income”, so that we can grab the data that relates to performers, royalties and income in a royalty account system, and create statistical indicators, such as average performer royalty income, or top percentile performer royalty income, or even average performer non-royalty income. Spotting the real, actual data of one particular performer, and making sure that it is both royalty and income is not an easy task. Conceptualisation helps in this, the way it also helps to create new surveys: you must come up with the concept of "Slovak", "music performer", and "sound recording" before you start to collect data on sound recordings of Slovak music performers.

I have so far several R packages that deal with niche topics (iotables: economic, environmental, social impact assessment; retroharmoinze: retrospective harmonisation of statistical surveys.) All are calling for a proper solution of conceptualisation.  For example, in a surveying concept to identify the concept of “sex”, “gender”, “sex or gender” and properly recode variables for a sex/gender based statistical indicator, or a statistical dataset “slice” (a strict statistical definition of dividing a dataset by a dimension such as sex or gender.)

I started the peer-review process of a package, “dataset&lt;https://dataset.dataobservatory.eu/articles/new-requirements.html&gt;” on ROpenSci and CRAN, and “dataset” as an early-stage package is already on CRAN but did not pass yet the more substantial ROpenSci&lt;https://github.com/ropensci/software-review/issues/553#issuecomment-2412697128&gt; peer review. My aim with “dataset” is to make this basis of the conceptualisation of my iotables, retroharmonize package, and your work with applying concepts to your algorithm could be also a case study.

This “dataset” package is aiming very high and it is unlikely that it will be finalised in half a year, though it could get to a publication, because I recently decided to create a niche version of it, called “wbdataset&lt;https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/wbdataset&gt;”, which will only connect the Wikibase semantic database system with the R system. I think that a paper on bringing conceptualisation to R in general, with an example of the Wikibase Data Model would be already publishable.  Even if not, you participating in the programming of “wbdataset”, and using our Wikibase database for the concepts that you apply in your algorithm is, in my opinion, something that would be independently publishable.

Data Science steps:
- Fork the dataset&lt;https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/dataset/&gt; repository
- Read these new requirements, which must be formatted into a conference paper format by mid-November for peer review
- Fork the wbdataset&lt;https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/wbdataset&gt; repository
- Let us come up with a plan of what “concepts” you want to use with your algorithm. Make sure that data conceptualised with them will be made with the “wbdataset” package, and you can connect it to your code.
- I think that your code could also be separately published, if you follow the publication guidelines of ROpenSci and CRAN, which you can learn with participating in the wbdataset and dataset project.

Statistical/Scientific steps (more urgent for OpenMuse)
- I would like to have a clearly defined series of hypotheses and data structure with synthetically created dummy data before we get the real data very soon.
- For example, “Having the named entity data on Wikidata for a musical artist increases popularity/income/follower growth by a significant amount (of x)”  Not having biographical data available on open knowledge graphs reduces follower growth, income, etc. with a significant amount, etc.
- And of course, for the base case or random sampling part: the “median/average/first decile number of follower growth/income/etc, for Slovak artists is Z%”

Conferences and CfPs
DHNB 2025&lt;https://dhnb.eu/conferences/dhnb2025/?fbclid=IwY2xjawF_OztleHRuA2FlbQIxMAABHQ6ehaCSSmxg41hMTGVRiauBA1pMdV6LX2rpa3eUYSP8LLDxCJ5Pgx-N5Q_aem_f8nhRehdCklhoPcGXOoupg&gt;, deadline tomorrow!

I was invited last minute, because I started to work with some Latvian, Estonian and French researchers on the edge of computer science, linguistics, and digital heritage, and we are preparing several new projects. The topic is only very loosely related to OpenMuse (we work with music data, but with no socio-economic statistical but ethnomusicological and humanities aims, however, having some statistics is always nice-to-have.) We want to use the same data science and computer science methodology that is behind or core Slovak work. So your role as a co-author could be very limited to conceptualisation that we will use in your other work, too, and connecting spotifyR, and my new conceptualisation packages, that you will anyways use in your sampling research.

IAMIC: Internatonal Assocation of Music Information Centers, we will present our Slovak work with the Slovak Music Info Center on 21 November 2025. We will reveal the database that you can exploit. This is only information that by this time you will certainly have rather extensive data access.

CISAC European Committee: April 2025. Our topic is named entity recognition and disambiguation, this relates to conceptualisation and your work, but leads into a different direction. No formal call for papers. This is interesting to you if you want to stay in music.
IAMIL25: The International Association of Music Libraries, Archives and Documentation Centers (IAML), deadline 15 December https://www.iaml.info/call-for-papers   I think that you can prepare an own submission, or join mine, this will be very strongly related to conceptualisation of music.
Potential publications:
R packages:
- You become a  a ctb (contributor) if you fork the repository, add improvements to unit test, documentation, or small, trivial bugs. You can easily become a ctb in almost any of my packages, the spotifyr package is a low hanging fruit as you use it extensively and it is a high-visibility package.
- Co-author if you add significant new functionality.
- Author if you have a product co-ownership.
Usually a co-author or even ctb will make you visible as a person who knows how to work with the softare and may be invited into scientific projects where they want to work with the data that the package handles.
Data papers:
- You become a co-author if you help to create a well-described dataset and publish it.
- In this project you could easily publish at least 3-4 interesting data papers.
I cannot state how underreated data papers are.  While they do not count a lot for your next job search, you will almost inevitably become a co-author if somebody wants to use your data in a new research. Publishing datasets with data papers is a low-hanging fruit that will eventually build you up a portfolio of co-authorship by data users.
Data science publications:
- They  are not easier, perhaps more difficult than other publications, because you have to pass the level of code peer review first.  But I have many unpublished code, which passed that level, but never was written up to a journal article, so there are low hanging fruits here, too. But their timespan would not be 3-4 months.
- The wbdataset package will almost certainly get its publication because it will be co-sponsored by the Wikimedia Foundation and they want to make sure that this is successful.
- a successful ROpenSci peer review of a package will almost certainly lead to a peer-reviewed publication, it is intended to bridge a software peer-review with a science peer review. Obviously even if this becomes a publication after your postdoc, if you are involved in your postdoc, you'll be a co-author.

Best regards,
Daniel

I was invited last minute, because I started to work with some Latvian, Estonian and French researchers on the edge of computer science, linguistics, and digital heritage, and we are preparing several new projects. The topic is only very loosely related to OpenMuse (we work with music data, but with no socio-economic statistical but ethnomusicological and humanities aims, however, having some statistics is always nice-to-have.) We want to use the same data science and computer science methodology that is behind or core Slovak work. So your role as a co-author could be very limited to conceptualisation that we will use in your other work, too, and connecting spotifyR, and my new conceptualisation packages, that you will anyways use in your sampling research.

IAMIC: Internatonal Assocation of Music Information Centers, we will present our Slovak work with the Slovak Music Info Center on 21 November 2025. We will reveal the database that you can exploit. This is only information that by this time you will certainly have rather extensive data access.

CISAC European Committee: April 2025. Our topic is named entity recognition and disambiguation, this relates to conceptualisation and your work, but leads into a different direction. No formal call for papers. This is interesting to you if you want to stay in music.
IAMIL25: The International Association of Music Libraries, Archives and Documentation Centers (IAML), deadline 15 December https://www.iaml.info/call-for-papers   I think that you can prepare an own submission, or join mine, this will be very strongly related to conceptualisation of music.
Potential publications:
R packages:
- You become a  a ctb (contributor) if you fork the repository, add improvements to unit test, documentation, or small, trivial bugs. You can easily become a ctb in almost any of my packages, the spotifyr package is a low hanging fruit as you use it extensively and it is a high-visibility package.
- Co-author if you add significant new functionality.
- Author if you have a product co-ownership.
Usually a co-author or even ctb will make you visible as a person who knows how to work with the softare and may be invited into scientific projects where they want to work with the data that the package handles.
Data papers:
- You become a co-author if you help to create a well-described dataset and publish it.
- In this project you could easily publish at least 3-4 interesting data papers.
I cannot state how underreated data papers are.  While they do not count a lot for your next job search, you will almost inevitably become a co-author if somebody wants to use your data in a new research. Publishing datasets with data papers is a low-hanging fruit that will eventually build you up a portfolio of co-authorship by data users.
Data science publications:
- They  are not easier, perhaps more difficult than other publications, because you have to pass the level of code peer review first.  But I have many unpublished code, which passed that level, but never was written up to a journal article, so there are low hanging fruits here, too. But their timespan would not be 3-4 months.
- The wbdataset package will almost certainly get its publication because it will be co-sponsored by the Wikimedia Foundation and they want to make sure that this is successful.
- a successful ROpenSci peer review of a package will almost certainly lead to a peer-reviewed publication, it is intended to bridge a software peer-review with a science peer review. Hi Fábio,

Yes, this is the dataset what I was asking for. Thank you very much!

About your data:

Now I think that this is a good opportunity to try to pass it over to me in a reproducible and reviewable way.  Can you please do it now with description and via GitHub, and also including the Finno-Ugric playlist data for the Nordic conference?

I showed you at the beginning of your postdoc the R documentation standards. The standard way to describe a dataset in R is here: https://roxygen2.r-lib.org/articles/rd-other.html This would be OK for me, but in fact it is our two packages that wants to improve this practice, because while this type of documentation provides the variable names and their descriptions, it does not provide a standardised definition for the variable. So this is not sufficient for me going forward, but for now, it is good.

Also, for simplicity, we do not need to use the Roxygen notation, I am perfectly fine with a qmd markdown that is currently included with RStudio.  So the way you pass on a dataset to me is the following.

- You create a QMD file, and in the header you put your name, ORCiD, bib files, etc, for example, you add your bibliographic references to the bib folder in bib/musicmetadata.bib

- You give a short narrative overview of how did you collect the data. This can be as little as one paragraph.

- Then you create a table, similar to the R standard, but in a simple tabular format. For example, in your dataset there are many variables, for example, these:

isrc:  An International Standard Recording code as defined by [@isrc_standard]  where the isrc_standard is defined in the bib/musicmetadata.bib BibLatex files.

isrc_year: A part of the ISRC code referring to `year`, as described in [@isrc_standard, p8] exact reference to the ISRC code text about years....

While this is not yet machine readable, at least it is human readable, and our task will be in the next few weeks to make it also machine readable.  Please describe all your variables in the dataset, add the bibliographic citations to the definitions, and commit it to the GitHub repository.

About the substantial part of the experiments:

Please write a short document as a qmd file (it can be easily rendered to a Word file for Joost)  describing what will be your control variables and how will you collect them. For example, the artist has an English Wikipedia page, a national language Wikipedia page, it has date of birth on Wikidata, it has date of birth on MusicBrainz, etc. We need to capture the quality of information known on the Internet about the artists and about the song so that we can start making hypothesises about metadata quality.

For simplicity, please define your control variables the same way as you passed on to me the variables in the Slovak dataset.

However simple are your hypothesizes, I would like to read exactly how you will collect the data for their testing and how you will make a decision on the hypothesis. If I were you, before starting to collect via SQL or SPARQL queries tons of data,  create a dataset by hand in Excel, describe the variables, and make a simple run on a hypothesis, even if you run it on a too small dataset to be statistically valid, for example, by putting in an Excel sheet (and then to R) the data of 10 artists manually.

Best regards,
Daniel

Hi Fábio,

The topic of conceptualisation is related to computer science, library/information science, and also to statistical production of an indicator. To measure performer royalty income, we must come up with a concept (abstract term) “music performer”, “royalty”, and “income”, so that we can grab the data that relates to performers, royalties and income in a royalty account system, and create statistical indicators, such as average performer royalty income, or top percentile performer royalty income, or even average performer non-royalty income. Spotting the real, actual data of one particular performer, and making sure that it is both royalty and income is not an easy task. Conceptualisation helps in this, the way it also helps to create new surveys: you must come up with the concept of "Slovak", "music performer", and "sound recording" before you start to collect data on sound recordings of Slovak music performers.

I have so far several R packages that deal with niche topics (iotables: economic, environmental, social impact assessment; retroharmoinze: retrospective harmonisation of statistical surveys.) All are calling for a proper solution of conceptualisation.  For example, in a surveying concept to identify the concept of “sex”, “gender”, “sex or gender” and properly recode variables for a sex/gender based statistical indicator, or a statistical dataset “slice” (a strict statistical definition of dividing a dataset by a dimension such as sex or gender.)

I started the peer-review process of a package, “dataset&lt;https://dataset.dataobservatory.eu/articles/new-requirements.html&gt;” on ROpenSci and CRAN, and “dataset” as an early-stage package is already on CRAN but did not pass yet the more substantial ROpenSci&lt;https://github.com/ropensci/software-review/issues/553#issuecomment-2412697128&gt; peer review. My aim with “dataset” is to make this basis of the conceptualisation of my iotables, retroharmonize package, and your work with applying concepts to your algorithm could be also a case study.

This “dataset” package is aiming very high and it is unlikely that it will be finalised in half a year, though it could get to a publication, because I recently decided to create a niche version of it, called “wbdataset&lt;https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/wbdataset&gt;”, which will only connect the Wikibase semantic database system with the R system. I think that a paper on bringing conceptualisation to R in general, with an example of the Wikibase Data Model would be already publishable.  Even if not, you participating in the programming of “wbdataset”, and using our Wikibase database for the concepts that you apply in your algorithm is, in my opinion, something that would be independently publishable.

Data Science steps:
- Fork the dataset&lt;https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/dataset/&gt; repository
- Read these new requirements, which must be formatted into a conference paper format by mid-November for peer review
- Fork the wbdataset&lt;https://github.com/dataobservatory-eu/wbdataset&gt; repository
- Let us come up with a plan of what “concepts” you want to use with your algorithm. Make sure that data conceptualised with them will be made with the “wbdataset” package, and you can connect it to your code.
- I think that your code could also be separately published, if you follow the publication guidelines of ROpenSci and CRAN, which you can learn with participating in the wbdataset and dataset project.

Statistical/Scientific steps (more urgent for OpenMuse)
- I would like to have a clearly defined series of hypotheses and data structure with synthetically created dummy data before we get the real data very soon.
- For example, “Having the named entity data on Wikidata for a musical artist increases popularity/income/follower growth by a significant amount (of x)”  Not having biographical data available on open knowledge graphs reduces follower growth, income, etc. with a significant amount, etc.
- And of course, for the base case or random sampling part: the “median/average/first decile number of follower growth/income/etc, for Slovak artists is Z%”

Hello Fábió

Thank you for adding your dataset documentation to the GitHub folder.  I think that this way we can really do business!

I made some thorough changes.
- You should familiarize yourself with our Consortium's Data Management Plan, but particularly on the vocabulary of the Statistical Data and Metadata Exchange: https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-data-cube/   Most of the "variables" that you wrote are "attributes" as constants, i.e., metadata. Some of them can be used as categorical variables in your model.
- You must connect your models and your descriptions to our joint dataspace model (you see my examples here.) You will get data via this system, so you must make sure that both on your side and on the Reprexbase/demo side the identifiers, attributes, variables are well-identified and consistently described.

Based on our meeting yesterday with the Slovak colleagues, I would like to urge you to read the document of yesterday's meeting, and the conference paper proposal where I added your name.

On Monday, I would like to read in your Repo in qmd, and for Joost, rendered to docx, a short document with data examples on how you will model the effects on internet data quality on the popularity of tracks.  As we know and discussed, Spotify relies on Wikipedia and Wikidata when it has no adequate information.  There are many ways to access available information quality and quantity on Wikipedia and Wikibase, and many R package interfaces to get the data.  See for example&lt;https://scholar.google.com/scholar?as_ylo=2020&amp;q=wikipedia+page+quality&amp;hl=en&amp;as_sdt=0,5&gt;.

A bit of housekeeping
- I connected some of your attributes to our shared database (please see the document.)
- In your fork, and your computer, you should create a docs/ subfolder within listen-local-slovakia, and you should add it to your .gitignore path. The PDF, docx, or Latex version will show up here.
- Your bibliography is not in the right place, please read the README of the repository and follow the example of the other papers there.

Best regards,
Daniel

There are many ways to access available information quality and quantity on Wikipedia and Wikibase, and many R package interfaces to get the data.  See for example&lt;https://scholar.google.com/scholar?as_ylo=2020&amp;q=wikipedia+page+quality&amp;hl=en&amp;as_sdt=0,5&gt;.

A bit of housekeeping
- I connected some of your attributes to our shared database (please see the document.)
- In your fork, and your computer, you should create a docs/ subfolder within listen-local-slovakia, and you should add it to your .gitignore path. The PDF, docx, or Latex version will show up here.
- Your bibliography is not in the right place, please read the README of the repository and follow the example of the other papers there.

Best regards,
Daniel
