Sent: Thursday, January 23, 2025 19:19
To: Arianna Martinelli
Cc: Jankovič Marián; Tomas Miks; Rosina Petrova; Dr. Kabai Eszter; Demčák Richard; Dr. Huszák Balázs; Olga Kavkaeva; Joost Poort; James Rhys Edwards
Subject: Re: OPENMUSE - List of target and request of a meeting

Hi Arianna,

The document that you sent to us today is something that cannot be connected to our work. We cannot design and build a survey frame and register for such a broad target group so late in the project. The reasons I well explained in the document that I created as a step-in for SSSA and submitted for the interim review in D1.1, which explains generally the enterprise surveying difficulties of a highly informal music sector.

I still have not seen in the last 2 years any written document about what you call "Orbis survey", so I can rely only on fragments of oral statements which make me think that the Orbis survey falls into the category that we described in D1.1 as a faulty approach that resulted in not having enterprise data in the last 15 years. (i.e., a NACE-based, random sample, online administered survey among enterprises.) As far as I understand, this is supposed to be added to the project as a comparator, a benchmark of "bad surveying" so that we can show how "good surveying" can improve.

In short, so that we do not have to come back in circles:
- NACE codes are useless, so administering a survey with a population frame based on NACE codes must overshoot its target response by at least 300-400%
- This means that your online survey response rate goes down from 2-3% to an inferred 0.5%.
- When you have a target population of 58, for example, then you have a chance to get 0 or 1 examples. This means that if you have 58 music publishing entities in a country, then an online survey sent out to addresses of all of them has a chance of 0 to 1 answers.
- No statistics can be made from less than 10 responses.

We were offered to participate in the enterprise surveying scheme of Slovakia in the cultural sector in both 2024 and 2025. Because those surveys come with a legal mandate, a fine for non-response, and a well-designed survey frame, they are useful, and they result in a 90%+ coverage. Also, there was a candidate who had to leave the Slovak ministry, and who had a PhD, had working experience with the enterprise survey administration and the register, and would have been available for this project, but she was not hired.   Apart from this, in various projects, we administered enterprise surveys with organisations, and it was a huge undertaking, and I do not think that either SOZA or Artisjus or MusicAutor or MusicExport Poland or Reprex would consider administering such a survey.  In some of our works in HU, SK and CZ we relied on cooperation with IFPI. The IFPI surveys among sound recording companies have about 90% coverage, for example, and they are done with great care. Usually one person who is already knowledgeable about the topic works part time about 3 months on the administration, per country, so the effective PM input, in true, calendar months, is 1.5PM, but that is like working 20 hours dedicated per week on it. And for two countries, that is 3 PMs, but calculated in calendar months.   In my opinion, you had more than 10 PMs for the enterprise survey, so an enterprise survey could have been designed and administered.

There are several tasks and deliverables in this project that require usable survey data, and in my understanding, SSSA and Sinus are responsible for designing and administering those surveys, and they are supposed to be an improvement to what we have done in Slovakia and Hungary with 5% of the budget of this project.

If we will not get suitable data for our tasks, we can think of the following alternatives
a) we present our deliverables with old data
b) we present our deliverables with simulated data
c) Reprex runs a survey for the societies, if we get a public, academic document stating that we have been doing it always the best possible way and there was no room for improvement.

Best regards,
Daniel







On Thu, Jan 23, 2025 at 6:39 PM Arianna Martinelli &lt;arianna.martinelli@santannapisa.it&lt;mailto:arianna.martinelli@santannapisa.it&gt;&gt; wrote:
Dear Daniel,
Dear All,
I want to clarify a few points that seem to have been overlooked and may have led to misunderstandings, especially following last Monday’s meeting. I understand the amendment’s aim in April was to better define tasks and roles. Below, I’ve outlined my interpretation of the responsibilities concerning the surveys. This understanding is based on the new version of the WP1 description, but it might require further discussion to ensure alignment. List of subtasks:

1. Two samples are going to be built, one based on ORBIS (done by SSSA) and one based on CMOs registers (T1.2 done by REPREX)
2. SSSA is going to design two questionnaires, one for professionals and one for MSMEs, and some survey design that was going to ensure that each respondent was going to get the “right” questionnaire
3. SSSA was going to administer the survey to the ORBIS sample and take care of non-response bias with available variables
4. SSSA was going to prepare a link that was going to be distributed by CMOs (so no access to the register by SSSA) to the entities in the register prepared in T1.2. SSSA was going to try to address the non-response issue using some aggregated data that CMOs could provide to the consortium considering their GDPR constraints.

This further task of "target definition" occurred to me only on Monday because the targets for the ORBIS sampling were established by the NACE codes (chosen based on the EUROSTAT and UNESCO report on cultural statistics). So, the target ex-ante definition does not make much sense, but I was planning for a respondent to describe their activity in the music industry better and, therefore, “self-select” in a target list similar to the one I sent to you today. Clearly, the CMO sampling needs a different approach and register preparation. For this reason, T1.2 is about designing and implementing a methodology for sampling music industry companies and music performers/rightsholders from CMO databases. In this respect, my reading is that the target definition for the CMOs sampling is part of T1.2 and the register preparation. I would expect the register to include targets to sample (which definition is based on industry model and CMOs priority). I start thinking maybe this is not the case, but then it is unclear what the register is given the task description.
I remember at the Bergfest discussing with Eszter sending a list of the types of entities I was planning to survey, but looking back at my notes, we were discussing the heterogeneity of NACE codes and the types of entities you could find in them. Maybe this has also been a further source of misunderstanding.

I wanted to share this because I think there is no agreement on this workflow, which might be “wrong,” but it is the one on which I based the work SSSA has been doing. I am aware that we are late, but I do not want to go through all the roadblocks we went through, as we all know them.

Best regards,
Arianna

Subject: Reprex financial issues

Hi  Isabella &amp; James,

I wrote a more personal note to Joost, partly explaining my edgy behavior for the repeated lateness of the partners, but I realised that I may need to make my situation clear to you, and perhaps others in the Consortium.

As you know, we won a competition of the EIT, which is technically financed by Horizon Europe (although it is a very different program than our RIA action.)  It is a startup prize, supposed to provide alternative, investment-type funding for startups working on a really big puzzle. We won with our ESG calculator, and the prize is partly an investment, and partly a grant. (There were 307 applicants in 5 sectors, and we won the Audiovisual prize.) In the granted period, the for-profit startups must work on a non-profit basis, and practically they cannot solicit other work. Because we still have some commitment to OpenMusE, and we have some smaller commercial work, we offered all our remaining capacity to them for a year ahead.

Because there was fraudulent misconduct in the EIT KIC the grant payments are prolonged or perhaps even cancelled, and may need to go through the anti-fraud authority and courts.  The misconduct also affected us: they tried to manipulate our score and give our money to somebody else, but we successfully appealed that. Unfortunately, in other parts of the KIC there was money going to pockets that they could not keep under the carpet.

There had always been questions about the financial stability of Reprex. Now the worst possible thing happened: we are entering the period when we are crediting the Horizon program, but at the same time, the Horizon program reserved most of our capacities and failed to pay for us. We should be receiving about 150,000 euros in the coming days, but it may take years as I see that we actually get this money; and this is of course just a first advance (this program has much lower advance rates.)  If Reprex will become insolvent, it will be because of "irregularities" committed on the EU side, and we are (acknowledged by their supervisory report) all but completely innocent victims.

Tomorrow I will go public with this problem, because we need to ask help from our partners, investors, and the least that we want to have is quarrelling within OpenMusE.  I am very edgy, but partly also because I feel that we put more work in than others, and in these extremely challenging times our schedule is often disrupted. I think that we can meet all our commitments in OpenMusE, but we do not want to put more work into the deliverables than others and we want to avoid any quarrelling.

I am doing the best that I can do, and I am by now thinking that Reprex will go under, but the next 3-6 months will be extremely challenging for us.  I think that it would be appropriate to communicate at one point to the PO and other WP leaders. I think that PO is critical; I think it is rather unprecedented that a fraud in the HE program makes a HE beneficiary insolvent, but it may happen.

Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder

Hi James,

I want to address this issue in the WP leaders call in 1.5 minutes.  I want everybody to know that our agenda is very tight and stressful, we have to accommodate MEPs, national contact points, anti-fraud investigators and also we are under a financial duress. But I think that eventually all this is a relevant issue for the PO and the Coordinator, nobody else.

With the PO, I think that disclosing the problem as early as possible is a good practice.  I do not see any real problems in the coming 3-4 months, so now this is only a disclosure.  At one point, it may become a critical risk, I hope every day that we will resolve sooner.  To be very clear with an example:

I may be late with paying wages in our project in 2025. This is an irregularity, but due to the fact that Horizon Europe owes me with reimbursement of a lot of money for wages in another project, and if it does not affect my delivery, this irregularity should and must not be held as a violation of the financial management of this project.  The HE gives advances and ex-post reimbursement; and we have received both advances and reimbursements from them in the past year in the other project. So the payslips will see that in some cases (and only for myself) I pay taxes on time, but wages late. Obviously I very much hope that eventually I will receive my salary, but this is really beyond my control. I quiet frankly could not imagine this level of misconduct and carelessnes from and EU organisation.

I cannot believe that they can hold this against our project, you, or me, because I have documentary proof that I am a victim of fraud in the HE program, but obviously it is better to inform in advance than to explain this in 2026 during the ex post audit.

Best regards,
Daniel

Hi James,

I want to address this issue in the WP leaders call in 1.5 minutes.  I want everybody to know that our agenda is very tight and stressful, we have to accommodate MEPs, national contact points, anti-fraud investigators and also we are under a financial duress. But I think that eventually all this is a relevant issue for the PO and the Coordinator, nobody else.

With the PO, I think that disclosing the problem as early as possible is a good practice.  I do not see any real problems in the coming 3-4 months, so now this is only a disclosure.  At one point, it may become a critical risk, I hope every day that we will resolve sooner.  To be very clear with an example:

I may be late with paying wages in our project in 2025. This is an irregularity, but due to the fact that Horizon Europe owes me with reimbursement of a lot of money for wages in another project, and if it does not affect my delivery, this irregularity should and must not be held as a violation of the financial management of this project.  The HE gives advances and ex-post reimbursement; and we have received both advances and reimbursements from them in the past year in the other project. So the payslips will see that in some cases (and only for myself) I pay taxes on time, but wages late. Obviously I very much hope that eventually I will receive my salary, but this is really beyond my control. I quiet frankly could not imagine this level of misconduct and carelessnes from and EU organisation.

I cannot believe that they can hold this against our project, you, or me, because I have documentary proof that I am a victim of fraud in the HE program, but obviously it is better to inform in advance than to explain this in 2026 during the ex post audit.

Best regards,
Daniel

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&lt;mailto:daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;&gt;
Sent: 26 January 2025 21:01
To: Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt;; James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt;
Subject: Reprex financial issues

Hi  Isabella &amp; James,

I wrote a more personal note to Joost, partly explaining my edgy behavior for the repeated lateness of the partners, but I realised that I may need to make my situation clear to you, and perhaps others in the Consortium.

As you know, we won a competition of the EIT, which is technically financed by Horizon Europe (although it is a very different program than our RIA action.)  It is a startup prize, supposed to provide alternative, investment-type funding for startups working on a really big puzzle. We won with our ESG calculator, and the prize is partly an investment, and partly a grant. (There were 307 applicants in 5 sectors, and we won the Audiovisual prize.) In the granted period, the for-profit startups must work on a non-profit basis, and practically they cannot solicit other work. Because we still have some commitment to OpenMusE, and we have some smaller commercial work, we offered all our remaining capacity to them for a year ahead.

Because there was fraudulent misconduct in the EIT KIC the grant payments are prolonged or perhaps even cancelled, and may need to go through the anti-fraud authority and courts.  The misconduct also affected us: they tried to manipulate our score and give our money to somebody else, but we successfully appealed that. Unfortunately, in other parts of the KIC there was money going to pockets that they could not keep under the carpet.

There had always been questions about the financial stability of Reprex. Now the worst possible thing happened: we are entering the period when we are crediting the Horizon program, but at the same time, the Horizon program reserved most of our capacities and failed to pay for us. We should be receiving about 150,000 euros in the coming days, but it may take years as I see that we actually get this money; and this is of course just a first advance (this program has much lower advance rates.)  If Reprex will become insolvent, it will be because of "irregularities" committed on the EU side, and we are (acknowledged by their supervisory report) all but completely innocent victims.

Tomorrow I will go public with this problem, because we need to ask help from our partners, investors, and the least that we want to have is quarrelling within OpenMusE.  I am very edgy, but partly also because I feel that we put more work in than others, and in these extremely challenging times our schedule is often disrupted. I think that we can meet all our commitments in OpenMusE, but we do not want to put more work into the deliverables than others and we want to avoid any quarrelling.

I am doing the best that I can do, and I am by now thinking that Reprex will go under, but the next 3-6 months will be extremely challenging for us.  I think that it would be appropriate to communicate at one point to the PO and other WP leaders. I think that PO is critical; I think it is rather unprecedented that a fraud in the HE program makes a HE beneficiary insolvent, but it may happen.

Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder
+31615058460
linkedin&lt;https://www.linkedin.com/in/antaldaniel/&gt; •  reprex bv&lt;http://reprex.nl/&gt;  • eviota&lt;https://eviota.nl/&gt;

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&lt;mailto:daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;&gt;

Subject: Reprex financial issues

Hi  Isabella &amp; James,

I wrote a more personal note to Joost, partly explaining my edgy behavior for the repeated lateness of the partners, but I realised that I may need to make my situation clear to you, and perhaps others in the Consortium.

As you know, we won a competition of the EIT, which is technically financed by Horizon Europe (although it is a very different program than our RIA action.)  It is a startup prize, supposed to provide alternative, investment-type funding for startups working on a really big puzzle. We won with our ESG calculator, and the prize is partly an investment, and partly a grant. (There were 307 applicants in 5 sectors, and we won the Audiovisual prize.) In the granted period, the for-profit startups must work on a non-profit basis, and practically they cannot solicit other work. Because we still have some commitment to OpenMusE, and we have some smaller commercial work, we offered all our remaining capacity to them for a year ahead.

Because there was fraudulent misconduct in the EIT KIC the grant payments are prolonged or perhaps even cancelled, and may need to go through the anti-fraud authority and courts.  The misconduct also affected us: they tried to manipulate our score and give our money to somebody else, but we successfully appealed that. Unfortunately, in other parts of the KIC there was money going to pockets that they could not keep under the carpet.

There had always been questions about the financial stability of Reprex. Now the worst possible thing happened: we are entering the period when we are crediting the Horizon program, but at the same time, the Horizon program reserved most of our capacities and failed to pay for us. We should be receiving about 150,000 euros in the coming days, but it may take years as I see that we actually get this money; and this is of course just a first advance (this program has much lower advance rates.)  If Reprex will become insolvent, it will be because of "irregularities" committed on the EU side, and we are (acknowledged by their supervisory report) all but completely innocent victims.

Tomorrow I will go public with this problem, because we need to ask help from our partners, investors, and the least that we want to have is quarrelling within OpenMusE.  I am very edgy, but partly also because I feel that we put more work in than others, and in these extremely challenging times our schedule is often disrupted. I think that we can meet all our commitments in OpenMusE, but we do not want to put more work into the deliverables than others and we want to avoid any quarrelling.

I am doing the best that I can do, and I am by now thinking that Reprex will go under, but the next 3-6 months will be extremely challenging for us.  I think that it would be appropriate to communicate at one point to the PO and other WP leaders. I think that PO is critical; I think it is rather unprecedented that a fraud in the HE program makes a HE beneficiary insolvent, but it may happen.

Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder

Dear Daniel,

Each permanent link to an item in the City Library consists of the 
following string:
http://opac.mestskakniznica.sk/opac/openURL?sid= followed by the signature.
This applies to books, LPs, CDs, sheet music, and more. I've requested a 
list of signatures for music documents from the City Library.

However, if you can scrape the signatures (and based on your attachment, 
I understand that you can), it should be easy to generate the URLs from 
them.

Regarding the comparison with our library—unfortunately, we haven’t 
recorded ISBNs in the past. Therefore, the comparison would have to rely 
on 4–5 data points: author, title, publisher, year of publication, and 
ISBN/ISMN (if available in the catalog).

Your points 1–4 look good!
It would be just as interesting to start thinking about how SKCMDb will 
look and how it will be presented.

These days, we are finishing the preliminary work on the data export for 
SK National Library—there’s still quite a bit of fine-tuning to do. 
We’ve also been making some tweaks and additions to our IS. We should 
have everything ready this week for the consultation with NL.
We'll keep you posted.

Best regards,
A.

From: Daniel Antal

Subject: Re-organising the artist/track tables into 3+2

Hi Fabio,

I think that the easiest way is the 11 table solution that I described, but to get there in steps, there is perhaps a different way.  I write the 3 minimum tables, and you can organise the entire handover in three tables, out of which perhaps some variables are extended even next week to tables 1-2.  I am sure that this is understandable for Joost and James, too.

The original 11 table solution was to organise your work the way I would do it, but if that is confusing, we actually are OK with tables 1, 2, 3 going through several revisions, where the revisions only relate to why you collected the data. You can save tremendous time if you think through, and perhaps implement step 1 and step 2 at the same time, because you do not have to go through your saved files and code twice. Step 2 records why you saved the data, Step 1 actually records the data but without purpose.

First step
1. Create a table called tracks with all non-variable (constant) properties of the tracks.The name of the label can be added as a property of the track, no need for a separate label table (we will create it for you.)
2. Create a table called artists with all non-variable (constant) properties of the artists.

You will then deal only with release date (date type) or string. Add them to an artist and a track table.

We need to maintain the connection between artists and tracks. To remain both machine connectible and human reviewable, you create the following relationship table.

3. artist_track_relationships:  add the names and identifiers of every track connected to any artist as you saved it.  For example, if the track is Let it Be, add Let It Be for human review, the spotify_track_id and isrc as identifier, and The Beatles as artist_name for human review, and spotify_artist_id as the ID of the artist.  You repeat this in any permutation.  If Let It Be has a different performer, say a Cover Band, you create a row of Cover Band, coverband_id, Let It Be, isrc of that cover, track_id of that cover.  If The Beatles has another track, you make a relationship row again.

@AnnA Mester&lt;mailto:anna.mester@reprex.nl&gt; will make sure that we understand and document every variable in the 2+1 tables (the relationship table just repeats the IDs of the two tables, no separate documentation is needed.)

@Mihaly Nagy&lt;mailto:nagy.lukin.mihaly@gmail.com&gt; will help to create the PostGreSQL table or take it over if you need help, although we greatly simplified your tables; you only work with text with the exception of release dates.

Second step, but you save time if you think this through before the first step
Now, you can save time if you deal with the only variable now, but we can leave it for later.

Create two tables for the true variables (not constants) to tracks and artists

That will require two popularity tables for artists and tracks.
- The artist_variables table saves the popularity table saves The Beatles, their spotify_artist_id, the popularity score, and the timestamp (because popularity changed over time.)
- The track_variables popularity table saves Let It Be, the spotify_track_id and isrc of this particular recording (original or covered), the popularity score and timestamp.
- You need two tables, because the popularity score is either saved in an artist JSON/table or a track JSON/table.

Further still, you can save time by adding to table 1. and 2. all clear instances of why you corrected them. That basically means adding a single variable, "collection_purpose" and adding a string that you add to a simple Google Doc or whatever.  The "collection_purpose"  is "Artist by Slovak stemword",  or "Artists by Slovak orchestras", or simply adding the spotify_playlist_id, i.e., the "collection_purpose" is retrieving all tracks or artists from the "Samoyed music" playlist.

In this case it will be more @AnnA Mester&lt;mailto:anna.mester@reprex.nl&gt; who helps you, because we basically need to classify the artists and tracks so that we understand why you collected them. The definitions that you add as "collecton_purpose" must be understood by Anna, and she will ensure its logical consistency (i.e., we do not use overlapping categories.)


Best regards

Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder

Betreff: Re: OpenMuseE questionbank

Hi James,

Anna was ill yesterday and if she is unwell, I will take over later today, but only briefly.    We were thinking about how to add the different versions and countries of the questions texts, and we came up with a bit of a complicated but extendible solution.

If you take a look at this, this is a so-called Lexeme: https://reprexbase.eu/demo/index.php?title=Lexeme:L1
It connects the meaning of the word "song" to the English language and to the language-independent concept of the song, which could be Lied or dal as well.  This is a lexicographical item that is used for proper and intelligent machine translation.

If you take a look at this further example, https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Lexeme:L791  it shows that the word "colour" should be used like this in the UK and Canada, but as "color" in the US.

We are working on an extension of our knowledge bases that can do trustworthy translations. This is of course not the intention in your case, you want to record already used and tested translations, but I think it is good to work like this, because that could still improve a lot in the reusability of the questionnaires. I think we are about a year from translating question texts, but for example, for a very reliable translation of categorical lists in response sets we are rather close.

So, we want to provide a solution that will be compatible with this lexicographical extension, because it allows a lot of powerful features, but we will not use it in the coming months.

So, we need to further think about differences, because I think that we have two different issues with localisations.

1)  There is a spelling or other different in the form of the question text, and the difference is due to the differences of the German language used in Austria and Germany; this should be reflected in the use of de-AT, de-DE, en-GB, en-US type abbreviations. The property that describes this is the language, not the country.
2) There is a contextual difference and you would frame differently the question for a Dutch speaker in the Netherlands and Belgium, for example, because the normal way of describing educational levels is country-specific, a Belgian will not understand what is a havo-level education. A similar issue arises when Eurobarometer asks the Swedish questionnaire for Sweden, and asks the Finnish questionnaire for the Swedish minority in Sweden. The property that describes the difference is the country, not the language.

Our system will enable us to record both differences, but it will work with less functionality (still fine for your use case) if you only record the country difference.

So, the easiest notation that I can find out is the following

QID: 9999 label: What is the color of your eyes?
questontext_en-US: What is the color of your eyes? -&gt; this easily splits to questiontext: "What is the color of your eyes?"; language: "en-US"
questiontext_country: United States of America
questontext_en-GB: What is the colour of your eyes? - &gt; we will record this as questionText: "What is the colour of your eyes? ", language: en-GB
questiontext_country: United Kingdom|Canada - &gt; we will record this Q9999 country: United Kingdom, country: Canada
[if you want to be pedantic, you can add an en-CA version, but I think it is not really necessary.]

It will be completely up to you if you want to use only the country-difference, which is easy to code, or both the country and language difference. If you fill out both information, we will be able to do more, if not, it is still useful.

The use of lexemes will be useful with response items, because often they are lexemes themselves:
What is your favorite season? / What is your favourite season:
en-GB: spring, summer, autumn, winter
en-US: spring, summer; fall, winter

Such differences are well captured by the Lexeme items, and if you have such repeating differences, we can cross-check them in every response range if they are correctly used. It would be also possible to machine check the What is your favorite season?/What is your favourite season but we will not do such things in the near future.

The real question here is how many languages and variations we want to work with? On the side of data processing, it is costless to add a new language, but if it only used for 1-2 questions, I think it will have a UX price, because for example, if you have only two questions in de-AT, then all over the place the interface will have empty Austrian versions.

Best regards,
Daniel

Hello James!



Sorry, I do not know Oscar’s email adress please forward this to him.



I am attaching the tutorial we made, please read it through closely, if you have any questions let us know.



Here is the schedule for consultations:



The preparatory steps for consultation 2 and consultation 3 are important to start now because they need time. For 2 we need the most important codebooks to be prepared for us to study and give examples. For 3, it is important that the researchers already now start to describe the concepts that they want to measure, for example, income or turnover definitions related to the uses of mechanical copies of music, public performance of music, etc.  We will use this for the complex questions that collect numbers connected to strictly structured conceptualisations of musicians revenues, or people’s enjoyment of various forms of music, or the notional time of enjoyment of various forms of music.



First consultation

The aim of the first consultation is

  1.  Understand the main classes that we record: Agent, Human, Corporate Body, Group, Universe, Coverage.
  2.  Create a dataset of Studies and Questionnaires. For example, Eurobarometer 93.7 (study) and Eurobarometer 93.7 basic, NL, HU questionnaires.  One study can relate to many questionnaires.
  3.  Create a dataset of basic questions (these are, for example, the EN versions of the Eurobarometer EN/FR bilingual master questionnaire.) The question definition does not yet contain a codebook, except for binary coded variables; it contains variable representation types (numeric, text, coded, datetime).  The actual addition of the codebooks is the task for next week.
  4.  Create a dataset of QuestionTexts, which are the language versions of the QuestionText properties of a Question.



We will be able to start building a questionbank, because we identify questions in questionnaires connected to studies, and we record the main data of the questions. This is not sufficient yet to model the answer options.



Second consultation

The second consultation will be about singular questions with a well-defined codebook (no scale) or codes ordinal or nominal scale variables; we will also talk about special values of numeric types.  This will be sufficient to harmonize questions and their answer options.



As a preparation for this, we would need to have the relevant SDMX cross-domain codebooks to use, and any other codebook that is important for the harmonised variables.



Third consultation

The third consultation will be about structured questions and concept harmonisation, because they are very important for our surveys. For example, when we ask different income categories in a table, in this case, one tabular question is a structured set of questions that connect to conceptual separate income types a numeric value qualified with a timespan and a currency unit.

You should be able to edit it, but if you encounter any problems please let me know.

As promised I am also including the list of representation base types we currently have in our demo: https://reprexbase.eu/demo/index.php?title=Item:Q1384



For the next meeting: we would need you to add the surveys/questionnaires to the uploader that you will need, the questions too, and send the well-defined codebooks (see: second consultation part).

As you know, we won a competition of the EIT, which is technically financed by Horizon Europe (although it is a very different program than our RIA action.)  It is a startup prize, supposed to provide alternative, investment-type funding for startups working on a really big puzzle. We won with our ESG calculator, and the prize is partly an investment, and partly a grant. (There were 307 applicants in 5 sectors, and we won the Audiovisual prize.) In the granted period, the for-profit startups must work on a non-profit basis, and practically they cannot solicit other work. Because we still have some commitment to OpenMusE, and we have some smaller commercial work, we offered all our remaining capacity to them for a year ahead.

Because there was fraudulent misconduct in the EIT KIC the grant payments are prolonged or perhaps even cancelled, and may need to go through the anti-fraud authority and courts.  The misconduct also affected us: they tried to manipulate our score and give our money to somebody else, but we successfully appealed that. Unfortunately, in other parts of the KIC there was money going to pockets that they could not keep under the carpet.

There had always been questions about the financial stability of Reprex. Now the worst possible thing happened: we are entering the period when we are crediting the Horizon program, but at the same time, the Horizon program reserved most of our capacities and failed to pay for us. We should be receiving about 150,000 euros in the coming days, but it may take years as I see that we actually get this money; and this is of course just a first advance (this program has much lower advance rates.)  If Reprex will become insolvent, it will be because of "irregularities" committed on the EU side, and we are (acknowledged by their supervisory report) all but completely innocent victims.

Tomorrow I will go public with this problem, because we need to ask help from our partners, investors, and the least that we want to have is quarrelling within OpenMusE.  I am very edgy, but partly also because I feel that we put more work in than others, and in these extremely challenging times our schedule is often disrupted. I think that we can meet all our commitments in OpenMusE, but we do not want to put more work into the deliverables than others and we want to avoid any quarrelling.

I am doing the best that I can do, and I am by now thinking that Reprex will go under, but the next 3-6 months will be extremely challenging for us.  I think that it would be appropriate to communicate at one point to the PO and other WP leaders. I think that PO is critical; I think it is rather unprecedented that a fraud in the HE program makes a HE beneficiary insolvent, but it may happen.

But factually, we already asked the European Ombudsman and MEP in her supervisory capacity to try to find out why our money is late; if they will be able to squeeze out some documentary evidence from the EIT, then we can say more.

The last thing I want is to have more reporting burden than other members in the Consortium,  I certainly do not want to report earlier and more than the rest of the consortium, this fraud already 10x increased our paperwork.

Best regards,
Daniel

The HE gives advances and ex-post reimbursement; and we have received both advances and reimbursements from them in the past year in the other project. So the payslips will see that in some cases (and only for myself) I pay taxes on time, but wages late. Obviously I very much hope that eventually I will receive my salary, but this is really beyond my control. I quiet frankly could not imagine this level of misconduct and carelessnes from and EU organisation.

I cannot believe that they can hold this against our project, you, or me, because I have documentary proof that I am a victim of fraud in the HE program, but obviously it is better to inform in advance than to explain this in 2026 during the ex post audit.

Best regards,
Daniel

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&lt;mailto:daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;&gt;
Sent: 26 January 2025 21:01
To: Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt;; James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt;
Subject: Reprex financial issues

Hi  Isabella &amp; James,

I wrote a more personal note to Joost, partly explaining my edgy behavior for the repeated lateness of the partners, but I realised that I may need to make my situation clear to you, and perhaps others in the Consortium.

As you know, we won a competition of the EIT, which is technically financed by Horizon Europe (although it is a very different program than our RIA action.)  It is a startup prize, supposed to provide alternative, investment-type funding for startups working on a really big puzzle. We won with our ESG calculator, and the prize is partly an investment, and partly a grant. (There were 307 applicants in 5 sectors, and we won the Audiovisual prize.) In the granted period, the for-profit startups must work on a non-profit basis, and practically they cannot solicit other work. Because we still have some commitment to OpenMusE, and we have some smaller commercial work, we offered all our remaining capacity to them for a year ahead.

Because there was fraudulent misconduct in the EIT KIC the grant payments are prolonged or perhaps even cancelled, and may need to go through the anti-fraud authority and courts.  The misconduct also affected us: they tried to manipulate our score and give our money to somebody else, but we successfully appealed that. Unfortunately, in other parts of the KIC there was money going to pockets that they could not keep under the carpet.

There had always been questions about the financial stability of Reprex. Now the worst possible thing happened: we are entering the period when we are crediting the Horizon program, but at the same time, the Horizon program reserved most of our capacities and failed to pay for us. We should be receiving about 150,000 euros in the coming days, but it may take years as I see that we actually get this money; and this is of course just a first advance (this program has much lower advance rates.)  If Reprex will become insolvent, it will be because of "irregularities" committed on the EU side, and we are (acknowledged by their supervisory report) all but completely innocent victims.

Tomorrow I will go public with this problem, because we need to ask help from our partners, investors, and the least that we want to have is quarrelling within OpenMusE.  I am very edgy, but partly also because I feel that we put more work in than others, and in these extremely challenging times our schedule is often disrupted. I think that we can meet all our commitments in OpenMusE, but we do not want to put more work into the deliverables than others and we want to avoid any quarrelling.

I am doing the best that I can do, and I am by now thinking that Reprex will go under, but the next 3-6 months will be extremely challenging for us.  I think that it would be appropriate to communicate at one point to the PO and other WP leaders. I think that PO is critical; I think it is rather unprecedented that a fraud in the HE program makes a HE beneficiary insolvent, but it may happen.

Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder
+31615058460
linkedin&lt;https://www.linkedin.com/in/antaldaniel/&gt; •  reprex bv&lt;http://reprex.nl/&gt;  • eviota&lt;https://eviota.nl/&gt;

James

### OpenMusE -- T1.2 {#email-879}

The HE gives advances and ex-post reimbursement; and we have received both advances and reimbursements from them in the past year in the other project. So the payslips will see that in some cases (and only for myself) I pay taxes on time, but wages late. Obviously I very much hope that eventually I will receive my salary, but this is really beyond my control. From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&lt;mailto:daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;&gt;
Sent: 26 January 2025 21:01
To: Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt;; James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&lt;mailto:JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;&gt;
Subject: Reprex financial issues

Hi  Isabella &amp; James,

I wrote a more personal note to Joost, partly explaining my edgy behavior for the repeated lateness of the partners, but I realised that I may need to make my situation clear to you, and perhaps others in the Consortium.

As you know, we won a competition of the EIT, which is technically financed by Horizon Europe (although it is a very different program than our RIA action.)  It is a startup prize, supposed to provide alternative, investment-type funding for startups working on a really big puzzle. We won with our ESG calculator, and the prize is partly an investment, and partly a grant. (There were 307 applicants in 5 sectors, and we won the Audiovisual prize.) In the granted period, the for-profit startups must work on a non-profit basis, and practically they cannot solicit other work. Because we still have some commitment to OpenMusE, and we have some smaller commercial work, we offered all our remaining capacity to them for a year ahead.

Because there was fraudulent misconduct in the EIT KIC the grant payments are prolonged or perhaps even cancelled, and may need to go through the anti-fraud authority and courts.  The misconduct also affected us: they tried to manipulate our score and give our money to somebody else, but we successfully appealed that. Unfortunately, in other parts of the KIC there was money going to pockets that they could not keep under the carpet.

There had always been questions about the financial stability of Reprex. Now the worst possible thing happened: we are entering the period when we are crediting the Horizon program, but at the same time, the Horizon program reserved most of our capacities and failed to pay for us. We should be receiving about 150,000 euros in the coming days, but it may take years as I see that we actually get this money; and this is of course just a first advance (this program has much lower advance rates.)  If Reprex will become insolvent, it will be because of "irregularities" committed on the EU side, and we are (acknowledged by their supervisory report) all but completely innocent victims.

Tomorrow I will go public with this problem, because we need to ask help from our partners, investors, and the least that we want to have is quarrelling within OpenMusE.  I am very edgy, but partly also because I feel that we put more work in than others, and in these extremely challenging times our schedule is often disrupted. I think that we can meet all our commitments in OpenMusE, but we do not want to put more work into the deliverables than others and we want to avoid any quarrelling.

I am doing the best that I can do, and I am by now thinking that Reprex will go under, but the next 3-6 months will be extremely challenging for us.  I think that it would be appropriate to communicate at one point to the PO and other WP leaders. I think that PO is critical; I think it is rather unprecedented that a fraud in the HE program makes a HE beneficiary insolvent, but it may happen.

Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder

From: Daniel Antal
Sent: Monday, February 03, 2025 14:05
To: Joost Poort; James Rhys Edwards
Cc: Mihaly Nagy; AnnA Mester
Subject: Re-organising the artist/track tables into 3+2



Hi Fabio,



I think that the easiest way is the 11 table solution that I described, but to get there in steps, there is perhaps a different way.  I write the 3 minimum tables, and you can organise the entire handover in three tables, out of which perhaps some variables are extended even next week to tables 1-2.  I am sure that this is understandable for Joost and James, too.



The original 11 table solution was to organise your work the way I would do it, but if that is confusing, we actually are OK with tables 1, 2, 3 going through several revisions, where the revisions only relate to why you collected the data. You can save tremendous time if you think through, and perhaps implement step 1 and step 2 at the same time, because you do not have to go through your saved files and code twice. Step 2 records why you saved the data, Step 1 actually records the data but without purpose.



First step

1. Create a table called tracks with all non-variable (constant) properties of the tracks.The name of the label can be added as a property of the track, no need for a separate label table (we will create it for you.)

2. Create a table called artists with all non-variable (constant) properties of the artists.



You will then deal only with release date (date type) or string. Add them to an artist and a track table.



We need to maintain the connection between artists and tracks. To remain both machine connectible and human reviewable, you create the following relationship table.



3. artist_track_relationships:  add the names and identifiers of every track connected to any artist as you saved it.  For example, if the track is Let it Be, add Let It Be for human review, the spotify_track_id and isrc as identifier, and The Beatles as artist_name for human review, and spotify_artist_id as the ID of the artist.  You repeat this in any permutation.  If Let It Be has a different performer, say a Cover Band, you create a row of Cover Band, coverband_id, Let It Be, isrc of that cover, track_id of that cover.  If The Beatles has another track, you make a relationship row again.



@AnnA Mester&lt;mailto:anna.mester@reprex.nl&gt; will make sure that we understand and document every variable in the 2+1 tables (the relationship table just repeats the IDs of the two tables, no separate documentation is needed.)



@Mihaly Nagy&lt;mailto:nagy.lukin.mihaly@gmail.com&gt; will help to create the PostGreSQL table or take it over if you need help, although we greatly simplified your tables; you only work with text with the exception of release dates.



Second step, but you save time if you think this through before the first step

Now, you can save time if you deal with the only variable now, but we can leave it for later.



Create two tables for the true variables (not constants) to tracks and artists



That will require two popularity tables for artists and tracks.

- The artist_variables table saves the popularity table saves The Beatles, their spotify_artist_id, the popularity score, and the timestamp (because popularity changed over time.)

- The track_variables popularity table saves Let It Be, the spotify_track_id and isrc of this particular recording (original or covered), the popularity score and timestamp.

- You need two tables, because the popularity score is either saved in an artist JSON/table or a track JSON/table.



Further still, you can save time by adding to table 1. and 2. all clear instances of why you corrected them. That basically means adding a single variable, "collection_purpose" and adding a string that you add to a simple Google Doc or whatever.  The "collection_purpose"  is "Artist by Slovak stemword",  or "Artists by Slovak orchestras", or simply adding the spotify_playlist_id, i.e., the "collection_purpose" is retrieving all tracks or artists from the "Samoyed music" playlist.



In this case it will be more @AnnA Mester&lt;mailto:anna.mester@reprex.nl&gt; who helps you, because we basically need to classify the artists and tracks so that we understand why you collected them. The definitions that you add as "collecton_purpose" must be understood by Anna, and she will ensure its logical consistency (i.e., we do not use overlapping categories.)





Best regards

Adapting the European Music Industry to the Platform Economy

When? During &lt;http://www.tmw.ee/&gt; Tallinn Music Week&lt;http://www.tmw.ee/&gt; (TMW) on Thursday, April 3rd, 2025, 09:30 - 16:30
Where? Nordic Hotel Forum, Viru väljak 3, Tallinn, Estonia
Register by March 1st, 2025 here&lt;https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=DQSIkWdsW0yxEjajBLZtrQAAAAAAAAAAAAMAAHFNMuNUQ08wVDRQRjZKWUcxQzRVNkRZVloxV1czQi4u&gt;.
Organizers: ekip&lt;https://ekipengine.eu/&gt; - European Cultural and Creative Industries Innovation Policy Platform and
TMW in collaboration with Federation of Music Conferences&lt;https://musicconferences.org/&gt;.

What?
You’re invited to take part in a workshop focused on finding solutions to one of the biggest challenges in the European music industry: adapting to the platform economy in a time of rapid technological change.

Global digital platforms like streaming services and social media are changing how music is distributed, monetized, and consumed — often leaving independent artists struggling for sustainable revenues. This workshop will explore how the European music ecosystem can adapt to the platform economy by using new technologies, developing innovative and fairer business models, and ensuring value is distributed more equitably.

The workshop builds on insights from the The European Music Ecosystem&lt;https://musicconferences.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/MME-Dialogue_The-European-Music-Ecosystem.pdf&gt; report, presented on January 17, 2025, at the Eurosonic Festival. The report highlights platformistion as a major challenge for the music sector, showing how digitalisation and globalisation have transformed the industry. Instead of linear and siloed processes, value is now created within complex, open and interconnected networks.

About the Workshop
Now, ekip is taking the discussion further — bringing together industry experts to tackle the pressing challenges of the platform economy, to analyze the impact and craft actionable solutions. This event builds on six months of research and social listening, offering you the opportunity to actively contribute to shaping actionable solutions for a sustainable and competitive European music industry. Recommendations designed as a result of the workshop will inform the European Commission and other stakeholders in supporting a resilient and competitive music ecosystem.

Moderation
The workshop will be moderated by Ragnar Siil&lt;https://www.linkedin.com/in/ragnarsiil/&gt;, an internationally renowned cultural policy and creative industries expert, and the founder of Creativity Lab. Ragnar has advised on cultural policies and creative industry strategies in dozens of countries worldwide. He is a former Estonian Undersecretary of Arts and Chair of the EU Working Group on Cultural and Creative Sectors.

Register!
Sign up by March 1st, 2025 to secure your spot: HERE&lt;https://forms.office.com/r/2jd2kwNcii?origin=lprLink&gt;.

For any questions about the workshop, you are welcome to contact us at ekip@creativitylab.ee&lt;mailto:ekip@creativitylab.ee&gt;. More about the ekip-project: www.ekipengine.eu&lt;http://www.ekipengine.eu/&gt;.

Don’t miss this chance to help shape the future of Europe’s music ecosystem during Tallinn Music Week 2024!


Sincerely,

The ekip Consortium

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;

Subject: For tomorrow - DDI implementation for survey use

Hello James,

This is our DDI primer. We revised it a bit, and therefore only this example (it does not require login) is relevant on Wikibase, but there are two detailed examples which hopefully speak for themselves.

I could not work on Friday because I was ill, and I could not detach the economic register document, however, I think that the only questionable part on how to do it is to prepare for survey use. And that is a bit of a DDI connection.

For an enterprise survey, I think that the connection is almost self-evident, and we will discuss it with related concepts.  For example, if you want to know the income of a company, you must use a well-defined income concept, for example gross profit, net profit after tax, or net turnover.

For a population or mixed mode survey, this gets more interesting because you need to identify your subjects by their role. The examples given here relate to that, but simplify the problem to gender identification, because it is easier to show the connection than with occupations.  You want to have a filtering question for well-identified groups, such as women, composers, men, producers, etc.  In a way this goes beyond the registration issue, in this case, you will use a person register, but because you cannot connect the data subjects registration data with the questionnaire (in the enterprise survey, you can), you only can group to an observable property of the people on the population register (women, composers, etc.)

Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA

Dear Colleagues,

Thank you very much again for the lively discussion today.  With my colleague Anna we tried to put into the Tuesday document as much detail as possible for the UN/EU/UK alignment in terms of classifications and data sources.   We clearly reference the occupation and economic activity classification for the UN, EU and UK.

These classifications change very slowly. After Brexit the UK reverted back to its 2007/08 national standards which were fully aligned with the EU. The first possible slight divergence will show perhaps in 2025, when the EU is making a few changes. However, I do not think that this divergence will affect us at all. So at this point I think that all research can be perfectly mapped between the EU and the UK.

I need to finalise this manuscript by the end of next week, and any suggestions, questions, details would be very welcome, before or after. We are working on a similar document on measuring the artistic output and diversity aspects of music which we aim to present to CISAC by the end of April.

What is not in this document (and will be a different document, anyways) is our extension of the ISCO/ESCO/SSC and  ISIC/NACE/SIC codes that we developed in 12 languages. I will create that document separately.

We will make our registers public together with this document, so you will be able to see how it actually works; and soon we will provide API access to it, too.

Best regards,
Daniel

Dear Colleagues,

Apologies for the delay from Friday, our report became too technical and we were parallel publishing the data and the documentation.  You can read the document in an HTML format best.

For researchers who are surveying a music ecosystem of a city or a country perhaps this is the best entry point: https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/open-music-registers/ambition.html#applications,&lt;https://music.dataobservatory.eu/documents/open_music_europe/open-music-registers/ambition.html#applications,&gt; and only the first 20 pages in the PDF version, i.e, the Summary and Ambition part are relevant. The rest is very technical.

We are aiming for a system that is compatible with statistical registers and products of UK Statistics, the registers of PRS and IFPI, or the building cadastres of a country or city where you have the venue physical data. At the same time we are conscious about the need of self-administered, or junior research administered surveys, questionnaires, etc, so we try to design a question bank with appropriate answer options the yield compatible data with official statistics or business registers.

Best regards,
Daniel

Subject: OpenMuseE questionbank


Hello James!



Sorry, I do not know Oscar’s email adress please forward this to him.



I am attaching the tutorial we made, please read it through closely, if you have any questions let us know.



Here is the schedule for consultations:



The preparatory steps for consultation 2 and consultation 3 are important to start now because they need time. For 2 we need the most important codebooks to be prepared for us to study and give examples. For 3, it is important that the researchers already now start to describe the concepts that they want to measure, for example, income or turnover definitions related to the uses of mechanical copies of music, public performance of music, etc.  We will use this for the complex questions that collect numbers connected to strictly structured conceptualisations of musicians revenues, or people’s enjoyment of various forms of music, or the notional time of enjoyment of various forms of music.



First consultation

The aim of the first consultation is

  1.  Understand the main classes that we record: Agent, Human, Corporate Body, Group, Universe, Coverage.
  2.  Create a dataset of Studies and Questionnaires. For example, Eurobarometer 93.7 (study) and Eurobarometer 93.7 basic, NL, HU questionnaires.  One study can relate to many questionnaires.
  3.  Create a dataset of basic questions (these are, for example, the EN versions of the Eurobarometer EN/FR bilingual master questionnaire.) The question definition does not yet contain a codebook, except for binary coded variables; it contains variable representation types (numeric, text, coded, datetime).  The actual addition of the codebooks is the task for next week.
  4.  Create a dataset of QuestionTexts, which are the language versions of the QuestionText properties of a Question.



We will be able to start building a questionbank, because we identify questions in questionnaires connected to studies, and we record the main data of the questions. This is not sufficient yet to model the answer options.



Second consultation

The second consultation will be about singular questions with a well-defined codebook (no scale) or codes ordinal or nominal scale variables; we will also talk about special values of numeric types.  This will be sufficient to harmonize questions and their answer options.



As a preparation for this, we would need to have the relevant SDMX cross-domain codebooks to use, and any other codebook that is important for the harmonised variables.



Third consultation

The third consultation will be about structured questions and concept harmonisation, because they are very important for our surveys. For example, when we ask different income categories in a table, in this case, one tabular question is a structured set of questions that connect to conceptual separate income types a numeric value qualified with a timespan and a currency unit.



Here is the uploader I made: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1hMn86NOmfjacMMbXByXKuUiddUT8Oo5bBNafHBdofpI/edit?gid=436612034#gid=436612034

You should be able to edit it, but if you encounter any problems please let me know.

As promised I am also including the list of representation base types we currently have in our demo: https://reprexbase.eu/demo/index.php?title=Item:Q1384



For the next meeting: we would need you to add the surveys/questionnaires to the uploader that you will need, the questions too, and send the well-defined codebooks (see: second consultation part).

Here is the schedule for consultations:



The preparatory steps for consultation 2 and consultation 3 are important to start now because they need time. For 2 we need the most important codebooks to be prepared for us to study and give examples. For 3, it is important that the researchers already now start to describe the concepts that they want to measure, for example, income or turnover definitions related to the uses of mechanical copies of music, public performance of music, etc.  We will use this for the complex questions that collect numbers connected to strictly structured conceptualisations of musicians revenues, or people’s enjoyment of various forms of music, or the notional time of enjoyment of various forms of music.



First consultation

The aim of the first consultation is

  1.  Understand the main classes that we record: Agent, Human, Corporate Body, Group, Universe, Coverage.
  2.  Create a dataset of Studies and Questionnaires. For example, Eurobarometer 93.7 (study) and Eurobarometer 93.7 basic, NL, HU questionnaires.  One study can relate to many questionnaires.
  3.  Create a dataset of basic questions (these are, for example, the EN versions of the Eurobarometer EN/FR bilingual master questionnaire.) The question definition does not yet contain a codebook, except for binary coded variables; it contains variable representation types (numeric, text, coded, datetime).  The actual addition of the codebooks is the task for next week.
  4.  Create a dataset of QuestionTexts, which are the language versions of the QuestionText properties of a Question.



We will be able to start building a questionbank, because we identify questions in questionnaires connected to studies, and we record the main data of the questions. This is not sufficient yet to model the answer options.



Second consultation

The second consultation will be about singular questions with a well-defined codebook (no scale) or codes ordinal or nominal scale variables; we will also talk about special values of numeric types.  This will be sufficient to harmonize questions and their answer options.



As a preparation for this, we would need to have the relevant SDMX cross-domain codebooks to use, and any other codebook that is important for the harmonised variables.



Third consultation

The third consultation will be about structured questions and concept harmonisation, because they are very important for our surveys. For example, when we ask different income categories in a table, in this case, one tabular question is a structured set of questions that connect to conceptual separate income types a numeric value qualified with a timespan and a currency unit.

You should be able to edit it, but if you encounter any problems please let me know.

As promised I am also including the list of representation base types we currently have in our demo: https://reprexbase.eu/demo/index.php?title=Item:Q1384



For the next meeting: we would need you to add the surveys/questionnaires to the uploader that you will need, the questions too, and send the well-defined codebooks (see: second consultation part).

Questionbank
Friday, February 21 · 10:00 – 10:45am
Time zone: Europe/Prague
Google Meet joining info
Video call link: https://meet.google.com/pam-czie-wbk

Regarding your question about DDI, I do not know what you plan to do. I think for reading and understanding DDI, the XML format and xml2 is not good. DDI, while not supported by a formal ontology yet comprehensively, is described in an RDF-esque graph format as it is part of GSIM (DDI+SDMX) where SDMX has been in RDF since 2009.  To me a logical application would be to read in the XML to any RDF reader and then convert it to Turtle, which is the human-readable format of graph data. If this is not clear to me, RDF uses RDFXML, but since DDI is part of GSIM, I would assume that those documents read and translate well to RDF.

My problem with loading it to R via xml2 will not make it more readable for you if you are not a good programmer, because R will translate a language (xml) to another language (R), and nested lists are not readable easily for an inexperienced programmer.

Also, DDI is huge. If you only want to understand the DDI variable representation, it is well documented in English.  So, it would be better to talk about your use case and I recommend a bettter tool than a simple R parser.


Best regards,
Daniel

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: 21 February 2025 11:09
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;; Isabella Tautscher &lt;Isabella.Tautscher@sinus-institut.de&gt;; Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;
Cc: Balázs Huszák &lt;bhuszak@artisjus.com&gt;; Dr. Kabai Eszter &lt;ekabai@artisjus.com&gt;
Subject: Questionnaires and models for valuing music: timeline

Dear Isabella, James, Tomas,

We had a call today on survey harmonisation and I told the Sinus colleagues that I am planning to go to Bratislava to prepare ground for the valuation study.  Tomas's aim is very clearly the public performance of music, but not live music, while for Artisjus, live music is important.  This is not a problem at all, as the licensing model is similar, and some of the licensees, too.


  1.  James suggested that we will have a report that our surveying methodology is sound. This is an important first step, but we also need this for the economic model.
  2.  James said that he used the Artisjus 2019 questionnaire as a basis, but that questionnaire is not focused on public performance but a special type of mechanical licensing, i.e., private copying.  We worked with public performance in Hungary in 2015 and in Slovakia in 2018. (And Czechia in 2017.)

When both the surveying methodology and the economic model is finalised, we can start selecting questions or write new ones, because we know what quantitative methodology will collect data about what variables.

Our understanding that we are not there yet, and therefore the actual planning of the questionnaires cannot be finalised.


  1.  So, a realistic timeline for us, provided that by 10 March the researchers come up with a useful corroboration of our earlier methods and possible improvements is that
  2.  we can finalise the economic model in the second half of March, and have the three final questionnaires by early April.
  3.  If we plan in parallel the administration of the surveys, I think it is realistic to think that we can start the fieldwork in mid-May.

We are counting on the following surveys:

- a general population survey, administered by SINUS
- a music population survey, administered by SOZA and Artisjus
- and an enterprise survey, which we do not know who will administer, because neither SSSA nor EUBA seem to be targeting the population segments and the geographical scope where we need data from.

I understand that Arianna wants to do something with Orbis, but that is not relevant for our work; in fact, I think she will confirm the results of the last 20 years that have many times proven that NACE-based sample surveys do not provide data for music. But if that is an admissible scientific result, in spite of countless studies that already proven this, that is their responsibility. However, it does not bring us closer to do valuations on real data.

We need to survey enterprises in Slovakia and Hungary for the purpose of a valuation exercise, and not enterprises randomly in random places. Reprex will most certainly not take on this task without financial compensation.

Whenever we surveyed enterprises for valuation purposes, it was not done via online self-administration, because enterprises are just not willing to do it. Their basic data is already in the company house or they gave it to the statistical office, and they will not give it to us again. Our only realistic chance was to freeride on the Slovak KULT survey but we missed it in 2024 and 2025, too.

Because enterprise surveys do not need to have a large sample, as we often target very small populations, I think that administering the surveys in a mixed mode is not a huge cost, or working out some administrative / mixed mode surveying.

For the public performance, if we go down that route, we need data that can be at least partially scraped. For the hedonic price model, we need price data from venues that have music, and some of this is available either online on menus, or can be bought from restaurant listing agencies. In 2015 and 2018 it was Artisjus and SOZA agents who surveyed the HORECA sector, as they do it anyway for monitoring the licensees. Because the financial data of the enterprises and their venues exists already in databases, usually you need very few questions, in 2018 we even programmed a small smartphone app where the fieldworkers could add the data with a few clicks. It even recorded the geolocation to know they were really at the venue.

We also worked with student associations, because such surveys can be administered face to face by students. I repeatedly suggested that if so far EUBA did so little in this consortium, at least they do contribute to the surveying with documentation and for example, organising student work.

I would find it extremely risky and unprofessional if the three surveys would be designed and administered independently, and if the fieldwork would start before even agreeing on what data is needed from the fieldwork. I do not think that the three questionnaires can be finished before the economic model is there, and they must relate to each other.

Best regards,

Daniel Antal, CFA
co-founder

From: Daniel Antal &lt;daniel.antal@reprex.nl&gt;
Sent: 21 February 2025 12:25
To: James Rhys Edwards &lt;JamesRhys.Edwards@sinus-institut.de&gt;; Mikš Tomáš &lt;tomas.miks@soza.sk&gt;; Richard Demčák &lt;richard.demcak@soza.sk&gt;; marian.jankovic@soza.sk &lt;Marian.Jankovic@soza.sk&gt;; Dr. Kabai Eszter &lt;ekabai@artisjus.com&gt;; Balazs Bodo &lt;B.Bodo@uva.nl&gt;; Tamara Kamińska &lt;tamara.kaminska@musicexportpoland.org&gt;
Subject: Re: OpenMusE general population survey -- final ONLINE draft


Dear James,


I understand that substituting in prior CEEMID questions is the aim, but our questions did not really work well for public performance.  We did try that in CAP2015 Hungary and CAP2015 Slovakia and the results were not good. We do not want to use most of those questions.


What I see in the Questionnaire that you  sent is really good, but what is missing is not something we can invent on the fly.  I think that it would be good if next week we could pin down the actual questions and available data, so that we can figure out what we may want to receive by surveys.


In the current questionnaire, there are a good questions, but rather critical ones are missing.  For the valuation of music, with Artisjus's interest in live performances and SOZA's in background music, we need to follow the following logical chain.


Aritsjus, SOZA (ZAIKS, MusicAutor) must give a license to the venue that is proportional to the value of the music in use.

They want to calculate the value of their license

-  L1 the shared part of the value of the music for the venue as a business entity as a licensing fee.


The value of the music in use has three components:

- V1 the value of the music for society;

- V2 the value of the music for the venue as a business entity;

- V3 the value of the music for the visitor of the venue as a member of the audience.


The value of the music for the venue V2 is a part of the V1 value, and the amount that CMOs can ask in a licensing fee L1 is a part of L2.


L1             &lt; V2                             =&lt; V3                       =&lt; V1

The V1 is a different thing, because musicians as members of society as well as the audience sees positive and adverse effects, and for the CMOs this is not a relevant research question now. It is a really ambiguous value here.

This follows from competition economics; if we would have L1 = V2 then the CMO would exploit its monopoly position to provide a license.


The V2 is proportional to V1, and it is captured by

a) selling tickets

b) selling sponsorship

c) increased occupancy

d) increased sale of beverages (food usually is not profitable.)

e) we also consider the travel costs for the audience


So we must focus on V2.


V2a: ticket sales: we have data on this from administrative survey and in CAP questions.

V2b: this data needs to be addressed in one of the three surveys or all of them

V2c: this data needs to be addressed in all surveys, because we have no evidence on this   [also relates somewhat to V1]

V2d1: more beverages are sold -&gt; needs to be addressed perhaps in CAP?  [relates to V1]

V2d2: the price of the beverages is higher if there is music -&gt; hedonic price model -&gt; enterprise survey   [relates to V1]

V2e: measured in CAP, but also with geolocation data, distance from population centers


For WP3 we can also collect data that do not affect the value of the license, but have a social, environmental or cascading music economy effect:


V1d1, V1d2: external benefits for the foods and drinks industry, and external adverse effects on health

V1e: external benefits for travel and transport, and external adverse effects on environment

V1f: musicians sell merchandise, which has all sorts of economic and environmental effects, which is positive for SOZA and Artisjus members but do not reflect the licensing fee.


This is very complex, and I do not see that we can solve it before we have the economic model, the target countries and areas, the available administrative sources, and clarity on the enterprise survey.


Best regards,
Daniel

Subject: Questionnaires and models for music ESG

Dear James,

These are my suggestions  if you want  to use the ESG and co-publish with the Eviota tool. The European Sustainability Reporting Standard defines about 200 standard indicators, and a CAP survey is very suitable to measure some directly, and to validate others indirectly.

S3: affected communities - this could connect well to WP3, WP2, and other projects.

What we would need:
Focus on the visitor's last yearly concerts and the very last concert.

Was the music that was staged claiming to be an authentic representation of an Indigenous community, such as an ethnic group or an Indigenous minority group? Our dataset on Finnougrin minority pop music would be a great fit.

Do the respondents consider themselves members of this particular group or such a group? -&gt; can go to demography to  not lead the conversation

Then, 1-2 questions directly related to the matters under S3, for example, if the event was positive or negative for the Indigenous group, did it treat them respectfully, was it at a location necessary for this group, or on the contrary, allowed the Indigenous group to showcase their culture elsewhere, did it allow to reconnect to the diaspora.

The liturgical use of music could also be considered here; in this case, we calculate the effects on faith-based groups.

S4—The S4 treats music users as "consumers," so all questions do not concern amateur and liturgical practices; the question is whether you will directly measure any S4 indicators. This is the lowest-hanging fruit.

E1—The travel and transport questions are the most important because live music generates the far largest climate footprint; this is not the case for recorded music. I argue that streaming use has the biggest E1 effect on recorded music.

You need to extend/review the travel questions a bit.

E5—Recycling is a huge issue, and I think it applies to recorded music (recycling the many gadgets, smartphones, etc) and live music. I believe that these indicators are easy to instrumentalise.

S1-S2: these are for example KeyChange relevant issues, it could be interesting to know gender representation on stage or in recorded music. It could be contrasted with data from the music professional surveys (direct access to the workforce.)  To me, it would be very interesting if anybody recalls an event that met the KeyChange objectives, i.e., had at least 40% non-male acts on stage. KeyChange does not measure at all its indicators, neither from concert organisers nor from the audience.  Tons of organisers claim compliance, but it is very questionable if much of the audience were present in such shows.

Best regards,
Daniel
